A company plans to deploy an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster for a workload. The company expects the cluster to support an unpredictable number of stateless pods. Many pods will be created over a brief period as the workload automatically scales the number of replicas it uses.  
  
Which solution will **MAXIMIZE** node resilience?

options.text: Use a separate launch template to deploy the EKS control plane into a second cluster that is separate from the workload node groups.
Update the workload node groups. Use a smaller number of node groups and larger instances in the node groups.
Configure the Kubernetes Cluster Autoscaler to ensure that the compute capacity of the workload node groups stays underprovisioned.
Configure the workload to use topology spread constraints that are based on Availability Zone.

questions.explanation:
Availability Zone–based topology spread constraints direct Kubernetes to distribute workload replicas across AZ failure domains. This limits the effect of a node or AZ failure on stateless replicas and preserves capacity for the workload in the remaining zones. AWS recommends using node labels with pod topology spread constraints to spread pods across zones and reduce the risk that a correlated failure affects the entire workload.

**Learn more:** [VPC and subnet considerations for Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/subnets.html) · [Running highly available applications on Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/best-practices/application.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses AWS Organizations to manage multiple accounts. Because of regulatory requirements, it needs to restrict specified member accounts to the AWS Regions in which they are allowed to deploy resources. Resources in those accounts must be tagged according to a group standard, with enforcement and central management requiring minimal configuration.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS Config rule in the specific member accounts to limit Regions and apply a tag policy.
From the AWS Billing and Cost Management console, in the management account, disable Regions for the specific member accounts and apply a tag policy on the root.
Associate the specific member accounts with the root. Apply a tag policy and an SCP using conditions to limit Regions.
Associate the specific member accounts with a new OU. Apply a tag policy and an SCP using conditions to limit Regions.

questions.explanation:
AWS Organizations tag policies centrally standardize and enforce tag requirements for resources in accounts. A service control policy (SCP) using `aws:RequestedRegion` conditions can deny actions in unapproved Regions. Attaching both policies to a dedicated organizational unit (OU) applies the controls automatically to the specified member accounts while avoiding an organization-wide root-level restriction.

**Learn more:** [Managing organization policies with AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies.html) · [Managing organizational units (OUs) with AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_ous.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect plans to migrate critical Microsoft SQL Server databases to AWS. Since the databases are legacy systems, the solutions architect will move them to a modern data architecture. The solutions architect must complete the database migration with near-zero downtime.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS Application Migration Service and the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT). Perform an in-place upgrade before the migration. Export the migrated data to Amazon Aurora Serverless after cutover. Repoint the applications to Amazon Aurora.

Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to rehost the database. Set Amazon S3 as a target. Set up change data capture (CDC) replication. When the source and destination are fully synchronized, load the data from Amazon S3 into an Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server DB instance.

Use native database high availability tools. Connect the source system to an Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server DB instance. Configure replication accordingly. When data replication is finished, transition the workload to an Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server DB instance.

Use AWS Application Migration Service. Rehost the database server on Amazon EC2. When data replication is finished, detach the database and move the database to an Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server DB instance. Reattach the database and then cut over all networking.

questions.explanation:
Native Microsoft SQL Server high availability tools (Always On Availability Groups, distributed availability group clusters) provide true active-active replication to Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server, achieving near-zero downtime during cutover by leveraging synchronous transactional replication. While setup requires careful coordination, native tools preserve application compatibility and offer the closest approach to zero-downtime migration. AWS DMS full-load-plus-CDC provides limited-downtime capability, but native SQL Server replication is the gold standard for the lowest RTO and RPO in SQL Server migrations.

**Learn more:** [Migrating SQL Server to Amazon RDS using native backup and restore](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/database/migrating-sql-server-to-amazon-rds-using-native-backup-and-restore/) · [Importing and exporting SQL Server databases using native backup and restore](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/SQLServer.Procedural.Importing.html)

options.text: Open the AWS CloudTrail console. Select the log group that contains the NAT gateway's elastic network interface and the private instance's elastic network interlace. Run a query to filter with the destination address set as

All environments run 24 hours a day, 7 days a week, using stateful Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon RDS for MySQL databases. The databases range from 500 GB to 800 GB in size.

What should a solutions architect do to reduce costs with the **LEAST** operational effort?

options.text: Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs once every day. Configure the rule to invoke one AWS Lambda function that starts or slops instances based on me tag, day, and time.

Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs every business day in the evening. Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function that stops instances based on the tag. Create a second EventBridge rule that runs every business day in the morning. Configure the second rule lo invoke another Lambda function that starts instances based on the tag.

Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs every business day in the evening, Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function that terminates, instances based on the lag. Create a second EventBridge rule that runs every business day in the morning. Configure the second rule lo invoke another Lambda function that restores the instances from their last backup based on the tag.

Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that runs every hour. Configure the rule to invoke one AWS Lambda function that terminates or restores instances from their last backup based on the tag. day, and time.

questions.explanation:
Stopping non-production EC2 instances and RDS DB instances after business hours, then starting them before the next business day, preserves their state while avoiding charges for running compute capacity when the development and testing environments are not needed. Amazon RDS supports temporarily stopping DB instances for intermittent daily development use, and Amazon EC2 can be scheduled for stop/start actions through Lambda and EventBridge. Terminating stateful resources and restoring 500–800 GB databases from backup adds unnecessary operational effort and recovery time.

A company with worldwide offices has one 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection to one AWS Region. Its on-premises network uses that connection to communicate with the company’s resources in the AWS Cloud. The connection has one private virtual interface that connects to a single VPC.  
  
A solutions architect must implement a solution that adds a redundant Direct Connect connection in the same Region. The solution must also deliver connectivity to other Regions through the same pair of Direct Connect connections as the company expands into additional Regions.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Provision a Direct Connect gateway. Delete the existing private virtual interface from the existing connection. Create the second Direct Connect connection. Create a new private virtual interface on each connection, and connect both private virtual interfaces to the Direct Connect gateway. Connect the Direct Connect gateway to the single VPC.

Keep the existing private virtual interface. Create the second Direct Connect connection. Create a new private virtual interface on the new connection, and connect the new private virtual interface to the single VPC.

Keep the existing private virtual interface. Create the second Direct Connect connection. Create a new public virtual interface on the new connection, and connect the new public virtual interface to the single VPC.

Provision a transit gateway. Delete the existing private virtual interface from the existing connection. Create the second Direct Connect connection. Create a new private virtual interface on each connection, and connect both private virtual interfaces to the transit gateway. Associate the transit gateway with the single VPC.

questions.explanation:
A Direct Connect gateway is a global construct that lets private virtual interfaces on multiple Direct Connect connections connect to VPCs in different AWS Regions. Attaching a private virtual interface directly to a virtual private gateway is limited to a single VPC in the same Region, while a public virtual interface provides access to public AWS services rather than private VPC resources.

**Learn more:** [AWS Direct Connect gateways](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-gateways-intro.html) · [AWS Direct Connect API: CreatePrivateVirtualInterface](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/APIReference/API_CreatePrivateVirtualInterface.html)

A company needs to move some on-premises Oracle databases to AWS. The company has chosen to keep some of the databases on premises for business compliance reasons.  
  
The on-premises databases contain spatial data and run cron jobs for maintenance. The company needs to connect to the on-premises systems directly from AWS to query data as a foreign table.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create Amazon DynamoDB global tables with auto scaling enabled. Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) and AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to move the data from on premises to DynamoDB. Create an AWS Lambda function to move the spatial data to Amazon S3. Query the data by using Amazon Athena. Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule jobs in DynamoDB for maintenance. Use Amazon API Gateway for foreign table support.

Create an Amazon RDS for Microsoft SQL Server DB instance. Use native replication to move the data from on premises to the DB instance. Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to modify the SQL Server schema as needed after replication. Move the spatial data to Amazon Redshift. Use stored procedures for system maintenance. Create AWS Glue crawlers to connect to the on-premises Oracle databases for foreign table support.

Launch Amazon EC2 instances to host the Oracle databases. Place the EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Use AWS Application Migration Service to move the data from on premises to the EC2 instances and for real-time bidirectional change data capture (CDC) synchronization. Use Oracle native spatial data support. Create an AWS Lambda function to run maintenance jobs as part of an AWS Step Functions workflow. Create an internet gateway for foreign table support.

Create an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) and AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to move the data from on premises to the DB instance. Use PostgreSQL native spatial data support. Run cron jobs on the DB instance for maintenance. Use AWS Direct Connect to connect the DB instance to the on-premises environment for foreign table support.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL natively supports spatial data through the PostGIS extension, making it suitable for Oracle spatial data. AWS Schema Conversion Tool and DMS enable schema migration with full support for stored procedures. AWS Direct Connect provides the secure, low-latency connectivity needed for foreign table queries to on-premises Oracle databases, while PostgreSQL's pg_cron extension supports scheduled maintenance jobs.

**Learn more:** [Working with Oracle databases using the oracle_fdw extension](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/postgresql-oracle-fdw.html) · [What is the AWS Schema Conversion Tool?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/SchemaConversionTool/latest/userguide/CHAP_Welcome.html)

A company wants to use AWS to build a business-continuity solution in the event that the company's primary on-premises application fails. The application runs on physical servers that also host other applications. The on-premises application the company plans to migrate uses a MySQL database as its data store. All of the company's on-premises applications use operating systems compatible with Amazon EC2.  
  
Which solution will meet the company's goal with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Install the AWS Replication Agent on the source servers, including the MySQL servers. Set up replication for all servers. Launch test instances for regular drills. Cut over to the test instances to fail over the workload in the case of a failure event.

Install the AWS Replication Agent on the source servers, including the MySQL servers. Initialize AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery in the target AWS Region. Define the launch settings. Frequently perform failover and fallback from the most recent point in time.

Create AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) replication servers and a target Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster to host the database. Create a DMS replication task to copy the existing data to the target DB cluster. Create a local AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) change data capture (CDC) task to keep the data synchronized. Install the rest of the software on EC2 instances by starting with a compatible base AMI.

Deploy an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway on premises. Mount volumes on all on-premises servers. Install the application and the MySQL database on the new volumes. Take regular snapshots. Install all the software on EC2 Instances by starting with a compatible base AMI. Launch a Volume Gateway on an EC2 instance. Restore the volumes from the latest snapshot. Mount the new volumes on the EC2 instances in the case of a failure event.

questions.explanation:
AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery uses an agent on each supported source server to continuously replicate its block-level state to AWS and can launch recovery instances using configured launch settings. It supports physical servers and preserves the server, application, operating system, and database state, avoiding separate database migration and synchronization or manual volume snapshot-and-restore processes. Its recovery and failback capabilities provide the lowest operational overhead for this workload.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/drs/latest/userguide/what-is-drs.html) · [On-premises DR to AWS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/backup-recovery/on-prem-dr-to-aws.html)

A company wants to manage the costs of migrating a group of 20 infrequently used but business-critical applications to AWS. The applications are a mixture of Java and Node.js, distributed across different instance clusters. The company wants to minimize costs while standardizing on a single deployment methodology.  
  
Most applications are part of month-end processing routines with few concurrent users, although they are occasionally run at other times. Average application memory consumption is less than 1 GB, though some applications consume as much as 2.5 GB of memory during peak processing. The most important application in the group is a Java billing report that accesses multiple data sources and frequently runs for several hours.  
  
Which solution is the **MOST** cost-effective?

options.text: Deploy a separate AWS Lambda function for each application. Use AWS CloudTrail logs and Amazon CloudWatch alarms to verify completion of critical jobs.

Deploy Amazon ECS containers on Amazon EC2 with Auto Scaling configured for memory utilization of 75%. Deploy an ECS task for each application being migrated with ECS task scaling. Monitor services and hosts by using Amazon CloudWatch.
Deploy AWS Elastic Beanstalk for each application with Auto Scaling to ensure that all requests have sufficient resources. Monitor each AWS Elastic Beanstalk deployment by using CloudWatch alarms.

Deploy a new Amazon EC2 instance cluster that co-hosts all applications by using EC2 Auto Scaling and Application Load Balancers. Scale cluster size based on a custom metric set on instance memory utilization. Purchase 3-year Reserved Instance reservations equal to the GroupMaxSize parameter of the Auto Scaling group.

questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda functions have a maximum invocation timeout of 900 seconds (15 minutes), so they cannot directly run a billing-report workload that often executes for several hours. Amazon ECS tasks running in containers can support long-running Java and Node.js workloads with one deployment model, while task and EC2 Auto Scaling allow compute capacity to scale with memory demand instead of maintaining or reserving capacity for the maximum cluster size.

**Learn more:** [AWS Lambda quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/gettingstarted-limits.html) · [Amazon ECS Service Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/service-auto-scaling.html)

Hundreds of the company’s Lambda functions have broad permissions, such as full access to Amazon S3 buckets and Amazon DynamoDB tables. The company wants every function to have only the minimum permissions required to complete its task.  
  
A solutions architect must identify the permissions required by each Lambda function.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to meet this requirement with the **LEAST** amount of effort?

options.text: Set up Amazon CodeGuru to profile the Lambda functions and search for AWS API calls. Create an inventory of the required API calls and resources for each Lambda function. Create new IAM access policies for each Lambda function. Review the new policies to ensure that they meet the company's business requirements.

Turn on AWS CloudTrail logging for the AWS account. Use AWS Identity and Access Management Access Analyzer to generate IAM access policies based on the activity recorded in the CloudTrail log. Review the generated policies to ensure that they meet the company's business requirements.

Turn on AWS CloudTrail logging for the AWS account. Create a script to parse the CloudTrail log, search for AWS API calls by Lambda execution role, and create a summary report. Review the report. Create IAM access policies that provide more restrictive permissions for each Lambda function.

Turn on AWS CloudTrail logging for the AWS account. Export the CloudTrail logs to Amazon S3. Use Amazon EMR to process the CloudTrail logs in Amazon S3 and produce a report of API calls and resources used by each execution role. Create a new IAM access policy for each role. Export the generated roles to an S3 bucket. Review the generated policies to ensure that they meet the company’s business requirements.

questions.explanation:
IAM Access Analyzer can analyze AWS CloudTrail activity for an IAM role over a selected time period and generate a policy based on the services and actions the role actually used. Reviewing the generated policies before replacing broad policies provides a low-effort path toward least-privilege Lambda execution roles.

A company deploys workloads in multiple AWS accounts. Each account has a VPC with VPC flow logs published in text log format to a centralized Amazon S3 bucket. Each log file is compressed with gzip compression. The company must retain the log files indefinitely.  
  
A security engineer occasionally analyzes the logs by using Amazon Athena to query the VPC flow logs. The query performance is degrading over time as the number of ingested logs is growing. A solutions architect must improve the performance of the log analysis and reduce the storage space that the VPC flow logs use.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LARGEST performance improvement?

options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function to decompress the gzip files and to compress the files with bzip2 compression. Subscribe the Lambda function to an s3:ObjectCreated:Put S3 event notification for the S3 bucket.
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration for the S3 bucket. Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration to move files to the S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class as soon as the files are uploaded.
Update the VPC flow log configuration to store the files in Apache Parquet format. Specify hourly partitions for the log files.
Create a new Athena workgroup without data usage control limits. Use Athena engine version 2.

questions.explanation:
Apache Parquet is a columnar storage format that dramatically improves Athena query performance compared to text/gzip files by enabling selective column projection and compression. Hourly partitions allow Athena to prune partitions during query execution, further reducing the data scanned. This combination provides the largest performance improvement and reduces storage overhead compared to recompression algorithms (bzip2) or storage class changes.

**Learn more:** [Create tables for flow logs in Apache Parquet format](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/athena/latest/ug/vpc-flow-logs-parquet.html) · [Optimize network analytics with VPC Flow Logs in Parquet](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/big-data/optimize-performance-and-reduce-costs-for-network-analytics-with-vpc-flow-logs-in-apache-parquet-format/)

options.text: Deploy a new Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) Multi-AZ file system. Configure the file system for 75 MiBps of provisioned throughput. Implement replication to a file system in the DR Region.
Deploy a new Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Configure Bursting Throughput mode for the file system. Use AWS Backup to back up the file system to the DR Region.

Deploy a General Purpose SSD (gp3) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume with 225 MiBps of throughput. Enable Multi-Attach for the EBS volume. Use AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery to replicate the EBS volume to the DR Region.

Deploy an Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system in both the production Region and the DR Region. Create an AWS DataSync scheduled task to replicate the data from the production file system to the DR file system every 10 minutes.

questions.explanation:
A Regional Amazon EFS file system provides shared NFS storage for multiple Linux application servers across multiple Availability Zones. With Provisioned throughput, EFS provides throughput independently of file-system size; its maximum read throughput is three times the configured provisioned throughput because reads are metered at one-third the rate of other requests. Thus, 75 MiBps provisioned throughput supports 225 MiBps of read throughput. EFS cross-Region replication automatically synchronizes a destination file system and maintains a 15-minute RPO for most file systems, satisfying an RPO of less than 1 hour.

**Learn more:** [Managing file system throughput - Amazon Elastic File System](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/managing-throughput.html) · [Replicating EFS file systems - Amazon Elastic File System](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/efs-replication.html)

A financial company plans to migrate its web application from on premises to AWS. The company uses a third-party security tool to monitor inbound traffic to the application. It has used this security tool for the past 15 years, and the tool’s vendor offers no cloud solution. The company’s security team is concerned about integrating the security tool with AWS technology.  
  
The company plans to deploy the migrated application on Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances will run in an Auto Scaling group in a dedicated VPC. The company must use the security tool to inspect every packet entering and leaving the VPC. The inspection must take place in real time and must not affect application performance. A solutions architect must design a target AWS architecture that is highly available within an AWS Region.  
  
Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Deploy the security tool on EC2 instances m a new Auto Scaling group in the existing VPC
Deploy the web application behind a Network Load Balancer
Deploy an Application Load Balancer in front of the security tool instances
Provision a Gateway Load Balancer for each Availability Zone to redirect the traffic to the security tool
Provision a transit gateway to facilitate communication between VPCs.

questions.explanation:
Gateway Load Balancer transparently routes IP traffic through a scalable fleet of third-party virtual security appliances and maintains flow stickiness. Deploying the security tool on EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group provides an available, scalable appliance fleet; enabling Gateway Load Balancer across Availability Zones directs traffic to that fleet for real-time inspection. [Gateway Load Balancer overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/gateway/introduction.html)

**Learn more:** [Gateway Load Balancer overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/gateway/introduction.html) · [Configure middlebox traffic routing and inspection in a VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/gwlb-route.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a legacy application that operates across multiple NET Framework components. The components use the same Microsoft SQL Server database and communicate asynchronously with one another by using Microsoft Message Queueing (MSMQ).  
  
The company is beginning a migration to containerized .NET Core components and wants to refactor the application to run on AWS. The .NET Core components need complex orchestration. The company must retain full control of networking and host configuration. The application's database model is strongly relational.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Host the INET Core components on AWS App Runner. Host the database on Amazon RDS for SQL Server. Use Amazon EventBiridge for asynchronous messaging.

Host the .NET Core components on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with the AWS Fargate launch type. Host the database on Amazon DynamoDUse Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) for asynchronous messaging.

Host the .NET Core components on AWS Elastic Beanstalk. Host the database on Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2. Use Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) for asynchronous messaging.

Host the NET Core components on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with the Amazon EC2 launch type. Host the database on Amazon Aurora MySQL Serverless v2. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) for asynchronous messaging.

questions.explanation:
Amazon ECS with the Amazon EC2 launch type supports container orchestration while allowing control of the EC2 hosts and EC2-specific networking modes. Amazon Aurora is a managed relational database engine compatible with MySQL, and Aurora Serverless v2 supports Aurora MySQL. Amazon SQS provides queue-based asynchronous messaging between distributed components.

**Learn more:** [Amazon ECS task networking options for EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/task-networking.html) · [Amazon ECS task definition parameters for Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/task_definition_parameters_ec2.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an application on AWS. The company curates data from several distinct sources and uses proprietary algorithms for data transformations and aggregations. After completing ETL processes, the company stores the results in Amazon Redshift tables. The company sells this data to other companies.  
  
The company downloads the data as files from the Amazon Redshift tables and sends the files to several data customers by using FTP. The number of data customers has increased significantly, making management of the data customers difficult.  
  
The company will use AWS Data Exchange to create a data product to share data with customers. The company wants to verify customer identities before sharing data. The customers also require access to the latest data when the company publishes it.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Use AWS Data Exchange for APIs to share data with customers. Configure subscription verification. In the AWS account of the company that produces the data, create an Amazon API Gateway Data API service integration with Amazon Redshift. Require the data customers to subscribe to the data product.

In the AWS account of the company that produces the data, create an AWS Data Exchange datashare by connecting AWS Data Exchange to the Redshift cluster. Configure subscription verification. Require the data customers to subscribe to the data product.

Download the data from the Amazon Redshift tables to an Amazon S3 bucket periodically. Use AWS Data Exchange for S3 to share data with customers. Configure subscription verification. Require the data customers to subscribe to the data product.

Publish the Amazon Redshift data to an Open Data on AWS Data Exchange. Require the customers to subscribe to the data product in AWS Data Exchange. In the AWS account of the company that produces the data, attach IAM resource-based policies to the Amazon Redshift tables to allow access only to verified AWS accounts.

questions.explanation:
An AWS Data Exchange datashare connected to Amazon Redshift provides subscribers read-only access to the shared Redshift objects and lets them access updated provider data without ETL or file exports. AWS Data Exchange subscription verification enables the provider to collect and review subscriber identity information before approving access. AWS Data Exchange manages subscriber access to the datashare based on active subscriptions.

**Learn more:** [AWS Data Exchange datashares - Amazon Redshift](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/redshift/latest/dg/adx_datashare_overview.html) · [Subscription verification for providers in AWS Data Exchange](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/data-exchange/latest/userguide/subscription-verification-pro.html)

A company uses Amazon API Gateway to deploy a private REST API that provides access to sensitive data. The API must be reachable only from an application deployed in a VPC. The company deploys the API successfully; however, an Amazon EC2 instance deployed in the VPC cannot access the API.  
  
Which solution will provide connectivity between the EC2 instance and the API?

options.text: Create an interface VPC endpoint for API Gateway. Attach an endpoint policy that allows apigateway:* actions. Disable private DNS naming for the VPC endpoint. Configure an API resource policy that allows access from the VPC. Use the VPC endpoint's DNS name to access the API.

Create an interface VPC endpoint for API Gateway. Attach an endpoint policy that allows the execute-api:Invoke action. Enable private DNS naming for the VPC endpoint. Configure an API resource policy that allows access from the VPC endpoint. Use the API endpoint’s DNS names to access the API.
Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and a VPC link. Configure private integration between API Gateway and the NLB. Use the API endpoint’s DNS names to access the API.
Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and a VPC Link. Configure private integration between API Gateway and the ALB. Use the ALB endpoint’s DNS name to access the API.

questions.explanation:
Private API Gateway REST APIs are accessible from within a VPC only through an interface VPC endpoint for API Gateway. The API resource policy can restrict access using the endpoint ID, the endpoint policy can grant `execute-api:Invoke`, and enabling private DNS allows the API’s standard endpoint DNS names to resolve privately through that endpoint. A VPC Link is for API Gateway to reach private backend integrations, not for clients to invoke a private API.

**Learn more:** [Private REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-private-apis.html) · [Invoke a private API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/apigateway-private-api-test-invoke-url.html)

",["$","p",null,{"children":"The solutions architect must create a Multi-AZ solution that makes a data copy available in another AWS Region for disaster recovery (DR). The DR copy must have an RPO of less than 1 hour."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution meets these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L54",null,{"choices":{"A":"Deploy a new Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) Multi-AZ file system. Configure the file system for 75 MiBps of provisioned throughput. Implement replication to a file system in the DR Region.","B":"Deploy a new Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Configure Bursting Throughput mode for the file system. Use AWS Backup to back up the file system to the DR Region.","C":"Deploy a General Purpose SSD (gp3) Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume with 225 MiBps of throughput. Enable Multi-Attach for the EBS volume. Use AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery to replicate the EBS volume to the DR Region.","D":"Deploy an Amazon FSx for OpenZFS file system in both the production Region and the DR Region. Create an AWS DataSync scheduled task to replicate the data from the production file system to the DR file system every 10 minutes."},"correctAnswer":"A","explanation":"A Regional Amazon EFS file system provides shared NFS storage for multiple Linux application servers across multiple Availability Zones. With Provisioned throughput, EFS provides throughput independently of file-system size; its maximum read throughput is three times the configured provisioned throughput because reads are metered at one-third the rate of other requests. Thus, 75 MiBps provisioned throughput supports 225 MiBps of read throughput. EFS cross-Region replication automatically synchronizes a destination file system and maintains a 15-minute RPO for most file systems, satisfying an RPO of less than 1 hour.

**Learn more:** [Managing file system throughput - Amazon Elastic File System](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/managing-throughput.html) · [Replicating EFS file systems - Amazon Elastic File System](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/efs-replication.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"c2cdfedd-5b5f-4a9b-b5e1-556694063c8d","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02","mode":"default"}}]]

A security engineer has found that an existing application obtains credentials for an Amazon RDS for MySQL database from an encrypted file in Amazon S3. For the application’s next version, the security engineer wants to make these design changes to improve security:  
  
- The database must use strong, randomly generated passwords that are stored in a secure AWS managed service.  
- Application resources must be deployed through AWS CloudFormation.  
- The application must rotate database credentials every 90 days.  
  
A solutions architect will create a CloudFormation template to deploy the application.  
  
Which resources specified in the CloudFormation template meet the security engineer’s requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Generate the database password as a secret resource using AWS Secrets Manager. Create an AWS Lambda function resource to rotate the database password. Specify a Secrets Manager RotationSchedule resource to rotate the database password every 90 days.

Generate the database password as a SecureString parameter type using AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Create an AWS Lambda function resource to rotate the database password. Specify a Parameter Store RotationSchedule resource to rotate the database password every 90 days.

Generate the database password as a secret resource using AWS Secrets Manager. Create an AWS Lambda function resource to rotate the database password. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule resource to trigger the Lambda function password rotation every 90 days.

Generate the database password as a SecureString parameter type using AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Specify an AWS AppSync DataSource resource to automatically rotate the database password every 90 days.

questions.explanation:
AWS Secrets Manager can generate and encrypt a random database password through the `GenerateSecretString` property of an `AWS::SecretsManager::Secret`. An `AWS::SecretsManager::RotationSchedule` configures a secret’s rotation rules and invokes its Lambda rotation function on the specified schedule, allowing Amazon RDS for MySQL credentials to be rotated every 90 days. This is the native CloudFormation and Secrets Manager mechanism; Parameter Store has no `RotationSchedule` resource, and AppSync does not perform database credential rotation.

**Learn more:** [AWS::SecretsManager::Secret - AWS CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-secretsmanager-secret.html) · [AWS::SecretsManager::RotationSchedule - AWS CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-secretsmanager-rotationschedule.html)

A solutions architect must define a reference architecture for a three-tier application with web, application, and NoSQL data layers. The reference architecture must satisfy these requirements:  
  
- High availability within an AWS Region  
- Ability to fail over to another AWS Region for disaster recovery within 1 minute  
- The most efficient solution with minimal impact on the user experience  
  
Which combination of steps meets these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Use an Amazon Route 53 weighted routing policy set to 100/0 across the two selected Regions. Set Time to Live (TTL) to 1 hour.
Use an Amazon Route 53 failover routing policy for failover from the primary Region to the disaster recovery Region. Set Time to Live (TTL) to 30 seconds.
Use a global table within Amazon DynamoDB so data can be accessed in the two selected Regions.

Back up data from an Amazon DynamoDB table in the primary Region every 60 minutes and then write the data to Amazon S3. Use S3 cross-Region replication to copy the data from the primary Region to the disaster recovery Region. Have a script import the data into DynamoDB in a disaster recovery scenario.

Implement a hot standby model using Auto Scaling groups for the web and application layers across multiple Availability Zones in the Regions. Use zonal Reserved Instances for the minimum number of servers and On-Demand Instances for any additional resources.
Use Auto Scaling groups for the web and application layers across multiple Availability Zones in the Regions. Use Spot Instances for the required resources.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Route 53 failover routing provides active-passive routing to a healthy secondary resource, and a 30-second TTL lets DNS resolvers refresh quickly enough to support rapid regional failover. DynamoDB global tables automatically replicate data across Regions so a replica in the recovery Region can serve the workload. A hot standby application tier deployed through Auto Scaling groups across multiple Availability Zones supplies in-Region high availability and pre-provisioned recovery capacity; Reserved Instances can cover the baseline while On-Demand Instances provide dependable additional capacity. Spot Instances are not appropriate for required capacity because they can be interrupted.

**Learn more:** [Failover routing - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-failover.html) · [Values specific for failover records - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resource-record-sets-values-failover.html)

The compliance team has deployed a security tool in every VPC in which the company has deployments. The company needs to identify the cost of the security tools running on the EC2 instances so it can charge the compliance team’s AWS account. The cost calculation must be as accurate as possible.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: In the management account of the organization, activate the costCenter user-defined tag. Configure monthly AWS Cost and Usage Reports to save to an Amazon S3 bucket in the management account. Use the tag breakdown in the report to obtain the total cost for the costCenter tagged resources.

In the member accounts of the organization, activate the costCenter user-defined tag. Configure monthly AWS Cost and Usage Reports to save to an Amazon S3 bucket in the management account. Schedule a monthly AWS Lambda function to retrieve the reports and calculate the total cost for the costCenter tagged resources.

In the member accounts of the organization activate the costCenter user-defined tag. From the management account, schedule a monthly AWS Cost and Usage Report. Use the tag breakdown in the report to calculate the total cost for the costCenter tagged resources.

Create a custom report in the organization view in AWS Trusted Advisor. Configure the report to generate a monthly billing summary for the costCenter tagged resources in the compliance team’s AWS account.

questions.explanation:
For an AWS Organization, activate the user-defined `costCenter` cost-allocation tag in the management account. A company uses AWS Organizations with one OU, named Production, to manage multiple accounts. Every account belongs to the Production OU. Administrators use deny-list SCPs at the organization root to control access to restricted services.  
  
The company recently acquired a new business unit and invited that unit’s existing AWS account into the organization. After onboarding, the new business unit’s administrators found that they could not update existing AWS Config rules to comply with company policies.  
  
Which option will enable administrators to make changes while continuing to enforce the current policies without adding long-term maintenance?

options.text: Remove the organization’s root SCPs that limit access to AWS Config. Create AWS Service Catalog products for the company’s standard AWS Config rules and deploy them throughout the organization, including the new account.

Create a temporary OU named Onboarding for the new account. Apply an SCP to the Onboarding OU to allow AWS Config actions. Move the new account to the Production OU when adjustments to AWS Config are complete.

Convert the organization’s root SCPs from deny list SCPs to allow list SCPs to allow the required services only. Temporarily apply an SCP to the organization’s root that allows AWS Config actions for principals only in the new account.

Create a temporary OU named Onboarding for the new account. Apply an SCP to the Onboarding OU to allow AWS Config actions. Move the organization’s root SCP to the Production OU. Move the new account to the Production OU when adjustments to AWS Config are complete.

questions.explanation:
An SCP attached to the organization root applies to every member account and OU below it, and an explicit Deny cannot be overridden by an Allow at a lower level. Moving the deny-list SCP from the root to the Production OU keeps the existing restrictions in force for all production accounts while an account in a separate Onboarding OU can perform the required AWS Config updates. The account can be moved to Production after onboarding, restoring the same guardrails without a permanent exception.

**Learn more:** [SCP evaluation - AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps_evaluation.html) · [Terminology and concepts for AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_getting-started_concepts.html)

A company must monitor an increasing number of Amazon S3 buckets in two AWS Regions. The company must also track the percentage of objects encrypted in Amazon S3. The company needs a dashboard that displays this information for internal compliance teams.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Create a new 3 Storage Lens dashboard in each Region to track bucket and encryption metrics. Aggregate data from both Region dashboards into a single dashboard in Amazon QuickSight for the compliance teams.

Deploy an AWS Lambda function in each Region to list the number of buckets and the encryption status of objects. Store this data in Amazon S3. Use Amazon Athena queries to display the data on a custom dashboard in Amazon QuickSight for the compliance teams.
Use the S3 Storage Lens default dashboard to track bucket and encryption metrics. Give the compliance teams access to the dashboard directly in the S3 console.

Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to detect AWS CloudTrail events for S3 object creation. Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function to record encryption metrics in Amazon DynamoDB. Use Amazon QuickSight to display the metrics in a dashboard for the compliance teams.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Storage Lens provides a preconfigured default account dashboard that aggregates S3 metrics and supports analysis by AWS Region and bucket. Its free data-protection metrics include encrypted object count and percentage of encrypted objects, so compliance teams can view the required information directly in the S3 console without custom data collection, processing, or visualization infrastructure.

**Learn more:** [Amazon S3 Storage Lens metrics glossary](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage_lens_metrics_glossary.html) · [Viewing S3 Storage Lens metrics on dashboards](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage_lens_view_metrics_dashboard.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company needs to improve the reliability of its ticketing application. The application runs on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. The company uses Amazon CloudFront to serve the application. A single ECS service of the ECS cluster is the CloudFront distribution’s origin.  
  
The application allows only a specific number of active users to enter a ticket purchasing flow. These users are identified by an encrypted attribute in their JSON Web Token (JWT). All other users are redirected to a waiting room module until there is available capacity for purchasing.  
  
The application is experiencing high loads. The waiting room module is working as designed, but load on the waiting room is disrupting the applications availability.  

This disruption is negatively affecting the application's ticket sale transactions.  
  
Which solution will provide the MOST reliability for ticket sale transactions during periods of high load?

options.text: Create a separate service in the ECS cluster for the waiting room. Use a separate scaling configuration. Ensure that the ticketing service uses the JWT information and appropriately forwards requests to the waiting room service.

Move the application to an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. Split the waiting room module into a pod that is separate from the ticketing pod. Make the ticketing pod part of a StatefulSet. Ensure that the ticketing pod uses the JWT information and appropriately forwards requests to the waiting room pod.

Create a separate service in the ECS cluster for the waiting room. Use a separate scaling configuration. Create a CloudFront function that inspects the JWT information and appropriately forwards requests to the ticketing service or the waiting room service.

Move the application to an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. Split the waiting room module into a pod that is separate from the ticketing pod. Use AWS App Mesh by provisioning the App Mesh controller for Kubernetes. Enable mTLS authentication and service-to-service authentication for communication between the ticketing pod and the waiting room pod. Ensure that the ticketing pod uses the JWT information and appropriately forwards requests to the waiting room pod.

questions.explanation:
CloudFront Functions inspect the JWT at the edge and route requests to either the ticketing or waiting room service before they reach the ECS cluster. This prevents waiting room load from affecting the ticketing service and provides the most reliability during high load. Option A requires the ticketing service to make routing decisions (still impacting its capacity). Options B and D introduce unnecessary complexity and migration overhead. The edge-based routing in Option C provides the optimal reliability solution.

**Learn more:** [Validate a token in a CloudFront Functions viewer request](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/example_cloudfront_functions_kvs_jwt_verify_section.html)

A company with several AWS accounts uses AWS Organizations and service control policies (SCPs). An administrator created the following SCP and attached it to an organizational unit (OU) that contains AWS account 1111-1111-1111:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783732395322-eh4l9ot6.png)  
  
Developers in account 1111-1111-1111 report that they cannot create Amazon S3 buckets. How should the administrator resolve this problem?

options.text: Add s3:CreateBucket with “Allow” effect to the SCP.
Remove the account from the OU, and attach the SCP directly to account 1111-1111-1111.
Instruct the developers to add Amazon S3 permissions to their IAM entities.
Remove the SCP from account 1111-1111-1111.

questions.explanation:
The SCP allows all actions except `cloudtrail:*`, so it does not block `s3:CreateBucket`. SCPs establish the maximum available permissions but never grant permissions to IAM users or roles. The developers’ IAM entities must be granted permission to create S3 buckets.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company processes environmental data and has deployed sensors that continuously stream data from various locations across a city. The data is in JSON format.  
  
The company wants to use an AWS solution to deliver the data in real time to a database that does not require fixed storage schemas.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to send the data to Amazon Redshift.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to send the data to Amazon DynamoDB.
Use Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) to send the data to Amazon Aurora.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to send the data to Amazon Keyspaces (for Apache Cassandra).

questions.explanation:
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams supports continuous real-time streaming, and a stream consumer can store the records in Amazon DynamoDB. DynamoDB is a schemaless NoSQL database and supports document attributes that represent nested JSON-style structures, so it does not require a fixed relational schema.

A company is designing its network configuration in the AWS Cloud. It uses AWS Organizations to manage a multi-account environment. The company has three OUs. Each OU contains more than 100 AWS accounts. Every account has one VPC, and all VPCs within each OU are in the same AWS Region.  
  
The CIDR ranges of all AWS accounts do not overlap. The company needs a solution where VPCs within the same OU can communicate with one another, but cannot communicate with VPCs in other OUs.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Create an AWS CloudFormation stack set that establishes VPC peering between accounts in each OU. Provision the stack set in each OU.

In each OU, create a dedicated networking account that has a single VPC. Share this VPC with all the other accounts in the OU by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). Create a VPC peering connection between the networking account and each account in the OU.

Provision a transit gateway in an account in each OU. Share the transit gateway across the organization by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM). Create transit gateway VPC attachments for each VPC.

In each OU, create a dedicated networking account that has a single VPC. Establish a VPN connection between the networking account and the other accounts in the OU. Use third-party routing software to route transitive traffic between the VPCs.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transit Gateway centrally routes traffic among attached VPCs across accounts. Deploying one transit gateway per OU creates separate routing domains: attachments within an OU can exchange routes through that OU’s gateway, while no gateway route or attachment connects them to another OU. AWS RAM can share each transit gateway with accounts in AWS Organizations so those accounts can create VPC attachments. This hub-and-spoke design scales far better operationally than creating a mesh of VPC peering connections. A peering-based hub VPC also cannot provide transitive spoke-to-spoke routing.

**Learn more:** [Transit gateways in AWS Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/tgw-transit-gateways.html) · [Work with AWS Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/working-with-transit-gateways.html)

A company hosts a Git repository in an on-premises data center and uses webhooks to invoke functionality running in the AWS Cloud. The company runs the webhook logic on a set of Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group configured as a target for an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The Git server calls the ALB for configured webhooks. The company wants to move this solution to a serverless architecture.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: For each webhook, create and configure an AWS Lambda function URL. Update the Git servers to call the individual Lambda function URLs.
Create an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API. Implement each webhook logic in a separate AWS Lambda function. Update the Git servers to call the API Gateway endpoint.
Deploy the webhook logic to AWS App Runner. Create an ALB, and set App Runner as the target. Update the Git servers to call the ALB endpoint.

Containerize the webhook logic. Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster, and run the webhook logic in AWS Fargate. Create an Amazon API Gateway REST API, and set Fargate as the target. Update the Git servers to call the API Gateway endpoint.

questions.explanation:
An API Gateway HTTP API gives all the webhooks a single stable endpoint, with routing, throttling, authorization and logging handled by the service, while each webhook's logic stays in its own Lambda function. The Git server is pointed at one URL and the EC2 instances, Auto Scaling group and load balancer all disappear.

Lambda function URLs would also remove the servers, but each webhook then has its own separate endpoint that the Git server must be configured with and that must be secured and monitored individually — more to operate, not less. App Runner and Fargate keep a container platform in the picture, which is more operational overhead than either serverless option.

**Learn more:** [Amazon API Gateway HTTP APIs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/http-api.html) · [Lambda function URLs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/lambda-urls.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A health insurance company keeps personally identifiable information (PII) in an Amazon S3 bucket. Under a new requirement, every existing and future object in the S3 bucket must be encrypted with keys managed by the company’s security team. Versioning is not enabled on the S3 bucket.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: In the S3 bucket properties, change the default encryption to SSE-S3 with a customer managed key. Use the AWS CLI to re-upload all objects in the S3 bucket. Set an S3 bucket policy to deny unencrypted PutObject requests.

In the S3 bucket properties, change the default encryption to server-side encryption with AWS KMS managed encryption keys (SSE-KMS). Set an S3 bucket policy to deny unencrypted PutObject requests. Use the AWS CLI to re-upload all objects in the S3 bucket.

In the S3 bucket properties, change the default encryption to server-side encryption with AWS KMS managed encryption keys (SSE-KMS). Set an S3 bucket policy to automatically encrypt objects on GetObject and PutObject requests.

In the S3 bucket properties, change the default encryption to AES-256 with a customer managed key. Attach a policy to deny unencrypted PutObject requests to any entities that access the S3 bucket. Use the AWS CLI to re-upload all objects in the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
SSE-KMS can use a customer managed AWS KMS key, allowing the security team to administer the key and its policy. Bucket default encryption ensures new objects use that encryption setting, while existing SSE-S3 objects must be rewritten to change their encryption. Re-uploading replaces each object because versioning is disabled. SSE-S3, also identified by AES256, uses Amazon S3 managed keys and cannot be configured with a customer managed key.

**Learn more:** [Using server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/UsingKMSEncryption.html) · [Updating server-side encryption for existing data](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/update-sse-encryption.html)

A company operates an application in the AWS Cloud. The application runs on a fleet of 20 Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances are persistent and retain data on multiple attached Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes.  
  
The company must keep backups in a separate AWS Region. It must be able to recover the EC2 instances and their configuration within 1 business day, with a loss of no more than 1 day’s worth of data. The company has limited staff and requires a backup solution that optimizes operational efficiency and cost. The company has already created an AWS CloudFormation template that can deploy the necessary network configuration in a secondary Region.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a second CloudFormation template that can recreate the EC2 instances in the secondary Region. Run daily multivolume snapshots by using AWS Systems Manager Automation runbooks. Copy the snapshots to the secondary Region. In the event of a failure launch the CloudFormation templates, restore the EBS volumes from snapshots, and transfer usage to the secondary Region.

Use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM) to create daily multivolume snapshots of the EBS volumes. In the event of a failure, launch the CloudFormation template and use Amazon DLM to restore the EBS volumes and transfer usage to the secondary Region.

Use AWS Backup to create a scheduled daily backup plan for the EC2 instances. Configure the backup task to copy the backups to a vault in the secondary Region. In the event of a failure, launch the CloudFormation template, restore the instance volumes and configurations from the backup vault, and transfer usage to the secondary Region.

Deploy EC2 instances of the same size and configuration to the secondary Region. Configure AWS DataSync daily to copy data from the primary Region to the secondary Region. In the event of a failure, launch the CloudFormation template and transfer usage to the secondary Region.

questions.explanation:
AWS Backup can run a scheduled daily backup plan for Amazon EC2 and automatically copy the recovery points to a backup vault in another AWS Region. Restoring an EC2 recovery point creates the instance, EBS root and data volumes, and supported instance configuration settings, enabling regional recovery while minimizing operational effort.

**Learn more:** [Creating backup copies across AWS Regions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/cross-region-backup.html) · [Restore an Amazon EC2 instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/restoring-ec2.html)

A company uses AWS CodePipeline for the CI/CD of an application that is deployed to an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group. All AWS resources are defined in AWS CloudFormation templates. The application artifacts are stored in an Amazon S3 bucket and are deployed to the Auto Scaling group through instance user-data scripts. As the application has grown more complex, recent resource changes to the CloudFormation templates have resulted in unplanned downtime.  
  
How can a solutions architect improve the CI/CD pipeline to reduce the chance that template changes will cause downtime?

options.text: Adapt the deployment scripts to detect and report CloudFormation error conditions when performing deployments. Write test plans for a testing team to run in a non-production environment before approving the change for production.

Implement automated testing using AWS CodeBuild in a test environment. Use CloudFormation change sets to evaluate changes before deployment. Use AWS CodeDeploy to leverage blue/green deployment patterns to allow evaluations and the ability to revert changes, if needed.

Use plugins for the integrated development environment (IDE) to check the templates for errors, and use the AWS CLI to validate that the templates are correct. Adapt the deployment code to check for error conditions and generate notifications on errors. Deploy to a test environment and run a manual test plan before approving the change for production.

Use AWS CodeDeploy and a blue/green deployment pattern with CloudFormation to replace the user data deployment scripts. Have the operators log in to running instances and go through a manual test plan to verify the application is running as expected.

questions.explanation:
AWS CloudFormation change sets let teams preview the resource changes, including potentially disruptive replacements, before executing a stack update. Automated CodeBuild tests validate the change in a test environment. For Amazon EC2 deployments, CodeDeploy blue/green deployments provision a replacement environment, deploy and verify the new revision, and shift load-balancer traffic only after it is ready, enabling rollback when validation or deployment fails. This minimizes exposure of production traffic to failed application or infrastructure changes.

**Learn more:** [Update CloudFormation stacks using change sets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/using-cfn-updating-stacks-changesets.html) · [Working with deployments in CodeDeploy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codedeploy/latest/userguide/deployments.html)

A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances. A solutions architect is designing VPC infrastructure in an AWS Region in which the application must access an Amazon Aurora DB Cluster. All EC2 instances are associated with the same security group, and the DB cluster has its own security group.  
  
The solutions architect must add security-group rules that give the application least-privilege access to the DB Cluster.  
  
Which combination of steps meets these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Add an inbound rule to the EC2 instances' security group. Specify the DB cluster's security group as the source over the default Aurora port.
Add an outbound rule to the EC2 instances' security group. Specify the DB cluster's security group as the destination over the default Aurora port.
Add an inbound rule to the DB cluster's security group. Specify the EC2 instances' security group as the source over the default Aurora port.
Add an outbound rule to the DB cluster's security group. Specify the EC2 instances' security group as the destination over the default Aurora port.
Add an outbound rule to the DB cluster's security group. Specify the EC2 instances' security group as the destination over the ephemeral ports.

questions.explanation:
An EC2 security group needs an outbound rule that permits connections to the DB cluster security group only on Aurora’s database port. The DB cluster security group needs an inbound rule allowing that same port only from the EC2 instances’ security group. Security groups are stateful, so response traffic for an allowed connection is automatically permitted without a separate outbound rule on the DB cluster for ephemeral ports.

**Learn more:** [Security group rules - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/security-group-rules.html) · [Amazon EC2 security groups for your EC2 instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-security-groups.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has used Amazon EC2 instances to deploy a web fleet that hosts a blog site. The EC2 instances are behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and configured in an Auto Scaling group. The web application stores all blog content on an Amazon EFS volume.  
  
The company recently introduced a feature that lets bloggers add video to their posts, which has attracted 10 times the prior user traffic. During peak times of day, users report buffering and timeout issues when trying to access the site or watch videos.  
  
Which deployment is the **MOST** cost-efficient and scalable solution to resolve the user issues?

options.text: Reconfigure Amazon EFS to enable maximum I/O.
Update the blog site to use instance store volumes for storage. Copy the site contents to the volumes at launch and to Amazon S3 at shutdown.
Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Point the distribution to an S3 bucket, and migrate the videos from EFS to Amazon S3.
Set up an Amazon CloudFront distribution for all site contents, and point the distribution at the ALB.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 provides scalable object storage for video, and Amazon CloudFront caches and delivers that video from edge locations. This reduces requests and transfer load on the EFS-backed application fleet, improving video delivery under high demand without scaling high-performance shared file storage for static media.

**Learn more:** [Tutorial: Hosting on-demand streaming video with Amazon S3, Amazon CloudFront, and Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/tutorial-s3-cloudfront-route53-video-streaming.html) · [What is Amazon CloudFront?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/Introduction.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A global manufacturing company intends to migrate most of its applications to AWS. However, the company is concerned about applications that must stay within a particular country or in the company’s central on-premises data center because of data-regulatory requirements or single-digit-millisecond latency requirements. The company is also concerned about applications it hosts at some factory sites, where network infrastructure is limited.  
  
The company wants a consistent developer experience so its developers can build applications once and deploy them on premises, in the cloud, or in a hybrid architecture. Developers must be able to use the same familiar tools, APIs, and services.  
  
Which solution will deliver a consistent hybrid experience that meets these requirements?

options.text: Migrate all applications to the closest AWS Region that is compliant. Set up an AWS Direct Connect connection between the central on-premises data center and AWS. Deploy a Direct Connect gateway.

Use AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized devices for the applications that have data regulatory requirements or requirements for latency of single-digit milliseconds. Retain the devices on premises. Deploy AWS Wavelength to host the workloads in the factory sites.

Install AWS Outposts for the applications that have data regulatory requirements or requirements for latency of single-digit milliseconds. Use AWS Snowball Edge Compute Optimized devices to host the workloads in the factory sites.

Migrate the applications that have data regulatory requirements or requirements for latency of single-digit milliseconds to an AWS Local Zone. Deploy AWS Wavelength to host the workloads in the factory sites.

questions.explanation:
AWS Outposts provides AWS infrastructure, services, APIs, and tools at customer premises, enabling local data processing, data residency, and low-latency access to on-premises systems with the same AWS programming interfaces used in Regions. Snowball Edge Compute Optimized devices can run edge-computing workloads locally and are suited to locations with limited or inconsistent network connectivity.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Outposts?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/outposts/latest/userguide/what-is-outposts.html) · [What is Snowball Edge?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/latest/developer-guide/whatisedge.html)

A company requires that all internal application connectivity use private IP addresses. To facilitate this policy, a solutions architect has created interface endpoints to connect to AWS Public services. Upon testing, the solutions architect notices that the service names are resolving to public IP addresses, and that internal services cannot connect to the interface endpoints.  
  
Which step should the solutions architect take to resolve this issue?

options.text: Update the subnet route table with a route to the interface endpoint.
Enable the private DNS option on the VPC attributes.
Configure the security group on the interface endpoint to allow connectivity to the AWS services.
Configure an Amazon Route 53 private hosted zone with a conditional forwarder for the internal application.

questions.explanation:
Enabling the private DNS option on VPC attributes ensures that service names for interface endpoints resolve to private IP addresses instead of public ones. This is the specific VPC setting that controls DNS resolution behavior for endpoint names. Without this setting, the VPC uses public DNS resolution by default, which is why service names are resolving to public IPs despite interface endpoints being deployed.

**Learn more:** [Configure an interface endpoint (private DNS)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/interface-endpoints.html) · [Manage DNS names for VPC endpoint services](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/manage-dns-names.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is migrating its blog platform to AWS. The company's on-premises servers connect to AWS through an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection. The blog content is updated several times a day by multiple authors and is served from a file share on a network-attached storage (NAS) server.  
  
The company needs to migrate the blog platform without delaying the content updates. The company has deployed Amazon EC2 instances across multiple Availability Zones to run the blog platform behind an Application Load Balancer. The company also needs to move 200 TB of archival data from its on-premises servers to Amazon S3 as soon as possible.  
  
Which combination of stops will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create a weekly cron job in Amazon EventBridge. Use the cron job to invoke an AWS Lambda function to update the EC2 instances from the NAS server.
Configure an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach volume for the EC2 instances to share for content access. Write code to synchronize the EBS volume with the NAS server weekly.

Mount an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system to the on-premises servers to act as the NAS server. Copy the blog data to the EFS file system. Mount the EFS file system to the C2 instances to serve the content.
Order an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device. Copy the static data artifacts to the device. Ship the device to AWS.
Order an AWS Snowcons SSD device. Copy the static data artifacts to the device. Ship the device to AWS.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EFS can be mounted to on-premises servers via the VPN connection to act as a shared NAS replacement, allowing multiple authors to update blog content in real-time. AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized handles the 200 TB archival data transfer efficiently and quickly without consuming the 10 GB Direct Connect bandwidth. This combination enables live content synchronization while solving the large-scale data migration in parallel.

**Learn more:** [Mounting Amazon EFS with on-premises servers via Direct Connect/VPN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/efs-onpremises.html) · [What is Snowball Edge?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/snowball/latest/developer-guide/whatisedge.html)

A company has implemented an Amazon Connect contact center. Contact center agents report receiving a high volume of computer-generated calls. The company is concerned about the cost and productivity impact of these calls. The company needs a solution that enables agents to flag a call as spam and automatically prevents those numbers from being sent to an agent in the future.  
  
What is the **MOST** operationally efficient solution that meets these requirements?

options.text: Customize the Contact Control Panel (CCP) by adding a flag call button that will invoke an AWS Lambda function that calls the UpdateContactAttributes API. Use an Amazon DynamoDB table to store the spam numbers. Modify the contact flows to look for the updated attribute and to use a Lambda function to read and write to the DynamoDB table.

Use a Contact Lens for Amazon Connect rule that will look for spam calls. Use an Amazon DynamoDB table to store the spam numbers. Modify the contact flows to look for the rule and to invoke an AWS Lambda function to read and write to the DynamoDB table.

Use an Amazon DynamoDB table to store the spam numbers. Create a quick connect that the agents can transfer the spam call to from the Contact Control Panel (CCP). Modify the quick connect contact flow to invoke an AWS Lambda function to write to the DynamoDB table.

Modify the initial contact flow to ask for caller input. If the agent does not receive input, the agent should mark the caller as spam. Use an Amazon DynamoDB table to store the spam numbers. Use an AWS Lambda function to read and write to the DynamoDB table.

questions.explanation:
A queue quick connect gives agents a built-in CCP action to transfer a voice contact to a dedicated transfer flow. That flow can invoke AWS Lambda to write the caller’s number to DynamoDB. The initial inbound contact flow can invoke Lambda to look up the caller number and route matching numbers away before agent assignment. This uses native transfer functionality instead of requiring a custom CCP control, while providing persistent future-call blocking.

A company is designing an AWS Organizations structure. It wants to standardize a process for applying tags throughout the organization. The company will require tags with specified values when a user creates a new resource. Each of the company’s OUs will have distinct tag values.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use an SCP to deny the creation of resources that do not have the required tags. Create a tag policy that includes the tag values that the company has assigned to each OU. Attach the tag policies to the OUs.

Use an SCP to deny the creation of resources that do not have the required tags. Create a tag policy that includes the tag values that the company has assigned to each OU. Attach the tag policies to the organization's management account.

Use an SCP to allow the creation of resources only when the resources have the required tags. Create a tag policy that includes the tag values that the company has assigned to each OU. Attach the tag policies to the OUs.
Use an SCP to deny the creation of resources that do not have the required tags. Define the list of tags. Attach the SCP to the OUs.

questions.explanation:
An SCP with explicit deny statements can prevent resource creation when required request tags are absent. Tag policies define standardized tag keys and allowed values; attaching separate tag policies to each OU applies the OU-specific tag-value requirements to accounts in that OU. SCPs do not grant permissions, so an allow-based SCP alone cannot be used to permit resource creation only under those conditions.

**Learn more:** [Tag policies - AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_tag-policies.html) · [Best practices for using tag policies - AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_tag-policies-best-practices.html)

options.text: Use a spread placement group. Set a minimum of eight instances for each Availability Zone.
Stop and start all the instances in the placement group. Try the launch again.
Create a new placement group. Merge the new placement group with the original placement group.
Launch the additional instances as Dedicated Hosts in the placement groups.

questions.explanation:
For a capacity error when launching an instance into a placement group that already contains running instances, stop and start all instances in that placement group and retry the launch. Starting the group again can migrate it to hardware with capacity for all requested instances.

**Learn more:** [AWS EC2 placement group strategies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/placement-strategies.html)
