lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A large company operates workloads in VPCs deployed across hundreds of AWS accounts. Every VPC contains public and private subnets spanning multiple Availability Zones. NAT gateways run in the public subnets and provide outbound internet connectivity for the private subnets.  
  
A solutions architect is designing a hub-and-spoke architecture. All private subnets in the spoke VPCs must send internet-bound traffic through an egress VPC. The solutions architect has already deployed a NAT gateway in an egress VPC in a central AWS account.  
  
Which additional set of steps should the solutions architect take to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Create peering connections between the egress VPC and the spoke VPCs. Configure the required routing to allow access to the internet.
Create a transit gateway, and share it with the existing AWS accounts. Attach existing VPCs to the transit gateway. Configure the required routing to allow access to the internet.
Create a transit gateway in every account. Attach the NAT gateway to the transit gateways. Configure the required routing to allow access to the internet.
Create an AWS PrivateLink connection between the egress VPC and the spoke VPCs. Configure the required routing to allow access to the internet.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transit Gateway provides the scalable hub for a multi-account hub-and-spoke network. It can be shared with other AWS accounts so they can attach their spoke VPCs. Routes in the spoke VPCs and transit gateway can send `0.0.0.0/0` traffic to the egress VPC attachment, where the existing public NAT gateway and internet gateway provide internet egress.

**Learn more:** [How AWS Transit Gateway works – Centralized outbound routing to the internet](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/how-transit-gateways-work.html) · [Transit gateways in AWS Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/tgw-transit-gateways.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A medical company runs a REST API on a group of Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The ALB operates in three public subnets, and the EC2 instances operate in three private subnets. The company has deployed an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the ALB as its only origin.  
  
Which solution should a solutions architect recommend to improve origin security?

options.text: Store a random string in AWS Secrets Manager. Create an AWS Lambda function for automatic secret rotation. Configure CloudFront to inject the random string as a custom HTTP header for the origin request. Create an AWS WAF web ACL rule with a string match rule for the custom header. Associate the web ACL with the ALB.
Create an AWS WAF web ACL rule with an IP match condition of the CloudFront service IP address ranges. Associate the web ACL with the ALMove the ALB into the three private subnets.

Store a random string in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Configure Parameter Store automatic rotation for the string. Configure CloudFront to inject the random string as a custom HTTP header for the origin request. Inspect the value of the custom HTTP header, and block access in the ALB.
Configure AWS Shield Advanced Create a security group policy to allow connections from CloudFront service IP address ranges. Add the policy to AWS Shield Advanced, and attach the policy to the ALB.

questions.explanation:
CloudFront can add a randomly generated custom HTTP header to origin requests, while an AWS WAF web ACL associated with the ALB can block requests whose header does not match the secret value. Keeping that header secret prevents direct requests to the public ALB from bypassing CloudFront. AWS recommends periodically rotating the header value; AWS Secrets Manager and a Lambda rotation function provide an automated mechanism for doing so.

**Learn more:** [Restrict access to Application Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/restrict-access-to-load-balancer.html) · [Protecting your origin (BP1, BP5)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/aws-best-practices-ddos-resiliency/protecting-your-origin-bp1-bp5.html)

A financial company must establish a separate AWS account for a new digital wallet application. The company manages its accounts by using AWS Organizations. A solutions architect uses the Support1 IAM user in the management account to create a new member account with [email protected] as its email address.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to create IAM users in the new member account?

options.text: Sign in to the AWS Management Console with AWS account root user credentials by using the 64-character password from the initial AWS Organizations email sent to [email protected]. Set up the IAM users as required.
From the management account, switch roles to assume the OrganizationAccountAccessRole role with the account ID of the new member account. Set up the IAM users as required.

Go to the AWS Management Console sign-in page. Choose “Sign in using root account credentials.” Sign in in by using the email address finance [email protected] and the management account's root password. Set up the IAM users as required.
Go to the AWS Management Console sign-in page. Sign in by using the account ID of the new member account and the Support1 IAM credentials. Set up the IAM users as required.

questions.explanation:
AWS Organizations automatically creates the `OrganizationAccountAccessRole` role when it creates a member account. The role grants administrative permissions in the member account to authorized principals from the management account, so an authorized management-account IAM user can assume that role and create the required IAM users.

**Learn more:** [Creating a member account in an organization with AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_accounts_create.html) · [Accessing a member account that has OrganizationAccountAccessRole with AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_accounts_access-cross-account-role.html)

",["$","p",null,{"children":"As more smart meters are deployed, the engineers notice the Lambda functions are taking from 1 to 2 minutes to complete. ",["$","p",null,{"children":["Which combination of changes will resolve these issues?"]}],"
",["$","$L56",null,{"choices":{"A":"Increase the write capacity units to the DynamoDB table.","B":"Increase the memory available to the Lambda functions.","C":"Increase the payload size from the smart meters to send more data.","D":"Stream the data into an Amazon Kinesis data stream from API Gateway and process the data in batches.","E":"Collect data in an Amazon SQS FIFO queue, which triggers a Lambda function to process each message"},"correctAnswer":"AD","explanation":"The ProvisionedThroughputExceededException indicates DynamoDB capacity is insufficient, addressed by Option A. A company operates a customer service center that receives calls and automatically sends every customer a managed, interactive, two-way experience survey through text message. The applications that support the customer service center run on machines hosted by the company in an on-premises data center. The company’s hardware is aging, and the system is experiencing downtime. The company wants to migrate the system to AWS to increase reliability.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements with the **LEAST** ongoing operational overhead?

options.text: Use Amazon Connect to replace the old call center hardware. Use Amazon Pinpoint to send text message surveys to customers.
Use Amazon Connect to replace the old call center hardware. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to send text message surveys to customers.
Migrate the call center software to Amazon EC2 instances that are in an Auto Scaling group. Use the EC2 instances to send text message surveys to customers.
Use Amazon Pinpoint to replace the old call center hardware and to send text message surveys to customers.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Connect provides a managed, cloud-based contact center, eliminating the need to operate and maintain on-premises call-center hardware or self-managed EC2-based call-center software. Amazon Pinpoint supports sending SMS messages and configuring two-way SMS so customers can reply, which supports an automated interactive survey workflow with low operational overhead.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon Connect Customer?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/adminguide/what-is-amazon-connect.html) · [Set up SMS in Amazon Pinpoint](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/pinpoint/latest/userguide/tutorials-two-way-sms-part-1.html)

A company must implement a disaster recovery (DR) plan for a web application that runs in one AWS Region.  
  
The application uses microservices running in containers. The containers are hosted on AWS Fargate in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). The application uses an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance as its data layer and Amazon Route 53 for DNS resolution. An Amazon CloudWatch alarm invokes an Amazon EventBridge rule when the application experiences a failure.  
  
A solutions architect must design a DR solution that provides application recovery in a separate Region. The solution must minimize the time required to recover from a failure.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Setup a second ECS cluster and ECS service on Fargate in the separate Region. Create an AWS Lambda function to perform the following actions: take a snapshot of the RDS DB instance, copy the snapshot to the separate Region, create a new RDS DB instance from the snapshot, and update Route 53 to route traffic to the second ECS cluster. Update the EventBridge rule to add a target that will invoke the Lambda function.

Create an AWS Lambda function that creates a second ECS cluster and ECS service in the separate Region. Configure the Lambda function to perform the following actions: take a snapshot of the RDS DB instance, copy the snapshot to the separate Region, create a new RDS DB instance from the snapshot, and update Route 53 to route traffic to the second ECS cluster. Update the EventBridge rule to add a target that will invoke the Lambda function.

Setup a second ECS cluster and ECS service on Fargate in the separate Region. Create a cross-Region read replica of the RDS DB instance in the separate Region. Create an AWS Lambda function to promote the read replica to the primary database. Configure the Lambda function to update Route 53 to route traffic to the second ECS cluster. Update the EventBridge rule to add a target that will invoke the Lambda function.

Setup a second ECS cluster and ECS service on Fargate in the separate Region. Take a snapshot of the RDS DB instance. Convert the snapshot to an Amazon DynamoDB global table. Create an AWS Lambda function to update Route 53 to route traffic to the second ECS cluster. Update the EventBridge rule to add a target that will invoke the Lambda function.

questions.explanation:
A preprovisioned ECS/Fargate deployment in the recovery Region eliminates container-platform provisioning during an outage. An RDS for MySQL cross-Region read replica continuously replicates data to that Region and can be promoted to a standalone writable DB instance for failure recovery. Promoting that replica and updating Route 53 is faster than taking, copying, and restoring a snapshot after the failure. RDS snapshots cannot be converted into DynamoDB global tables. [Creating a read replica in a different AWS Region](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.XRgn.html) and [Promoting a read replica to be a standalone DB instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.Promote.html).

**Learn more:** [Creating a read replica in a different AWS Region](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.XRgn.html) · [Promoting a read replica to be a standalone DB instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.Promote.html)

AWS Transit Gateway provides centralized, scalable routing between attached VPCs, avoiding the operational burden of maintaining a full mesh of peering connections. AWS PrivateLink publishes the license-validation service through an endpoint service backed by a Network Load Balancer; customer VPCs can privately consume that specific service, providing unidirectional client-to-service access rather than broad bidirectional VPC connectivity.

**Learn more:** [How AWS Transit Gateway works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/how-transit-gateways-work.html) · [Create a service powered by AWS PrivateLink](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/create-endpoint-service.html)

A company wants to use Amazon WorkSpaces in combination with thin client devices to replace aging desktops. Employees use the desktops to access applications that work with Clinical trial data. Corporate security policy states that access to the applications must be restricted to only company branch office locations. The company is considering adding an additional branch office in the next 6 months.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the MOST operational efficiency?

options.text: Create an IP access control group rule with the list of public addresses from the branch offices. Associate the IP access control group with the WorkSpaces directory.
Use AWS Firewall Manager to create a web ACL rule with an IPSet with the list of public addresses from the branch office locations. Associate the web ACL with the WorkSpaces directory.
Use AWS Certificate Manager (ACM) to issue trusted device certificates to the machines deployed in the branch office locations. Enable restricted access on the WorkSpaces directory.
Create a custom WorkSpace image with Windows Firewall configured to restrict access to the public addresses of the branch offices. Use the image to deploy the WorkSpaces.

questions.explanation:
AWS WorkSpaces IP access control groups provide a native, operationally efficient mechanism to restrict access by source IP address. This feature allows administrators to specify approved IP ranges and automatically enforce access restrictions without requiring additional infrastructure or endpoint protection. AWS WAF is not compatible with WorkSpaces (it protects CloudFront, ALB, API Gateway, and other resources), and device certificate management is overly complex for simple location-based access control.

**Learn more:** [IP access control groups for WorkSpaces](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/workspaces/latest/adminguide/amazon-workspaces-ip-access-control-groups.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is creating a hybrid environment that includes servers in an on-premises data center and the AWS Cloud. The company has deployed Amazon EC2 instances in three VPCs. Each VPC is located in a different AWS Region. The company has established an AWS Direct Connect connection from the Region closest to the data center.  
  
The servers in the on-premises data center need access to the EC2 instances in all three VPCs. They must also be able to access AWS public services.  
  
Which combination of steps meets these requirements at the **LOWEST cost**? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create a Direct Connect gateway in the Region that is closest to the data center. Attach the Direct Connect connection to the Direct Connect gateway. Use the Direct Connect gateway to connect the VPCs in the other two Regions.
Set up additional Direct Connect connections from the on-premises data center to the other two Regions.
Create a private VIF. Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection over the private VIF to the VPCs in the other two Regions.
Create a public VIF. Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection over the public VIF to the VPCs in the other two Regions.
Use VPC peering to establish a connection between the VPCs across the Regions Create a private VIF with the existing Direct Connect connection to connect to the peered VPCs.

questions.explanation:
A Direct Connect gateway enables a single Direct Connect connection, through a private VIF, to reach VPCs in different AWS Regions. A public VIF provides connectivity to AWS public services and can be used as the dedicated transport to AWS Site-to-Site VPN endpoints. This uses the existing Direct Connect connection instead of adding regional Direct Connect connections; VPC peering does not support transitive routing.

**Learn more:** [Access to remote Direct Connect Regions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/remote_regions.html) · [Direct Connect virtual interfaces and hosted virtual interfaces](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/WorkingWithVirtualInterfaces.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to migrate its on-premises VMware cluster containing 120 VMs to AWS. The VMs use many different operating systems and have many custom software packages installed. The company also operates an on-premises NFS server that is 10 TB in size. The company has established a 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection to AWS for the migration.  
  
Which solution will complete the migration to AWS in the **LEAST** amount of time?

options.text: Export the on-premises VMs and copy them to an Amazon S3 bucket. Use VM Import/Export to create AMIs from the VM images that are stored in Amazon S3. Order an AWS Snowball Edge device. Copy the NFS server data to the device. Restore the NFS server data to an Amazon EC2 instance that has NFS configured.

Configure AWS Application Migration Service with a connection to the VMware cluster. Create a replication job for the VMS. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Configure AWS DataSync to copy the NFS server data to the EFS file system over the Direct Connect connection.

Recreate the VMs on AWS as Amazon EC2 instances. Install all the required software packages. Create an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system. Configure AWS DataSync to copy the NFS server data to the FSx for Lustre file system over the Direct Connect connection.

Order two AWS Snowball Edge devices. Copy the VMs and the NFS server data to the devices. Run VM Import/Export after the data from the devices is loaded to an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Copy the NFS server data from Amazon S3 to the EFS file system.

questions.explanation:
AWS Application Migration Service rehosts VMware virtual machines by replicating server data at the operating-system level, avoiding the time required to export and import VM images or manually recreate VMs and install their custom software. AWS DataSync supports transfers from NFS file servers to Amazon EFS and can route the transfer through AWS Direct Connect. The existing 10 Gbps Direct Connect link enables the VM replication and 10 TB NFS transfer without the provisioning, shipping, import, and extra-copy delays of Snowball-based approaches.

**Learn more:** [AWS Transform MGN general questions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mgn/latest/ug/General-Questions-FAQ.html) · [Configuring AWS DataSync transfers with an NFS file server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/create-nfs-location.html)

options.text: Deploy an additional CloudFront distribution. Create a new Route 53 failover record set with health checks for both CloudFront distributions.
Set the TTL to 4 second for the existing Route 53 record sets that are used for the backend service in each Region.
Create new record sets for the backend services by using a latency routing policy. Use the record sets as an origin in the CloudFront distribution.
Create a CloudFront origin group that includes two origins, one for each backend service Region. Configure origin failover as a cache behavior for the CloudFront distribution.

questions.explanation:
A CloudFront origin group places the primary and DR backend endpoints directly behind the same distribution. When the configured failover conditions occur, CloudFront routes the request to the secondary origin without waiting for Route 53 DNS failover and cached DNS TTLs to expire. CloudFront origin groups support a primary and secondary origin and can fail over on configured HTTP error codes or connection/time-out failures.

**Learn more:** [Optimize high availability with CloudFront origin failover](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/high_availability_origin_failover.html) · [Configuring DNS failover](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/dns-failover-configuring.html)

An ecommerce company runs an application on AWS. The application has an Amazon API Gateway API that invokes an AWS Lambda function. The data is stored in an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance.  
  
During the company’s most recent flash sale, a sudden increase in API calls negatively affected the application's performance. A solutions architect reviewed the Amazon CloudWatch metrics during that time and noticed a significant increase in Lambda invocations and database connections. The CPU utilization also was high on the DB instance.  
  
What should the solutions architect recommend to optimize the application's performance?

options.text: Increase the memory of the Lambda function. Modify the Lambda function to close the database connections when the data is retrieved.
Add an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster to store the frequently accessed data from the RDS database.
Create an RDS proxy by using the Lambda console. Modify the Lambda function to use the proxy endpoint.
Modify the Lambda function to connect to the database outside of the function's handler. Check for an existing database connection before creating a new connection.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS Proxy pools and multiplexes the large number of short-lived Lambda-driven connections into a small, stable set of connections to the PostgreSQL instance, which prevents connection exhaustion and high CPU overhead during a sudden spike in invocations. It can be attached to a Lambda function directly from the Lambda console's configuration page, requiring only that the function point at the proxy endpoint instead of the database endpoint.

**Learn more:** [Using Amazon RDS Proxy with AWS Lambda](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/compute/using-amazon-rds-proxy-with-aws-lambda/)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company stores data on premises on a Windows file server. The company generates 5 GB of new data each day.  
  
The company has migrated part of its Windows-based workload to AWS and requires the data to be available on a cloud file system. The company has already established an AWS Direct Connect connection between its on-premises network and AWS.  
  
Which data-migration strategy should the company use?

options.text: Use the file gateway option in AWS Storage Gateway to replace the existing Windows file server, and point the existing file share to the new file gateway.
Use AWS DataSync to schedule a daily task to replicate data between the on-premises Windows file server and Amazon FSx.
Use AWS Data Pipeline to schedule a daily task to replicate data between the on-premises Windows file server and Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS).
Use AWS DataSync to schedule a daily task to replicate data between the on-premises Windows file server and Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS).

questions.explanation:
AWS DataSync can schedule recurring transfers from an on-premises SMB file server to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server over AWS Direct Connect. FSx for Windows File Server provides native Windows file-system features and SMB access, making it the appropriate managed cloud file system for a Windows-based workload. AWS recommends DataSync for migrating existing file storage to FSx for Windows File Server.

**Learn more:** [Migrating existing file storage to FSx for Windows File Server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/migrate-files-fsx.html) · [Configuring AWS DataSync transfers with an SMB file server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/create-smb-location.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is deploying a third-party firewall-appliance solution from AWS Marketplace to monitor and protect traffic leaving the company’s AWS environments. The company wants to place this appliance in a shared services VPC and send all outbound, internet-bound traffic through the appliances.  
  
A solutions architect must recommend a deployment method that emphasizes reliability and minimizes firewall-appliance failover time within one AWS Region. The company has configured routing between the shared services VPC and other VPCs.  
  
Which steps should the solutions architect recommend to satisfy these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Deploy two firewall appliances into the shared services VPC, each in a separate Availability Zone.

Create a new Network Load Balancer in the shared services VPC. Create a new target group, and attach it to the new Network Load Balancer. Add each of the firewall appliance instances to the target group.
Create a new Gateway Load Balancer in the shared services VPCreate a new target group, and attach it to the new Gateway Load Balancer Add each of the firewall appliance instances to the target group.
Create a VPC interface endpoint. Add a route to the route table in the shared services VPC. Designate the new endpoint as the next hop for traffic that enters the shared services VPC from other VPCs.
Deploy two firewall appliances into the shared services VPC, each in the same Availability Zone.

Create a VPC Gateway Load Balancer endpoint. Add a route to the route table in the shared services VPC. Designate the new endpoint as the next hop for traffic that enters the shared services VPC from other VPCs.

questions.explanation:
Gateway Load Balancer is purpose-built to deploy and manage fleets of virtual appliances, including firewalls, and distributes flows only to healthy registered targets. Deploying firewall appliances across separate Availability Zones removes a single-AZ failure domain. A Gateway Load Balancer target group registers those appliances, while a Gateway Load Balancer endpoint provides the route-table target that transparently steers traffic arriving from the connected VPCs through the inspection appliances.

**Learn more:** [What is a Gateway Load Balancer?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/gateway/introduction.html) · [Getting started with Gateway Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/gateway/getting-started.html)

A global company operates a mobile app that shows ticket barcodes. Customers use tickets in the mobile app to attend live events. Event scanners read the ticket barcodes and invoke a backend API to validate the barcode data against data in a database. After a barcode is scanned, the backend logic writes to the database’s single table to mark that barcode as used.  
  
The company must deploy the app on AWS with a DNS name of `api.example.com`. The company will host the database in three AWS Regions worldwide.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements with the **LOWEST** latency?

options.text: Host the database on Amazon Aurora global database clusters. Host the backend on three Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) clusters that are in the same Regions as the database. Create an accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator to route requests to the nearest ECS cluster. Create an Amazon Route 53 record that maps api.example.com to the accelerator endpoint

Host the database on Amazon Aurora global database clusters. Host the backend on three Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) clusters that are in the same Regions as the database. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the three clusters as origins. Route requests to the nearest EKS cluster. Create an Amazon Route 53 record that maps api.example.com to the CloudFront distribution.

Host the database on Amazon DynamoDB global tables. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Associate the CloudFront distribution with a CloudFront function that contains the backend logic to validate the barcodes. Create an Amazon Route 53 record that maps api.example.com to the CloudFront distribution.

Host the database on Amazon DynamoDB global tables. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Associate the CloudFront distribution with a Lambda@Edge function that contains the backend logic to validate the barcodes. Create an Amazon Route 53 record that maps api.example.com to the CloudFront distribution.

questions.explanation:
Amazon DynamoDB global tables provide multi-Region, multi-active replicas with fast local reads and writes, so barcode validation and the update that marks a ticket used can be handled close to the request. Lambda@Edge runs at AWS locations near viewers and supports network access, allowing it to call DynamoDB. CloudFront Functions do not support network access, so they cannot perform the required database operation. Aurora Global Database has one writable primary Region and read-only secondary Regions, which adds cross-Region latency for writes outside the primary Region.

**Learn more:** [Differences between CloudFront Functions and Lambda@Edge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/edge-functions-choosing.html) · [Global tables – multi-active, multi-Region replication](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/GlobalTables.html)

",["$","$L55",null,{"choices":{"A":"Increase the memory of the Lambda function. Modify the Lambda function to close the database connections when the data is retrieved.","B":"Add an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster to store the frequently accessed data from the RDS database.","C":"Create an RDS proxy by using the Lambda console. Modify the Lambda function to use the proxy endpoint.","D":"Modify the Lambda function to connect to the database outside of the function's handler. Check for an existing database connection before creating a new connection."},"correctAnswer":"C","explanation":"Amazon RDS Proxy pools and multiplexes the large number of short-lived Lambda-driven connections into a small, stable set of connections to the PostgreSQL instance, which prevents connection exhaustion and high CPU overhead during a sudden spike in invocations. A company runs a Python script on an Amazon EC2 instance to process data. The script executes every 10 minutes. It ingests files from an Amazon S3 bucket and processes them. On average, the script requires approximately 5 minutes to process each file. The script will not reprocess a file it has already processed.  
  
The company reviewed Amazon CloudWatch metrics and found that the EC2 instance is idle approximately 40% of the time because of the file-processing speed. The company wants to make the workload highly available and scalable, while also reducing long-term management overhead.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.text: Migrate the data processing script to an AWS Lambda function. Use an S3 event notification to invoke the Lambda function to process the objects when the company uploads the objects.

Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure Amazon S3 to send event notifications to the SQS queue. Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group with a minimum size of one instance. Update the data processing script to poll the SQS queue. Process the S3 objects that the SQS message identifies.

Migrate the data processing script to a container image. Run the data processing container on an EC2 instance. Configure the container to poll the S3 bucket for new objects and to process the resulting objects.

Migrate the data processing script to a container image that runs on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate. Create an AWS Lambda function that calls the Fargate RunTaskAPI operation when the container processes the file. Use an S3 event notification to invoke the Lambda function.

questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda can run a file-processing invocation for up to 15 minutes, so a workload averaging 5 minutes per file is suitable. Amazon S3 can asynchronously invoke a Lambda function when objects are created, enabling per-file event-driven processing that automatically scales and removes the need to operate EC2 instances or containers. The existing protection against processing a file more than once also accommodates duplicate event delivery.

**Learn more:** [Configure Lambda function timeout](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-timeout.html) · [Process Amazon S3 event notifications with Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-s3.html)

A company delivers files to its customers by using an internet-accessible SFTP server. The SFTP server runs on a single Amazon EC2 instance with an attached Elastic IP address. Customers connect to the SFTP server through the Elastic IP address and authenticate by using SSH. The EC2 instance also has an attached security group that permits access from every customer IP address.  
  
A solutions architect must implement a solution that improves availability, minimizes infrastructure-management complexity, and minimizes disruption for customers accessing files. The solution must not alter how customers connect.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Disassociate the Elastic IP address from the EC2 instance. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to be used for SFTP file hosting. Create an AWS Transfer Family server. Configure the Transfer Family server with a publicly accessible endpoint. Associate the SFTP Elastic IP address with the new endpoint. Point the Transfer Family server to the S3 bucket. Sync all files from the SFTP server to the S3 bucket.

Disassociate the Elastic IP address from the EC2 instance. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to be used for SFTP file hosting. Create an AWS Transfer Family server. Configure the Transfer Family server with a VPC-hosted, internet-facing endpoint. Associate the SFTP Elastic IP address with the new endpoint. Attach the security group with customer IP addresses to the new endpoint. Point the Transfer Family server to the S3 bucket. Sync all files from the SFTP server to the S3 bucket.

Disassociate the Elastic IP address from the EC2 instance. Create a new Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system to be used for SFTP file hosting. Create an AWS Fargate task definition to run an SFTP server. Specify the EFS file system as a mount in the task definition. Create a Fargate service by using the task definition, and place a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in front of the service. When configuring the service, attach the security group with customer IP addresses to the tasks that run the SFTP server. Associate the Elastic IP address with the NLB. Sync all files from the SFTP server to the S3 bucket.

Disassociate the Elastic IP address from the EC2 instance. Create a multi-attach Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume to be used for SFTP file hosting. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) with the Elastic IP address attached. Create an Auto Scaling group with EC2 instances that run an SFTP server. Define in the Auto Scaling group that instances that are launched should attach the new multi-attach EBS volume. Configure the Auto Scaling group to automatically add instances behind the NLB. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use the security group that allows customer IP addresses for the EC2 instances that the Auto Scaling group launches. Sync all files from the SFTP server to the new multi-attach EBS volume.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon S3-backed AWS Transfer Family SFTP server with a VPC-hosted, internet-facing endpoint is a managed, highly available replacement for the single EC2 SFTP server. This endpoint type supports directly associating Elastic IP addresses and applying VPC security groups for source-IP restrictions, preserving the customers’ existing connection address and IP allow list.

**Learn more:** [Configuring an SFTP, FTPS, or FTP server endpoint](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transfer/latest/userguide/sftp-for-transfer-family.html) · [Create a server in a virtual private cloud](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transfer/latest/userguide/create-server-in-vpc.html)

The finance team has allocated a daily budget for AWS costs. The finance team must receive an email notification when the organization’s AWS costs exceed 80% of that allocated budget. A solutions architect must implement a solution to monitor the costs and deliver the notifications.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: In the organization's management account, use AWS Budgets to create a budget that has a daily period. Add an alert threshold and set the value to 80%. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to notify the finance team.

In the organization’s management account, set up the organizational view feature for AWS Trusted Advisor. Create an organizational view report for cost optimization. Set an alert threshold of 80%. Configure notification preferences. Add the email addresses of the finance team.

Register the organization with AWS Control Tower. Activate the optional cost control (guardrail). Set a control (guardrail) parameter of 80%. Configure control (guardrail) notification preferences. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to notify the finance team.

Configure the member accounts to save a daily AWS Cost and Usage Report to an Amazon S3 bucket in the organization's management account. Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule a daily Amazon Athena query to calculate the organization’s costs. Configure Athena to send an Amazon CloudWatch alert if the total costs are more than 80% of the allocated budget. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to notify the finance team.

questions.explanation:
AWS Budgets can be created in an AWS Organizations management account to monitor consolidated costs. A daily cost budget can have an actual-cost alert expressed as an 80% percentage threshold. The alert can publish to an Amazon SNS topic, and an email subscription to that topic delivers the notification to the finance team.

A company hosts an application on AWS for a project that will operate for the next 3 years. The application comprises 20 Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances registered in a target group for a Network Load Balancer (NLB). The instances are distributed across two Availability Zones. The application is stateless and operates 24 hours a day, 7 days a week.  
  
The company receives reports from users experiencing slow application responses. Performance metrics indicate that the instances run at 10% CPU utilization during normal application use. However, CPU utilization rises to 100% during busy periods, which usually last for a few hours.  
  
The company requires a new architecture to solve the application's slow-response problem.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.text: Create an Auto Scaling group. Attach the Auto Scaling group to the target group of the NLB. Set the minimum capacity to 20 and the desired capacity to 28. Purchase Reserved Instances for 20 instances.

Create a Spot Fleet that has a request type of request. Set the TotalTargetCapacity parameter to 20. Set the DefaultTargetCapacityType parameter to On-Demand. Specify the NLB when creating the Spot Fleet.

Create a Spot Fleet that has a request type of maintain. Set the TotalTargetCapacity parameter to 20. Set the DefaultTargetCapacityType parameter to Spot. Replace the NLB with an Application Load Balancer.

Create an Auto Scaling group. Attach the Auto Scaling group to the target group of the NLB. Set the minimum capacity to 4 and the maximum capacity to 28. Purchase Reserved Instances for four instances.

questions.explanation:
An Auto Scaling group can register and deregister EC2 instances with the NLB target group as demand changes. Four instances are sufficient for the low-utilization baseline and can receive Reserved Instance discounts for the three-year continuous workload, while scaling out to 28 instances supplies capacity during short CPU-saturating peaks. This avoids paying a three-year reservation commitment for the much larger capacity needed only intermittently.

**Learn more:** [Use Elastic Load Balancing to distribute incoming application traffic in your Auto Scaling group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/autoscaling-load-balancer.html) · [Amazon EC2 billing and purchasing options](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/instance-purchasing-options.html)

A large mobile gaming company has completed a successful migration of all its on-premises infrastructure to the AWS Cloud. A solutions architect is reviewing the environment to confirm that it was built according to the design and operates in alignment with the Well-Architected Framework.  
  
When reviewing prior monthly costs in Cost Explorer, the solutions architect observes that creating and later terminating several large instance types represents a high proportion of the costs. The solutions architect discovers that the company’s developers are launching new Amazon EC2 instances for testing and are not selecting the appropriate instance types.  
  
The solutions architect must implement a control mechanism that limits the instance types that only the developers can launch.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a desired-instance-type managed rule in AWS Config. Configure the rule with the instance types that are allowed. Attach the rule to an event to run each time a new EC2 instance is launched.
In the EC2 console, create a launch template that specifies the instance types that are allowed. Assign the launch template to the developers’ IAM accounts.
Create a new IAM policy. Specify the instance types that are allowed. Attach the policy to an IAM group that contains the IAM accounts for the developers
Use EC2 Image Builder to create an image pipeline for the developers and assist them in the creation of a golden image.

questions.explanation:
An IAM policy can allow or deny the `ec2:RunInstances` action according to the `ec2:InstanceType` condition key. Applying that policy to the developers’ IAM group centrally enforces the approved instance types at launch time for those developers, preventing costly unapproved types from being created.

**Learn more:** [Example policies to control access to the Amazon EC2 API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ExamplePolicies_EC2.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An e-commerce company is modernizing its IT infrastructure and plans to use AWS services. The company’s CIO has asked a solutions architect to create a simple, highly available, loosely coupled order-processing application. The application must receive and process orders before storing them in an Amazon DynamoDB table. It has a sporadic traffic pattern and must be able to scale during marketing campaigns to process orders with minimal delay.  
  
Which of the following is the **MOST reliable** approach for meeting these requirements?

options.text: Receive the orders in an Amazon EC2-hosted database and use EC2 instances to process them.
Receive the orders in an Amazon SQS queue and invoke an AWS Lambda function to process them.
Receive the orders using the AWS Step Functions program and launch an Amazon ECS container to process them.
Receive the orders in Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and use Amazon EC2 instances to process them.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SQS durably buffers incoming orders, decoupling receipt from processing and absorbing traffic bursts. An AWS Lambda function can poll the queue and automatically scale its concurrent processing as message volume grows, providing a highly available serverless design that handles sporadic demand and campaign spikes with minimal operational overhead.

**Learn more:** [Using Lambda with Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html) · [Configuring scaling behavior for SQS event source mappings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-scaling.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect must advise a company on migrating its on-premises data-processing application to the AWS Cloud. At present, users upload input files through a web portal. The web server stores the uploaded files on NAS and sends messages to the processing server through a message queue. Each media file can require up to 1 hour to process. The company has identified that the number of media files waiting for processing is substantially higher during business hours, and that the number of files decreases rapidly after business hours.  
  
What is the **MOST** cost-effective migration recommendation?

options.text: Create a queue using Amazon SQS. Configure the existing web server to publish to the new queue. When there are messages in the queue, invoke an AWS Lambda function to pull requests from the queue and process the files. Store the processed files in an Amazon S3 bucket.

Create a queue using Amazon MQ. Configure the existing web server to publish to the new queue. When there are messages in the queue, create a new Amazon EC2 instance to pull requests from the queue and process the files. Store the processed files in Amazon EFS. Shut down the EC2 instance after the task is complete.

Create a queue using Amazon MQ. Configure the existing web server to publish to the new queue. When there are messages in the queue, invoke an AWS Lambda function to pull requests from the queue and process the files. Store the processed files in Amazon EFS.

Create a queue using Amazon SQS. Configure the existing web server to publish to the new queue. Use Amazon EC2 instances in an EC2 Auto Scaling group to pull requests from the queue and process the files. Scale the EC2 instances based on the SQS queue length. Store the processed files in an Amazon S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda functions have a maximum execution timeout of 15 minutes, so they cannot process media files that can take up to 1 hour. Amazon SQS decouples file submission from processing, while Amazon EC2 workers in an Auto Scaling group can process long-running jobs and adjust capacity in response to the queue backlog. Amazon S3 provides durable, cost-effective object storage for processed media files. AWS documents the SQS queue-backlog-per-instance pattern for scaling EC2 Auto Scaling groups.

**Learn more:** [Configure Lambda function timeout](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-timeout.html) · [Scaling policy based on Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/as-using-sqs-queue.html)

A company runs a large containerized workload in the AWS Cloud. The workload comprises approximately 100 distinct services, and the company uses Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to orchestrate it.  
  
Recently, the company’s development team began using AWS Fargate rather than Amazon EC2 instances in the ECS cluster. Previously, the workload had nearly reached the maximum number of EC2 instances available in the account.  
  
The company is concerned that the workload might reach the maximum permitted number of ECS tasks. A solutions architect must implement a solution that notifies the development team when Fargate reaches 80% of the maximum task count.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to satisfy this requirement?

options.text: Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor the Sample Count statistic for each service in the ECS cluster. Set an alarm for when the math expression sample count/SERVICE_QUOTA(service)*100 is greater than 80. Notify the development team by using Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).

Use Amazon CloudWatch to monitor service quotas that are published under the AWS/Usage metric namespace. Set an alarm for when the math expression metric/SERVICE_QUOTA(metric)*100 is greater than 80. Notify the development team by using Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS).

Create an AWS Lambda function to poll detailed metrics from the ECS cluster. When the number of running Fargate tasks is greater than 80, invoke Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to notify the development team.

Create an AWS Config rule to evaluate whether the Fargate SERVICE_QUOTA is greater than 80. Use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to notify the development team when the AWS Config rule is not compliant.

questions.explanation:
AWS Fargate publishes service-quota usage metrics in the `AWS/Usage` namespace. A CloudWatch metric-math expression of `metric/SERVICE_QUOTA(metric)*100` calculates usage as a percentage of the applicable quota. A CloudWatch alarm with a threshold above 80 can send its notification through Amazon SNS.

**Learn more:** [Visualizing your service quotas and setting alarms](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Quotas-Visualize-Alarms.html) · [AWS usage metrics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/CloudWatch-Service-Quota-Integration.html)

A company plans to refactor its retail-ordering web application, which currently uses a load-balanced fleet of Amazon EC2 instances for web hosting, database API services, and business logic. The company must create a decoupled, scalable architecture that includes a way to retain failed orders while minimizing operational costs.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon S3 for web hosting with Amazon API Gateway for database API services. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) for order queuing. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) for business logic with Amazon SQS long polling for retaining failed orders.

Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk for web hosting with Amazon API Gateway for database API services. Use Amazon MQ for order queuing. Use AWS Step Functions for business logic with Amazon S3 Glacier Deep Archive for retaining failed orders.

Use Amazon S3 for web hosting with AWS AppSync for database API services. Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) for order queuing. Use AWS Lambda for business logic with an Amazon SQS dead-letter queue for retaining failed orders.

Use Amazon Lightsail for web hosting with AWS AppSync for database API services. Use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) for order queuing. Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) for business logic with Amazon OpenSearch Service for retaining failed orders.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 can host scalable static web content, Amazon SQS decouples order producers from consumers, and AWS Lambda processes queued work with serverless scaling and no server fleet to operate. For an SQS-triggered Lambda function, a redrive policy can move messages that fail processing repeatedly to an Amazon SQS dead-letter queue, preserving failed orders for later inspection or reprocessing.

**Learn more:** [Hosting a static website using Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/WebsiteHosting.html) · [Creating and configuring an Amazon SQS event source mapping](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-configure.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is moving a legacy application from an on-premises data center to AWS. The application consists of one application server and one Microsoft SQL Server database server. Each server runs on a VMware VM and uses 500 TB of data spread across multiple attached volumes.  
  
The company has set up a 10 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection between the nearest AWS Region and its on-premises data center. No other services currently use the Direct Connect connection.  
  
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to migrate the application with the **LEAST** downtime? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use an AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS) replication job to migrate the database server VM to AWS.
Use VM Import/Export to import the application server VM.
Export the VM images to an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device.
Use an AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS) replication job to migrate the application server VM to AWS.
Use an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) replication instance to migrate the database to an Amazon RDS DB instance.

questions.explanation:
An AWS SMS replication job performs an initial full copy of the application server VM followed by incremental syncs over the Direct Connect link, so only a brief final sync is needed at cutover. AWS DMS with change data capture continuously replicates ongoing transactions from the SQL Server database into the target so the destination stays nearly caught up, keeping the cutover window short. VM Import/Export and Snowball Edge are one-time, offline transfer methods that cannot keep a 500 TB source and target continuously synchronized, so they would require far more downtime.

**Learn more:** [AWS Server Migration Service announcement](https://aws.amazon.com/about-aws/whats-new/2016/10/new-aws-server-migration-service-sms-makes-it-easier-and-faster-to-migrate-on-premises-servers-to-aws/) · [AWS Database Migration Service User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has recently acquired several other companies. Each company uses a separate AWS account with a different billing and reporting approach. The acquiring company has consolidated all accounts into a single organization in AWS Organizations. However, it has found it challenging to generate a cost report that provides meaningful groupings for every team.  
  
The acquiring company’s finance team needs a solution to report on costs for all companies through a self-managed application.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS Cost and Usage Report for the organization. Define tags and cost categories in the report. Create a table in Amazon Athena. Create an Amazon QuickSight dataset based on the Athena table. Share the dataset with the finance team.

Create an AWS Cost and Usage Report for the organization. Define tags and cost categories in the report. Create a specialized template in AWS Cost Explorer that the finance department will use to build reports.
Create an Amazon QuickSight dataset that receives spending information from the AWS Price List Query API. Share the dataset with the finance team.
Use the AWS Price List Query API to collect account spending information. Create a specialized template in AWS Cost Explorer that the finance department will use to build reports.

questions.explanation:
AWS Cost and Usage Reports provide detailed cost and usage data for an AWS organization and can include cost-allocation tags and Cost Category columns for meaningful team groupings. Amazon Athena can query the report data, and Amazon QuickSight can consume the Athena results as a dataset for custom, self-managed cost reporting. The AWS Price List Query API provides service pricing data, not an account’s incurred spending.

**Learn more:** [What are AWS Cost and Usage Reports?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cur/latest/userguide/what-is-cur.html) · [Querying Cost and Usage Reports using Amazon Athena](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cur/latest/userguide/cur-query-athena.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates numerous workloads on AWS and uses AWS Organizations to manage its accounts. The workloads run on Amazon EC2, AWS Fargate, and AWS Lambda. Some workloads experience unpredictable demand. The accounts show high usage in certain months and low usage in other months.  
  
The company wants to optimize compute costs for the next 3 years. A solutions architect obtains a 6-month average for every account in the organization to calculate usage.  
  
Which solution will deliver the **MOST** cost savings for all compute usage across the organization?

options.text: Purchase Reserved Instances for the organization to match the size and number of the most common EC2 instances from the member accounts.
Purchase a Compute Savings Plan for the organization from the management account by using the recommendation at the management account level.
Purchase Reserved Instances for each member account that had high EC2 usage according to the data from the last 6 months.
Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan for each member account from the management account based on EC2 usage data from the last 6 months.

questions.explanation:
A Compute Savings Plan applies discounted rates to eligible Amazon EC2, AWS Fargate, and AWS Lambda usage and is flexible when compute configuration or service usage changes. Management-account Savings Plan recommendations consider eligible usage across AWS Organizations accounts with discount sharing enabled and calculate the commitment intended to maximize savings across those accounts. Reserved Instances and EC2 Instance Savings Plans do not cover Fargate or Lambda usage.

**Learn more:** [AWS Savings Plans types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/latest/userguide/plan-types.html) · [Understanding Savings Plans recommendation calculations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/latest/userguide/sp-rec-calculations.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a web application that lets users upload short videos. The videos are kept on Amazon EBS volumes and categorized by custom recognition software.  
  
The website serves static content with variable traffic that peaks during certain months. Its architecture uses Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group for the web application, plus EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group to process an Amazon SQS queue. The company wants to rearchitect the application to reduce operational overhead by using AWS managed services where possible and to eliminate dependencies on third-party software.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon ECS containers for the web application and Spot instances for the Auto Scaling group that processes the SQS queue. Replace the custom software with Amazon Rekognition to categorize the videos.

Store the uploaded videos in Amazon EFS and mount the file system to the EC2 instances for the web application. Process the SQS queue with an AWS Lambda function that calls the Amazon Rekognition API to categorize the videos.

Host the web application in Amazon S3. Store the uploaded videos in Amazon S3. Use S3 event notification to publish events to the SQS queue. Process the SQS queue with an AWS Lambda function that calls the Amazon Rekognition API to categorize the videos.

Use AWS Elastic Beanstalk to launch EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group for the web application and launch a worker environment to process the SQS queue. Replace the custom software with Amazon Rekognition to categorize the videos.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 provides managed object storage for uploaded videos and can host static website content, avoiding EBS and web-server fleet management. S3 event notifications can publish object-created events to Amazon SQS, while AWS Lambda can consume SQS messages without managed worker instances. Amazon Rekognition Video performs label detection for videos stored in Amazon S3, replacing custom recognition software with a managed AWS service.

**Learn more:** [Amazon S3 Event Notifications](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/EventNotifications.html) · [Calling Amazon Rekognition Video operations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/rekognition/latest/dg/api-video.html)

A company uses AWS Control Tower to manage AWS accounts in an AWS Organizations organization. The company has an OU that contains accounts. The company must stop any new or existing Amazon EC2 instances in the OU’s accounts from obtaining a public IP address.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure all instances in each account in the OU to use AWS Systems Manager. Use a Systems Manager Automation runbook to prevent public IP addresses from being attached to the instances.

Implement the AWS Control Tower proactive control to check whether instances in the OU's accounts have a public IP address. Set the AssociatePublicIpAddress property to False. Attach the proactive control to the OU.

Create an SCP that prevents the launch of instances that have a public IP address. Additionally, configure the SCP to prevent the attachment of a public IP address to existing instances. Attach the SCP to the OU.

Create an AWS Config custom rule that detects instances that have a public IP address. Configure a remediation action that uses an AWS Lambda function to detach the public IP addresses from the instances.

questions.explanation:
A service control policy (SCP) attached to the OU provides a centralized, preventive permission guardrail for every member account. It can explicitly deny EC2 instance launches that request public IP assignment and deny public-IP association actions for existing instances. The EC2 authorization reference provides the `ec2:AssociatePublicIpAddress` condition key for controlling requests to associate public IP addresses. AWS Control Tower proactive controls validate supported CloudFormation provisioning requests before resource creation; they do not comprehensively prevent public-IP changes to existing instances.

**Learn more:** [Amazon EC2 controls - AWS Control Tower](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/controlreference/ec2-rules.html) · [Actions, resources, and condition keys for Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/service-authorization/latest/reference/list_amazonec2.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an AWS Organizations organization that contains a separate AWS account for every company department. Application teams in different departments independently develop and deploy solutions.  
  
The company wants to lower compute costs and appropriately manage costs across departments. The company also wants better visibility into billing for individual departments. The company does not want to sacrifice operational flexibility when selecting compute resources.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS Budgets for each department. Use Tag Editor to apply tags to appropriate resources. Purchase EC2 Instance Savings Plans.

Configure AWS Organizations to use consolidated billing. Implement a tagging strategy that identifies departments. Use SCPs to apply tags to appropriate resources. Purchase EC2 Instance Savings Plans.

Configure AWS Organizations to use consolidated billing. Implement a tagging strategy that identifies departments. Use Tag Editor to apply tags to appropriate resources. Purchase Compute Savings Plans.
Use AWS Budgets for each department. Use SCPs to apply tags to appropriate resources. Purchase Compute Savings Plans.

questions.explanation:

Department-identifying cost-allocation tags enable costs to be categorized by department, and Tag Editor can apply those tags to supported resources. Compute Savings Plans provide discounted compute usage while retaining broad flexibility across EC2 instance families, sizes, operating systems, tenancies, and Regions, and can also apply to Fargate and Lambda.

**Learn more:** [Consolidating billing for AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/consolidated-billing.html) · [Savings Plans types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/latest/userguide/plan-types.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an application in an on-premises data center. The application lets users upload media files, which are stored persistently on a file server. The web application has many users. The application server is overutilized, causing data uploads to occasionally fail. The company frequently adds storage to the file server. The company wants to address these challenges by migrating the application to AWS.  
  
Users throughout the United States and Canada access the application. Only authenticated users must be able to access the application to upload files. The company will consider refactoring the application and needs to accelerate application development.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Use AWS Application Migration Service to migrate the application server to Amazon EC2 instances. Create an Auto Scaling group for the EC2 instances. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute the requests. Modify the application to use Amazon S3 to persist the files. Use Amazon Cognito to authenticate users.

Use AWS Application Migration Service to migrate the application server to Amazon EC2 instances. Create an Auto Scaling group for the EC2 instances. Use an Application Load Balancer to distribute the requests. Set up AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to give users the ability to sign in to the application. Modify the application to use Amazon S3 to persist the files.

Create a static website for uploads of media files. Store the static assets in Amazon S3. Use AWS AppSync to create an API. Use AWS Lambda resolvers to upload the media files to Amazon S3. Use Amazon Cognito to authenticate users.

Use AWS Amplify to create a static website for uploads of media files. Use Amplify Hosting to serve the website through Amazon CloudFront. Use Amazon S3 to store the uploaded media files. Use Amazon Cognito to authenticate users.

questions.explanation:
AWS Amplify provides managed tooling and hosting that accelerates development of web applications. Amplify Hosting delivers the static site through the global CloudFront content delivery network, Amazon S3 supplies durable and scalable object storage for uploaded media, and Amazon Cognito authenticates application users and can authorize their access to AWS resources. This eliminates the operational management required for application servers, scaling groups, load balancers, and custom upload-processing components.

A solutions architect must establish the baseline infrastructure. The solution must deliver a consistent management and security baseline while allowing flexibility for differing compliance requirements across AWS accounts. It must also integrate with the existing on-premises Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS) server.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Create a single SCP for least privilege access across all accounts. Create a single OU for all accounts. Configure an IAM identity provider for federation with the on-premises AD FS server. Configure a central logging account with a defined process for log generating services to send log events to the central account. Enable AWS Config in the central account with conformance packs for all accounts.

Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Enable AWS Control Tower on the organization. Review included controls (guardrails) for SCPs. Check AWS Config for areas that require additions. Add OUs as necessary. Connect AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to the on-premises AD FS server.

Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Create SCPs for least privilege access. Create an OU structure, and use it to group AWS accounts. Connect AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to the on-premises AD FS server. Configure a central logging account with a defined process for log generating services to send log events to the central account. Enable AWS Config in the central account with aggregators and conformance packs.

Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Enable AWS Control Tower on the organization. Review included controls (guardrails) for SCPs. Check AWS Config for areas that require additions. Configure an IAM identity provider for federation with the on-premises AD FS server.

questions.explanation:
AWS Control Tower automates a governed multi-account landing zone, including security and logging accounts and controls based on AWS Organizations and AWS Config. Controls can be applied to specific OUs, allowing accounts with different compliance requirements to receive different governance policies. IAM Identity Center centralizes access across organization accounts and supports federation with SAML 2.0 external identity providers, which includes an AD FS deployment that supports SAML 2.0.

A company ingests and processes streaming market data. The data rate remains constant. A nightly job that computes aggregate statistics requires 4 hours to finish. The statistical analysis is not business-critical, and data points are processed in the next iteration if an individual run fails.  
  
The current architecture uses a pool of Amazon EC2 Reserved Instances with 1-year reservations. These EC2 instances operate continuously to ingest and store streaming data on attached Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. A scheduled script starts EC2 On-Demand Instances every night to carry out the nightly processing. The instances access the stored data through NFS shares on the ingestion servers. The script terminates the instances after processing completes.  
  
The Reserved Instance reservations are expiring. The company must decide whether to buy new reservations or implement a new design.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.text: Update the ingestion process to use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to save data to Amazon S3. Use a scheduled script to launch a fleet of EC2 On-Demand Instances each night to perform the batch processing of the S3 data. Configure the script to terminate the instances when the processing is complete.

Update the ingestion process to use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to save data to Amazon S3. Use AWS Batch with Spot Instances to perform nightly processing with a maximum Spot price that is 50% of the On-Demand price.

Update the ingestion process to use a fleet of EC2 Reserved Instances with 3-year reservations behind a Network LoadBalancer. Use AWS Batch with Spot Instances to perform nightly processing with a maximum Spot price that is 50% of the On-Demand price.

Update the ingestion process to use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to save data to Amazon Redshift. Use Amazon EventBridge to schedule an AWS Lambda function to run nightly to query Amazon Redshift to generate the daily statistics.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Data Firehose can deliver streaming data to Amazon S3, which provides durable storage without maintaining continuously running ingestion servers and attached EBS volumes. AWS Batch is designed to schedule and run batch computing jobs, and the nightly analysis is fault-tolerant because a failed execution can be deferred to the next iteration. EC2 Spot Instances are appropriate for flexible, interruptible batch and data-analysis workloads and offer substantial savings compared with On-Demand capacity.

**Learn more:** [Choose source and destination for your Firehose stream](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/create-name.html) · [Best practices for Amazon EC2 Spot](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/spot-best-practices.html)

Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Set up an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) change data capture (CDC) task. Specify the Aurora DB cluster as the source. Specify Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose as the target. Use Kinesis Data Firehose to upload the data into an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster for further analysis.

Start a database activity stream on the Aurora DB cluster to capture the activity stream in Amazon EventBridge. Define an AWS Lambda function as a target for EventBridge. Program the Lambda function to decrypt the messages from EventBridge and to publish all database activity to Amazon S3 for further analysis.

Start a database activity stream on the Aurora DB cluster to push the activity stream to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Configure Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to consume the Kinesis data stream and to deliver the data to Amazon S3 for further analysis.

Set up an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) change data capture (CDC) task. Specify the Aurora DB cluster as the source. Specify Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose as the target. Use Kinesis Data Firehose to upload the data into an Amazon Redshift cluster. Run queries on the Amazon Redshift data to determine database activities on the Aurora database.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Aurora Database Activity Streams captures audited database activity at the cluster level, including all DB instances in the cluster, and delivers it to an Amazon Kinesis Data Stream. Amazon Data Firehose can consume that stream and store the activity records in Amazon S3 for analysis. AWS DMS CDC tracks data changes rather than comprehensive database activity auditing.

**Learn more:** [Monitoring Amazon Aurora with Database Activity Streams](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/DBActivityStreams.html) · [Starting a database activity stream](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/DBActivityStreams.Enabling.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing a software-as-a-service (SaaS) solution on AWS. The company has deployed an Amazon API Gateway REST API with AWS Lambda integration across multiple AWS Regions in the same production account.  
  
The company provides tiered pricing that allows customers to pay for capacity to make a specified number of API calls per second. The premium tier provides up to 3,000 calls per second, and customers are identified by a unique API key. Several premium-tier customers in different Regions report receiving `429 Too Many Requests` error responses from multiple API methods during peak-use hours. Logs show that the Lambda function is never invoked.  
  
What could be causing the error messages for these customers?

options.text: The Lambda function reached its concurrency limit.
The Lambda function its Region limit for concurrency.
The company reached its API Gateway account limit for calls per second.
The company reached its API Gateway default per-method limit for calls per second.

questions.explanation:
Amazon API Gateway throttles requests before the Lambda integration is invoked when the request rate or burst exceeds its limits, returning `429 Too Many Requests`. Its account-level throttle quota is shared by all APIs in an AWS account within a Region, so the aggregate traffic can exceed that quota even when individual customers have premium API-key usage-plan limits. The effect across multiple methods is consistent with account-level throttling.

**Learn more:** [Throttle requests to your REST APIs for better throughput in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-request-throttling.html) · [Amazon API Gateway quotas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/limits.html)

options.text: Create IAM roles for each user persona. Attach identity-based policies to define which actions the user who assumes the role can perform. Create an AWS Config rule to check for noncompliant resources. Configure the rule to notify the administrator to remediate the noncompliant resources.
Setup Kerberos-based authentication for EMR clusters upon launch. Specify a Kerberos security configuration along with cluster-specific Kerberos options.
Use AWS Service Catalog to control the Amazon EMR versions available for deployment, the cluster configuration, and the permissions for each user persona.

Launch the EMR cluster by using AWS CloudFormation, Attach resource-based policies to the EMR cluster during cluster creation. Create an AWS. Config rule to check for noncompliant clusters and noncompliant Amazon S3 buckets. Configure the rule to notify the administrator to remediate the noncompliant resources.

questions.explanation:
AWS Service Catalog provides governed portfolios of approved products, including controlled product versions and deployment configurations. Portfolio permissions and launch constraints enable persona-specific, least-privilege access, while TagOptions apply a consistent tagging taxonomy to provisioned products. This combines approval control, access governance, and provisioning-time tagging.

**Learn more:** [What Is AWS Service Catalog?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/servicecatalog/latest/adminguide/introduction.html) · [AWS Service Catalog Launch Constraints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/servicecatalog/latest/adminguide/constraints-launch.html)
