A manufacturing company is developing an inspection solution for its factory. The company has IP cameras at the end of every assembly line. The company has used Amazon SageMaker to train a machine learning (ML) model that identifies common defects from still images.  
  
The company wants to give factory workers local feedback when a defect is detected. The company must be able to provide this feedback even when the factory's internet connectivity is unavailable. The company has a local Linux server that hosts an API to provide local feedback to the workers.  
  
How should the company deploy the ML model to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Set up an Amazon Kinesis video stream from each IP camera to AWS. Use Amazon EC2 instances to take still images of the streams. Upload the images to an Amazon S3 bucket. Deploy a SageMaker endpoint with the ML model. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to call the inference endpoint when new images are uploaded. Configure the Lambda function to call the local API when a defect is detected.

Deploy AWS IoT Greengrass on the local server. Deploy the ML model to the Greengrass server. Create a Greengrass component to take still images from the cameras and run inference. Configure the component to call the local API when a defect is detected.

Order an AWS Snowball device. Deploy a SageMaker endpoint the ML model and an Amazon EC2 instance on the Snowball device. Take still images from the cameras. Run inference from the EC2 instance. Configure the instance to call the local API when a defect is detected.

Deploy Amazon Monitron devices on each IP camera. Deploy an Amazon Monitron Gateway on premises. Deploy the ML model to the Amazon Monitron devices. Use Amazon Monitron health state alarms to call the local API from an AWS Lambda function when a defect is detected.

questions.explanation:
AWS IoT Greengrass supports deployment of cloud-trained models to an on-premises core device for inference on locally generated data. A Greengrass component on the local Linux server can obtain still images from the IP cameras, run inference locally, and call the local feedback API without requiring internet connectivity at inference time.

**Learn more:** [Perform machine learning inference - AWS IoT Greengrass](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/greengrass/v2/developerguide/perform-machine-learning-inference.html) · [How AWS IoT Greengrass works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/greengrass/v2/developerguide/how-it-works.html)

A company is building a new service that will be accessed over TCP on a static port. A solutions architect must ensure that the service is highly available, provides redundancy across Availability Zones, and can be reached through the publicly accessible DNS name `my.service.com`. The service must use fixed address assignments so that other companies can place the addresses on their allow lists.  
  
Assuming resources are deployed across multiple Availability Zones in one Region, which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create Amazon EC2 instances with an Elastic IP address for each instance. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and expose the static TCP port. Register EC2 instances with the NLB. Create a new name server record set named my.service.com, and assign the Elastic IP addresses of the EC2 instances to the record set. Provide the Elastic IP addresses of the EC2 instances to the other companies to add to their allow lists.

Create an Amazon ECS cluster and a service definition for the application. Create and assign public IP addresses for the ECS cluster. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and expose the TCP port. Create a target group and assign the ECS cluster name to the NLCreate a new A record set named my.service.com, and assign the public IP addresses of the ECS cluster to the record set. Provide the public IP addresses of the ECS cluster to the other companies to add to their allow lists.

Create Amazon EC2 instances for the service. Create one Elastic IP address for each Availability Zone. Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) and expose the assigned TCP port. Assign the Elastic IP addresses to the NLB for each Availability Zone. Create a target group and register the EC2 instances with the NLB. Create a new A (alias) record set named my.service.com, and assign the NLB DNS name to the record set.

Create an Amazon ECS cluster and a service definition for the application. Create and assign public IP address for each host in the cluster. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and expose the static TCP port. Create a target group and assign the ECS service definition name to the ALB. Create a new CNAME record set and associate the public IP addresses to the record set. Provide the Elastic IP addresses of the Amazon EC2 instances to the other companies to add to their allow lists.

questions.explanation:
An internet-facing Network Load Balancer can expose a TCP listener and use one Elastic IP address per Availability Zone, giving external clients fixed IP addresses to allow-list. EC2 instances registered in the NLB target group provide redundant backends across Availability Zones, while a Route 53 A alias record maps `my.service.com` to the NLB endpoint.

**Learn more:** [AWS CLI set-subnets reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/elbv2/set-subnets.html) · [Elastic Load Balancing v2 CLI examples](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/userguide/cli_elastic-load-balancing-v2_code_examples.html)

A publishing company’s design team updates the icons and other static assets used by an ecommerce web application. The company serves the icons and assets from an Amazon S3 bucket hosted in the company’s production account. The company also has a development account that design team members can access.  
  
After the design team tests the static assets in the development account, it needs to load the assets into the S3 bucket in the production account. A solutions architect must give the design team access to the production account without exposing other portions of the web application to the risk of unintended changes.  
  
Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: In the production account, create a new IAM policy that allows read and write access to the S3 bucket.
In the development account, create a new IAM policy that allows read and write access to the S3 bucket.
In the production account, create a role Attach the new policy to the role. Define the development account as a trusted entity.
In the development account, create a role. Attach the new policy to the role Define the production account as a trusted entity.

In the development account, create a group that contains all the IAM users of the design team Attach a different IAM policy to the group to allow the sts:AssumeRole action on the role In the production account.

In the development account, create a group that contains all the IAM users of the design team Attach a different IAM policy to the group to allow the sts:AssumeRole action on the role in the development account.

questions.explanation:
Cross-account access through an IAM role requires a role in the production account with an S3 read/write permissions policy and a trust policy that allows the development account to assume it. The design-team users in the development account must also receive an identity-based policy permitting `sts:AssumeRole` on that production role. Granting these permissions through their IAM group limits the production access to the required S3 operations.

**Learn more:** [Grant a user permissions to switch roles — AWS IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_use_permissions-to-switch.html) · [Update a role trust policy — AWS IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_update-role-trust-policy.html)

A company plans to use a third-party software-as-a-service (SaaS) application. The third-party SaaS application is accessed through several API calls and also operates on AWS within a VPC.  
  
The company will access the third-party SaaS application from within a VPC. Its internal security policies require private connectivity that does not traverse the internet. No resources running in the company VPC may be accessible from outside the company’s VPC. All permissions must follow the principles of least privilege.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS PrivateLink interface VPC endpoint. Connect this endpoint to the endpoint service that the third-party SaaS application provides. Create a security group to limit the access to the endpoint. Associate the security group with the endpoint.
Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the third-party SaaS application and the company VPC. Configure network ACLs to limit access across the VPN tunnels.
Create a VPC peering connection between the third-party SaaS application and the company VPUpdate route tables by adding the needed routes for the peering connection.

Create an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service. Ask the third-party SaaS provider to create an interface VPC endpoint for this endpoint service. Grant permissions for the endpoint service to the specific account of the third-party SaaS provider.

questions.explanation:
AWS PrivateLink lets a SaaS customer create an interface VPC endpoint in its VPC to privately connect to the provider’s endpoint service without traversing the public internet. The interface endpoint is reachable through private IP addresses in the customer VPC, and an associated security group can limit traffic to only the required sources and ports. This provides consumer-initiated, service-specific connectivity without exposing the customer VPC’s resources to the SaaS provider.

",["$","p",null,{"children":"The company wants to give factory workers local feedback when a defect is detected. The company has a local Linux server that hosts an API to provide local feedback to the workers."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"How should the company deploy the ML model to satisfy these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L52",null,{"choices":{"A":"Set up an Amazon Kinesis video stream from each IP camera to AWS. Use Amazon EC2 instances to take still images of the streams. Upload the images to an Amazon S3 bucket. Deploy a SageMaker endpoint with the ML model. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to call the inference endpoint when new images are uploaded. Configure the Lambda function to call the local API when a defect is detected.","B":"Deploy AWS IoT Greengrass on the local server. Deploy the ML model to the Greengrass server. Create a Greengrass component to take still images from the cameras and run inference. Configure the component to call the local API when a defect is detected.","C":"Order an AWS Snowball device. Deploy a SageMaker endpoint the ML model and an Amazon EC2 instance on the Snowball device. Take still images from the cameras. Run inference from the EC2 instance. Configure the instance to call the local API when a defect is detected.","D":"Deploy Amazon Monitron devices on each IP camera. Deploy an Amazon Monitron Gateway on premises. Deploy the ML model to the Amazon Monitron devices. Use Amazon Monitron health state alarms to call the local API from an AWS Lambda function when a defect is detected."},"correctAnswer":"B","explanation":"AWS IoT Greengrass supports deployment of cloud-trained models to an on-premises core device for inference on locally generated data. A Greengrass component on the local Linux server can obtain still images from the IP cameras, run inference locally, and call the local feedback API without requiring internet connectivity at inference time.

**Learn more:** [Perform machine learning inference - AWS IoT Greengrass](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/greengrass/v2/developerguide/perform-machine-learning-inference.html) · [How AWS IoT Greengrass works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/greengrass/v2/developerguide/how-it-works.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"81cac904-25f3-494f-9bff-1225b0acf79c","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02","mode":"default"}}]]

A company built a pilot application using AWS Elastic Beanstalk and Java. To reduce development costs, the development team deployed the application in a single-instance environment. Recent testing shows that the application uses more CPU than anticipated. CPU utilization is consistently above 85%, causing performance bottlenecks.  
  
A solutions architect must resolve the performance issues before the company deploys the application to production.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Create a new Elastic Beanstalk application. Select a load-balanced environment type. Select all Availability Zones. Add a scale-out rule that will run if the maximum CPU utilization is over 85% for 5 minutes.

Create a second Elastic Beanstalk environment. Apply the traffic-splitting deployment policy. Specify a percentage of incoming traffic to direct to the new environment in the average CPU utilization is over 85% for 5 minutes.

Modify the existing environment’s capacity configuration to use a load-balanced environment type. Select all Availability Zones. Add a scale-out rule that will run if the average CPU utilization is over 85% for 5 minutes.
Select the Rebuild environment action with the load balancing option. Select an Availability Zones. Add a scale-out rule that will run if the sum CPU utilization is over 85% for 5 minutes.

questions.explanation:
A load-balanced Elastic Beanstalk environment supports an Auto Scaling group that can add instances in response to load, whereas a single-instance environment remains at one instance. Updating the existing environment’s capacity configuration avoids the overhead of creating and operating a separate application or environment. Elastic Beanstalk Auto Scaling can use average CPU utilization as a scaling metric, so scaling out after average CPU exceeds 85% for 5 minutes addresses sustained CPU pressure.

**Learn more:** [Environment types - AWS Elastic Beanstalk](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features-managing-env-types.html) · [Auto Scaling your Elastic Beanstalk environment instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features.managing.as.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A public retail web application uses an Application Load Balancer (ALB) before Amazon EC2 instances running across multiple Availability Zones (AZs) in a Region, backed by an Amazon RDS MySQL Multi-AZ deployment. A company operates a VPN in an on-premises data center. Employees currently use the VPN to access files in their Windows home directories. Recently, the number of employees working remotely has grown substantially. Consequently, bandwidth utilization for connections into the data center has started reaching 100% during business hours.

options.text: Create an AWS Storage Gateway Volume Gateway. Mount a volume from the Volume Gateway to the on-premises file server.

Migrate the home directories to Amazon FSx for Lustre.
Migrate remote users to AWS Client VPN.

questions.explanation:

Use Amazon Redshift Spectrum to query the data. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition data that is more than 1 year old to S3 Intelligent-Tiering.

questions.explanation:

options.text: Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Assign an Elastic IP address to the NLB.
Allocate an Elastic IP address. Assign the Elastic IP address to the ALProvide the Elastic IP address to the customer.
Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator. Specify the ALB as the accelerator's endpoint. Provide the accelerator's IP addresses to the customer.
Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Set the ALB as the origin. Ping the distribution's DNS name to determine the distribution's public IP address. Provide the IP address to the customer.

questions.explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator provides static IP addresses that act as fixed client entry points, and a standard accelerator supports an Application Load Balancer as an endpoint. It therefore supplies customer-facing IP addresses while retaining the existing ALB and its AWS WAF protection, without replacing the load balancer or managing a separate IP-based architecture.

**Learn more:** [How AWS Global Accelerator works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/introduction-how-it-works.html) · [Endpoints for standard accelerators in AWS Global Accelerator](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/about-endpoints.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a software-as-a-service (SaaS) application on AWS. The application includes AWS Lambda functions and an Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ database. During market events, the application experiences a workload that is much higher than normal. Users observe slow response times during peak periods because of numerous database connections. The company needs to improve the database's scalable performance and availability.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm action that triggers a Lambda function to add an Amazon RDS for MySQL read replica when resource utilization hits a threshold.
Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora, and add a read replica. Add a database connection pool outside of the Lambda handler function.
Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora, and add a read replica. Use Amazon Route 53 weighted records.
Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora, and add an Aurora Replica. Configure Amazon RDS Proxy to manage database connection pools.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Aurora provides high availability through Aurora Replicas, which can be promoted during a failure. Amazon RDS Proxy pools and reuses database connections, preventing Lambda’s rapidly created connections from oversubscribing the database; it also improves resilience by handling database failovers more efficiently.

**Learn more:** [Amazon RDS Proxy for Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/rds-proxy.html) · [High availability for Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Concepts.AuroraHighAvailability.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has installed sensors that collect information about environmental conditions, such as humidity and light, across all of the company’s factories. The company must stream and analyze this data in the AWS Cloud in real time. If any parameter is outside its acceptable range, the factory operations team must be notified immediately.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Stream the data to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Use AWS Step Functions to consume and analyze the data in the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to notify the operations team.

Stream the data to an Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka (Amazon MSK) cluster. Set up a trigger in Amazon MSK to invoke an AWS Fargate task to analyze the data. Use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to notify the operations team.

Stream the data to an Amazon Kinesis data stream. Create an AWS Lambda function to consume the Kinesis data stream and to analyze the data. Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to notify the operations team.

Stream the data to an Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics application. Use an automatically scaled and containerized service in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) to consume and analyze the data. Use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to notify the operations team.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams supports real-time ingestion, and AWS Lambda can be configured to consume and analyze its records through an event source mapping. The function can detect out-of-range environmental values and publish an alert to an Amazon SNS topic, which provides immediate notification delivery to subscribed operations-team endpoints.

**Learn more:** [Using Lambda to process records from Amazon Kinesis Data Streams](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-kinesis.html) · [Process Amazon Kinesis Data Streams records with Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-kinesis-create.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a two-tier, web-based application in an on-premises data center. The application tier consists of one server that runs a stateful application. The application connects to a PostgreSQL database hosted on a separate server. Because the application's user base is expected to grow substantially, the company is migrating both the application and database to AWS. The solution will use Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL, Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling, and Elastic Load Balancing.  
  
Which solution will deliver a consistent user experience while allowing the application and database tiers to scale?

options.text: Enable Aurora Auto Scaling for Aurora Replicas. Use a Network Load Balancer with the least outstanding requests routing algorithm and sticky sessions enabled.
Enable Aurora Auto Scaling for Aurora writers. Use an Application Load Balancer with the round robin routing algorithm and sticky sessions enabled.
Enable Aurora Auto Scaling for Aurora Replicas. Use an Application Load Balancer with the round robin routing and sticky sessions enabled.
Enable Aurora Scaling for Aurora writers. Use a Network Load Balancer with the least outstanding requests routing algorithm and sticky sessions enabled.

questions.explanation:
Aurora Auto Scaling dynamically adds and removes Aurora Replicas to scale read workloads; it does not scale writer instances. An Application Load Balancer supports round robin routing and sticky sessions, which bind a user's session to one application target and preserve continuity for a stateful application. [Amazon Aurora Auto Scaling with Aurora Replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Integrating.AutoScaling.html), [Application Load Balancer target-group attributes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/edit-target-group-attributes.html)

A company hosts an image-processing service on AWS in a VPC. The VPC spans two Availability Zones. Each Availability Zone has one public subnet and one private subnet.  
  
The service operates on Amazon EC2 instances in the private subnets. An Application Load Balancer in the public subnets sits in front of the service. The service must communicate with the internet and does so through two NAT gateways. The service uses Amazon S3 for image storage. The EC2 instances retrieve approximately 1 ТВ of data from an S3 bucket every day.  
  
The company has marketed the service as highly secure. A solutions architect must minimize cloud costs as much as possible without compromising the service’s security posture or increasing the time required for ongoing operations.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Replace the NAT gateways with NAT instances. In the VPC route table, create a route from the private subnets to the NAT instances.
Move the EC2 instances to the public subnets. Remove the NAT gateways.
Set up an S3 gateway VPC endpoint in the VPAttach an endpoint policy to the endpoint to allow the required actions on the S3 bucket.
Attach an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume to the EC2 instances. Host the images on the EFS volume.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon S3 gateway VPC endpoint sends S3 traffic from the private subnets over the AWS network rather than through NAT gateways, eliminating NAT processing for the large daily S3 transfer volume. Gateway endpoints are not billed, and an endpoint policy can restrict the endpoint to the necessary S3 bucket actions while preserving private connectivity.

**Learn more:** [AWS PrivateLink for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/privatelink-interface-endpoints.html) · [Amazon VPC endpoints for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/glue/latest/dg/vpc-endpoints-s3.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is running a web-crawling process on a list of target URLs to obtain training documents for machine learning training algorithms. A fleet of Amazon EC2 t2.micro instances pulls the target URLs from an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. The instances then write the result of the crawling algorithm as a .csv file to an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume. The EFS volume is mounted on all instances of the fleet.  
  
A separate system adds the URLs to the SQS queue at infrequent rates. The instances crawl each URL in 10 seconds or less.  
  
Metrics indicate that some instances are idle when no URLs are in the SQS queue. A solutions architect needs to redesign the architecture to optimize costs.  
  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use m5.8xlarge instances instead of t2.micro instances for the web-crawling process. Reduce the number of instances in the fleet by 50%.
Convert the web-crawling process into an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to pull URLs from the SQS queue.
Modify the web-crawling process to store results in Amazon Neptune.
Modify the web-crawling process to store results in an Amazon Aurora Serverless MySQL instance.
Modify the web-crawling process to store results in Amazon S3.

questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda eliminates idle EC2 instance costs by processing URLs on-demand with per-invocation billing, ideal for infrequent workloads. Amazon S3 is a cost-effective object storage solution for CSV results compared to maintaining an EFS volume. Lambda's pull-based model with SQS integration automatically scales without pre-provisioned capacity. Neptune and Aurora Serverless databases are unnecessary for this stateless crawling workflow that only produces CSV results. Larger EC2 instances increase per-hour costs without addressing the core issue of idle instances.

**Learn more:** [Using Lambda with Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html) · [Creating an SQS event source mapping](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-configure.html)

A solutions architect at a large company must configure network security for outbound internet traffic from every AWS account in an AWS Organizations organization. The organization contains more than 100 AWS accounts, which route traffic to one another through a centralized AWS Transit Gateway. Each account has an internet gateway and a NAT gateway for outbound internet traffic. The company deploys resources in only one AWS Region.  
  
The company requires centrally managed, rule-based filtering for all outbound internet traffic from every AWS account in the organization. Peak outbound traffic will not exceed 25 Gbps in each Availability Zone.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Create a new VPC for outbound traffic to the internet. Connect the existing transit gateway to the new VPC. Configure a new NAT gateway. Create an Auto Scaling group of Amazon EC2 instances that run an open-source internet proxy for rule-based filtering across all Availability Zones in the Region. Modify all default routes to point to the proxy's Auto Scaling group.

Create a new VPC for outbound traffic to the internet. Connect the existing transit gateway to the new VPC. Configure a new NAT gateway. Use an AWS Network Firewall firewall for rule-based filtering. Create Network Firewall endpoints in each Availability Zone. Modify all default routes to point to the Network Firewall endpoints.
Create an AWS Network Firewall firewall for rule-based filtering in each AWS account. Modify all default routes to point to the Network Firewall firewalls in each account.

In each AWS account, create an Auto Scaling group of network-optimized Amazon EC2 instances that run an open-source internet proxy for rule-based filtering. Modify all default routes to point to the proxy's Auto Scaling group.

questions.explanation:
AWS Network Firewall can be deployed centrally in an egress VPC attached to AWS Transit Gateway, with NAT gateway access to the internet. Routing internet-bound traffic through Network Firewall endpoints applies one centrally managed rule set to traffic from all accounts. Network Firewall supports up to 100 Gbps per Availability Zone across its associated endpoints, so it accommodates a 25 Gbps per-Availability-Zone peak load.

**Learn more:** [How AWS Network Firewall works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/how-it-works.html) · [VPC route table configuration for AWS Network Firewall](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/network-firewall/latest/developerguide/vpc-config-route-tables.html)

A company has multiple business units, each with separate AWS accounts. Each business unit manages its own network containing several VPCs with overlapping CIDR ranges. The company’s marketing team has developed a new internal application and wants to make it available to all other business units. The solution must use only private IP addresses.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Instruct each business unit to add a unique secondary CIDR range to the business unit's VPC. Peer the VPCs and use a private NAT gateway in the secondary range to route traffic to the marketing team.

Create an Amazon EC2 instance to serve as a virtual appliance in the marketing account's VPC. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the marketing team and each business unit's VPC. Perform NAT where necessary.

Create an AWS PrivateLink endpoint service to share the marketing application. Grant permission to specific AWS accounts to connect to the service. Create interface VPC endpoints in other accounts to access the application by using private IP addresses.

Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in front of the marketing application in a private subnet. Create an API Gateway API. Use the Amazon API Gateway private integration to connect the API to the NLB. Activate IAM authorization for the API. Grant access to the accounts of the other business units.

questions.explanation:
AWS PrivateLink provides private, account-authorized access to an application through interface VPC endpoints. It does not require VPC peering, routed connectivity between consumer and provider VPCs, or non-overlapping CIDR ranges, so it avoids the NAT and network-management overhead required by the alternatives.

**Learn more:** [Share your services through AWS PrivateLink](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/privatelink-share-your-services.html) · [Connecting Networks with Overlapping IP Ranges](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/connecting-networks-with-overlapping-ip-ranges/)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is introducing a new online game on Amazon EC2 instances. The game must be globally available. The company intends to operate the game in three AWS Regions: us-east-1, eu-west-1, and ap-southeast-1. The game's leaderboards, player inventory, and event status must be accessible across Regions.  
  
A solutions architect must design a solution that enables any Region to scale to support the load for all Regions. Additionally, users must automatically be connected to the Region that delivers the lowest latency.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Create an EC2 Spot Fleet. Attach the Spot Fleet to a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in each Region. Create an AWS Global Accelerator IP address that points to the NLB. Create an Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing entry for the Global Accelerator IP address. Save the game metadata to an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance in each Region. Set up a read replica in the other Regions.

Create an Auto Scaling group for the EC2 instances Attach the Auto Scaling group to a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in each Region. For each Region, create an Amazon Route 53 entry that uses geoproximity routing and points to the NLB in that Region. Save the game metadata to MySQL databases on EC2 instances in each Region. Set up replication between the database EC2 instances in each Region.

Create an Auto Scaling group for the EC2 instances. Attach the Auto Scaling group to a Network Load Balancer (NLB) in each Region. For each Region, create an Amazon Route 53 entry that uses latency-based routing and points to the NLB in that Region. Save the game metadata to an Amazon DynamoDB global table.

Use EC2 Global View. Deploy the EC2 instances to each Region. Attach the instances to a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Deploy a DNS server on an EC2 instance in each Region. Set up custom logic on each DNS server to redirect the user to the Region that provides the lowest latency. Save the game metadata to an Amazon Aurora global database.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing directs users to the Regional endpoint with the lowest latency. Amazon DynamoDB global tables are a fully managed, multi-Region, multi-active data store that automatically replicates table data and allows each replica to serve reads and writes. Auto Scaling groups provide scalable EC2 capacity in each Region, avoiding the operational burden of managing database replication or custom DNS routing.

**Learn more:** [Latency-based routing - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-latency.html) · [Global tables - multi-active, multi-Region replication - Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/GlobalTables.html)

A company must implement a server patching process. Its on-premises servers and Amazon EC2 instances currently use various tools for patching. Management requires one report that shows the patch status for every server and instance.  
  
Which set of actions should a solutions architect take to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS Systems Manager to manage patches on the on-premises servers and EC2 instances. Use Systems Manager to generate patch compliance reports.
Use AWS OpsWorks to manage patches on the on-premises servers and EC2 instances. Use Amazon QuickSight integration with OpsWorks to generate patch compliance reports.
Use an Amazon EventBridge rule to apply patches by scheduling an AWS Systems Manager patch remediation job. Use Amazon Inspector to generate patch compliance reports.
Use AWS OpsWorks to manage patches on the on-premises servers and EC2 instances. Use AWS X-Ray to post the patch status to AWS Systems Manager OpsCenter to generate patch compliance reports.

questions.explanation:
AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager centrally manages patching for Amazon EC2 instances and registered on-premises servers. It can also generate patch compliance reports, providing a consolidated view of patch status across managed nodes.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs an intranet web application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). At present, users authenticate to the application against an internal user database.  
  
The company must authenticate application users by using an existing AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory directory. Every user who has an account in the directory must be able to access the application.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a new app client in the directory. Create a listener rule for the ALB. Specify the authenticate-oidc action for the listener rule. Configure the listener rule with the appropriate issuer, client ID and secret, and endpoint details for the Active Directory service. Configure the new app client with the callback URL that the ALB provides.

Configure an Amazon Cognito user pool. Configure the user pool with a federated identity provider (ldP) that has metadata from the directory. Create an app client. Associate the app client with the user pool. Create a listener rule for the ALSpecify the authenticate-cognito action for the listener rule. Configure the listener rule to use the user pool and app client.

Add the directory as a new IAM identity provider (ldP). Create a new IAM role that has an entity type of SAML 2.0 federation. Configure a role policy that allows access to the ALB. Configure the new role as the default authenticated user role for the ldP. Create a listener rule for the ALB. Specify the authenticate-oidc action for the listener rule.

Enable AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On). Configure the directory as an external identity provider (ldP) that uses SAML. Use the automatic provisioning method. Create a new IAM role that has an entity type of SAML 2.0 federation. Configure a role policy that allows access to the ALB. Attach the new role to all groups. Create a listener rule for the ALB. Specify the authenticate-cognito action for the listener rule.

questions.explanation:
Application Load Balancer listener rules support the `authenticate-cognito` action. An Amazon Cognito user pool can federate with a corporate SAML identity provider using its metadata, so directory users authenticate through the federated provider and Cognito supplies the authentication flow used by the ALB. IAM roles and IAM Identity Center do not authenticate users to an ALB-protected application, and direct `authenticate-oidc` configuration requires an OIDC-compliant identity provider.

**Learn more:** [Authenticate users using an Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/listener-authenticate-users.html) · [Using SAML identity providers with a user pool](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/cognito-user-pools-saml-idp.html)

options.text: Store all the keys in AWS Secrets Manager. Define a Secrets Manager rotation schedule to invoke an AWS Lambda function to generate new key pairs. Replace public keys on EC2 instances. Update the private keys in Secrets Manager.

Store all the keys in Parameter Store, a capability of AWS Systems Manager, as a string. Define a Systems Manager maintenance window to invoke an AWS Lambda function to generate new key pairs. Replace public keys on EC2 instances. Update the private keys in Parameter Store.

Import the EC2 key pairs into AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Configure automatic key rotation for these key pairs. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function to initiate the key rotation in AWS KMS.

Add all the EC2 instances to Fleet Manager, a capability of AWS Systems Manager. Define a Systems Manager maintenance window to issue a Systems Manager Run Command document to generate new key pairs and to rotate public keys to all the instances in Fleet Manager.

questions.explanation:
AWS Secrets Manager encrypts secret values at rest with AWS KMS and supports rotation through a Lambda function. A custom rotation function can generate a replacement SSH key pair, install and test the new public key on the Linux instance before removing the old public key, and store the corresponding private key as the updated secret. This supports secure private-key storage and a short, controlled rotation interval. Parameter Store configured as a plain String does not meet the encryption requirement, and AWS KMS key rotation does not rotate EC2 SSH key pairs.

**Learn more:** [Rotation by Lambda function — AWS Secrets Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotate-secrets_lambda.html) · [Secret encryption and decryption — AWS Secrets Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/security-encryption.html)

A car rental company built a serverless REST API that supplies data to its mobile app. The app includes an Amazon API Gateway API with a Regional endpoint, AWS Lambda functions, and an Amazon Aurora MySQL Serverless DB cluster. The company recently opened the API to its partners’ mobile apps. A substantial increase in request volume has resulted, causing intermittent database memory errors.  
  
Analysis of the API traffic shows that clients make multiple HTTP GET requests for the same queries within a short time. Traffic is concentrated during business hours, with spikes around holidays and other events.  
  
The company must improve its ability to support the added usage while minimizing the increase in solution-related costs.  
  
Which strategy meets these requirements?

options.text: Convert the API Gateway Regional endpoint to an edge-optimized endpoint. Enable caching in the production stage.
Implement an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cache to store the results of the database calls. Modify the Lambda functions to use the cache.
Modify the Aurora Serverless DB cluster configuration to increase the maximum amount of available memory.
Enable throttling in the API Gateway production stage. Set the rate and burst values to limit the incoming calls.

questions.explanation:
Amazon API Gateway caching stores GET endpoint responses for a configured TTL and returns cache hits without making requests to the backend. This reduces repeated Lambda invocations and Aurora queries, mitigating database memory pressure at lower complexity and cost than adding an application-managed Redis cache. Edge-optimized API endpoints route geographically distributed clients through nearby CloudFront points of presence.

**Learn more:** [Cache settings for REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-caching.html) · [API endpoint types for REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-api-endpoint-types.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An AWS customer operates a web application on premises. The web application retrieves data from a third-party API that is protected by a firewall. The third party allows only one public CIDR block in each client’s allow list.  
  
The customer wants to migrate the web application to the AWS Cloud. The application will run on a group of Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in a VPC. The ALB is in public subnets. The EC2 instances are in private subnets. NAT gateways provide the private subnets with internet access.  
  
How should a solutions architect ensure that the web application can still call the third-party API after migration?

options.text: Associate a block of customer-owned public IP addresses to the VPC. Enable public IP addressing for public subnets in the VPC.
Register a block of customer-owned public IP addresses in the AWS account. Create Elastic IP addresses from the address block and assign them to the NAT gateways in the VPC.
Create Elastic IP addresses from the block of customer-owned IP addresses. Assign the static Elastic IP addresses to the ALB.
Register a block of customer-owned public IP addresses in the AWS account. Set up AWS Global Accelerator to use Elastic IP addresses from the address block. Set the ALB as the accelerator endpoint.

questions.explanation:
Outbound traffic from instances in private subnets is translated by the NAT gateway, so the NAT gateway’s Elastic IP address is the source address observed by the third-party API. AWS BYOIP lets a customer allocate Elastic IP addresses from a registered public IPv4 pool and use them with NAT gateways, providing stable addresses from the customer’s single allow-listed CIDR block.

**Learn more:** [Use your BYOIP address range in Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/byoip-working-with.html) · [Bring your own IP addresses (BYOIP) to Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-byoip.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company must establish connectivity from its on-premises data center to AWS. It needs to connect all of its VPCs, which are in different AWS Regions, with transitive routing between VPC networks. The company must also reduce network outbound traffic costs, increase bandwidth throughput, and deliver a consistent network experience for end users.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the on-premises data center and a new central VPC. Create VPC peering connections that initiate from the central VPC to all other VPCs.

Create an AWS Direct Connect connection between the on-premises data center and AWS. Provision a transit VIF, and connect it to a Direct Connect gateway. Connect the Direct Connect gateway to all the other VPCs by using a transit gateway in each Region.
Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between the on-premises data center and a new central VPUse a transit gateway with dynamic routing. Connect the transit gateway to all other VPCs.

Create an AWS Direct Connect connection between the on-premises data center and AWS. Establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection between all VPCs in each Region. Create VPC peering connections that initiate from the central VPC to all other VPCs.

questions.explanation:
AWS Direct Connect provides a private, dedicated connection that can reduce network costs, increase bandwidth throughput, and provide a more consistent experience than internet-based connections. A transit virtual interface connected to a Direct Connect gateway supports associations with Transit Gateways across AWS Regions. Transit Gateways provide the transit hub for VPC attachments and routing, enabling centralized connectivity among the VPC networks.

**Learn more:** [AWS Direct Connect + AWS Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/aws-vpc-connectivity-options/aws-direct-connect-aws-transit-gateway.html) · [Direct Connect gateways and Transit Gateway associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-transit-gateways.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company collects data from a large number of IoT devices. The data is kept in an Amazon S3 data lake. Data scientists run analytics on Amazon EC2 instances in two public subnets of a VPC in a separate AWS account.  
  
The data scientists require access to the data lake from the EC2 instances. The EC2 instances already have an assigned role that includes permissions to access Amazon S3.  
  
Company policy permits only authorized networks to access the IoT data.  
  
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to satisfy these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create a gateway VPC endpoint for Amazon S3 in the data scientists’ VPC.
Create an S3 access point in the data scientists' AWS account for the data lake.
Update the EC2 instance role. Add a policy with a condition that allows the s3:GetObject action when the value for the s3:DataAccessPointArn condition key is a valid access point ARN.
Update the VPC route table to route S3 traffic to an S3 access point.
Add an S3 bucket policy with a condition that allows the s3:GetObject action when the value for the s3:DataAccessPointArn condition key is a valid access point ARN.

questions.explanation:
An S3 access point can be created in the data scientists’ account for a bucket in another account and configured to accept requests only from the specified VPC. The bucket owner must authorize the cross-account access point in its bucket policy. Restricting `s3:GetObject` with the `s3:DataAccessPointArn` condition ensures that reads use the approved access point, which enforces the authorized-network boundary.

**Learn more:** [Configuring IAM policies for using access points](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/access-points-policies.html) · [Managing access to shared datasets with access points](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/access-points.html)

3e:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company operates Linux-based Amazon EC2 instances. Users must connect to the instances over SSH by using EC2 SSH key pairs. Every machine needs its own unique EC2 key pair."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"The company wants to implement a key-rotation policy that, on request, automatically rotates every EC2 key pair and keeps the keys in a securely encrypted location. The company can tolerate less than 1 minute of downtime during key rotation."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution meets these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L55",null,{"choices":{"A":"Store all the keys in AWS Secrets Manager. Define a Secrets Manager rotation schedule to invoke an AWS Lambda function to generate new key pairs. Replace public keys on EC2 instances. Update the private keys in Secrets Manager.","B":"Store all the keys in Parameter Store, a capability of AWS Systems Manager, as a string. Define a Systems Manager maintenance window to invoke an AWS Lambda function to generate new key pairs. Replace public keys on EC2 instances. Update the private keys in Parameter Store.","C":"Import the EC2 key pairs into AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS). Configure automatic key rotation for these key pairs. Create an Amazon EventBridge scheduled rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function to initiate the key rotation in AWS KMS.","D":"Add all the EC2 instances to Fleet Manager, a capability of AWS Systems Manager. Define a Systems Manager maintenance window to issue a Systems Manager Run Command document to generate new key pairs and to rotate public keys to all the instances in Fleet Manager."},"correctAnswer":"A","explanation":"AWS Secrets Manager encrypts secret values at rest with AWS KMS and supports rotation through a Lambda function. A custom rotation function can generate a replacement SSH key pair, install and test the new public key on the Linux instance before removing the old public key, and store the corresponding private key as the updated secret. This supports secure private-key storage and a short, controlled rotation interval. Parameter Store configured as a plain String does not meet the encryption requirement, and AWS KMS key rotation does not rotate EC2 SSH key pairs.

**Learn more:** [Rotation by Lambda function — AWS Secrets Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotate-secrets_lambda.html) · [Secret encryption and decryption — AWS Secrets Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/security-encryption.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"7aa2bcd1-1553-4c77-ac57-1ea8046a817e","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02","mode":"default"}}]]

",["$","p",null,{"children":"Analysis of the API traffic shows that clients make multiple HTTP GET requests for the same queries within a short time. Traffic is concentrated during business hours, with spikes around holidays and other events."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"The company must improve its ability to support the added usage while minimizing the increase in solution-related costs."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which strategy meets these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L55",null,{"choices":{"A":"Convert the API Gateway Regional endpoint to an edge-optimized endpoint. Enable caching in the production stage.","B":"Implement an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cache to store the results of the database calls. Modify the Lambda functions to use the cache.","C":"Modify the Aurora Serverless DB cluster configuration to increase the maximum amount of available memory.","D":"Enable throttling in the API Gateway production stage. Set the rate and burst values to limit the incoming calls."},"correctAnswer":"A","explanation":"Amazon API Gateway caching stores GET endpoint responses for a configured TTL and returns cache hits without making requests to the backend. This reduces repeated Lambda invocations and Aurora queries, mitigating database memory pressure at lower complexity and cost than adding an application-managed Redis cache. Edge-optimized API endpoints route geographically distributed clients through nearby CloudFront points of presence.

**Learn more:** [Cache settings for REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-caching.html) · [API endpoint types for REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-api-endpoint-types.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"7dcd50bb-2080-4259-b248-002dc8f21536","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02","mode":"default"}}]]

",["$","p",null,{"children":"The customer wants to migrate the web application to the AWS Cloud. NAT gateways provide the private subnets with internet access."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"How should a solutions architect ensure that the web application can still call the third-party API after migration?"}],"
",["$","$L55",null,{"choices":{"A":"Associate a block of customer-owned public IP addresses to the VPC. Enable public IP addressing for public subnets in the VPC.","B":"Register a block of customer-owned public IP addresses in the AWS account. Create Elastic IP addresses from the address block and assign them to the NAT gateways in the VPC.","C":"Create Elastic IP addresses from the block of customer-owned IP addresses. Assign the static Elastic IP addresses to the ALB.","D":"Register a block of customer-owned public IP addresses in the AWS account. Set up AWS Global Accelerator to use Elastic IP addresses from the address block. Set the ALB as the accelerator endpoint."},"correctAnswer":"B","explanation":"Outbound traffic from instances in private subnets is translated by the NAT gateway, so the NAT gateway’s Elastic IP address is the source address observed by the third-party API. AWS BYOIP lets a customer allocate Elastic IP addresses from a registered public IPv4 pool and use them with NAT gateways, providing stable addresses from the customer’s single allow-listed CIDR block.

**Learn more:** [Use your BYOIP address range in Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/byoip-working-with.html) · [Bring your own IP addresses (BYOIP) to Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/ec2-byoip.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"a3c5160d-b56a-4a09-81c9-9ec469f856ce","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02","mode":"default"}}]]

A startup recently migrated a large ecommerce website to AWS. The website has seen a 70% increase in sales. Software engineers use a private GitHub repository to manage code, and the DevOps team uses Jenkins for builds and unit testing. The engineers require notifications for failed builds and zero downtime during deployments. They must also ensure that production changes are seamless for users and can be rolled back if a major issue occurs.  
  
The software engineers have chosen AWS CodePipeline to manage their build and deployment process.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use GitHub websockets to trigger the CodePipeline pipeline. Use the Jenkins plugin for AWS CodeBuild to conduct unit testing. Send alerts to an Amazon SNS topic for any bad builds. Deploy in an in-place, all-at-once deployment configuration using AWS CodeDeploy.

Use GitHub webhooks to trigger the CodePipeline pipeline. Use the Jenkins plugin for AWS CodeBuild to conduct unit testing. Send alerts to an Amazon SNS topic for any bad builds. Deploy in a blue/green deployment using AWS CodeDeploy.

Use GitHub websockets to trigger the CodePipeline pipeline. Use AWS X-Ray for unit testing and static code analysis. Send alerts to an Amazon SNS topic for any bad builds. Deploy in a blue/green deployment using AWS CodeDeploy.

Use GitHub webhooks to trigger the CodePipeline pipeline. Use AWS X-Ray for unit testing and static code analysis. Send alerts to an Amazon SNS topic for any bad builds. Deploy in an in-place, all-at-once deployment configuration using AWS CodeDeploy.

questions.explanation:
GitHub webhooks can trigger CodePipeline when repository changes occur. Jenkins can provide build and unit-test integration, and Amazon SNS can notify engineers of failed builds. CodeDeploy blue/green deployments place the new version alongside the existing version, allow traffic to be shifted after validation, and support rapid rollback if a problem occurs; this provides seamless, zero-downtime releases.

**Learn more:** [GitHub source actions for AWS CodePipeline](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/appendix-github-oauth.html) · [Create a pipeline with Amazon ECS and CodeDeploy blue/green deployment](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codepipeline/latest/userguide/tutorials-ecs-ecr-codedeploy.html)

A company is implementing AWS Organizations to limit its developers to using only Amazon EC2, Amazon S3, and Amazon DynamoDB. The developers account is in a dedicated organizational unit (OU). The solutions architect has applied the following SCP to the developers account:  
  
![Question Image](https://cdn.examcademy.com/images/questions/1783731629232-9ema7hsq.png)  
  
After deploying this policy, IAM users in the developers account can still use AWS services that are not included in the policy. What should the solutions architect do to remove the developers’ ability to use services outside this policy’s scope?

options.text: Create an explicit deny statement for each AWS service that should be constrained.
Remove the FullAWSAccess SCP from the developers account’s OU.
Modify the FullAWSAccess SCP to explicitly deny all services.
Add an explicit deny statement using a wildcard to the end of the SCP.

questions.explanation:
The AWS managed `FullAWSAccess` SCP permits every AWS service and action. To use an SCP as an allowlist for only EC2, DynamoDB, and S3, the applicable `FullAWSAccess` SCP must be removed or replaced so that services not explicitly allowed are implicitly denied. The service-specific allow statements do not themselves override a broader applicable allow policy.

**Learn more:** [SCP evaluation - AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps_evaluation.html) · [Service control policies (SCPs) - AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates IoT sensors that track traffic patterns across a large city. The company needs to read and collect sensor data and perform aggregations on it.  
  
A solutions architect designs a solution where the IoT devices stream to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Several applications read from the stream. However, several consumers experience throttling and periodically receive a `ReadProvisionedThroughputExceeded` error.  
  
Which actions should the solutions architect take to resolve this problem? (Choose three.)

options.text: Reshard the stream to increase the number of shards in the stream.
Use the Kinesis Producer Library (KPL). Adjust the polling frequency.
Use consumers with the enhanced fan-out feature.
Reshard the stream to reduce the number of shards in the stream.
Use an error retry and exponential backoff mechanism in the consumer logic.
Configure the stream to use dynamic partitioning.

questions.explanation:
Kinesis Data Streams shards have finite shared read capacity for standard consumers. Adding shards increases the stream’s aggregate read capacity. Enhanced fan-out provides each registered consumer dedicated per-shard read throughput, preventing multiple consumers from contending for the shared read limit. Consumers should also retry throughput-exceeded errors with exponential backoff to handle temporary throttling.

**Learn more:** [Provisioned throughput exception errors — Amazon Kinesis Data Streams](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/kinesis-fis-provisioned-throughput.html) · [Develop enhanced fan-out consumers with dedicated throughput — Amazon Kinesis Data Streams](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/enhanced-consumers.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a workload consisting of thousands of Amazon EC2 instances. The workload runs in a VPC that includes several public and private subnets. The public subnets have a `0.0.0.0/0` route to an existing internet gateway. The private subnets have a `0.0.0.0/0` route to an existing NAT gateway.  
  
A solutions architect must migrate the complete EC2 fleet to IPv6. EC2 instances in private subnets must not be reachable from the public internet.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Update the existing VPC, and associate a custom IPv6 CIDR block with the VPC and all subnets. Update all the VPC route tables, and add a route for ::/0 to the internet gateway.

Update the existing VPC, and associate an Amazon-provided IPv6 CIDR block with the VPC and all subnets. Update the VPC route tables for all private subnets, and add a route for ::/0 to the NAT gateway.

Update the existing VPC, and associate an Amazon-provided IPv6 CIDR block with the VPC and all subnets. Create an egress-only internet gateway. Update the VPC route tables for all private subnets, and add a route for ::/0 to the egress-only internet gateway.

Update the existing VPC, and associate a custom IPV6 CIDR block with the VPC and all subnets. Create a new NAT gateway, and enable IPV6 support. Update the VPC route tables for all private subnets, and add a route for ::/0 to the IPv6-enabled NAT gateway.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon-provided IPv6 CIDR block enables IPv6 addressing for the VPC and its subnets. An egress-only internet gateway is stateful and permits instances in private subnets to initiate IPv6 connections to the internet while blocking unsolicited inbound IPv6 connections. The private subnet route `::/0` must therefore target the egress-only internet gateway. AWS documents this route pattern for private IPv6 workloads.

**Learn more:** [DNS64 and NAT64 - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/nat-gateway-nat64-dns64.html) · [Add IPv6 support for your VPC - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-migrate-ipv6.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company recently completed a successful proof of concept of Amazon WorkSpaces. A solutions architect needs to make the solution highly available across two AWS Regions. Amazon WorkSpaces is deployed in a failover Region, and a hosted zone is deployed in Amazon Route 53.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to configure high availability for the solution?

options.text: Create a connection alias in the primary Region and in the failover Region. Associate the connection aliases with a directory in each Region. Create a Route 53 failover routing policy. Set Evaluate Target Health to Yes.

Create a connection alias in the primary Region and in the failover Region. Associate the connection aliases with a directory in the primary Region. Create a Route 53 multivalue answer routing policy.
Create a connection alias in the primary Region. Associate the connection alias with a directory in the primary Region. Create a Route 53 weighted routing policy.
Create a connection alias in the primary Region Associate the connection alias with a directory in the failover Region. Create a Route 53 failover routing policy. Set Evaluate Target Health to Yes.

questions.explanation:
High availability for WorkSpaces across regions requires connection aliases in both the primary and failover regions, each associated with a separate directory. Route 53 failover routing policy detects health status and automatically switches users to the failover region during an outage. Option D incorrectly associates the single connection alias with only the failover region (defeating primary region access). Options B and C don't provide failover capability.

**Learn more:** [Cross-Region redirection for WorkSpaces Personal](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/workspaces/latest/adminguide/cross-region-redirection.html) · [CreateConnectionAlias API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/workspaces/latest/api/API_CreateConnectionAlias.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company intends to deploy a new private intranet service on Amazon EC2 instances within a VPC. An AWS Site-to-Site VPN links the VPC with the company's on-premises network. The new service must communicate with existing on-premises services. The on-premises services can be reached by using hostnames in the `company.example` DNS zone. This DNS zone is entirely hosted on premises and is available only on the company's private network.  
  
A solutions architect must make sure that the new service can resolve hostnames in the `company.example` domain in order to integrate with the existing services.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Create an empty private zone in Amazon Route 53 for company.example. Add an additional NS record to the company's on-premises company.example zone that points to the authoritative name servers for the new private zone in Route 53.
Turn on DNS hostnames for the VPC. Configure a new outbound endpoint with Amazon Route 53 Resolver. Create a Resolver rule to forward requests for company.example to the on-premises name servers.

Turn on DNS hostnames for the VPConfigure a new inbound resolver endpoint with Amazon Route 53 Resolver. Configur&the on-premises DNS server to forward requests for company.example to the new resolver.

Use AWS Systems Manager to configure a run document that will install a hosts file that contains any required hostnames. Use an Amazon EventBridge rule to run the document when an instance is entering the running state.

questions.explanation:
A Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoint forwards DNS queries originating from VPC resources to DNS resolvers on a connected private network. Associating a conditional forwarding rule for `company.example` with the VPC sends queries for that domain to the on-premises name servers through the Site-to-Site VPN, allowing EC2 workloads to resolve the existing private hostnames.

A live-events company is designing an AWS scaling solution for its ticketing application. The application experiences high utilization peaks during sale events. Each sale event is a scheduled, one-time occurrence. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group and uses PostgreSQL for its database layer.  
  
The company needs a scaling solution that maximizes availability during the sale events.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Use a predictive scaling policy for the EC2 instances. Host the database on an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Serverless v2 Multi-AZ DB instance with automatically scaling read replicas. Create an AWS Step Functions state machine to run parallel AWS Lambda functions to pre-warm the database before a sale event. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke the state machine.

Use a scheduled scaling policy for the EC2 instances. Host the database on an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL Mulli-AZ DB instance with automatically scaling read replicas. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function to create a larger read replica before a sale event. Fail over to the larger read replica. Create another EventBridge rule that invokes another Lambda function to scale down the read replica after the sale event.

Use a predictive scaling policy for the EC2 instances. Host the database on an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL MultiAZ DB instance with automatically scaling read replicas. Create an AWS Step Functions state machine to run parallel AWS Lambda functions to pre-warm the database before a sale event. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke the state machine.

Use a scheduled scaling policy for the EC2 instances. Host the database on an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL Multi-AZ DB cluster. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function to create a larger Aurora Replica before a sale event. Fail over to the larger Aurora Replica. Create another EventBridge rule that invokes another Lambda function to scale down the Aurora Replica after the sale event.

questions.explanation:
Scheduled scaling can provision Amazon EC2 capacity ahead of explicitly scheduled sale events. Aurora PostgreSQL supports Aurora Replicas in a Multi-AZ cluster; a replica can be created before the event and promoted through failover to become the writer, providing greater database compute capacity with resilient Aurora replica-based failover. Amazon RDS does not automatically scale out or scale in read replicas, so the RDS PostgreSQL alternatives do not meet their stated design.

**Learn more:** [Scheduled scaling for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-scheduled-scaling.html) · [Amazon Aurora DB clusters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Overview.html)

A company uses AWS Organizations to manage more than 1,000 AWS accounts. The company has established a new developer organization. It must move 540 developer member accounts into the new developer organization. Every account has been configured with all required information so that it can operate as a standalone account.  
  
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect perform to move all developer accounts to the new developer organization? (Choose three.)

options.text: Call the MoveAccount operation in the Organizations API from the old organization's management account to migrate the developer accounts to the new developer organization.
From the management account, remove each developer account from the old organization using the RemoveAccountFromOrganization operation in the Organizations API.
From each developer account, remove the account from the old organization using the RemoveAccountFromOrganization operation in the Organizations API.
Sign in to the new developer organization's management account and create a placeholder member account that acts as a target for the developer account migration.
Call the InviteAccountToOrganization operation in the Organizations API from the new developer organization's management account to send invitations to the developer accounts.
Have each developer sign in to their account and confirm to join the new developer organization.

questions.explanation:
To migrate an AWS account between organizations, the account must leave or be removed from the source organization, becoming a standalone account. The source organization’s management account can remove member accounts with `RemoveAccountFromOrganization`; the standalone accounts can then receive invitations from the destination organization’s management account through `InviteAccountToOrganization` and must accept those invitations. The prerequisite for standalone operation is satisfied.

**Learn more:** [Migrate an account to another organization with AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_account_migration.html) · [RemoveAccountFromOrganization API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/APIReference/API_RemoveAccountFromOrganization.html)

A company has a new application that must run on five Amazon EC2 instances within one AWS Region. The application needs high-throughput, low-latency network connectivity among all EC2 instances on which it runs. The application does not need to be fault tolerant.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Launch five new EC2 instances into a cluster placement group. Ensure that the EC2 instance type supports enhanced networking.
Launch five new EC2 instances into an Auto Scaling group in the same Availability Zone. Attach an extra elastic network interface to each EC2 instance.
Launch five new EC2 instances into a partition placement group. Ensure that the EC2 instance type supports enhanced networking.
Launch five new EC2 instances into a spread placement group. Attach an extra elastic network interface to each EC2 instance.

questions.explanation:
A cluster placement group packs EC2 instances close together in a single Availability Zone, enabling the low-latency, high-throughput networking needed by tightly coupled instances. Enhanced networking provides the high-performance network capability; fault-isolation placement strategies are unnecessary when fault tolerance is not required.

**Learn more:** [Placement strategies for your placement groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/placement-strategies.html) · [Placement groups for your Amazon EC2 instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/placement-groups.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company stores on-premises information in approximately 1 million `.csv` files hosted on a VM. The data is initially 10 TB and increases by 1 TB per week. The company must automate backups of this data to the AWS Cloud.  
  
Backups must run daily. The solution must apply custom filters so that only a subset of data in designated source directories is backed up. The company has established an AWS Direct Connect connection.  
  
Which solution meets the backup requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Use the Amazon S3 CopyObject API operation with multipart upload to copy the existing data to Amazon S3. Use the CopyObject API operation to replicate new data to Amazon S3 daily.
Create a backup plan in AWS Backup to back up the data to Amazon S3. Schedule the backup plan to run daily.
Install the AWS DataSync agent as a VM that runs on the on-premises hypervisor. Configure a DataSync task to replicate the data to Amazon S3 daily.
Use an AWS Snowball Edge device for the initial backup. Use AWS DataSync for incremental backups to Amazon S3 daily.

questions.explanation:
AWS DataSync uses an agent deployed in the on-premises environment to transfer data to Amazon S3. It supports scheduled tasks and include/exclude filters that select the files and directories to transfer. Direct Connect provides a private network path for the transfer, and DataSync manages repeated incremental synchronization without requiring a Snowball device or custom object-copy logic.

**Learn more:** [Do I need an AWS DataSync agent?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/do-i-need-datasync-agent.html) · [Scheduling when your AWS DataSync task runs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/task-scheduling.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company deploys a containerized application using Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) and Amazon API Gateway. The application data is stored in Amazon Aurora databases and Amazon DynamoDB databases. The company automates infrastructure provisioning by using AWS CloudFormation. The company automates application deployments by using AWS CodePipeline.  
  
A solutions architect must implement a disaster recovery (DR) strategy that provides an RPO of 2 hours and an RTO of 4 hours.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements in the **MOST** cost-effective way?

options.text: Set up an Aurora global database and DynamoDB global tables to replicate the databases to a secondary AWS Region. In the primary Region and in the secondary Region, configure an API Gateway API with a Regional endpoint. Implement Amazon CloudFront with origin failover to route traffic to the secondary Region during a DR scenario.

Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS), Amazon EventBridge, and AWS Lambda to replicate the Aurora databases to a secondary AWS Region. Use DynamoDB Streams, EventBridge. and Lambda to replicate the DynamoDB databases to the secondary Region. In the primary Region and in the secondary Region, configure an API Gateway API with a Regional endpoint. Implement Amazon Route 53 failover routing to switch traffic from the primary Region to the secondary Region.

Use AWS Backup to create backups of the Aurora databases and the DynamoDB databases in a secondary AWS Region. In the primary Region and in the secondary Region, configure an API Gateway API with a Regional endpoint. Implement Amazon Route 53 failover routing to switch traffic from the primary Region to the secondary Region.

Set up an Aurora global database and DynamoDB global tables to replicate the databases to a secondary AWS Region. In the primary Region and in the secondary Region, configure an API Gateway API with a Regional endpoint. Implement Amazon Route 53 failover routing to switch traffic from the primary Region to the secondary Region.

questions.explanation:
AWS Backup can create and copy Aurora and DynamoDB backups to a secondary Region, providing a low-cost backup-and-restore DR strategy. Scheduling backups no more than two hours apart meets the 2-hour RPO, and the secondary application endpoint plus Route 53 primary/secondary failover routing supports recovery within the 4-hour RTO when restoration procedures are planned and tested. This avoids the ongoing cost of continuously replicated Aurora global databases and DynamoDB global tables. Route 53 failover routing directs traffic to a secondary resource when the primary resource is unhealthy.

**Learn more:** [Backup and recovery using AWS Backup](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/backup-recovery/aws-backup.html) · [Copying a backup of a DynamoDB table with AWS Backup](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/CrossRegionAccountCopyAWS.html)

Which network configuration should a solutions architect use to provide connectivity from the client applications in the business-unit VPCs to the centralized application in the shared VPC?

What is the **MOST** operationally efficient solution that meets these requirements?

S3 Batch Operations can copy large object sets back into the same bucket and apply encryption at scale, making it appropriate for buckets containing millions of objects.
