A solutions architect must implement a multi-Region architecture for an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database that supports a web application. The database launches from an AWS CloudFormation template that includes AWS services and features that are present in both the primary and secondary Regions.  
  
The database is configured for automated backups, and it has an RTO of 15 minutes and an RPO of 2 hours. The web application is configured to use an Amazon Route 53 record to route traffic to the database.  
  
Which combination of steps will result in a highly available architecture that meets all the requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create a cross-Region read replica of the database in the secondary Region. Configure an AWS Lambda function in the secondary Region to promote the read replica during a failover event.

In the primary Region, create a health check on the database that will invoke an AWS Lambda function when a failure is detected. Program the Lambda function to recreate the database from the latest database snapshot in the secondary Region and update the Route 53 host records for the database.
Create an AWS Lambda function to copy the latest automated backup to the secondary Region every 2 hours.
Create a failover routing policy in Route 53 for the database DNS record. Set the primary and secondary endpoints to the endpoints in each Region.
Create a hot standby database in the secondary Region. Use an AWS Lambda function to restore the secondary database to the latest RDS automatic backup in the event that the primary database fails.

questions.explanation:
To achieve an RTO of 15 minutes and RPO of 2 hours, a cross-Region read replica (Option A) must be promoted during failover—this replica stays synchronized with the primary and can be promoted quickly to meet the RTO. Option D uses Route 53 failover routing to automatically detect primary database failure and route traffic to the secondary region's endpoint. Together, these ensure both rapid failover and automatic traffic routing. Restoring from backups alone would exceed the 15-minute RTO.

**Learn more:** [Creating a read replica in a different AWS Region](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.XRgn.html) · [Route 53 failover routing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-failover.html)

A company’s interactive web application uses an Amazon CloudFront distribution to deliver images from an Amazon S3 bucket. At times, third-party tools ingest corrupted images into the S3 bucket. This image corruption later creates a poor user experience in the application. The company has successfully implemented and tested Python logic for detecting corrupt images.  
  
A solutions architect must recommend a solution that integrates the detection logic with minimal latency between ingestion and serving.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use a Lambda@Edge function that is invoked by a viewer-response event.
Use a Lambda@Edge function that is invoked by an origin-response event.
Use an S3 event notification that invokes an AWS Lambda function.
Use an S3 event notification that invokes an AWS Step Functions state machine.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 event notifications can invoke an AWS Lambda function asynchronously when an object is created. This runs the existing Python corruption-detection logic as soon as an image is ingested, rather than waiting for CloudFront to receive and process a viewer request. Lambda@Edge response events occur during content delivery, and Step Functions adds orchestration that is unnecessary for a single detection function.

**Learn more:** [Process Amazon S3 event notifications with Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-s3.html) · [CloudFront events that can trigger a Lambda@Edge function](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/lambda-cloudfront-trigger-events.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect needs to update an application environment in AWS Elastic Beanstalk by using a blue/green deployment approach. The solutions architect creates an environment identical to the existing application environment and deploys the application to that new environment.  
  
What should be done next to complete the update?

options.text: Redirect to the new environment using Amazon Route 53.
Select the Swap Environment URLs option.
Replace the Auto Scaling launch configuration.
Update the DNS records to point to the green environment.

questions.explanation:
AWS Elastic Beanstalk blue/green deployments complete the production cutover by swapping the two environments’ URLs (CNAMEs). The swap redirects traffic from the existing environment to the newly deployed environment without an application-service interruption.

**Learn more:** [Blue/Green deployments with Elastic Beanstalk](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/using-features.CNAMESwap.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a website on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances are in an Auto Scaling group, and the ALB is associated with an AWS WAF web ACL.  
  
The website frequently experiences application-layer attacks. These attacks cause abrupt, substantial traffic increases on the application server. Access logs indicate that each attack comes from different IP addresses. A solutions architect must implement a solution to mitigate these attacks.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST operational overhead**?

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that monitors server access. Set a threshold based on access by IP address. Configure an alarm action that adds the IP address to the web ACL’s deny list.
Deploy AWS Shield Advanced in addition to AWS WAF. Add the ALB as a protected resource.

Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that monitors user IP addresses. Set a threshold based on access by IP address. Configure the alarm to invoke an AWS Lambda function to add a deny rule in the application server’s subnet route table for any IP addresses that activate the alarm.
Inspect access logs to find a pattern of IP addresses that launched the attacks. Use an Amazon Route 53 geolocation routing policy to deny traffic from the countries that host those IP addresses.

questions.explanation:
AWS Shield Advanced provides managed DDoS detection and mitigation at the application layer (layer 7) and supports Application Load Balancers as protected resources. Protecting the ALB lets Shield Advanced analyze traffic patterns and mitigate distributed request-flood attacks without maintaining manual IP deny lists, subnet route rules, or country blocks.

**Learn more:** [Protecting the application layer with AWS Shield Advanced and AWS WAF](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-app-layer-protections.html) · [List of resources that AWS Shield Advanced protects](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/ddos-protections-by-resource-type.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],To comply with industry regulations, a solutions architect must create a solution that stores a company’s critical data across multiple public AWS Regions, including in the United States, where the company headquarters is located. The solutions architect must provide the company’s global WAN network with access to the data stored in AWS. The security team requires that no traffic used to access this data traverses the public internet.  
  
How should the solutions architect design a highly available, cost-effective solution that meets these requirements?

options.text: Establish AWS Direct Connect connections from the company headquarters to all AWS Regions in use. Use the company WAN to send traffic over to the headquarters and then to the respective DX connection to access the data.

Establish two AWS Direct Connect connections from the company headquarters to an AWS Region. Use the company WAN to send traffic over a DX connection. Use inter-region VPC peering to access the data in other AWS Regions.

Establish two AWS Direct Connect connections from the company headquarters to an AWS Region. Use the company WAN to send traffic over a DX connection. Use an AWS transit VPC solution to access data in other AWS Regions.

Establish two AWS Direct Connect connections from the company headquarters to an AWS Region. Use the company WAN to send traffic over a DX connection. Use Direct Connect Gateway to access data in other AWS Regions.

questions.explanation:
Two AWS Direct Connect connections provide redundant private network paths from the headquarters to AWS. A Direct Connect gateway can use that connectivity to reach VPCs in multiple AWS Regions, so global WAN traffic can access regional data without traversing the public internet and without deploying separate Direct Connect connections for every Region.

**Learn more:** [Direct Connect gateways](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-gateways.html) · [Access to remote Direct Connect Regions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/remote_regions.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to migrate its on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud. The environment includes thousands of virtualized Linux and Microsoft Windows servers, SAN storage, Java and PHP applications using MySQL, and Oracle databases. Many dependent services are hosted either within the same data center or externally. The technical documentation is incomplete and out of date. A solutions architect must understand the existing environment and estimate cloud resource costs after migration.  
  
Which tools or services should the solutions architect use to plan the cloud migration? (Choose three.)

options.text: AWS Application Discovery Service
AWS SMS
AWS X-Ray
AWS Cloud Adoption Readiness Tool (CART)
Amazon Inspector
AWS Migration Hub

questions.explanation:
AWS Application Discovery Service collects on-premises server and database configuration, utilization, and network-connection data. Its exported utilization data supports AWS cost modeling, while dependency data supports application grouping and migration planning. AWS Migration Hub provides a central place to discover servers, plan migrations, visualize application connections, and track migration status. AWS Cloud Adoption Readiness Tool (CART) evaluates cloud-adoption readiness, complementing the technical discovery and migration-planning work.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Application Discovery Service?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/application-discovery/latest/userguide/what-is-appdiscovery.html) · [What Is AWS Migration Hub?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/migrationhub/latest/ug/whatishub.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An online gaming company must optimize the costs of its AWS workloads. The company uses a dedicated account to host the production environment for its online gaming application and an analytics application.  
  
Amazon EC2 instances host the gaming application and must be available at all times. The EC2 instances operate throughout the year. The analytics application uses data stored in Amazon S3. The analytics application can be interrupted and resumed without problems.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements in the **MOST** cost-effective way?

options.text: Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan for the online gaming application instances. Use On-Demand Instances for the analytics application.
Purchase an EC2 Instance Savings Plan for the online gaming application instances. Use Spot Instances for the analytics application.
Use Spot Instances for the online gaming application and the analytics application. Set up a catalog in AWS Service Catalog to provision services at a discount.
Use On-Demand Instances for the online gaming application. Use Spot Instances for the analytics application. Set up a catalog in AWS Service Catalog to provision services at a discount.

questions.explanation:
EC2 Instance Savings Plans reduce cost for predictable, steady EC2 usage, making them appropriate for a production application that runs continuously and requires uninterrupted availability. Spot Instances use spare EC2 capacity at substantial discounts and are appropriate for interruption-tolerant analytics workloads that can resume after interruption. AWS Service Catalog standardizes provisioning but does not create an EC2 pricing discount.

**Learn more:** [Choosing a purchasing option for Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/decision-guides/latest/ec2-purchasing-options-aws-how-to-choose/ec2-purchasing-options-aws-how-to-choose.html) · [Savings Plans types](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/latest/userguide/plan-types.html)

A company runs a critical, stateful web application on two Linux Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB), with an Amazon RDS for MySQL database. The company hosts the application's DNS records in Amazon Route 53. A solutions architect must recommend a solution to increase application resiliency.  
  
The solution must satisfy these objectives:  
  
- Application tier: RPO of 2 minutes; RTO of 30 minutes  
- Database tier: RPO of 5 minutes; RTO of 30 minutes  
  
The company does not want to make substantial changes to the current application architecture. The company must ensure optimal latency following a failover.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure the EC2 instances to use AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery. Create a cross-Region read replica for the RDS DB instance. Create an ALB in a second AWS Region. Create an AWS Global Accelerator endpoint, and associate the endpoint with the ALBs. Update DNS records to point to the Global Accelerator endpoint.

Configure the EC2 instances to use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM) to take snapshots of the EBS volumes. Configure RDS automated backups. Configure backup replication to a second AWS Region. Create an ALB in the second Region. Create an AWS Global Accelerator endpoint, and associate the endpoint with the ALBs. Update DNS records to point to the Global Accelerator endpoint.

Create a backup plan in AWS Backup for the EC2 instances and RDS DB instance. Configure backup replication to a second AWS Region. Create an ALB in the second Region. Configure an Amazon CloudFront distribution in front of the ALB. Update DNS records to point to CloudFront.

Configure the EC2 instances to use Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM) to take snapshots of the EBS volumes. Create a cross-Region read replica for the RDS DB instance. Create an ALB in a second AWS Region. Create an AWS Global Accelerator endpoint, and associate the endpoint with the ALBs.

questions.explanation:
AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates server blocks and supports an RPO measured in seconds with an RTO typically measured in minutes, meeting the application-tier targets with minimal change to the existing EC2 workload. A cross-Region Amazon RDS for MySQL read replica supplies a recoverable database in the secondary Region that can be promoted during disaster recovery. AWS Global Accelerator health-checks the regional ALB endpoints and routes traffic to healthy endpoints based on client location, supporting resilient, low-latency post-failover access.

**Learn more:** [AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery concepts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/drs/latest/userguide/CloudEndure-Concepts.html) · [Creating a read replica in a different AWS Region](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.XRgn.html)

A life sciences company uses a combination of open-source tools to manage data-analysis workflows and Docker containers running on servers in its on-premises data center to process genomics data. Sequencing data is created and stored on a local storage area network (SAN), after which it is processed. The research and development teams are encountering capacity constraints and have decided to re-architect their genomics analysis platform on AWS to scale according to workload demand and reduce turnaround time from weeks to days.  
  
The company has a high-speed AWS Direct Connect connection. Sequencers will produce approximately 200 GB of data for each genome, and individual jobs can require several hours to process the data with ideal compute capacity. The final result will be stored in Amazon S3. The company expects 10–15 job requests per day.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use regularly scheduled AWS Snowball Edge devices to transfer the sequencing data into AWS. When AWS receives the Snowball Edge device and the data is loaded into Amazon S3, use S3 events to trigger an AWS Lambda function to process the data.

Use AWS Data Pipeline to transfer the sequencing data to Amazon S3. Use S3 events to trigger an Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling group to launch custom-AMI EC2 instances running the Docker containers to process the data.

Use AWS DataSync to transfer the sequencing data to Amazon S3. Use S3 events to trigger an AWS Lambda function that starts an AWS Step Functions workflow. Store the Docker images in Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) and trigger AWS Batch to run the container and process the sequencing data.

Use an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway to transfer the sequencing data to Amazon S3. Use S3 events to trigger an AWS Batch job that executes on Amazon EC2 instances running the Docker containers to process the data.

questions.explanation:
AWS DataSync transfers data between on-premises storage systems and Amazon S3. An S3 event can invoke Lambda to start a Step Functions workflow, which can coordinate an AWS Batch job. AWS Batch is designed for high-scale, compute-intensive containerized batch workloads and automatically provisions compute capacity based on submitted jobs; its job definitions specify the Docker image to run, including an image stored in Amazon ECR.

**Learn more:** [Transferring to or from on-premises storage with AWS DataSync](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/transferring-on-premises-storage.html) · [What is AWS Batch?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/batch/latest/userguide/what-is-batch.html)

A company has recently begun hosting new application workloads in the AWS Cloud. The company uses Amazon EC2 instances, Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file systems, and Amazon RDS DB instances.  
  
To satisfy regulatory and business requirements for data backups, the company must make these changes:  
  
- Backups must be retained according to custom daily, weekly, and monthly requirements.  
- Backups must be replicated to at least one other AWS Region immediately after they are captured.  
- The backup solution must offer a single source of backup status throughout the AWS environment.  
- The backup solution must send immediate notifications if any resource backup fails.  
  
Which combination of steps meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create an AWS Backup plan with a backup rule for each of the retention requirements.
Configure an AWS Backup plan to copy backups to another Region.
Create an AWS Lambda function to replicate backups to another Region and send notification if a failure occurs.
Add an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic to the backup plan to send a notification for finished jobs that have any status except BACKUP_JOB_COMPLETED.
Create an Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM) snapshot lifecycle policy for each of the retention requirements.
Set up RDS snapshots on each database.

questions.explanation:
AWS Backup centralizes backup management for EC2, EFS, and RDS across multiple AWS accounts. Multiple backup rules within a single plan enable different retention schedules (daily, weekly, monthly). A backup-plan copy action automatically replicates backups to another Region. AWS Backup integrates with Amazon SNS to notify on backup-job completion events, allowing subscriptions to alert on non-successful statuses. This avoids custom Lambda-based replication and notification logic, providing centralized management and monitoring.

**Learn more:** [Creating backup copies across AWS Regions (AWS Backup)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/cross-region-backup.html) · [Notification options with AWS Backup](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/backup-notifications.html)

A company is moving to the cloud. It needs to assess the configurations of virtual machines in its current data center environment so it can accurately size new Amazon EC2 instances.  
  
The company wants to collect metrics such as CPU, memory, and disk utilization, and it requires an inventory of the processes running on every instance. It would also like to monitor network connections to map communications between servers.  
  
Which option would enable this data to be collected **MOST** cost effectively?

options.text: Use AWS Application Discovery Service and deploy the data collection agent to each virtual machine in the data center.
Configure the Amazon CloudWatch agent on all servers within the local environment and publish metrics to Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
Use AWS Application Discovery Service and enable agentless discovery in the existing virtualization environment.
Enable AWS Application Discovery Service in the AWS Management Console and configure the corporate firewall to allow scans over a VPN.

questions.explanation:
AWS Application Discovery Service Discovery Agent is installed on each on-premises virtual machine and collects system configuration, time-series performance and utilization data, running-process data, and TCP network connections. This provides the utilization data needed for EC2 sizing, process inventory, and server-dependency mapping in one migration-discovery service.

**Learn more:** [AWS Application Discovery Agent](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/application-discovery/latest/userguide/discovery-agent.html) · [View and explore discovered data — AWS Application Discovery Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/application-discovery/latest/userguide/view-and-explore.html)

An AWS partner company is developing a service in AWS Organizations with its organization, named `org1`. The service requires the partner company to access AWS resources in a customer account that belongs to a separate organization, named `org2`. The company must establish least-privilege security access to the customer account by using an API or command-line tool.  
  
What is the **MOST secure** way to allow `org1` to access resources in `org2`?

options.text: The customer should provide the partner company with their AWS account access keys to log in and perform the required tasks.

The customer should create an IAM user and assign the required permissions to the IAM user. The customer should then provide the credentials to the partner company to log in and perform the required tasks.

The customer should create an IAM role and assign the required permissions to the IAM role. The partner company should then use the IAM role’s Amazon Resource Name (ARN) when requesting access to perform the required tasks.

The customer should create an IAM role and assign the required permissions to the IAM role. The partner company should then use the IAM role’s Amazon Resource Name (ARN), including the external ID in the IAM role’s trust policy, when requesting access to perform the required tasks.

questions.explanation:
For third-party cross-account programmatic access, the customer should delegate only the required permissions through an IAM role that the partner assumes with temporary AWS STS credentials. Requiring a unique external ID in the role trust policy ensures the role can be assumed only when the partner is acting for that customer, mitigating the confused-deputy problem. This avoids sharing long-term account or IAM-user credentials.

**Learn more:** [Access to AWS accounts owned by third parties](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_common-scenarios_third-party.html) · [Cross account resource access in IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies-cross-account-resource-access.html)

An education company operates a web application used by college students worldwide. The application runs in an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). A system administrator identifies a weekly surge in failed login attempts that overwhelms the application's authentication service. All failed login attempts come from about 500 distinct IP addresses, which change every week. A solutions architect must stop the failed login attempts from overwhelming the authentication service.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements with the **MOST** operational efficiency?

options.text: Use AWS Firewall Manager to create a security group and security group policy to deny access from the IP addresses.
Create an AWS WAF web ACL with a rate-based rule, and set the rule action to Block. Connect the web ACL to the ALB.
Use AWS Firewall Manager to create a security group and security group policy to allow access only to specific CIDR ranges.
Create an AWS WAF web ACL with an IP set match rule, and set the rule action to Block. Connect the web ACL to the ALB.

questions.explanation:
An AWS WAF rate-based rule automatically aggregates and rate-limits requests by source IP address by default. With a Block action and an association to the ALB, it blocks sources that exceed the configured request threshold before their requests reach the ECS-hosted authentication service. This avoids the recurring operational work of maintaining a block list for IP addresses that change weekly.

**Learn more:** [Using rate-based rule statements in AWS WAF](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-statement-type-rate-based.html) · [Aggregating rate-based rules in AWS WAF](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/waf-rule-statement-type-rate-based-aggregation-options.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An online retail company is moving its legacy on-premises .NET application to AWS. The application operates on load-balanced frontend web servers, load-balanced application servers, and a Microsoft SQL Server database.  
  
The company wants to use AWS managed services wherever possible and does not want to rewrite the application. A solutions architect must implement a solution that resolves scaling issues and minimizes licensing costs as the application grows.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.text: Deploy Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer for the web tier and for the application tier. Use Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL with Babelfish turned on to replatform the SQL Server database.

Create images of all the servers by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Deploy Amazon EC2 instances that are based on the on-premises imports. Deploy the instances in an Auto Scaling group behind a Network Load Balancer for the web tier and for the application tier. Use Amazon DynamoDB as the database tier.

Containerize the web frontend tier and the application tier. Provision an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster. Create an Auto Scaling group behind a Network Load Balancer for the web tier and for the application tier. Use Amazon RDS for SQL Server to host the database.

Update the application’s Route 53 record with a failover policy that routes traffic to the ALB in the backup Region when a health check failure occurs.

Configure the Auto Scaling group in the backup Region to have the same values as the Auto Scaling group in the primary Region. Reconfigure the application’s Route 53 record with a latency-based routing policy that load balances traffic between the two ALBs. Remove the read replica. Replace the read replica with a standalone RDS DB instance. Configure Cross-Region Replication between the RDS DB instances by using snapshots and Amazon S3.

Configure an endpoint in AWS Global Accelerator with the two ALBs as equal weighted targets. Create an AWS Lambda function in the backup Region to promote the read replica and modify the Auto Scaling group values. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm that is based on the HTTPCode_Target_5XX_Count metric for the ALB in the primary Region. Configure the CloudWatch alarm to invoke the Lambda function.

questions.explanation:
Route 53 DNS failover uses health checks to route traffic away from an unhealthy primary record to a healthy secondary record. A health-check notification can initiate an SNS-triggered Lambda workflow that promotes the cross-Region RDS read replica to an independent DB instance and increases the backup Auto Scaling group capacity. This provides automated active-passive recovery while avoiding the continuous compute cost of active-active deployment. RDS read-replica promotion is specifically supported as a failure-recovery mechanism.

**Learn more:** [How Amazon Route 53 checks the health of your resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/welcome-health-checks.html) · [Promoting a read replica to be a standalone DB instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.Promote.html)

Accompany is developing an application to gather and transmit sensor data from a factory. The application will use AWS IoT Core to send data from hundreds of devices to an Amazon S3 data lake. The company must enrich the data before it loads the data into Amazon S3.  
  
The application will send the sensor data every 5 seconds. New sensor data must be available in Amazon S3 in less than 30 minutes after the application collects the data. No other applications process the sensor data from AWS IoT Core.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.text: Create a topic in AWS IoT Core to ingest the sensor data. Create an AWS Lambda function to enrich the data and to write the data to Amazon S3. Configure an AWS IoT rule action to invoke the Lambda function.

Use AWS IoT Core Basic Ingest to ingest the sensor data. Configure an AWS IoT rule action to write the data to Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose. Set the Kinesis Data Firehose buffering interval to 900 seconds. Use Kinesis Data Firehose to invoke an AWS Lambda function to enrich the data, Configure Kinesis Data Firehose to deliver the data to Amazon S3.

Create a topic in AWS IoT Core to ingest the sensor data. Configure an AWS IoT rule action to send the data to an Amazon Timestream table. Create an AWS Lambda, function to read the data from Timestream. Configure the Lambda function to enrich the data and to write the data to Amazon S3.

Use AWS loT Core Basic Ingest to ingest the sensor data. Configure an AWS IoT rule action to write the data to Amazon Kinesis Data Streams. Create a consumer AWS Lambda function to process the data from Kinesis Data Streams and to enrich the data. Call the S3 PutObject API operation from the Lambda function to write the data to Amazon S3.

questions.explanation:
AWS IoT Core Basic Ingest routes device messages directly to an IoT rule without publish/subscribe messaging charges, which is suitable when no other application needs to consume the messages. Amazon Data Firehose batches records, can invoke AWS Lambda to transform or enrich them, and delivers the transformed data to Amazon S3. A 900-second buffer supports the required availability period while reducing Lambda invocations and S3 write operations.

**Learn more:** [Reducing messaging costs with Basic Ingest - AWS IoT Core](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/iot-basic-ingest.html) · [Transform source data in Amazon Data Firehose](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/firehose/latest/dev/data-transformation.html)

A software development company has multiple engineers who are working remotely. The company is running Active Directory Domain Services (AD DS) on an Amazon EC2 instance. The company's security policy states that all internal, nonpublic services that are deployed in a VPC must be accessible through a VPN. Multi-factor authentication (MFA) must be used for access to a VPN.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection. Configure integration between a VPN and AD DS. Use an Amazon WorkSpaces client with MFA support enabled to establish a VPN connection.
Create an AWS Client VPN endpoint. Create an AD Connector directory for integration with AD DS. Enable MFA for AD Connector. Use AWS Client VPN to establish a VPN connection.
Create multiple AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections by using AWS VPN CloudHub. Configure integration between AWS VPN CloudHub and AD DS. Use AWS Copilot to establish a VPN connection.
Create an Amazon WorkLink endpoint. Configure integration between Amazon WorkLink and AD DS. Enable MFA in Amazon WorkLink. Use AWS Client VPN to establish a VPN connection.

questions.explanation:
AWS Client VPN is the correct service for providing remote user VPN access with Active Directory integration and MFA support. It works with AD Connector to authenticate against the on-premises AD DS instance and enforces MFA when configured. Site-to-Site VPN connects networks, not individual users; WorkLink provides secure web/app access (not VPN); AWS Copilot deploys container applications (not relevant here).

**Learn more:** [Active Directory authentication in Client VPN](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/clientvpn-admin/ad.html) · [Enabling MFA for AD Connector](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/ad_connector_mfa.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an asynchronous HTTP application hosted by an AWS Lambda function. A public Amazon API Gateway endpoint invokes the Lambda function. Both the Lambda function and the API Gateway endpoint are located in the `us-east-1` Region. A solutions architect must redesign the application to support failover to another AWS Region.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Create an API Gateway endpoint in the us-west-2 Region to direct traffic to the Lambda function in us-east-1. Configure Amazon Route 53 to use a failover routing policy to route traffic for the two API Gateway endpoints.

Create an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure API Gateway to direct traffic to the SQS queue instead of to the Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to pull messages from the queue for processing.

Deploy the Lambda function to the us-west-2 Region. Create an API Gateway endpoint in us-west-2 10 direct traffic to the Lambda function in us-west-2. Configure AWS Global Accelerator and an Application Load Balancer to manage traffic across the two API Gateway endpoints.
Deploy the Lambda function and an API Gateway endpoint to the us-west-2 Region. Configure Amazon Route 53 to use a failover routing policy to route traffic for the two API Gateway endpoints.

questions.explanation:
Cross-Region failover requires the Lambda function and its API Gateway endpoint to be deployed in the secondary Region so that the secondary endpoint can process requests independently of the primary Region. Amazon Route 53 failover routing, with appropriate health checks, can route a custom domain from the primary API Gateway API to the secondary API Gateway API when the primary Region is unavailable. AWS documents this as DNS failover from an API Gateway API in a primary Region to one in a secondary Region.

**Learn more:** [Configure custom health checks for DNS failover for an API Gateway API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/dns-failover.html) · [Failover routing - Amazon Route 53](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-failover.html)

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution to serve assets from the S3 bucket. Configure S3 Cross-Region Replication. Create a new DynamoDB table in a new Region. Use the new table as a replica target for DynamoDB global tables.

Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution to serve assets from the S3 bucket. Configure S3 Same-Region Replication. Create a new DynamoDB table in a new Region. Configure asynchronous replication between the DynamoDB tables by using AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) with change data capture (CDC).

Create another S3 bucket in a new Region, and configure S3 Cross-Region Replication between the buckets. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution and configure origin failover with two origins accessing the S3 buckets in each Region. Configure DynamoDB global tables by enabling Amazon DynamoDB Streams, and add a replica table in a new Region.

Create another S3 bucket in the sine Region, and configure S3 Same-Region Replication between the buckets. Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution and configure origin failover with two origins accessing the S3 buckets. Create a new DynamoDB table in a new Region. Use the new table as a replica target for DynamoDB global tables.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront delivers and caches Amazon S3 game assets close to globally distributed users. Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication maintains asset copies in another Region, and DynamoDB global tables provide managed multi-Region replication of player-score data through replica tables. This combines low-latency content delivery and cross-Region resilience without building custom replication with AWS DMS or relying on same-Region replication.

**Learn more:** [Replicating objects within and across Regions - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication.html) · [How DynamoDB global tables work](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/V2globaltables_HowItWorks.html)

A scientific company must process text and image data from an Amazon S3 bucket. Several radar stations collect the data during a live, time-critical phase of a deep-space mission. The radar stations upload their data to the source S3 bucket, and the data is prefixed with the radar station identification number.  
  
The company created a destination S3 bucket in a second account. To meet a compliance objective, data must be copied from the source S3 bucket to the destination S3 bucket. An S3 replication rule replicates all objects in the source S3 bucket.  
  
One particular radar station has been identified as providing the most accurate data. Replication of data from this radar station must be monitored to confirm completion within 30 minutes after it uploads objects to the source S3 bucket.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Setup an AWS DataSync agent to replicate the prefixed data from the source S3 bucket to the destination S3 bucket. Select to use all available bandwidth on the task, and monitor the task to ensure that itis in the TRANSFERRING status. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to initiate an alert if this status changes.

In the second account, create another S3 bucket to receive data from the radar station with the most accurate data. Set up a new replication rule for this new S3 bucket to separate the replication from the other radar stations. Monitor the maximum replication time to the destination. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to initiate an alert when the time exceeds the desired threshold.

Enable Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration on the source S3 bucket, and configure the radar station with the most accurate data to use the new endpoint. Monitor the S3 destination bucket's TotalRequestLatency metric. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to initiate an alert if this status changes.

Create a new S3 replication rule on the source S3 bucket that filters for the keys that use the prefix of the radar station with the most accurate data. Enable S3 Replication Time Control (S3 RTC). Monitor the maximum replication time to the destination. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to initiate an alert when the time exceeds the desired threshold.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Replication Time Control (S3 RTC) provides predictable replication and automatically publishes replication metrics at the replication-rule level, including maximum replication time to the destination. A replication rule filtered by the selected radar station’s prefix isolates that station’s data for monitoring. S3 RTC replicates 99.99% of new objects within 15 minutes under its SLA, satisfying a 30-minute completion requirement; an EventBridge-triggered alert can notify when the monitored replication time exceeds the threshold.

**Learn more:** [Meeting compliance requirements with S3 Replication Time Control](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication-time-control.html) · [Using S3 Replication metrics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/repl-metrics.html)

A company is migrating its data center to the AWS Cloud and needs to complete the migration as quickly as possible. The company has many applications that are running on hundreds of VMware VMs in the data center. Each VM is configured with a shared Windows folder that contains common shared files. The file share is larger than 100 GB in size.  
  
The company’s compliance team requires a change request to be fled and approved for every software installation and modification to each VM. The company has an AWS Direct Connect connection with 10 GB of bandwidth between AWS and the data center.  
  
Which set of steps should the company take to complete the migration in the LEAST amount of time?

options.text: Use VM ImporvExport to create images of each VM. Use AWS Application Migration Service to manage and view the images. Copy the Windows file share data to an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. After migration, remap the file share to the EFS file system.
Deploy the AWS Application Discovery Service agentless appliance to VMware vCenter. Review the portfolio of discovered VMs in AWS Migration Hub.

Deploy the AWS Application Migration Service agentless appliance to VMware vCenter. Copy the Windows file share data to a new Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. After migration, remap the file share on each VM to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.C. Create and review a portfolio in AWS Migration Hub. Order an AWS Snowcone device. Deploy AWS Application Migration Service to VMware vCenter and export all the VMs to the Snowcone device. Copy all Windows file share data to the Snowcone device. Ship the Snowcone device to AWS. Use Application Migration Service to deploy all the migrated instances.

Deploy the AWS Application Discovery Service Agent and the AWS Application Migration Service Agent onto each VMware hypervisor directly. Review the portfolio in AWS Migration Hub. Copy each VM’s file share data to a new Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. After migration, remap the file share on each VM to the FSx for Windows File Server file system.

questions.explanation:
AWS Application Migration Service agentless appliance deployed to VMware vCenter eliminates the need for installing software on VMs, satisfying the compliance requirement for change request approval. Amazon FSx for Windows File Server preserves the native Windows file share experience for the large shared folder. This approach migrates hundreds of VMs quickly (agentless at scale) while respecting compliance requirements that preclude software installation on individual VMs.

**Learn more:** [Agentless replication for vCenter - Application Migration Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/mgn/latest/ug/agentless-mgn.html) · [What is FSx for Windows File Server?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/what-is.html)

A company runs an application in the AWS Cloud. Its core business logic runs on a group of Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. An Application Load Balancer (ALB) distributes traffic across the EC2 instances. The Amazon Route 53 record `api.example.com` points to the ALB.  
  
The company’s development team makes major changes to the business logic. The company has a rule that, when changes are deployed, only 10% of customers may receive the new logic during a testing window. Each customer must use the same version of the business logic throughout the testing window.  
  
How should the company deploy the updates to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a second ALB, and deploy the new logic to a set of EC2 instances in a new Auto Scaling group. Configure the ALB to distribute traffic to the EC2 instances. Update the Route 53 record to use weighted routing, and point the record to both of the ALBs.

Create a second target group that is referenced by the ALDeploy the new logic to EC2 instances in this new target group. Update the ALB listener rule to use weighted target groups. Configure ALB target group stickiness.

Create a new launch configuration for the Auto Scaling group. Specify the launch configuration to use the AutoScalingRollingUpdate policy, and set the MaxBatchSize option to 10. Replace the launch configuration on the Auto Scaling group. Deploy the changes.

Create a second Auto Scaling group that is referenced by the ALB. Deploy the new logic on a set of EC2 instances in this new Auto Scaling group. Change the ALB routing algorithm to least outstanding requests (LOR). Configure ALB session stickiness.

questions.explanation:
An Application Load Balancer listener rule can forward traffic to multiple target groups using relative weights, so the target group containing the new EC2 instances can receive 10% of traffic. Target group stickiness binds subsequent requests from a client to the target group initially selected, ensuring that customer continues to use the same business-logic version during the testing window.

**Learn more:** [Action types for listener rules - Elastic Load Balancing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/rule-action-types.html) · [Target group stickiness - AWS Prescriptive Guidance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/load-balancer-stickiness/target-group-stickiness.html)

A company runs its cloud infrastructure on AWS. A solutions architect must define the infrastructure as code. The infrastructure is currently deployed in a single AWS Region. The company’s business expansion plan includes deployments across multiple Regions and multiple AWS accounts.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to fulfill these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS CloudFormation templates. Add IAM policies to control the various accounts, Deploy the templates across the multiple Regions.
Use AWS Organizations. Deploy AWS CloudFormation templates from the management account Use AWS Control Tower to manage deployments across accounts.
Use AWS Organizations and AWS CloudFormation StackSets. Deploy a Cloud Formation template from an account that has the necessary IAM permissions.
Use nested stacks with AWS CloudFormation templates. Change the Region by using nested stacks.

questions.explanation:
AWS CloudFormation StackSets deploy, update, or delete stacks from a single CloudFormation template across multiple AWS accounts and AWS Regions. AWS Organizations supports centralized management of the accounts, while the StackSet administrator requires the appropriate IAM permissions to perform deployments.

**Learn more:** [Managing stacks across accounts and Regions with StackSets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/what-is-cfnstacksets.html) · [StackSets concepts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/stacksets-concepts.html)

The company is deploying the application to additional Regions. It must give customers static IP addresses for the application so customers can add those addresses to allow lists. The solution must automatically route customers to the geographically nearest Region.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Create a CloudFront origin group. Add the NLB for each additional Region to the origin group. Provide customers with the IP address ranges of the distribution’s edge locations.
Create an AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerator. Create a standard accelerator endpoint for the NLB in each additional Region. Provide customers with the Global Accelerator IP address.
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Create a custom origin for the NLB in each additional Region. Provide customers with the IP address ranges of the distribution’s edge locations.

Create an AWS Global Accelerator custom routing accelerator. Create a listener for the custom routing accelerator. Add the IP address and ports for the NLB in each additional Region. Provide customers with the Global Accelerator IP address.

questions.explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerators provide persistent global static IP addresses that customers can allow-list. A standard accelerator can use Network Load Balancers in multiple AWS Regions as endpoints and routes traffic to the optimal healthy regional endpoint based on client location, satisfying geographic routing and availability requirements. [AWS Global Accelerator standard accelerators](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/about-accelerators.html)

A company runs applications in an AWS account named Source. The account belongs to an organization in AWS Organizations. One application uses AWS Lambda functions and stores inventory data in an Amazon Aurora database. The application deploys its Lambda functions by using a deployment package. The company has configured automated backups for Aurora.  
  
The company needs to migrate the Lambda functions and the Aurora database to a new AWS account named Target. Because the application processes critical data, the company must minimize downtime.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Download the Lambda function deployment package from the Source account. Use the deployment package and create new Lambda functions in the Target account. Share the automated Aurora DB cluster snapshot with the Target account.

Download the Lambda function deployment package from the Source account. Use the deployment package and create new Lambda functions in the Target account. Share the Aurora DB cluster with the Target account by using AWS Resource Access Manager {AWS RAM). Grant the Target account permission to clone the Aurora DB cluster.
Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the Lambda functions and the Aurora DB cluster with the Target account. Grant the Target account permission to clone the Aurora DB cluster.
Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the Lambda functions with the Target account. Share the automated Aurora DB cluster snapshot with the Target account.

questions.explanation:
AWS RAM can share an Aurora DB cluster with another account so that the recipient can create a cross-account clone; this is faster than creating and restoring a database snapshot. Lambda functions are recreated in the target account from their deployment packages. Automated Aurora DB cluster snapshots cannot be shared directly: they must be copied to a manual snapshot before sharing.

**Learn more:** [Cross-account cloning with AWS RAM and Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Managing.Clone.Cross-Account.html) · [Sharing a DB cluster snapshot](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-share-snapshot.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to use AWS for disaster recovery of an on-premises application. The company has hundreds of Windows-based servers that run the application. Every server mounts a shared common share.  
  
The company requires an RTO of 15 minutes and an RPO of 5 minutes. The solution must provide native failover and fallback capabilities.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.text: Create an AWS Storage Gateway File Gateway. Schedule daily Windows server backups. Save the data to Amazon S3. During a disaster, recover the on-premises servers from the backup. During tailback, run the on-premises servers on Amazon EC2 instances.

Create a set of AWS CloudFormation templates to create infrastructure. Replicate all data to Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) by using AWS DataSync. During a disaster, use AWS CodePipeline to deploy the templates to restore the on-premises servers. Fail back the data by using DataSync.

Create an AWS Cloud Development Kit (AWS CDK) pipeline to stand up a multi-site active-active environment on AWS. Replicate data into Amazon S3 by using the s3 sync command. During a disaster, swap DNS endpoints to point to AWS. Fail back the data by using the s3 sync command.

Use AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery to replicate the on-premises servers. Replicate data to an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system by using AWS DataSync. Mount the file system to AWS servers. During a disaster, fail over the on-premises servers to AWS. Fail back to new or existing servers by using Elastic Disaster Recovery.

questions.explanation:
AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery continuously replicates the on-premises servers and can launch recovery instances in AWS, providing a typical RPO in the sub-second range and an RTO typically of 5–20 minutes. It also supports failback to the source infrastructure. Amazon FSx for Windows File Server provides a Windows file share for the recovered servers, while AWS DataSync can transfer the shared data to that file system. This avoids the insufficient recovery point of daily backups and the added cost and operational complexity of an active-active environment.

**Learn more:** [Elastic Disaster Recovery Concepts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/drs/latest/userguide/CloudEndure-Concepts.html) · [Using Elastic Disaster Recovery for recovery and failback](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/drs/latest/userguide/failback.html)

Which combination of steps must the solutions architect take to improve application-performance visibility during peak-traffic events? (Choose three.)

options.text: Configure the Aurora MySQL DB cluster to publish slow query and error logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs.
Implement the AWS X-Ray SDK to trace incoming HTTP requests on the EC2 instances and implement tracing of SQL queries with the X-Ray SDK for Java.

The AWS X-Ray SDK for Java instruments incoming HTTP requests and SQL database calls, providing request-level traces that identify latency and failures across the application and database tiers.

If game assets become unavailable in the closest Region, they should be fetched from the other Region.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Create an origin group with one origin for each ALB. Set one of the origins as primary.
Create an Amazon Route 53 health check for each ALCreate a Route 53 failover routing record pointing to the two ALBs. Set the Evaluate Target Health value to Yes.

Create two Amazon CloudFront distributions, each with one ALB as the origin. Create an Amazon Route 53 failover routing record pointing to the two CloudFront distributions. Set the Evaluate Target Health value to Yes.
Create an Amazon Route 53 health check for each ALB. Create a Route 53 latency alias record pointing to the two ALBs. Set the Evaluate Target Health value to Yes.

questions.explanation:
A Route 53 latency alias record automatically directs each client to the ALB in the AWS Region with the lowest latency, which is effectively the closest Region, and pairing it with a health check per ALB (Evaluate Target Health set to Yes) removes an unhealthy Region from DNS answers so traffic automatically fails over to the other Region. A CloudFront distribution with an origin group instead always serves from the configured primary origin and only fails over on error, so it does not route to the closest Region by default.

**Learn more:** [Choosing a routing policy: Latency routing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/routing-policy-latency.html)

A solutions architect must assess a company’s Amazon EC2 instances and Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes to determine whether the company is using resources efficiently. The company runs several large, high-memory EC2 instances to host database clusters deployed in active/passive configurations. Utilization of these EC2 instances varies according to the applications that use the databases, and the company has not found a pattern.  
  
The solutions architect must analyze the environment and take action according to the findings.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.text: Create a dashboard by using AWS Systems Manager OpsCenter. Configure visualizations for Amazon CloudWatch metrics that are associated with the EC2 instances and their EBS volumes. Review the dashboard periodically, and identify usage patterns. Rightsize the EC2 instances based on the peaks in the metrics.

Turn on Amazon CloudWatch detailed monitoring for the EC2 instances and their EBS volumes. Create and review a dashboard that is based on the metrics. Identify usage patterns. Rightsize the EC2 instances based on the peaks in the metrics.

Install the Amazon CloudWatch agent on each of the EC2 instances. Turn on AWS Compute Optimizer, and let it run for at least 12 hours. Review the recommendations from Compute Optimizer, and rightsize the EC2 instances as directed.
Sign up for the AWS Enterprise Support plan. Turn on AWS Trusted Advisor. Wait 12 hours. Review the recommendations from Trusted Advisor, and rightsize the EC2 instances as directed.

questions.explanation:
AWS Compute Optimizer analyzes Amazon EC2 configuration and utilization data to generate rightsizing recommendations, and it also generates Amazon EBS volume recommendations. Installing the CloudWatch agent enables Compute Optimizer to analyze EC2 memory utilization, which is particularly relevant for high-memory database workloads. This provides automated cost and performance recommendations without requiring an AWS Enterprise Support plan or relying on manual review of dashboards.

A company is building a gene-reporting device that will gather genomic information to help researchers collect large data samples from a diverse population. The device will send 8 KB of genomic data every second to a data platform that must process and analyze the data and return information to researchers. The data platform must meet these requirements:  
  
- Provide near-real-time analytics for incoming genomic data.  
- Ensure that the data is flexible, parallel, and durable.  
- Send processing results to a data warehouse.  
  
Which strategy should a solutions architect use to meet these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to collect the inbound sensor data, analyze the data with Kinesis clients, and save the results to an Amazon RDS instance.
Use Amazon Kinesis Data Streams to collect the inbound sensor data, analyze the data with Kinesis clients, and save the results to an Amazon Redshift cluster using Amazon EMR.
Use Amazon S3 to collect the inbound device data, analyze the data from Amazon SQS with Kinesis, and save the results to an Amazon Redshift cluster.
Use an Amazon API Gateway to put requests into an Amazon SQS queue, analyze the data with an AWS Lambda function, and save the results to an Amazon Redshift cluster using Amazon EMR.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams ingests data in real time, durably stores it, and distributes records across shards for scalable parallel processing. Kinesis client applications can perform near-real-time analysis, and Amazon EMR can process Kinesis streams and load output into an Amazon Redshift data warehouse.

**Learn more:** [Create and manage Kinesis data streams](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/working-with-streams.html) · [Read data from Amazon Kinesis Data Streams using Amazon EMR](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/streams/latest/dev/using-other-services-emr.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates a cloud application composed of a database and a website. Users can submit data through the website, have that data processed, and receive it back by email. The data is stored in a MySQL database that runs on an Amazon EC2 instance. The database runs in a VPC with two private subnets. The website runs on Apache Tomcat on a single EC2 instance in another VPC with one public subnet. A single VPC peering connection exists between the database VPC and the website VPC.  
  
The website has experienced several outages over the previous month because of heavy traffic.  
  
Which actions should a solutions architect take to improve the application's reliability? (Choose three.)

options.text: Place the Tomcat server in an Auto Scaling group with multiple EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer.
Provision an additional VPC peering connection.
Migrate the MySQL database to Amazon Aurora with one Aurora Replica.
Provision two NAT gateways in the database VPC.
Move the Tomcat server to the database VPC.
Create an additional public subnet in a different Availability Zone in the website VPC.

questions.explanation:
An Application Load Balancer distributes requests across healthy EC2 targets and works with Auto Scaling to add or replace web-server capacity. An Application Load Balancer requires subnets in at least two Availability Zones, so an additional public subnet in a different Availability Zone enables a resilient multi-AZ web tier. An Aurora cluster replicates storage across Availability Zones, and an Aurora Replica can be promoted automatically during a writer failure, removing the database instance as a single point of failure.

**Learn more:** [What is an Application Load Balancer?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/introduction.html) · [Application Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/application-load-balancers.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A finance company runs its business-critical application on current-generation Linux EC2 instances. The application contains a self-managed MySQL database that performs heavy I/O operations. It handles a moderate amount of traffic successfully during most of the month. However, it slows down during the final three days of every month because of month-end reporting, despite the company using Elastic Load Balancers and Auto Scaling in its infrastructure to meet the increased demand.  
  
Which action would enable the database to handle the month-end load with the **LEAST** performance impact?

options.text: Pre-warming Elastic Load Balancers, using a bigger instance type, changing all Amazon EBS volumes to GP2 volumes.
Performing a one-time migration of the database cluster to Amazon RDS, and creating several additional read replicas to handle the load during end of month.
Using Amazon CloudWatch with AWS Lambda to change the type, size, or IOPS of Amazon EBS volumes in the cluster based on a specific CloudWatch metric.

Replacing all existing Amazon EBS volumes with new PIOPS volumes that have the maximum available storage size and I/O per second by taking snapshots before the end of the month and reverting back afterwards.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EBS Elastic Volumes lets current-generation EC2 instances dynamically modify an attached volume’s type, size, and IOPS without detaching it or restarting the instance. CloudWatch metrics and Lambda can automate a temporary increase in database-storage performance for the predictable I/O peak, avoiding the disruption of replacing volumes or the larger migration required for a database redesign. [AWS: Modify an Amazon EBS volume using Elastic Volumes operations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-modify-volume.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has 10 accounts that are members of an organization in AWS Organizations. AWS Config is configured in every account. Each account belongs to either the Prod OU or the NonProd OU.  
  
The company has configured an Amazon EventBridge rule in each AWS account to notify an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic whenever an Amazon EC2 security group inbound rule is created with `0.0.0.0/0` as its source. The company’s security team subscribes to the SNS topic.  
  
For every account in the NonProd OU, the security team must remove the ability to create a security group inbound rule that has `0.0.0.0/0` as its source.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Modify the EventBridge rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function to remove the security group inbound rule and to publish to the SNS topic. Deploy the updated rule to the NonProd OU.
Add the vpc-sg-open-only-to-authorized-ports AWS Config managed rule to the NonProd OU.
Configure an SCP to allow the ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress action when the value of the aws:SourceIp condition key is not 0.0.0.0/0. Apply the SCP to the NonProd OU.
Configure an SCP to deny the ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress action when the value of the aws:SourceIp condition key is 0.0.0.0/0. Apply the SCP to the NonProd OU.

questions.explanation:
A service control policy that explicitly denies ec2:AuthorizeSecurityGroupIngress whenever the request matches a 0.0.0.0/0 source acts as an organization-wide preventive guardrail: once attached to the NonProd OU, it stops the risky rule from ever being created in any account under that OU, with no per-account maintenance required afterward. This has far less ongoing operational effort than a detective AWS Config rule or an EventBridge-triggered Lambda function that must remediate the rule after it has already been created, and an explicit Deny statement is the standard, safer SCP authoring pattern compared to a narrowly scoped Allow statement, which adds no real restriction unless the account's default full-access allow policy is also removed.

**Learn more:** [How to use service control policies to set permission guardrails across accounts in your AWS Organization](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/security/how-to-use-service-control-policies-to-set-permission-guardrails-across-accounts-in-your-aws-organization/)

A solutions architect is creating the data storage and retrieval architecture for a new application that a company will launch soon. The application is intended to ingest millions of small records per minute from devices worldwide. Each record is smaller than 4 KB and must be stored durably so that it can be retrieved with low latency. The data is ephemeral, and the company must retain it for only 120 days, after which it may be deleted.  
  
The solutions architect estimates that storage needs over a year would be approximately 10–15 TB.  
  
Which storage strategy is the **MOST** cost-effective and satisfies the design requirements?

options.text: Design the application to store each incoming record as a single .csv file in an Amazon S3 bucket to allow for indexed retrieval. Configure a lifecycle policy to delete data older than 120 days.

Design the application to store each incoming record in an Amazon DynamoDB table properly configured for the scale. Configure the DynamoDB Time to Live (TTL) feature to delete records older than 120 days.
Design the application to store each incoming record in a single table in an Amazon RDS MySQL database. Run a nightly cron job that runs a query to delete any records older than 120 days.

Design the application to batch incoming records before writing them to an Amazon S3 bucket. Update the metadata for the object to contain the list of records in the batch and use the Amazon S3 metadata search feature to retrieve the data. Configure a lifecycle policy to delete the data after 120 days.

questions.explanation:
Amazon DynamoDB supports durable, single-digit-millisecond access at high request rates and is suitable for records smaller than its 400-KB item limit. A TTL attribute can set an expiry timestamp for each item; DynamoDB automatically deletes expired items asynchronously without consuming write throughput. This provides record-level low-latency retrieval and automated retention handling without the per-object overhead of storing each small record separately in Amazon S3.

**Learn more:** [Using time to live (TTL) in DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/TTL.html) · [DynamoDB quotas and constraints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/ServiceQuotas.html)

A company created an application using AWS Lambda that is deployed in an AWS CloudFormation stack. The most recent production release of the web application introduced an issue that caused an outage lasting several minutes. A solutions architect must modify the deployment process to support a canary release.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an alias for every new deployed version of the Lambda function. Use the AWS CLI update-alias command with the routing-config parameter to distribute the load.
Deploy the application into a new CloudFormation stack. Use an Amazon Route 53 weighted routing policy to distribute the load.
Create a version for every new deployed Lambda function. Use the AWS CLI update-function-configuration command with the routing-config parameter to distribute the load.
Configure AWS CodeDeploy and use CodeDeployDefault.OneAtATime in the Deployment configuration to distribute the load.

questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda aliases can route a weighted percentage of invocations to a second published function version, enabling a canary release while the remaining traffic continues to use the primary version. The AWS CLI `update-alias` command supports the `routing-config` parameter for this weighted version routing.

**Learn more:** [Implement Lambda canary deployments using a weighted alias](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuring-alias-routing.html) · [AWS CLI update-alias command reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cli/latest/reference/lambda/update-alias.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has multiple AWS accounts that are in an organization in AWS Organizations. The company needs to store AWS account activity and query the data from a central location by using SQL.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS CloudTrail trail in each account. Specify CloudTrail management events for the trail. Configure CloudTrail to send the events to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. Configure CloudWatch cross-account observability. Query the data in CloudWatch Logs Insights.

Use a delegated administrator account to create an AWS CloudTrail Lake data store. Specify CloudTrail management events for the data store. Enable the data store for all accounts in the organization. Query the data in CloudTrail Lake.

Use a delegated administrator account to create an AWS CloudTrail trail. Specify CloudTrail management events for the trail. Enable the trail for all accounts in the organization. Keep all other settings as default. Query the CloudTrail data from the CloudTrail event history page.

Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets to deploy AWS CloudTrail Lake data stores in each account. Specify CloudTrail management events for the data stores. Keep all other settings as default. Query the data in CloudTrail Lake.

questions.explanation:
AWS CloudTrail Lake is purpose-built for storing and querying AWS account activity across an organization using SQL. It integrates with AWS Organizations to aggregate events from all accounts through a delegated administrator, and supports full SQL queries on the collected data. This is more centralized and scalable than managing CloudTrail trails in individual accounts and forwarding to CloudWatch Logs.

**Learn more:** [Working with AWS CloudTrail Lake](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-lake.html) · [CloudTrail Lake concepts and terminology](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/cloudtrail-lake-concepts.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a web application that uses Amazon API Gateway, AWS Lambda, and Amazon DynamoDB. A recent marketing campaign has raised demand. Monitoring software reports that many requests have response times that are significantly longer than they were before the marketing campaign.  
  
A solutions architect enabled Amazon CloudWatch Logs for API Gateway and observed errors on 20% of requests. In CloudWatch, the Lambda function **Throttles** metric represents 1% of requests, and the **Errors** metric represents 10% of requests. Application logs show that, when errors occur, a call is made to DynamoDB.  
  
What change should the solutions architect make to improve current response times as the web application grows in popularity?

options.text: Increase the concurrency limit of the Lambda function.
Implement DynamoDB auto scaling on the table.
Increase the API Gateway throttle limit.
Re-create the DynamoDB table with a better-partitioned primary index.

questions.explanation:
DynamoDB auto scaling dynamically adjusts a table’s provisioned read and write throughput in response to workload demand. Increased DynamoDB capacity prevents throughput-related throttling and the resulting Lambda errors and latency when the DynamoDB call is made. The low Lambda throttling rate does not indicate that Lambda concurrency is the primary bottleneck.

**Learn more:** [Managing throughput capacity automatically with DynamoDB auto scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/AutoScaling.html) · [DynamoDB provisioned capacity mode](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/provisioned-capacity-mode.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A startup hosts a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets that use the latest Amazon Linux 2 AMI. The company’s engineers depend heavily on SSH access to the instances for troubleshooting.  
  
The company’s current architecture includes the following:  
  
- A VPC with private and public subnets, plus a NAT gateway.  
- Site-to-Site VPN connectivity to the on-premises environment.  
- EC2 security groups that allow direct SSH access from the on-premises environment.  
  
The company must strengthen security controls for SSH access and provide auditing of commands executed by the engineers.  
  
Which strategy should a solutions architect use?

options.text: Install and configure EC2 Instance Connect on the fleet of EC2 instances. Remove all security group rules attached to EC2 instances that allow inbound TCP on port 22. Advise the engineers to remotely access the instances by using the EC2 Instance Connect CLI.

Update the EC2 security groups to only allow inbound TCP on port 22 to the IP addresses of the engineer’s devices. Install the Amazon CloudWatch agent on all EC2 instances and send operating system audit logs to CloudWatch Logs.

Update the EC2 security groups to only allow inbound TCP on port 22 to the IP addresses of the engineer’s devices. Enable AWS Config for EC2 security group resource changes. Enable AWS Firewall Manager and apply a security group policy that automatically remediates changes to rules.

Create an IAM role with the AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore managed policy attached. Attach the IAM role to all the EC2 instances. Remove all security group rules attached to the EC2 instances that allow inbound TCP on port 22. Have the engineers install the AWS Systems Manager Session Manager plugin for their devices and remotely access the instances by using the start-session API call from Systems Manager.

questions.explanation:
AWS Systems Manager Session Manager gives engineers interactive access to managed EC2 instances through Systems Manager rather than an inbound SSH rule, allowing TCP port 22 access to be removed. Session Manager can record session activity to Amazon S3 or CloudWatch Logs for audit purposes, and the instance role with AmazonSSMManagedInstanceCore enables the Systems Manager managed-node functionality. The Session Manager plugin supports starting a session with the `start-session` API.

**Learn more:** [Configure instance permissions required for Systems Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/setup-instance-permissions.html) · [Start a session](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/session-manager-working-with-sessions-start.html)

The solutions architect must recommend a solution that creates snapshots every 6 hours and retains them for 30 days. The company uses AWS Organizations to manage all its AWS accounts. The company requires a consolidated view of the RDS snapshot health.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?
