A company uses AWS CloudFormation to create all new infrastructure in its AWS member accounts. The resources change infrequently, are correctly sized for the anticipated load, and result in a consistent monthly AWS bill.  
  
At times, a developer creates a resource for testing and forgets to delete it after the test is finished. Most such tests run for a few days before their resources are no longer required.  
  
The company wants to automate the discovery of unused resources. A solutions architect must design a solution that determines whether AWS billing costs are rising. The solution must help identify the resources responsible for a cost increase and must automatically notify the company’s operations team.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Turn on billing alerts. Use AWS Cost Explorer to determine the costs for the past month. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for total estimated charges. Specify a cost threshold that is higher than the costs that Cost Explorer determined. Add a notification to alert the operations team if the alarm threshold is breached.

Turn on billing alerts. Use AWS Cost Explorer to determine the average monthly costs for the past 3 months. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for total estimated charges. Specify a cost threshold that is higher than the costs that Cost Explorer determined. Add a notification to alert the operations team if the alarm threshold is breached.

Use AWS Cost Anomaly Detection to create a cost monitor that has a monitor type of Linked account. Create a subscription to send daily AWS cost summaries to the operations team. Specify a threshold for cost variance.

Use AWS Cost Anomaly Detection to create a cost monitor that has a monitor type of AWS services. Create a subscription to send daily AWS cost summaries to the operations team. Specify a threshold for cost variance.

questions.explanation:
AWS Cost Anomaly Detection uses spending patterns to detect anomalous cost increases and can provide root-cause information by AWS service, account, Region, and usage type. An AWS services monitor evaluates AWS services independently, including newly used services, so it can isolate service-level abnormal spend caused by temporary test resources. A daily-summary alert subscription sends detected anomalies to the operations team when the configured cost-variance threshold is met.

**Learn more:** [Getting started with AWS Cost Anomaly Detection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/getting-started-ad.html) · [Detecting unusual spend with AWS Cost Anomaly Detection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/manage-ad.html)

options.text: Deploy the storage gateway to AWS in file gateway mode. Use Amazon EBS volume encryption using an AWS KMS key to encrypt the storage gateway volumes.
Use Amazon S3 with a bucket policy to enforce HTTPS for connections to the bucket and to enforce server-side encryption and AWS KMS for object encryption.
Use Amazon DynamoDB with SSL to connect to DynamoDB. Use an AWS KMS key to encrypt DynamoDB objects at rest.
Deploy instances with Amazon EBS volumes attached to store this data. Use EBS volume encryption using an AWS KMS key to encrypt the data.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 is a fully managed object storage service designed for highly durable and available document storage. A bucket policy can require HTTPS/TLS for all access and deny uploads that do not use SSE-KMS. Using a customer managed AWS KMS key provides company control of the key and supports configurable automatic key rotation.

A company using AWS Organizations permits developers to experiment on AWS. As part of the landing zone the company deployed, developers use their company email addresses to request an account. The company needs to ensure that developers do not launch costly services or run services unnecessarily. The company must provide developers with a fixed monthly budget to limit AWS costs.  
  
Which combination of steps meets these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create an SCP to set a fixed monthly account usage limit. Apply the SCP to the developer accounts.
Use AWS Budgets to create a fixed monthly budget for each developer’s account as part of the account creation process.
Create an SCP to deny access to costly services and components. Apply the SCP to the developer accounts.
Create an IAM policy to deny access to costly services and components. Apply the IAM policy to the developer accounts.
Create an AWS Budgets alert action to terminate services when the budgeted amount is reached. Configure the action to terminate all services.

Create an AWS Budgets alert action to send an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) notification when the budgeted amount is reached. Invoke an AWS Lambda function to terminate all services.

questions.explanation:
AWS Budgets can establish a recurring fixed monthly cost budget for each developer account. Service control policies (SCPs) provide centrally managed guardrails for accounts in AWS Organizations and can deny access to costly services or components. A budget alert can publish to Amazon SNS, and a Lambda function subscribed to that notification can perform custom termination actions across services. Native AWS Budgets actions can apply IAM policies or SCPs and target specified EC2 or RDS instances; they do not provide a single action to terminate all services.

**Learn more:** [Configuring budget actions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/budgets-controls.html) · [Configuring a budget action](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/budgets-action-configure.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has numerous AWS accounts and uses AWS Organizations to manage them all. A solutions architect must implement a solution that enables the company to share a common network across multiple accounts.  
  
The company’s infrastructure team has a dedicated infrastructure account containing a VPC. The infrastructure team must manage the network from this account. Individual accounts must not be able to manage their own networks. However, individual accounts must be able to create AWS resources in subnets.  
  
Which combination of actions should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create a transit gateway in the infrastructure account.
Enable resource sharing from the AWS Organizations management account.

Create VPCs in each AWS account within the organization in AWS Organizations. Configure the VPCs to share the same CIDR range and subnets as the VPC in the infrastructure account. Peer the VPCs in each individual account with the VPC in the infrastructure account.

Create a resource share in AWS Resource Access Manager in the infrastructure account. Select the specific AWS Organizations OU that will use the shared network. Select each subnet to associate with the resource share.

Create a resource share in AWS Resource Access Manager in the infrastructure account. Select the specific AWS Organizations OU that will use the shared network. Select each prefix list to associate with the resource share.

questions.explanation:
AWS RAM VPC sharing lets the VPC-owning account centrally manage the VPC and share selected subnets with accounts in an AWS Organizations OU. Participant accounts can create, modify, and delete their own application resources in the shared subnets, while network ownership and management remain with the VPC owner. Sharing resources with an OU requires RAM resource sharing to be enabled from the AWS Organizations management account.

**Learn more:** [Share your VPC subnets with other accounts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-sharing.html) · [Sharing your AWS resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ram/latest/userguide/getting-started-sharing.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a web application in the AWS Cloud. The application contains dynamic content generated by a set of Amazon EC2 instances. The EC2 instances run in an Auto Scaling group that is configured as a target group for an Application Load Balancer (ALB).  
  
The company uses an Amazon CloudFront distribution to deliver the application globally. The CloudFront distribution uses the ALB as an origin. The company uses Amazon Route 53 for DNS and has created an A record for `www.example.com` for the CloudFront distribution.  
  
A solutions architect must configure the application to be highly available and fault tolerant.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Provision a full, secondary application deployment in a different AWS Region. Update the Route 53 A record to be a failover record. Add both of the CloudFront distributions as values. Create Route 53 health checks.

Provision an ALB, an Auto Scaling group, and EC2 instances in a different AWS Region. Update the CloudFront distribution, and create a second origin for the new ALCreate an origin group for the two origins. Configure one origin as primary and one origin as secondary.
Provision an Auto Scaling group and EC2 instances in a different AWS Region. Create a second target for the new Auto Scaling group in the ALB. Set up the failover routing algorithm on the ALB.

Provision a full, secondary application deployment in a different AWS Region. Create a second CloudFront distribution, and add the new application setup as an origin. Create an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator. Add both of the CloudFront distributions as endpoints.

questions.explanation:
CloudFront origin failover supports an origin group with a primary and secondary origin. Deploying a separate ALB and Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances in another Region provides an independent secondary origin; CloudFront can automatically route requests to it when the primary origin meets configured failover conditions.

**Learn more:** [Optimize high availability with CloudFront origin failover](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/high_availability_origin_failover.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has created a high performance computing (HPC) cluster in AWS for a tightly coupled workload that produces a large number of shared files stored in Amazon EFS. The cluster performed well with 100 Amazon EC2 instances. However, after the company increased the cluster size to 1.000 EC2 instances, overall performance was far below expectations.  
  
Which set of design choices should a solutions architect make to obtain maximum performance from the HPC cluster? (Choose three.)

options.text: Ensure the HPC cluster is launched within a single Availability Zone.
Launch the EC2 instances and attach elastic network interfaces in multiples of four.
Select EC2 instance types with an Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA) enabled.
Ensure the cluster is launched across multiple Availability Zones.
Replace Amazon EFS with multiple Amazon EBS volumes in a RAID array.
Replace Amazon EFS with Amazon FSx for Lustre.

questions.explanation:
Tightly coupled workloads should run within a single Availability Zone to minimize inter-node latency. Elastic Fabric Adapter (EFA)-enabled EC2 instances provide the low-latency, high-bandwidth networking needed for HPC communication at scale. Amazon FSx for Lustre is a parallel, high-performance shared file system designed for HPC workloads and large numbers of clients, making it better suited than Amazon EFS for this highly concurrent shared-file workload.

**Learn more:** [AWS Well-Architected High Performance Computing Lens — Workload architecture](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/high-performance-computing-lens/workload-architecture.html) · [AWS Well-Architected High Performance Computing Lens — Tightly coupled scenarios](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/wellarchitected/latest/high-performance-computing-lens/tightly-coupled-scenarios.html)

A company plans a one-time migration of an on-premises MySQL database to Amazon Aurora MySQL in the `us-east-1` Region. The company’s existing internet connection has limited bandwidth. The on-premises MySQL database is 60 TB in size. The company estimates that transferring the data to AWS over its current internet connection will take a month. The company needs a migration solution that can migrate the database more quickly.  
  
Which solution will migrate the database in the **LEAST** amount of time?

options.text: Request a 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection between the on-premises data center and AWS. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the on-premises MySQL database to Aurora MySQL.

Use AWS DataSync with the current internet connection to accelerate the data transfer between the on-premises data center and AWS. Use AWS Application Migration Service to migrate the on-premises MySQL database to Aurora MySQL.
Order an AWS Snowball Edge device. Load the data into an Amazon S3 bucket by using the S3 interface. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the data from Amazon S3 to Aurora MySQL.
Order an AWS Snowball device. Load the data into an Amazon S3 bucket by using the S3 Adapter for Snowball. Use AWS Application Migration Service to migrate the data from Amazon S3 to Aurora MySQL.

questions.explanation:
A Snowball Edge device enables the bulk 60 TB dataset to be transferred locally and physically transported to AWS, avoiding the bandwidth-limited internet transfer. Data can be loaded to Amazon S3 through the device’s S3-compatible interface, and AWS DMS supports Amazon S3 as a source and Aurora MySQL as a target. AWS Application Migration Service rehosts servers and is not the appropriate service to load an S3-based database export into Aurora MySQL.

**Learn more:** [Using Amazon S3 as a source for AWS DMS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Source.S3.html) · [Using a MySQL-compatible database as a target for AWS DMS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Target.MySQL.html)

A company runs quick-service restaurants. The restaurants operate on a predictable model with high sales traffic for 4 hours each day. Sales traffic is lower outside these peak hours.  
  
The point-of-sale and management platform is deployed in the AWS Cloud and has a backend based on Amazon DynamoDB. The database table uses provisioned throughput mode with 100,000 RCUs and 80,000 WCUs to meet known peak resource consumption.  
  
The company wants to lower its DynamoDB cost and minimize operational overhead for the IT staff.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements **MOST** cost-effectively?

options.text: Reduce the provisioned RCUs and WCUs.
Change the DynamoDB table to use on-demand capacity.
Enable Dynamo DB auto scaling for the table.
Purchase 1-year reserved capacity that is sufficient to cover the peak load for 4 hours each day.

questions.explanation:
DynamoDB auto scaling dynamically adjusts provisioned read and write capacity in response to traffic patterns. It can scale capacity up for the predictable daily peak and reduce it during lower-traffic periods, so the table does not remain provisioned at peak capacity all day. This preserves the cost advantage of provisioned capacity for predictable workloads while reducing manual capacity-management effort.

**Learn more:** [Managing throughput capacity automatically with DynamoDB auto scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/AutoScaling.html) · [Evaluate your DynamoDB table's capacity mode](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/CostOptimization_TableCapacityMode.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing an application on AWS. The application sends logs to an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster for analysis. All data must remain stored inside a VPC.  
  
Some company developers work from home, while others work from three separate company office locations. The developers must access OpenSearch Service directly from their local development machines to analyze and visualize logs.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure and set up an AWS Client VPN endpoint. Associate the Client VPN endpoint with a subnet in the VPC. Configure a Client VPN self-service portal. Instruct the developers to connect by using the client for Client VPN.
Create a transit gateway, and connect it to the VPC. Create an AWS Site-to-Site VPN. Create an attachment to the transit gateway. Instruct the developers to connect by using an OpenVPN client.

Create a transit gateway, and connect it to the VPOrder an AWS Direct Connect connection. Set up a public VIF on the Direct Connect connection. Associate the public VIF with the transit gateway. Instruct the developers to connect to the Direct Connect connection.

Create and configure a bastion host in a public subnet of the VPC. Configure the bastion host security group to allow SSH access from the company CIDR ranges. Instruct the developers to connect by using SSH.

questions.explanation:
AWS Client VPN is a managed, client-based remote-access VPN service that lets users connect from any location using an OpenVPN-based client. A Client VPN endpoint associated with a subnet in the VPC can give authenticated developers private network access to VPC resources, enabling direct access to a VPC-only OpenSearch Service cluster.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Client VPN?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/clientvpn-admin/what-is.html) · [How AWS Client VPN works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/clientvpn-admin/how-it-works.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company wants to establish a dedicated connection between its on-premises infrastructure and AWS. The company is setting up a 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection to its account VPC. The architecture includes a transit gateway and a Direct Connect gateway to connect multiple VPCs and the on-premises infrastructure.  
  
The company must connect to VPC resources over a transit VIF by using the Direct Connect connection.  
  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Update the 1 Gbps Direct Connect connection to 10 Gbps.
Advertise the on-premises network prefixes over the transit VIF.
Advertise the VPC prefixes from the Direct Connect gateway to the on-premises network over the transit VIF.
Update the Direct Connect connection's MACsec encryption mode attribute to must_encrypt.
Associate a MACsec Connection Key Name/Connectivity Association Key (CKN/CAK) pair with the Direct Connect connection.

questions.explanation:
To establish connectivity over a transit VIF between on-premises and VPC resources, both directions of prefix advertisement are required. Option B enables on-premises network prefixes to be advertised to AWS (allowing AWS resources to route back to on-premises), while Option C enables VPC prefixes to be advertised from the Direct Connect gateway to on-premises systems. MACsec is not applicable at 1 Gbps (requires 10+ Gbps), and the connection speed upgrade is unnecessary.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates hundreds of AWS accounts. It recently introduced a centralized internal process for buying new Reserved Instances and modifying existing Reserved Instances. Under this process, every business unit that wants to purchase or modify Reserved Instances must submit a request to a dedicated procurement team. Previously, business units independently purchased or modified Reserved Instances in their own AWS accounts.

Use AWS Config to report on the attachment of an IAM policy that denies access to the ec2:PurchaseReservedInstancesOffering action and the ec2:ModifyReservedInstances action.

An SCP with explicit denies for `ec2:PurchaseReservedInstancesOffering` and `ec2:ModifyReservedInstances`, attached to every organizational unit, prevents business units from performing those actions even if their IAM policies otherwise allow them. The company has connected the AWS environment to the company’s on-premises data center by using a 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection. The company has configured BGP for this connection.

Add a static AWS Site-to-Site VPN as a secondary path to secure data in transit and to provide resilience for the Direct Connect connection.

A company is using GitHub Actions to run a CI/CD pipeline that accesses resources on AWS. The company has an IAM user that uses a secret key in the pipeline to authenticate to AWS. An existing IAM role with an attached policy grants the required permissions to deploy resources.

Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Create an IAM SAML 2.0 identity provider (IdP) in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). Create a new IAM role with the appropriate trust policy that allows the sts:AssumeRole API call. Attach the existing IAM policy to the new IAM role. Update GitHub to use SAML authentication for the pipeline.

Create an IAM OpenID Connect (OIDC) identity provider (IdP) in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). Create a new IAM role with the appropriate trust policy that allows the sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity API call from the GitHub OIDC IdP. Update GitHub to assume the role for the pipeline.

Create a new IAM role with the appropriate trust policy that allows the sts:AssumeRoleWithWebIdentity API call from the GitHub authentication provider. Create a new IAM role with the appropriate trust policy that allows the sts:AssumeRole API call. Attach the existing IAM policy to the new IAM role. questions.explanation:

options.text: Attach a policy to the S3 bucket to prompt the IAM user for an MFA code when the IAM user performs actions on the S3 bucket. Use IAM access keys with the AWS CLI to call Amazon S3.

Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create an Amazon EventBridge (Amazon CloudWatch Events) rule. Define a pattern with the detail-type value set to AWS API Call via CloudTrail and an eventName of CreateUser.
Configure CloudTrail to send a notification for the CreateUser event to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic.
Invoke a container that runs in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with AWS Fargate technology to remove access.
Invoke an AWS Step Functions state machine to remove access.
Use Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to notify the security team.
Use Amazon Pinpoint to notify the security team.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EventBridge can match AWS CloudTrail events using the `AWS API Call via CloudTrail` detail type and a specific API event name such as `CreateUser`. The rule can invoke a Step Functions state machine, which can orchestrate IAM API calls that remove credentials and permissions from the newly created IAM user. Amazon SNS delivers a published message to subscribed endpoints, making it suitable for notifying the security team.

**Learn more:** [AWS CloudTrail events - Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/ref/events-ref-cloudtrail.html) · [AWS service events delivered via AWS CloudTrail - Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/userguide/eb-service-event-cloudtrail.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The instances belong to an Auto Scaling group. The application experiences unpredictable workloads and scales out and in frequently. The company’s development team wants to analyze application logs to identify ways to improve the application's performance. However, the logs are unavailable after instances scale in.  
  
Which solution will enable the development team to view the application logs after a scale-in event?

options.text: Enable access logs for the ALB. Store the logs in an Amazon S3 bucket.
Configure the EC2 instances to publish logs to Amazon CloudWatch Logs by using the unified CloudWatch agent.
Modify the Auto Scaling group to use a step scaling policy.
Instrument the application with AWS X-Ray tracing.

questions.explanation:
The unified CloudWatch agent collects configured application log files from EC2 instances and publishes them to Amazon CloudWatch Logs. CloudWatch Logs retains the centrally stored log events after an Auto Scaling instance is terminated, allowing the development team to search and analyze them.

**Learn more:** [Collect metrics, logs, and traces using the CloudWatch agent](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/monitoring/Install-CloudWatch-Agent.html) · [Getting started with CloudWatch Logs](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/CWL_GettingStarted.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect must evaluate the application and database portfolio of a newly acquired company and develop a business case for migrating that portfolio to AWS. The acquired company operates applications in an on-premises data center that is poorly documented. The solutions architect cannot initially establish how many applications and databases are present. Application traffic varies, and some applications run as end-of-month batch processes.  
  
The solutions architect needs a better understanding of the portfolio before migration to AWS can start.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS) and AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to evaluate migration. Use AWS Service Catalog to understand application and database dependencies.

Use AWS Application Migration Service. Run agents on the on-premises infrastructure. Manage the agents by using AWS Migration Hub. Use AWS Storage Gateway to assess local storage needs and database dependencies.

Use Migration Evaluator to generate a list of servers. Build a report for a business case. Use AWS Migration Hub to view the portfolio. Use AWS Application Discovery Service to gain an understanding of application dependencies.

Use AWS Control Tower in the destination account to generate an application portfolio. Use AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS) to generate deeper reports and a business case. Use a landing zone for core accounts and resources.

questions.explanation:
Migration Evaluator discovers the server estate, collects utilization data that reflects changing and periodic workloads, and supports creation of a directional AWS migration business case. AWS Application Discovery Service gathers on-premises configuration and network-dependency information, and AWS Migration Hub provides a consolidated view of the discovered application portfolio for migration planning.

**Learn more:** [Discover on-premises resources using AWS Migration Hub discovery tools](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/migrationhub/latest/ug/gs-new-user-discovery.html) · [Migration Evaluator](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/migration-tools/discovery-migration-evaluator.html)

A company operates an environment with a single AWS account. A solutions architect is reviewing the environment to recommend improvements specifically for access to the AWS Management Console. The company’s IT support workers currently perform administrative console tasks by authenticating with named IAM users mapped to their job roles.  
  
The IT support workers no longer want to maintain both Active Directory and IAM user accounts. They want to access the console by using their existing Active Directory credentials. The solutions architect is using AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to implement this functionality.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST** cost-effectively?

options.text: Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Turn on the IAM Identity Center feature in Organizations. Create and configure a directory in AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory (AWS Managed Microsoft AD) with a two-way trust to the company’s on-premises Active Directory. Configure IAM Identity Center and set the AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory as the identity source. Create permission sets and map them to the existing groups within the AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory.

Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Turn on the IAM Identity Center feature in Organizations. Create and configure an AD Connector to connect to the company’s on-premises Active Directory. Configure IAM Identity Center and select the AD Connector as the identity source. Create permission sets and map them to the existing groups within the company’s Active Directory.

Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Turn on all features for the organization. Create and configure a directory in AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory (AWS Managed Microsoft AD) with a two-way trust to the company’s on-premises Active Directory. Configure IAM Identity Center and select the AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory as the identity source. Create permission sets and map them to the existing groups within the AWS Managed Microsoft AD directory.

Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Turn on all features for the organization. Create and configure an AD Connector to connect to the company’s on-premises Active Directory. Configure IAM Identity Center and set the AD Connector as the identity source. Create permission sets and map them to the existing groups within the company’s Active Directory.

questions.explanation:
An IAM Identity Center organization instance requires AWS Organizations with all features enabled. AD Connector forwards authentication requests to the existing self-managed Active Directory and supports using its existing users and groups as the IAM Identity Center identity source. It avoids the additional managed directory deployment and two-way trust required by AWS Managed Microsoft AD, making it the cost-effective choice for a single existing Active Directory domain.

**Learn more:** [IAM Identity Center and AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/singlesignon/latest/userguide/identity-center-and-orgs.html) · [What gets created with your AD Connector](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/create_details_ad_connector.html)

options.text: Store data in Amazon S3. Use Amazon Redshift Spectrum to query data.
Store data in Amazon S3. Use the AWS Glue Data Catalog and Amazon Athena to query data.
Store data in EMR File System (EMRFS). Use Presto in Amazon EMR to query data.
Store data in Amazon Redshift. Use Amazon Redshift to query data.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Athena is a serverless SQL query service for data in Amazon S3, so it removes the always-on Amazon EMR compute cost and charges only for the queries that run. The AWS Glue Data Catalog stores the metadata that Athena uses to query S3 data. This fits an intermittent workload and supports columnar ORC data.

A company operates an IoT application in the AWS Cloud. The company has millions of sensors that gather data from homes in the United States. The sensors use the MQTT protocol to connect to and send data through a custom MQTT broker. The MQTT broker saves the data on one Amazon EC2 instance. The sensors reach the broker by using the domain name `iot.example.com`. The company uses Amazon Route 53 for DNS service. The company stores the data in Amazon DynamoDB.  
  
On several occasions, the data volume has overloaded the MQTT broker, causing sensor data to be lost. The company must increase the solution’s reliability.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and an Auto Scaling group for the MQTT broker. Use the Auto Scaling group as the target for the ALB. Update the DNS record in Route 53 to an alias record. Point the alias record to the ALB. Use the MQTT broker to store the data.

Set up AWS IoT Core to receive the sensor data. Create and configure a custom domain to connect to AWS IoT Core. Update the DNS record in Route 53 to point to the AWS IoT Core Data-ATS endpoint. Configure an AWS IoT rule to store the data.

Create a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Set the MQTT broker as the target. Create an AWS Global Accelerator accelerator. Set the NLB as the endpoint for the accelerator. Update the DNS record in Route 53 to a multivalue answer record. Set the Global Accelerator IP addresses as values. Use the MQTT broker to store the data.

Set up AWS IoT Greengrass to receive the sensor data. Update the DNS record in Route 53 to point to the AWS IoT Greengrass endpoint. Configure an AWS IoT rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function to store the data.

questions.explanation:
AWS IoT Core provides a managed MQTT broker that can ingest data from large device fleets without relying on a single EC2-hosted broker. A customer-managed domain can be configured for an AWS IoT Core data endpoint, with DNS directed to the `iot:Data-ATS` endpoint. An AWS IoT rule can route received MQTT messages directly to an Amazon DynamoDB table.

**Learn more:** [Creating and configuring customer managed domains - AWS IoT Core](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/iot-custom-endpoints-configurable-custom.html) · [DynamoDB - AWS IoT Core](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/dynamodb-rule-action.html)

A software-as-a-service (SaaS) provider makes APIs available through an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The ALB connects to an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster deployed in the us-east-1 Region. The exposed APIs use several non-standard REST methods: LINK, UNLINK, LOCK, and UNLOCK.  
  
Users located outside the United States report long and inconsistent response times for these APIs. A solutions architect must solve this problem with a solution that minimizes operational overhead.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Add an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Configure the ALB as the origin.
Add an Amazon API Gateway edge-optimized API endpoint to expose the APIs. Configure the ALB as the target.
Add an accelerator in AWS Global Accelerator. Configure the ALB as the origin.
Deploy the APIs to two additional AWS Regions: eu-west-1 and ap-southeast-2. Add latency-based routing records in Amazon Route 53.

questions.explanation:
AWS Global Accelerator can use an Application Load Balancer as an endpoint and routes users into the AWS global network at an edge location close to them, providing lower-latency, more consistent paths to the regional application. It operates at the network layer, so the non-standard HTTP methods are not restricted. Amazon CloudFront supports only GET, HEAD, OPTIONS, PUT, PATCH, POST, and DELETE, so it cannot forward the required methods.

**Learn more:** [How AWS Global Accelerator works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/global-accelerator/latest/dg/introduction-how-it-works.html) · [CloudFront AllowedMethods API reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cloudfront/latest/APIReference/API_AllowedMethods.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to migrate its on-premises application to AWS. The application's database contains structured product data and temporary user session data. The company must decouple the product data from the user session data. The company must also implement replication to another AWS Region for disaster recovery.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements with the **HIGHEST** performance?

options.text: Create an Amazon RDS DB instance with separate schemas to host the product data and the user session data. Configure a read replica for the DB instance in another Region.

Create an Amazon RDS DB instance to host the product data. Configure a read replica for the DB instance in another Region. Create a global datastore in Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached to host the user session data.
Create two Amazon DynamoDB global tables. Use one global table to host the product data. Use the other global table to host the user session data. Use DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) for caching.
Create an Amazon RDS DB instance to host the product data. Configure a read replica for the DB instance in another Region. Create an Amazon DynamoDB global table to host the user session data.

questions.explanation:
DynamoDB global tables provide separate, automatically replicated tables in multiple AWS Regions, supporting disaster recovery while keeping product and session data decoupled. DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) is an in-memory cache that reduces eventually consistent read latency from single-digit milliseconds to microseconds, making this the highest-performance option.

**Learn more:** [How DynamoDB global tables work](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/V2globaltables_HowItWorks.html) · [In-memory acceleration with DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is developing a solution that can transition 400 employees to a remote-work environment if an unexpected disaster occurs. User desktops run a mix of Windows and Linux operating systems. Each desktop has several kinds of software installed, including web browsers and mail clients.  
  
A solutions architect must implement a solution that integrates with the company’s on-premises Active Directory so employees can use their existing identity credentials. The solution must provide multifactor authentication (MFA) and reproduce the user experience of the current desktops.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Use Amazon WorkSpaces for the cloud desktop service. Set up a VPN connection to the on-premises network. Create an AD Connector, and connect to the on-premises Active Directory. Activate MFA for Amazon WorkSpaces by using the AWS Management Console.

Use Amazon AppStream 2.0 as an application streaming service. Configure Desktop View for the employees. Set up a VPN connection to the on-premises network. Set up Active Directory Federation Services (AD FS) on premises. Connect the VPC network to AD FS through the VPN connection.

Use Amazon WorkSpaces for the cloud desktop service. Set up a VPN connection to the on-premises network. Create an AD Connector, and connect to the on-premises Active Directory. Configure a RADIUS server for MFA.
Use Amazon AppStream 2.0 as an application streaming service. Set up Active Directory Federation Services on premises. Configure MFA to grant users access on AppStream 2.0.

questions.explanation:
Amazon WorkSpaces provides managed full virtual desktops, including Windows and Linux options, and supports custom images and bundles containing the required operating system, software, and settings. An AD Connector lets users sign in with existing on-premises Active Directory credentials through network connectivity to the on-premises environment. MFA for an AD Connector directory requires a reachable RADIUS server, making a WorkSpaces deployment with an AD Connector, VPN connectivity, and RADIUS-based MFA the complete solution.

**Learn more:** [Manage directories for WorkSpaces Personal](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/workspaces/latest/adminguide/manage-workspaces-directory.html) · [Multi-factor authentication (AD Connector) for WorkSpaces Personal](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/workspaces/latest/adminguide/connect-mfa.html)

A company is migrating an on-premises application and a MySQL database to AWS. The application handles highly sensitive data, and new data is continuously updated in the database. The data must not traverse the internet. The company must also encrypt the data both in transit and at rest.  
  
The database is 5 TB. The company has already created the database schema in an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. The company has configured a 1 Gbps AWS Direct Connect connection to AWS, along with a public VIF and a private VIF. A solutions architect must design a solution to migrate the data to AWS with the least possible downtime.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Perform a database backup. Copy the backup files to an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device. Import the backup to Amazon S3. Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3) for encryption at rest. Use TLS for encryption in transit. Import the data from Amazon S3 to the DB instance.

Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the data to AWS. Create a DMS replication instance in a private subnet. Create VPC endpoints for AWS DMS. Configure a DMS task to copy data from the on-premises database to the DB instance by using full load plus change data capture (CDC). Use the AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) default key for encryption at rest. Use TLS for encryption in transit.

Perform a database backup. Use AWS DataSync to transfer the backup files to Amazon S3. Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3) for encryption at rest. Use TLS for encryption in transit. Import the data from Amazon S3 to the DB instance.

Use Amazon S3 File Gateway. Set up a private connection to Amazon S3 by using AWS PrivateLink. Perform a database backup. Copy the backup files to Amazon S3. Use server-side encryption with Amazon S3 managed encryption keys (SSE-S3) for encryption at rest. Use TLS for encryption in transit. Import the data from Amazon S3 to the DB instance.

questions.explanation:
AWS DMS can perform a full load and then continue change data capture (CDC), which keeps the target synchronized with ongoing source changes and minimizes downtime at cutover. A replication instance in private subnets can use private connectivity to the on-premises source through AWS Direct Connect and the private VIF. AWS DMS supports TLS/SSL for source and target endpoint connections and AWS KMS encryption for replication storage and endpoint connection information.

**Learn more:** [Setting up a network for homogeneous data migrations in AWS DMS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/dm-network.html) · [Data protection in AWS Database Migration Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Security.DataProtection.html)

A company is migrating an application from on-premises infrastructure to the AWS Cloud. During migration-design meetings, the company raised concerns about the availability and recovery options for its legacy Windows file server. The file server holds sensitive, business-critical data that cannot be recreated if data corruption or loss occurs. Compliance requirements state that the data must not traverse the public internet. The company wants to use AWS managed services wherever possible.  
  
The company chooses to store the data in an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. A solutions architect must design a solution to copy the data to another AWS Region for disaster recovery (DR) purposes.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a destination Amazon S3 bucket in the DR Region. Establish connectivity between the FSx for Windows File Server file system in the primary Region and the S3 bucket in the DR Region by using Amazon FSx File Gateway. Configure the S3 bucket as a continuous backup source in FSx File Gateway.

Create an FSx for Windows File Server file system in the DR Region. Establish connectivity between the VPC the primary Region and the VPC in the DR Region by using AWS Site-to-Site VPN. Configure AWS DataSync to communicate by using VPN endpoints.

Create an FSx for Windows File Server file system in the DR Region. Establish connectivity between the VPC in the primary Region and the VPC in the DR Region by using VPC peering. Configure AWS DataSync to communicate by using interface VPC endpoints with AWS PrivateLink.

Create an FSx for Windows File Server file system in the DR Region. Establish connectivity between the VPC in the primary Region and the VPC in the DR Region by using AWS Transit Gateway in each Region. Use AWS Transfer Family to copy files between the FSx for Windows File Server file system in the primary Region and the FSx for Windows File Server file system in the DR Region over the private AWS backbone network.

questions.explanation:
AWS DataSync can replicate data between FSx for Windows File Server file systems, including to a file system in another AWS Region, and can be scheduled for data protection and recovery. A DataSync VPC service endpoint uses AWS PrivateLink to keep DataSync communication private. Inter-Region VPC peering routes traffic by private IP addresses over the AWS global backbone and never traverses the public internet.

**Learn more:** [Protecting your data with Amazon FSx for Windows File Server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/data-protection.html) · [Choosing a service endpoint for your AWS DataSync agent](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/datasync/latest/userguide/choose-service-endpoint.html)

A company’s solutions architect is assessing the costs of a multi-application environment. The environment is deployed across multiple Availability Zones within a single AWS Region. Following a recent acquisition, the company operates two organizations in AWS Organizations. In one organization, the company has created multiple service provider applications as AWS PrivateLink-powered VPC endpoint services. In the other organization, it has created multiple service consumer applications.  
  
Data transfer charges are far higher than the company anticipated, and the solutions architect must lower these costs. The solutions architect must recommend deployment guidelines for developers to follow. The guidelines must minimize data transfer charges across the entire environment.  
  
Which guidelines satisfy these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use AWS Resource Access Manager to share the subnets that host the service provider applications with other accounts in the organization.
Place the service provider applications and the service consumer applications in AWS accounts in the same organization.
Turn off cross-zone load balancing for the Network Load Balancer in all service provider application deployments.
Ensure that service consumer compute resources use the Availability Zone-specific endpoint service by using the endpoint's local DNS name.
Create a Savings Plan that provides adequate coverage for the organization's planned inter-Availability Zone data transfer usage.

questions.explanation:
Network Load Balancer cross-zone load balancing can send traffic from a load balancer node to targets in another Availability Zone, incurring Regional data-transfer charges. Turning it off prevents that cross-zone load-balancer traffic. Interface VPC endpoints provide zonal DNS names; using the zonal endpoint that is local to the consumer compute resource keeps traffic directed to an endpoint network interface in the same Availability Zone, avoiding unnecessary cross-AZ paths.

**Learn more:** [Share your services through AWS PrivateLink](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/privatelink-share-your-services.html) · [Create a service powered by AWS PrivateLink](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/create-endpoint-service.html)

A company has migrated an application to the AWS Cloud. The application runs on two Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB).  
  
Application data is stored in a MySQL database running on an additional EC2 instance. The application's database workload is read-heavy.  
  
The application retrieves static content from Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes attached to each EC2 instance. This static content is updated frequently and must be copied to every EBS volume.  
  
Application load varies throughout the day. At peak times, the application cannot process all incoming requests. Trace data indicates that the database cannot support the read load during those peak times.  
  
Which solution will increase the application's reliability?

options.text: Migrate the application to a set of AWS Lambda functions. Set the Lambda functions as targets for the ALB. Create a new single EBS volume for the static content. Configure the Lambda functions to read from the new EBS volume. Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ DB cluster.

Migrate the application to a set of AWS Step Functions state machines. Set the state machines as targets for the ALCreate an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system for the static content. Configure the state machines to read from the EFS file system. Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora MySQL Serverless v2 with a reader DB instance.

Containerize the application. Migrate the application to an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. Use the AWS Fargate launch type for the tasks that host the application. Create a new single EBS volume for the static content. Mount the new EBS volume on the ECS cluster. Configure AWS Application Auto Scaling on the ECS cluster. Set the ECS service as a target for the ALB. Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ DB cluster.

Containerize the application. Migrate the application to an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. Use the AWS Fargate launch type for the tasks that host the application. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system for the static content. Mount the EFS file system to each container. Configure AWS Application Auto Scaling on the ECS cluster. Set the ECS service as a target for the ALB. Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora MySQL Serverless v2 with a reader DB instance.

questions.explanation:
Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate can run the application as an ALB-targeted service that scales task capacity with Application Auto Scaling. Amazon EFS supplies shared, persistent file storage that all container tasks can mount, eliminating the need to copy frequently updated static content to separate volumes. Aurora MySQL Serverless v2 scales database capacity for variable demand, and its reader DB instance can process read-only queries, reducing pressure on the writer during peaks.

**Learn more:** [Storage options for Amazon ECS tasks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/using_data_volumes.html) · [Using Aurora Serverless](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-serverless-v2.html)

A company offers auction services for artwork and has users throughout North America and Europe. The company hosts its application on Amazon EC2 instances in the `us-east-1` Region. Artists upload large-size, high-resolution photo files of their work from mobile phones to a centralized Amazon S3 bucket that was created in the `us-east-1` Region. European users report slow performance when uploading their images.  
  
How can a solutions architect improve the performance of the image-upload process?

options.text: Redeploy the application to use S3 multipart uploads.
Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution and point to the application as a custom origin.
Configure the buckets to use S3 Transfer Acceleration.
Create an Auto Scaling group for the EC2 instances and create a scaling policy.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration improves uploads from geographically distant clients to a centralized S3 bucket. It uses globally distributed AWS edge locations to receive the upload near the client and routes the data to Amazon S3 over an optimized network path, reducing latency caused by the distance between Europe and `us-east-1`.

**Learn more:** [Configuring fast, secure file transfers using Amazon S3 Transfer Acceleration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/transfer-acceleration.html) · [Performance guidelines for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/optimizing-performance-guidelines.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to migrate an application from VMware Infrastructure running in an on-premises data center to Amazon EC2. A solutions architect must retain the software and configuration settings throughout the migration.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Configure the AWS DataSync agent to start replicating the data store to Amazon FSx for Windows File Server. Use the SMB share to host the VMware data store. Use VM Import/Export to move the VMs to Amazon EC2.

Use the VMware vSphere client to export the application as an image in Open Virtualization Format (OVF) format. Create an Amazon S3 bucket to store the image in the destination AWS Region. Create and apply an IAM role for VM Import. Use the AWS CLI to run the EC2 import command.

Configure AWS Storage Gateway for files service to export a Common Internet File System (CIFS) share. Create a backup copy to the shared folder. Sign in to the AWS Management Console and create an AMI from the backup copy. Launch an EC2 instance that is based on the AMI.

Create a managed-instance activation for a hybrid environment in AWS Systems Manager. Download and install Systems Manager Agent on the on-premises VM. Register the VM with Systems Manager to be a managed instance. Use AWS Backup to create a snapshot of the VM and create an AMI. Launch an EC2 instance that is based on the AMI.

questions.explanation:
AWS VM Import/Export migrates a VMware virtual machine by exporting its virtual-machine image, uploading it to Amazon S3, and importing it into an Amazon Machine Image (AMI) that can be launched on Amazon EC2. This preserves the VM's operating system, installed software, and configuration as part of the image migration.

**Learn more:** [Import your VM as an image - VM Import/Export](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vm-import/latest/userguide/import-vm-image.html) · [Image import overview - VM Import/Export](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vm-import/latest/userguide/image-import.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect has created a web application that uses an Amazon API Gateway Regional endpoint and an AWS Lambda function. All consumers of the web application are located close to the AWS Region in which the application will be deployed. The Lambda function queries only an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. The solutions architect has configured the database with three read replicas.  
  
During testing, the application fails to meet performance requirements. When under high load, the application opens a large number of database connections. The solutions architect must improve the application's performance.  
  
Which actions should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use the cluster endpoint of the Aurora database.
Use RDS Proxy to set up a connection pool to the reader endpoint of the Aurora database.
Use the Lambda Provisioned Concurrency feature.
Move the code for opening the database connection in the Lambda function outside of the event handler.
Change the API Gateway endpoint to an edge-optimized endpoint.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS Proxy pools and reuses database connections, preventing frequent Lambda invocations from overwhelming Aurora with rapidly created connections. A read-only proxy endpoint routes connections through the Aurora reader endpoint, which balances read-only connections across Aurora Replicas. Initializing the database connection outside the Lambda event handler enables warm execution environments to reuse it across invocations, reducing connection setup overhead.

**Learn more:** [Amazon RDS Proxy for Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/rds-proxy.html) · [Best practices for working with AWS Lambda functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/best-practices.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A retail company runs its ecommerce application on AWS. The application runs on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The company uses an Amazon RDS DB instance for the database backend. Amazon CloudFront is configured with one origin that points to the ALB. Static content is cached. Amazon Route 53 hosts all public zones.  
  
After an application update, the ALB intermittently returns a 502 status code (Bad Gateway) error. The cause is malformed HTTP headers returned to the ALB. The webpage loads successfully when a solutions architect immediately reloads it after the error occurs.  
  
While the company works on the issue, the solutions architect must present visitors with a custom error page instead of the standard ALB error page.  
  
Which combination of steps meets this requirement with the **LEAST** operational overhead? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure the S3 bucket to host a static webpage. Upload the custom error pages to Amazon S3.

Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to invoke an AWS Lambda function if the ALB health check response Target.FailedHealthChecks is greater than 0. Configure the Lambda function to modify the forwarding rule at the ALB to point to a publicly accessible web server.
Modify the existing Amazon Route 53 records by adding health checks. Configure a fallback target if the health check fails. Modify DNS records to point to a publicly accessible webpage.

Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to invoke an AWS Lambda function if the ALB health check response Elb.InternalError is greater than 0. Configure the Lambda function to modify the forwarding rule at the ALB to point to a public accessible web server.
Add a custom error response by configuring a CloudFront custom error page. Modify DNS records to point to a publicly accessible web page.

questions.explanation:
CloudFront can return a configured custom error page when its origin returns a 502 response. Hosting that static error content in Amazon S3 keeps it independent of the unhealthy application origin, and configuring a CloudFront custom error response provides the replacement page at the edge. Alarm-driven Lambda changes to ALB forwarding rules and Route 53 DNS failover add operational complexity and do not reliably address intermittent per-request 502 responses.

**Learn more:** [Create a custom error page for specific HTTP status codes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/creating-custom-error-pages.html) · [Custom error pages and error caching](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/DownloadDistValuesErrorPages.html)

A company undergoes regulatory audits of its financial information. External auditors using a single AWS account require access to the company’s AWS account. A solutions architect must grant the auditors secure, read-only access to the company’s AWS account. The solution must follow AWS security best practices.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: In the company's AWS account, create resource policies for all resources in the account to grant access to the auditors' AWS account. Assign a unique external ID to the resource policy.

In the company's AWS account, create an IAM role that trusts the auditors' AWS account. Create an IAM policy that has the required permissions. Attach the policy to the role. Assign a unique external ID to the role's trust policy.
In the company's AWS account, create an IAM user. Attach the required IAM policies to the IAM user. Create API access keys for the IAM user. Share the access keys with the auditors.
In the company's AWS account, create an IAM group that has the required permissions. Create an IAM user in the company's account for each auditor. Add the IAM users to the IAM group.

questions.explanation:
An IAM cross-account role can trust the auditors’ AWS account, grant only the required read-only permissions through its permissions policy, and issue temporary credentials when assumed. Requiring a unique external ID in the role trust policy helps prevent the confused deputy problem for third-party access without sharing long-term credentials.

**Learn more:** [Access to AWS accounts owned by third parties](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/id_roles_common-scenarios_third-party.html) · [Cross account resource access in IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies-cross-account-resource-access.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],Accompany is deploying a new cluster on AWS for big data analytics. The cluster will run on many Linux Amazon EC2 instances distributed across multiple Availability Zones.  
  
Every cluster node must have read and write access to shared underlying file storage. The file storage must be highly available, resilient, compatible with the Portable Operating System Interface (POSIX), and able to support high throughput levels.  
  
Which storage solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Provision an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway NFS file share that is attached to an Amazon S3 bucket. Mount the NFS file share on each EC2 instance in the cluster.
Provision a new Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system that uses General Purpose performance mode. Mount the EFS file system on each EC2 instance in the cluster.
Provision a new Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume that uses the io2 volume type. Attach the EBS volume to all of the EC2 instances in the cluster.
Provision a new Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system that uses Max I/O performance mode. Mount the EFS file system on each EC2 instance in the cluster.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EFS is a managed, POSIX-compatible shared file system that can be mounted by multiple Linux EC2 instances. A Regional EFS file system stores data redundantly across multiple Availability Zones for availability and resilience. Max I/O performance mode is designed for highly parallelized workloads and can scale to higher aggregate throughput and operations per second, making it appropriate for a large big-data analytics cluster.

**Learn more:** [Amazon EFS performance specifications](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/performance.html) · [Features of Amazon EFS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/features.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company stores and manages documents in an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. The file system is encrypted using an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. The file system is mounted on an Amazon EC2 instance that runs proprietary software.  
  
The company has enabled automatic backups for the file system. The automatic backups use the AWS Backup default backup plan.  
  
A solutions architect must ensure that deleted documents are recoverable within an RPO of 100 minutes.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a new IAM role. Create a new backup plan. Use the new IAM role to create backups. Update the KMS key policy to allow the new IAM role to use the key. Implement an hourly backup schedule for the file system.

Create a new backup plan. Update the KMS key policy to allow the AWSServiceRoleForBackup IAM role to use the key. Implement a custom cron expression to run a backup of the file system every 30 minutes.
Create a new IAM role. Use the existing backup plan. Update the KMS key policy to allow the new IAM role to use the key. Enable continuous backups for point-in-time recovery.
Use the existing backup plan. Update the KMS key policy to allow the AWSServiceRoleForBackup IAM role to use the key. Enable Cross-Region Replication for the file system.

questions.explanation:
The AWS Backup default plan for Amazon EFS creates daily backups, so it cannot satisfy a 100-minute recovery point objective. AWS Backup supports scheduled snapshot backups as frequently as hourly, making an hourly EFS backup schedule sufficient. The backup role must be permitted by the AWS KMS key policy to use the encryption key. Amazon EFS does not support AWS Backup continuous backups for point-in-time recovery, and AWS Backup cron schedules cannot run snapshot backups every 30 minutes.

**Learn more:** [Backing up EFS file systems](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/efs/latest/ug/awsbackup.html) · [Backup plan options and configuration](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/plan-options-and-configuration.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has deployed its database on an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance in the `us-east-1` Region. The company must make its data available to customers in Europe. European customers must access the same data as customers in the United States (US) and cannot tolerate high application latency or stale data. Customers in both Europe and the US must write to the database, and each group must see the other group’s updates in real time.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon Aurora MySQL replica of the RDS for MySQL DB instance. Pause application writes to the RDS DB instance. Promote the Aurora Replica to a standalone DB cluster. Reconfigure the application to use the Aurora database and resume writes. Add eu-west-1 as a secondary Region to the DB cluster. Enable write forwarding on the DB cluster. Deploy the application in eu-west-1. Configure the application to use the Aurora MySQL endpoint in eu-west-1.

Add a cross-Region replica in eu-west-1 for the RDS for MySQL DB instance. Configure the replica to replicate write queries back to the primary DB instance. Deploy the application in eu-west-1. Configure the application to use the RDS for MySQL endpoint in eu-west-1.

Copy the most recent snapshot from the RDS for MySQL DB instance to eu-west-1. Create a new RDS for MySQL DB instance in eu-west-1 from the snapshot. Configure MySQL logical replication from us-east-1 to eu-west-1. Enable write forwarding on the DB cluster. Deploy the application in eu-wes&1. Configure the application to use the RDS for MySQL endpoint in eu-west-1.

Convert the RDS for MySQL DB instance to an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster. Add eu-west-1 as a secondary Region to the DB cluster. Enable write forwarding on the DB cluster. Deploy the application in eu-west-1. Configure the application to use the Aurora MySQL endpoint in eu-west-1.

questions.explanation:
An Aurora MySQL Global Database can use a secondary cluster in `eu-west-1` for low-latency local access. With global write forwarding enabled, SQL write operations sent to that secondary cluster are forwarded to the primary cluster, which remains the single source of truth and replicates the resulting changes to secondary Regions. An RDS for MySQL DB instance can be migrated to Aurora MySQL by creating an Aurora read replica and promoting it to a standalone DB cluster after replication lag reaches zero.

**Learn more:** [Migrating data from RDS for MySQL to Aurora MySQL using an Aurora read replica](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/AuroraMySQL.Migrating.RDSMySQL.Replica.html) · [Using write forwarding in an Aurora MySQL global database](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database-write-forwarding-ams.html)

A company uses multiple AWS accounts, with multiple DevOps teams operating production and non-production workloads in those accounts. The company wants to centrally restrict access to certain AWS services that the DevOps teams do not use. The company chose AWS Organizations and successfully invited all AWS accounts into the organization. It wants to allow access to services currently in use while denying a few specific services. It also wants to manage multiple accounts together as one unit.  
  
What combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Use a Deny list strategy.
Review the Access Advisor in AWS IAM to determine services recently used
Review the AWS Trusted Advisor report to determine services recently used.
Remove the default FullAWSAccess SCP.
Define organizational units (OUs) and place the member accounts in the OUs.
Remove the default DenyAWSAccess SCP.

questions.explanation:
A deny-list service control policy (SCP) leaves AWS services available through the default `FullAWSAccess` SCP while explicitly denying the few services that must be restricted. IAM service-last-accessed data, available through Access Advisor, identifies services used by accounts and can be used to refine SCPs. Organizational units group member accounts so policies and administration can be applied collectively. Detaching `FullAWSAccess` without replacing it with appropriate allow policies would block actions, so it should remain in place for this strategy.

**Learn more:** [SCP evaluation - AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps_evaluation.html) · [View last accessed information for AWS Organizations - IAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies_last-accessed-view-data-orgs.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company hosts an application that uses several Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB). During the initial startup of the EC2 instances, the EC2 instances run user data scripts to download critical content for the application from an Amazon S3 bucket.  
  
The EC2 instances are launching correctly. However, after a period of time, the EC2 instances are terminated with the following error message: “An instance was taken out of service in response to an ELB system health check failure.” EC2 instances continue to launch and be terminated because of Auto Scaling events in an endless loop.  
  
The only recent change to the deployment is that the company added a large amount of critical content to the S3 bucket. The company does not want to alter the user data scripts in production.  
  
What should a solutions architect do so that the production environment can deploy successfully?

options.text: Increase the size of the EC2 instances.
Increase the health check timeout for the ALB.
Change the health check path for the ALB.
Increase the health check grace period for the Auto Scaling group.

questions.explanation:
The Auto Scaling health check grace period allows new instances to complete their initialization without failing health checks. Since instances are downloading large amounts of content during startup via user data scripts, increasing this grace period provides sufficient time for that process before the ALB begins health checks. Simply increasing the ALB timeout (option B) would not resolve the issue because the instance fails the health check before it's ready to respond.

**Learn more:** [Set the health check grace period for an Auto Scaling group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/health-check-grace-period.html) · [Health checks for instances in an Auto Scaling group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-health-checks.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company must aggregate Amazon CloudWatch logs from its AWS accounts into a single central logging account. The collected logs must stay in the AWS Region in which they were created. The central logging account will process the logs, normalize them into a standard output format, and stream the output logs to a security tool for additional processing.  
  
A solutions architect must design a solution that can accommodate a large volume of logging data to ingest. Logging activity will be lower outside normal business hours than during normal business hours. The logging solution must scale for the expected load. The solutions architect has chosen an AWS Control Tower design to manage the multi-account logging process.  
  
Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create a destination Amazon Kinesis data stream in the central logging account.
Create a destination Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue in the central logging account.

Create an IAM role that grants Amazon CloudWatch Logs the permission to add data to the Amazon Kinesis data stream. Create a trust policy. Specify the trust policy in the IAM role. In each member account, create a subscription filter for each log group to send data to the Kinesis data stream.

Create an IAM role that grants Amazon CloudWatch Logs the permission to add data to the Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Create a trust policy. Specify the trust policy in the IAM role. In each member account, create a single subscription filter for all log groups to send data to the SQS queue.
Create an AWS Lambda function. Program the Lambda function to normalize the logs in the central logging account and to write the logs to the security tool.
Create an AWS Lambda function. Program the Lambda function to normalize the logs in the member accounts and to write the logs to the security tool.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams provides a scalable destination for variable, high-volume log ingestion, including an on-demand capacity mode that accommodates changing workloads. CloudWatch Logs needs an IAM role that it can assume to deliver subscription events to the Kinesis stream, and cross-account log subscriptions are configured for the sending accounts’ log groups. A Lambda function in the central logging account can consume the centralized stream, normalize the records, and forward them to the security tool. Amazon SQS is not a supported CloudWatch Logs subscription-filter destination.

**Learn more:** [Cross-account cross-Region log data sharing using Amazon Kinesis Data Streams](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/CrossAccountSubscriptions-Kinesis.html) · [Log group-level subscription filters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudWatch/latest/logs/SubscriptionFilters.html)

Which combination of actions should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Purchase AWS Business Support or AWS Enterprise Support for the account.
Turn on AWS Trusted Advisor and review any “Low Utilization Amazon EC2 Instances” recommendations.
Install the Amazon CloudWatch agent and configure memory metric collection on the EC2 instances.
Configure AWS Compute Optimizer in the AWS account to receive findings and optimization recommendations.
Create an EC2 Instance Savings Plan for the AWS Regions, instance families, and operating systems of interest.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company with multiple business units uses AWS Organizations with all features enabled. It has implemented an account structure where each business unit has a separate AWS account. Administrators in every AWS account must be able to use Amazon Athena to view detailed cost and utilization data for their own account.  
  
Each business unit may access only its own cost and utilization data. IAM policies governing the ability to configure AWS Cost and Usage Reports are already in place. A central Cost and Usage Report containing data for the entire organization is already available in an Amazon S3 bucket.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational complexity?

options.text: In the organization's management account, use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the Cost and Usage Report data with each member account.

In the organization's management account, configure an S3 event to invoke an AWS Lambda function each time a new file arrives in the S3 bucket that contains the central Cost and Usage Report. Configure the Lambda function to extract each member account’s data and to place the data in Amazon S3 under a separate prefix. Modify the S3 bucket policy to allow each member account to access its own prefix.

In each member account, access AWS Cost Explorer. Create a new report that contains relevant cost information for the account. Save the report in Cost Explorer. Provide instructions that the account administrators can use to access the saved report.
In each member account, create a new S3 bucket to store Cost and Usage Report data. Set up a Cost and Usage Report to deliver the data to the new S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
In AWS Organizations, a member account that has permission to create a Cost and Usage Report can create a report containing only that member account’s cost and usage data. The report creator must own the destination S3 bucket, and the report can be configured for Amazon Athena integration. Separate member-account reports and buckets therefore provide both isolation and Athena-queryable detail without maintaining Lambda-based report partitioning.

**Learn more:** [Using Cost and Usage Reports for AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cur/latest/userguide/cur-consolidated-billing.html) · [Querying Cost and Usage Reports using Amazon Athena](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cur/latest/userguide/cur-query-athena.html)
