A company operates a microservice as an AWS Lambda function. The microservice writes data to an on-premises SQL database that permits only a limited number of concurrent connections. If Lambda function invocations become too numerous, the database crashes, causing application downtime. The company has an AWS Direct Connect connection between the company’s VPC and the on-premises data center. The company needs to safeguard the database from crashes.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Write the data to an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue. Configure the Lambda function to read from the queue and write to the existing database. Set a reserved concurrency limit on the Lambda function that is less than the number of connections that the database supports.
Create a new Amazon Aurora Serverless DB cluster. Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data from the existing database to Aurora Serverless. Reconfigure the Lambda function to write to Aurora.
Create an Amazon RDS Proxy DB instance. Attach the RDS Proxy DB instance to the Amazon RDS DB instance. Reconfigure the Lambda function to write to the RDS Proxy DB instance.

Write the data to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. Invoke the Lambda function to write to the existing database when the topic receives new messages. Configure provisioned concurrency for the Lambda function to be equal to the number of connections that the database supports.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SQS buffers incoming write requests so that they can be processed asynchronously. Reserved concurrency sets an upper bound on concurrent Lambda executions, allowing the database-writing function to be limited to fewer simultaneous connections than the database supports. AWS documents reserved concurrency as a way to prevent Lambda from overwhelming downstream resources such as database connections.

**Learn more:** [Configuring reserved concurrency for a function](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-concurrency.html) · [Creating and configuring an Amazon SQS event source mapping](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-configure.html)

The company must not expose credentials in application code and must rotate passwords automatically.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Store the database credentials for both environments in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store. Encrypt the credentials by using an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. Within the application code of the Lambda functions, pull the credentials from the Parameter Store parameter by using the AWS SDK for Python (Boto3). Store the database credentials for both environments in AWS Secrets Manager with distinct key entry for the QA environment and the production environment. Turn on rotation. Provide a reference to the Secrets Manager key as an environment variable for the Lambda functions.

Create separate S3 buckets for the QA environment and the production environment. Turn on server-side encryption with AWS KMS keys (SSE-KMS) for the S3 buckets. Use an object naming pattern that gives each Lambda function’s application code the ability to pull the correct credentials for the function's corresponding environment. Grant each Lambda function's execution role access to Amazon S3.

A Lambda function can receive a reference to the relevant secret rather than a hard-coded credential value, allowing it to retrieve the current rotated password at runtime.

A company is running a serverless ecommerce application on AWS. The application uses Amazon API Gateway to invoke AWS Lambda Java functions. The Lambda functions connect to an Amazon RDS for MySQL database to store data.  
  
During a recent sale event, a sudden increase in web traffic resulted in poor API performance and database connection failures. The company needs to implement a solution to minimize the latency for the Lambda functions and to support bursts in traffic.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST amount of change to the application?

options.text: Update the code of the Lambda functions so that the Lambda functions open the database connection outside of the function handler. Increase the provisioned concurrency for the Lambda functions.

Create an RDS Proxy endpoint for the database. Store database secrets in AWS Secrets Manager. Set up the required IAM permissions. Update the Lambda functions to connect to the RDS Proxy endpoint. Increase the provisioned concurrency for the Lambda functions.

Create a custom parameter group. Increase the value of the max_connections parameter. Associate the custom parameter group with the RDS DB instance and schedule a reboot. Increase the reserved concurrency for the Lambda functions.

Create an RDS Proxy endpoint for the database. Store database secrets in AWS Secrets Manager. Set up the required IAM permissions. Update the Lambda functions to connect to the RDS Proxy endpoint. Increase the reserved concurrency for the Lambda functions.

questions.explanation:
An RDS Proxy pools and multiplexes database connections, which stops the flood of new Lambda-driven connections from overwhelming MySQL during traffic bursts. Increasing provisioned concurrency keeps a set number of execution environments pre-initialized so functions respond immediately when demand spikes, directly minimizing latency. Reserved concurrency only caps or guarantees a concurrency allocation; it does not pre-warm execution environments, so it does not reduce cold-start latency the way provisioned concurrency does.

**Learn more:** [Using Amazon RDS Proxy for Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-rds-proxy.html) · [Managing Lambda reserved concurrency and provisioned concurrency](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-concurrency.html)

Deploy an Amazon FSx File Gateway. Configure an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server Multi-AZ file system that uses SSD storage.

Deploy an Amazon S3 File Gateway. Configure the S3 File Gateway to use Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) for the metadata files and to use S3 Glacier Deep Archive for the image files.
Deploy an Amazon S3 File Gateway. Configure the S3 File Gateway to use Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) for the metadata files and image files.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 File Gateway provides SMB access to data stored in Amazon S3. Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access is intended for long-lived, infrequently accessed data and provides millisecond access, satisfying the five-minute availability requirement for both file types. S3 Glacier Deep Archive is unsuitable because archived objects require restoration and retrieval can take hours.

A company is deploying a new application on AWS. The application consists of an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster and an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. The EKS cluster has an AWS managed node group.  
  
The company's security guidelines state that all resources on AWS must be continuously scanned for security vulnerabilities.  
  
Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Activate AWS Security Hub. Configure Security Hub to scan the EKS nodes and the ECR repository.
Activate Amazon Inspector to scan the EKS nodes and the ECR repository.

Launch a new Amazon EC2 instance and install a vulnerability scanning tool from AWS Marketplace. Configure the EC2 instance to scan the EKS nodes. Configure Amazon ECR to perform a basic scan on push.
Install the Amazon CloudWatch agent on the EKS nodes. Configure the CloudWatch agent to scan continuously. Configure Amazon ECR to perform a basic scan on push.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Inspector is the native AWS service for continuous vulnerability scanning of EC2 instances and container images (ECR). It automatically scans both EKS nodes and images in the repository without additional configuration. Security Hub is a findings aggregator (not a scanner), manual tools require ongoing management, and CloudWatch doesn't perform vulnerability scanning. Inspector provides the least operational overhead while meeting the continuous scanning requirement.

**Learn more:** [Amazon Inspector ECR scanning](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/inspector/latest/user/scanning-ecr.html) · [Amazon Inspector EC2 scanning](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/inspector/latest/user/scanning-ec2.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances in the AWS Cloud. The application uses a MongoDB database with a replica set for its data tier. The MongoDB database is installed on systems in the company’s on-premises data center and can be accessed through an AWS Direct Connect connection to the data center environment.  
  
A solutions architect must migrate the on-premises MongoDB database to Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility).  
  
Which strategy should the solutions architect use to perform this migration?

options.text: Create a fleet of EC2 instances. Install MongoDB Community Edition on the EC2 instances, and create a database. Configure continuous synchronous replication with the database that is running in the on-premises data center.

Create an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) replication instance. Create a source endpoint for the on-premises MongoDB database by using change data capture (CDC). Create a target endpoint for the Amazon DocumentDB database. Create and run a DMS migration task.

Create a data migration pipeline by using AWS Data Pipeline. Define data nodes for the on-premises MongoDB database and the Amazon DocumentDB database. Create a scheduled task to run the data pipeline.

Create a source endpoint for the on-premises MongoDB database by using AWS Glue crawlers. Configure continuous asynchronous replication between the MongoDB database and the Amazon DocumentDB database.

questions.explanation:
AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) supports migration from a self-managed or on-premises MongoDB source to an Amazon DocumentDB target. A replication instance, MongoDB source endpoint, Amazon DocumentDB target endpoint, and DMS migration task enable the initial load and change data capture (CDC) of ongoing source changes for a low-downtime cutover.

**Learn more:** [Migrating from MongoDB to Amazon DocumentDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/sbs/chap-mongodb2documentdb.html) · [Using Amazon DocumentDB as a target for AWS Database Migration Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Target.DocumentDB.html)

The company has deployed that Docker image as an AWS Fargate service in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). An Application Load Balancer (ALB) routes traffic to the application.  
  
The company must allow only a specified list of users to access the application from the internet. The company cannot modify the application or integrate it with an identity provider. Every user must authenticate by using multi-factor authentication (MFA).  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a user pool in Amazon Cognito. Configure the pool for the application. Populate the pool with the required users. Configure the pool to require MFConfigure a listener rule on the ALB to require authentication through the Amazon Cognito hosted UI.

Configure the users in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). Attach a resource policy to the Fargate service to require users to use MFA. Configure a listener rule on the ALB to require authentication through IAM.

Configure the users in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). Enable AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On). Configure resource protection for the ALB. Create a resource protection rule to require users to use MFA.

Create a user pool in AWS Amplify. Configure the pool for the application. Populate the pool with the required users. Configure the pool to require MFA. Configure a listener rule on the ALB to require authentication through the Amplify hosted UI.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Cognito user pools provide a managed user directory in which the approved users can be created and MFA can be required. An Application Load Balancer listener can use an `authenticate-cognito` action to redirect users to the Cognito hosted/managed login flow and allow requests to reach the target only after successful authentication. This protects the application without modifying it or integrating it with a separate identity provider.

**Learn more:** [Authenticate users using an Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/listener-authenticate-users.html) · [Using Amazon Cognito user pools security features](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/managing-security.html)

A company is developing a serverless application that runs on an AWS Lambda function connected to a VPC. The company must integrate the application with a new service from an external provider. The external provider supports only requests originating from public IPv4 addresses included in an allow list.  
  
Before the application can use the new service, the company must give the external provider one public IP address.  
  
Which solution will enable the application to access the new service?

options.text: Deploy a NAT gateway. Associate an Elastic IP address with the NAT gateway. Configure the VPC to use the NAT gateway.

Deploy an egress-only internet gateway. Associate an Elastic IP address with the egress-only internet gateway. Configure the elastic network interface on the Lambda function to use the egress-only internet gateway.
Deploy an internet gateway. Associate an Elastic IP address with the internet gateway. Configure the Lambda function to use the internet gateway.
Deploy an internet gateway. Associate an Elastic IP address with the internet gateway. Configure the default route in the public VPC route table to use the internet gateway.

questions.explanation:
A public NAT gateway with an Elastic IP provides a stable public IPv4 source address for outbound traffic from private VPC subnets. The Lambda function’s outbound traffic can be routed through that NAT gateway, allowing the external provider to allow-list the NAT gateway’s Elastic IP. AWS notes that VPC-connected Lambda functions in private subnets access the internet through a NAT gateway, and that the gateway can be assigned an Elastic IP.

**Learn more:** [Enable internet access for VPC-connected Lambda functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/configuration-vpc-internet.html) · [NAT gateways](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/vpc-nat-gateway.html)

40:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company needs to design a disaster recovery (DR) solution for an application that runs in the company’s data center. The application writes to an SMB file share and makes a copy to a second file share. Both file shares reside in the data center. The application uses two file types: metadata files and image files."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"The company wants to store the copy in AWS. It needs to be able to use SMB to access the data from either the data center or AWS if a disaster occurs. The data copy is rarely accessed but must be available within 5 minutes."}],"
",["$","$L58",null,{"choices":{"A":"Deploy AWS Outposts with Amazon S3 storage. Configure a Windows Amazon EC2 instance on Outposts as a file server.","B":"Deploy an Amazon FSx File Gateway. Configure an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server Multi-AZ file system that uses SSD storage.","C":"Deploy an Amazon S3 File Gateway. Configure the S3 File Gateway to use Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) for the metadata files and to use S3 Glacier Deep Archive for the image files.","D":"Deploy an Amazon S3 File Gateway. Configure the S3 File Gateway to use Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) for the metadata files and image files."},"correctAnswer":"D","explanation":"Amazon S3 File Gateway provides SMB access to data stored in Amazon S3. Amazon S3 Standard-Infrequent Access is intended for long-lived, infrequently accessed data and provides millisecond access, satisfying the five-minute availability requirement for both file types. S3 Glacier Deep Archive is unsuitable because archived objects require restoration and retrieval can take hours.

**Learn more:** [Using storage classes - AWS Storage Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/storage-classes.html) · [Understanding and managing Amazon S3 storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"044d6c35-f1b0-43c6-b393-485a48a5c576","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02","mode":"default"}}]]
54:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company is deploying a new application on AWS. The application consists of an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster and an Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. The EKS cluster has an AWS managed node group."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"The company's security guidelines state that all resources on AWS must be continuously scanned for security vulnerabilities."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST operational overhead?"}],"
",["$","$L58",null,{"choices":{"A":"Activate AWS Security Hub. Configure Security Hub to scan the EKS nodes and the ECR repository.","B":"Activate Amazon Inspector to scan the EKS nodes and the ECR repository.","C":"Launch a new Amazon EC2 instance and install a vulnerability scanning tool from AWS Marketplace. Configure the EC2 instance to scan the EKS nodes. Configure Amazon ECR to perform a basic scan on push.","D":"Install the Amazon CloudWatch agent on the EKS nodes. Configure the CloudWatch agent to scan continuously. Configure Amazon ECR to perform a basic scan on push."},"correctAnswer":"B","explanation":"Amazon Inspector is the native AWS service for continuous vulnerability scanning of EC2 instances and container images (ECR). It automatically scans both EKS nodes and images in the repository without additional configuration. Security Hub is a findings aggregator (not a scanner), manual tools require ongoing management, and CloudWatch doesn't perform vulnerability scanning. Inspector provides the least operational overhead while meeting the continuous scanning requirement.

**Learn more:** [Amazon Inspector ECR scanning](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/inspector/latest/user/scanning-ecr.html) · [Amazon Inspector EC2 scanning](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/inspector/latest/user/scanning-ec2.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"50dd22a7-68cb-4d09-b1d2-696c9bb5bc2d","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02","mode":"default"}}]]
55:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company runs an application on Amazon EC2 instances in the AWS Cloud. The application uses a MongoDB database with a replica set for its data tier. The MongoDB database is installed on systems in the company’s on-premises data center and can be accessed through an AWS Direct Connect connection to the data center environment."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"A solutions architect must migrate the on-premises MongoDB database to Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility)."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which strategy should the solutions architect use to perform this migration?"}],"
",["$","$L58",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create a fleet of EC2 instances. Install MongoDB Community Edition on the EC2 instances, and create a database. Configure continuous synchronous replication with the database that is running in the on-premises data center.","B":"Create an AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) replication instance. Create a source endpoint for the on-premises MongoDB database by using change data capture (CDC). Create a target endpoint for the Amazon DocumentDB database. Create and run a DMS migration task.","C":"Create a data migration pipeline by using AWS Data Pipeline. Define data nodes for the on-premises MongoDB database and the Amazon DocumentDB database. Create a scheduled task to run the data pipeline.","D":"Create a source endpoint for the on-premises MongoDB database by using AWS Glue crawlers. Configure continuous asynchronous replication between the MongoDB database and the Amazon DocumentDB database."},"correctAnswer":"B","explanation":"AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) supports migration from a self-managed or on-premises MongoDB source to an Amazon DocumentDB target. A replication instance, MongoDB source endpoint, Amazon DocumentDB target endpoint, and DMS migration task enable the initial load and change data capture (CDC) of ongoing source changes for a low-downtime cutover.

**Learn more:** [Migrating from MongoDB to Amazon DocumentDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/sbs/chap-mongodb2documentdb.html) · [Using Amazon DocumentDB as a target for AWS Database Migration Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Target.DocumentDB.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"9afe4aa8-6f73-4799-b9e1-6d30b3bd01ba","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02","mode":"default"}}]]
56:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company is rolling out a third-party web application on AWS. The application is packaged as a Docker image. The company has deployed that Docker image as an AWS Fargate service in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). An Application Load Balancer (ALB) routes traffic to the application."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"The company must allow only a specified list of users to access the application from the internet. The company cannot modify the application or integrate it with an identity provider. Every user must authenticate by using multi-factor authentication (MFA)."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution meets these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L58",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create a user pool in Amazon Cognito. Configure the pool for the application. Populate the pool with the required users. Configure the pool to require MFConfigure a listener rule on the ALB to require authentication through the Amazon Cognito hosted UI.","B":"Configure the users in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). Attach a resource policy to the Fargate service to require users to use MFA. Configure a listener rule on the ALB to require authentication through IAM.","C":"Configure the users in AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM). Enable AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On). Configure resource protection for the ALB. Create a resource protection rule to require users to use MFA.","D":"Create a user pool in AWS Amplify. Configure the pool for the application. Populate the pool with the required users. Configure the pool to require MFA. Configure a listener rule on the ALB to require authentication through the Amplify hosted UI."},"correctAnswer":"A","explanation":"Amazon Cognito user pools provide a managed user directory in which the approved users can be created and MFA can be required. An Application Load Balancer listener can use an `authenticate-cognito` action to redirect users to the Cognito hosted/managed login flow and allow requests to reach the target only after successful authentication. This protects the application without modifying it or integrating it with a separate identity provider.

**Learn more:** [Authenticate users using an Application Load Balancer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/listener-authenticate-users.html) · [Using Amazon Cognito user pools security features](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cognito/latest/developerguide/managing-security.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"a1d5ede6-c921-428b-95fb-cff4e879ddfb","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02","mode":"default"}}]]

",["$","p",null,{"children":"Before the application can use the new service, the company must give the external provider one public IP address."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution will enable the application to access the new service?"}],"

A company plans to revise its internal cloud billing strategy for every business unit. At present, the cloud governance team provides each business-unit head with reports of total cloud spend. The company uses AWS Organizations to manage separate AWS accounts for each business unit. The current Organizations tagging standard includes application, environment, and owner. The cloud governance team needs a centralized solution that gives each business unit monthly reports of its cloud spending. The solution must also send notifications when cloud spending exceeds a defined threshold.  
  
Which solution is the **MOST cost-effective** way to meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure AWS Budgets in each account and configure budget alerts that are grouped by application, environment, and owner. Add each business unit to an Amazon SNS topic for each alert. Use Cost Explorer in each account to create monthly reports for each business unit.

Configure AWS Budgets in the organization's management account and configure budget alerts that are grouped by application, environment, and owner. Add each business unit to an Amazon SNS topic for each alert. Use Cost Explorer in the organization's management account to create monthly reports for each business unit.

Configure AWS Budgets in each account and configure budget alerts that are grouped by application, environment, and owner. Add each business unit to an Amazon SNS topic for each alert. Use the AWS Billing and Cost Management dashboard in each account to create monthly reports for each business unit.

Enable AWS Cost and Usage Reports in the organization's management account and configure reports grouped by application, environment. and owner. Create an AWS Lambda function that processes AWS Cost and Usage Reports, sends budget alerts, and sends monthly reports to each business unit's email list.

questions.explanation:
The AWS Organizations management account has visibility into consolidated costs for all member accounts, making it the appropriate central location for cost reporting across business units. AWS Budgets supports cost budgets filtered by activated cost-allocation tags and can send threshold notifications to Amazon SNS. Cost Explorer supports organization-wide cost analysis from the management account, while cost-allocation tags can be used to filter and categorize the spending. Using these managed services avoids the custom Lambda processing required for Cost and Usage Reports.

**Learn more:** [Controlling access to Cost Explorer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/ce-access.html) · [Budget filters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/budgets-create-filters.html)

A software as a service (SaaS) company uses AWS to host a service powered by AWS PrivateLink. The service comprises proprietary software running on three Amazon EC2 instances behind a Network Load Balancer (NLB). The instances are located in private subnets across multiple Availability Zones in the eu-west-2 Region. All of the company’s customers are in eu-west-2.  
  
However, the company has now acquired a new customer in the us-east-1 Region. The company creates a new VPC and new subnets in us-east-1. The company establishes inter-Region VPC peering between the VPCs in the two Regions.  
  
The company needs to provide the new customer access to the SaaS service, but it does not want to deploy new EC2 resources in us-east-1 immediately.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure a PrivateLink endpoint service in us-east-1 to use the existing NLB that is in eu-west-2. Grant specific AWS accounts access to connect to the SaaS service.

Create an NLB in us-east-1. Create an IP target group that uses the IP addresses of the company's instances in eu-west-2 that host the SaaS service. Configure a PrivateLink endpoint service that uses the NLB that is in us-east-1. Grant specific AWS accounts access to connect to the SaaS service.

Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB) in front of the EC2 instances in eu-west-2. Create an NLB in us-east-1. Associate the NLB that is in us-east-1 with an ALB target group that uses the ALB that is in eu-west-2. Configure a PrivateLink endpoint service that uses the NLB that is in us-east-1. Grant specific AWS accounts access to connect to the SaaS service.

Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the EC2 instances that are in eu-west-2. In us-east-1, create an NLB and an instance target group that includes the shared EC2 instances from eu-west-2. Configure a PrivateLink endpoint service that uses the NLB that is in us-east-1. Grant specific AWS accounts access to connect to the SaaS service.

questions.explanation:
A Network Load Balancer can use an IP target group to route to private IP addresses outside its own VPC, including instances in a VPC peered in a different Region. The us-east-1 NLB can therefore front a PrivateLink endpoint service locally while forwarding traffic through inter-Region VPC peering to the existing eu-west-2 EC2 instances. An endpoint service created in us-east-1 cannot use an NLB in eu-west-2; ALB targets for an NLB must be in the same VPC and account; and EC2 instances cannot be shared through AWS RAM for registration as instance targets.

**Learn more:** [Target groups for your Network Load Balancers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticloadbalancing/latest/network/load-balancer-target-groups.html) · [Create a service powered by AWS PrivateLink](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/create-endpoint-service.html)

A company has automated nightly retraining of its machine learning models by using AWS Step Functions. The workflow contains multiple steps that use AWS Lambda. Each step can fail for different reasons, and any failure results in failure of the entire workflow.  
  
A review finds that retraining has failed for multiple consecutive nights without the company detecting the failure. A solutions architect must enhance the workflow so that notifications are sent for every type of failure in the retraining process.  
  
Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic with a subscription of type
Create a task named
Add a Catch field to all Task, Map, and Parallel states that have a statement of
Add a new email address to Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES). Verify the email address.
Create a task named
Add a Catch field to all Task, Map, and Parallel states that have a statement of

questions.explanation:
Amazon SNS can deliver notifications to an email subscription, and a Step Functions Task state can publish the failure details to the SNS topic. Catch handlers are supported on Task, Map, and Parallel states. A catcher using `States.ALL` is the wildcard error matcher, allowing those states to transition to the notification Task for errors they can catch. `States.Runtime` alone is not a complete failure-notification strategy.

**Learn more:** [Handling errors in Step Functions workflows](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/concepts-error-handling.html) · [Publish messages to an Amazon SNS topic with Step Functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/connect-sns.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has an organization with many AWS accounts in AWS Organizations. A solutions architect must improve the company’s management of common security group rules for the AWS accounts in the organization.  
  
The company maintains a common allow list of IP CIDR ranges in each AWS account to permit access to and from the company’s on-premises network. Developers in each account are responsible for adding new IP CIDR ranges to their security groups. The security team has its own AWS account. Currently, the security team notifies the owners of the other AWS accounts whenever changes are made to the allow list.  
  
The solutions architect must design a solution that distributes the common set of CIDR ranges to all accounts.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Set up an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic in the security team's AWS account. Deploy an AWS Lambda function in each AWS account. Configure the Lambda function to run every time an SNS topic receives a message. Configure the Lambda function to take an IP address as input and add it to a list of security groups in the account. Instruct the security team to distribute changes by publishing messages to its SNS topic.

Create new customer-managed prefix lists in each AWS account within the organization. Populate the prefix lists in each account with all internal CIDR ranges. Notify the owner of each AWS account to allow the new customer-managed prefix list IDs in their accounts in their security groups. Instruct the security team to share updates with each AWS account owner.

Create a new customer-managed prefix list in the security team’s AWS account. Populate the customer-managed prefix list with all internal CIDR ranges. Share the customer-managed prefix list with the organization by using AWS Resource Access Manager. Notify the owner of each AWS account to allow the new customer-managed prefix list ID in their security groups.

Create an IAM role in each account in the organization. Grant permissions to update security groups. Deploy an AWS Lambda function in the security team’s AWS account. Configure the Lambda function to take a list of internal IP addresses as input, assume a role in each organization account, and add the list of IP addresses to the security groups in each account.

questions.explanation:
A customer-managed prefix list provides a centrally maintained set of CIDR ranges that can be referenced by security group rules. Its owner can share it with an entire AWS Organization through AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM), allowing member accounts to use the same prefix list ID. Updates to the centrally owned list are available to all consumers, eliminating duplicated lists, notifications, and cross-account automation.

**Learn more:** [Share customer-managed prefix lists - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/sharing-managed-prefix-lists.html) · [Customer-managed prefix lists - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/working-with-managed-prefix-lists.html)

A company is building a new on-demand video application based on microservices. The application will have 5 million users at launch and 30 million users after 6 months. The company has deployed the application on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) using AWS Fargate. The application was developed by using ECS services that use the HTTPS protocol.  
  
A solutions architect must implement application updates by using blue/green deployments. The solution must route traffic to each ECS service through a load balancer. The application must automatically adjust its number of tasks in response to an Amazon CloudWatch alarm.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure the ECS services to use the blue/green deployment type and a Network Load Balancer. Request increases to the service quota for tasks per service to meet the demand.
Configure the ECS services to use the blue/green deployment type and a Network Load Balancer. Implement Auto Scaling group for each ECS service by using the Cluster Autoscaler.
Configure the ECS services to use the blue/green deployment type and an Application Load Balancer. Implement an Auto Scaling group for each ECS service by using the Cluster Autoscaler.
Configure the ECS services to use the blue/green deployment type and an Application Load Balancer. Implement Service Auto Scaling for each ECS service.

questions.explanation:
An Application Load Balancer supports HTTP/HTTPS traffic and can route traffic for Amazon ECS blue/green deployments. Amazon ECS Service Auto Scaling changes an ECS service’s desired task count in response to CloudWatch alarms, including for services that run on Fargate. Auto Scaling groups scale EC2 capacity rather than Fargate service tasks.

**Learn more:** [Automatically scale your Amazon ECS service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/service-auto-scaling.html) · [Application Load Balancer resources for blue/green, linear, and canary deployments](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/alb-resources-for-blue-green.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is rolling out a distributed in-memory database across a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances. The fleet includes one primary node and eight worker nodes. The primary node is responsible for monitoring cluster health, receiving user requests, routing user requests to worker nodes, and returning an aggregated response to a client. Worker nodes communicate with one another to replicate data partitions.  
  
The company needs the lowest possible network latency to attain maximum performance.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Launch memory optimized EC2 instances in a partition placement group.
Launch compute optimized EC2 instances in a partition placement group.
Launch memory optimized EC2 instances in a cluster placement group.
Launch compute optimized EC2 instances in a spread placement group.

questions.explanation:
Memory-optimized EC2 instances are appropriate for an in-memory database. A cluster placement group places tightly coupled instances close together within a single Availability Zone and is recommended for workloads requiring low network latency and high network throughput, which supports the request-routing and data-replication traffic among the nodes.

**Learn more:** [Placement strategies for your placement groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/placement-strategies.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a critical application whose data tier is deployed in one AWS Region. The data tier uses an Amazon DynamoDB table and an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster. The current Aurora MySQL engine version supports a global database. The application tier is already deployed across two Regions.  
  
Company policy requires critical applications to deploy both application-tier components and data-tier components across two Regions. The RTO and RPO must each be no greater than a few minutes. A solutions architect must recommend a solution that makes the data tier compliant with company policy.  
  
Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Add another Region to the Aurora MySQL DB cluster
Add another Region to each table in the Aurora MySQL DB cluster
Set up scheduled cross-Region backups for the DynamoDB table and the Aurora MySQL DB cluster
Convert the existing DynamoDB table to a global table by adding another Region to its configuration
Use Amazon Route 53 Application Recovery Controller to automate database backup and recovery to the secondary Region

questions.explanation:
An Aurora global database spans a primary Aurora DB cluster and at least one secondary Aurora DB cluster in a different AWS Region, enabling cross-Region replication and failover. DynamoDB global tables replicate table data among replica tables in multiple AWS Regions. These services provide the required multi-Region data deployment with recovery objectives measured in minutes, unlike scheduled backups, which require restoration before use.

**Learn more:** [Adding an AWS Region to an Amazon Aurora global database](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-global-database-attaching.html) · [How DynamoDB global tables work](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/V2globaltables_HowItWorks.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates applications across hundreds of production AWS accounts. The company uses AWS Organizations with all features enabled and runs centralized backups with AWS Backup.  
  
The company is worried about ransomware attacks. To address this concern, it has established a new policy requiring all backups to remain resilient if privileged-user credentials in any production account are breached.  
  
Which combination of steps will satisfy this new requirement? (Choose three.)

options.text: Implement cross-account backup with AWS Backup vaults in designated non-production accounts.
Add an SCP that restricts the modification of AWS Backup vaults.
Implement AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode.C. Implement least privilege access for the IAM service role that is assigned to AWS Backup.
Configure the backup frequency, lifecycle, and retention period to ensure that at least one backup always exists in the cold tier.
Configure AWS Backup to write all backups to an Amazon S3 bucket in a designated non-production account. Ensure that the S3 bucket has S3 Object Lock enabled.

questions.explanation:
Cross-account AWS Backup copies preserve recovery points in separate designated accounts, limiting the impact of a compromise in a production account. An AWS Organizations SCP can enforce a deny on backup-vault modification actions in member accounts. AWS Backup Vault Lock in compliance mode makes the vault configuration and recovery points immutable after its grace period; deletion or lifecycle changes are denied even when attempted by privileged users, including the root user.

**Learn more:** [Creating backup copies across AWS accounts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/create-cross-account-backup.html) · [AWS Backup Vault Lock](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/aws-backup/latest/devguide/vault-lock.html)

A company has an organization in AWS Organizations and is using AWS Control Tower to deploy a landing zone for that organization. The company wants to implement governance and policy enforcement. It must implement a policy that detects Amazon RDS DB instances in the company’s production OU that are not encrypted at rest.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Turn on mandatory guardrails in AWS Control Tower. Apply the mandatory guardrails to the production OU.
Enable the appropriate guardrail from the list of strongly recommended guardrails in AWS Control Tower. Apply the guardrail to the production OU.
Use AWS Config to create a new mandatory guardrail. Apply the rule to all accounts in the production OU.
Create a custom SCP in AWS Control Tower. Apply the SCP to the production OU.

questions.explanation:
AWS Control Tower provides the strongly recommended detective control **Detect Whether Storage Encryption is Enabled for Amazon RDS Database Instances**. When enabled on the production OU, it uses the AWS Config `RDS_STORAGE_ENCRYPTED` rule to identify RDS DB instances that are not encrypted at rest. SCPs prevent actions and do not provide this detective capability.

**Learn more:** [Strongly recommended controls with detective behavior — AWS Control Tower](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/controlreference/strongly-recommended-detective-controls.html) · [How controls work — AWS Control Tower](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/userguide/how-controls-work.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs an application that uses an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster as its caching layer. A recent security audit found that the company configured encryption at rest for ElastiCache. However, it did not configure ElastiCache to use encryption in transit. In addition, users can access the cache without authentication.  
  
A solutions architect must make changes that require user authentication and ensure the company uses end-to-end encryption.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an AUTH token. Store the token in AWS System Manager Parameter Store, as an encrypted parameter. Create a new cluster with AUTH, and configure encryption in transit. Update the application to retrieve the AUTH token from Parameter Store when necessary and to use the AUTH token for authentication.

Create an AUTH token. Store the token in AWS Secrets Manager. Configure the existing cluster to use the AUTH token, and configure encryption in transit. Update the application to retrieve the AUTH token from Secrets Manager when necessary and to use the AUTH token for authentication.

Create an SSL certificate. Store the certificate in AWS Secrets Manager. Create a new cluster, and configure encryption in transit. Update the application to retrieve the SSL certificate from Secrets Manager when necessary and to use the certificate for authentication.

Create an SSL certificate. Store the certificate in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, as an encrypted advanced parameter. Update the existing cluster to configure encryption in transit. Update the application to retrieve the SSL certificate from Parameter Store when necessary and to use the certificate for authentication.

questions.explanation:
ElastiCache for Redis OSS uses an AUTH token to require client authentication, and AUTH is supported only on clusters with encryption in transit enabled. A newly created cluster configured with TLS and AUTH can require encrypted, authenticated client connections. An encrypted Systems Manager Parameter Store parameter can securely hold the AUTH token for the application to retrieve. Enabling transit encryption on an existing cluster is a staged process that begins in preferred mode, which permits unencrypted connections until clients are migrated and required mode is set.

**Learn more:** [Authenticating with the Valkey and Redis OSS AUTH command](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/auth.html) · [Enabling in-transit encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/in-transit-encryption-enable.html)

A solutions architect is deciding the DNS approach for an existing VPC. The VPC is configured with the `10.24.34.0/24` CIDR block and uses Amazon Route 53 Resolver for DNS. New requirements require DNS queries to use private hosted zones. In addition, instances with public IP addresses must be assigned corresponding public hostnames.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements and ensures that domain names resolve correctly within the VPC?

options.text: Create a private hosted zone. Activate the enableDnsSupport attribute and the enableDnsHostnames attribute for the VPC. Update the VPC DHCP options set to include domain-name-servers=10.24.34.2.

Create a private hosted zone Associate the private hosted zone with the VPC. Activate the enableDnsSupport attribute and the enableDnsHostnames attribute for the VPC. Create a new VPC DHCP options set, and configure domain-name-servers=AmazonProvidedDNS. Associate the new DHCP options set with the VPC.

Deactivate the enableDnsSupport attribute for the VPActivate the enableDnsHostnames attribute for the VPCreate a new VPC DHCP options set, and configure doman-name-servers=10.24.34.2. Associate the new DHCP options set with the VPC.

Create a private hosted zone. Associate the private hosted zone with the VPC. Activate the enableDnsSupport attribute for the VPC. Deactivate the enableDnsHostnames attribute for the VPC. Update the VPC DHCP options set to include domain-name-servers=AmazonProvidedDNS.

questions.explanation:
A private hosted zone must be associated with the VPC, and both `enableDnsSupport` and `enableDnsHostnames` must be enabled for Route 53 Resolver to resolve private hosted-zone names and for instances with public IP addresses to receive public DNS hostnames. A DHCP options set configured with `AmazonProvidedDNS` directs instances to the Amazon Route 53 Resolver.

**Learn more:** [Understanding Amazon DNS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/AmazonDNS-concepts.html) · [Work with DHCP option sets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/DHCPOptionSet.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has a monolithic application that is essential to its business operations. The company hosts the application on an Amazon EC2 instance running Amazon Linux 2. The company’s application team receives a directive from the legal department to back up data from the instance’s encrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume to an Amazon S3 bucket. The application team does not possess the instance’s administrative SSH key pair. The application must remain available to serve users.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Attach a role to the instance with permission to write to Amazon S3. Use the AWS Systems Manager Session Manager option to gain access to the instance and run commands to copy data into Amazon S3.

Create an image of the instance with the reboot option turned on. Launch a new EC2 instance from the image. Attach a role to the new instance with permission to write to Amazon S3. Run a command to copy data into Amazon S3.
Take a snapshot of the EBS volume by using Amazon Data Lifecycle Manager (Amazon DLM). Copy the data to Amazon S3.

options.text: Configure a periodic process to run the aws s3 sync command from the on-premises file system to Amazon S3. Configure an AWS Lambda function to process event notifications from Amazon S3 and copy the images from Amazon S3 to the EFS file system.

questions.explanation:

The company wants to monitor, in near-real time, which EC2 instances connect to the databases. The company already has an on-premises monitoring solution that uses Splunk. A solutions architect must determine how to send network traffic to Splunk.  
  
How should the solutions architect satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Enable VPC flows logs, and send them to CloudWatch. Create an AWS Lambda function to periodically export the CloudWatch logs to an Amazon S3 bucket by using the pre-defined export function. Generate ACCESS_KEY and SECRET_KEY AWS credentials. Configure Splunk to pull the logs from the S3 bucket by using those credentials.

Create an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream with Splunk as the destination. Configure a pre-processing AWS Lambda function with a Kinesis Data Firehose stream processor that extracts individual log events from records sent by CloudWatch Logs subscription filters. Enable VPC flows logs, and send them to CloudWatch. Create a CloudWatch Logs subscription that sends log events to the Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream.

Send the CloudWatch logs to an Amazon Kinesis data stream with Amazon Kinesis Data Analytics for SQL Applications. Configure a 1-minute sliding window to collect the events. Create a SQL query that uses the anomaly detection template to monitor any networking traffic anomalies in near-real time. Send the result to an Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose delivery stream with Splunk as the destination.

questions.explanation:

Processing the subscription payload to extract individual log events enables Splunk to receive usable individual flow-log records.

options.text: Migrate the database to an Amazon RDS MySQL Multi-AZ DB instance. Deploy the application in an Auto Scaling group on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. Store sessions in Amazon Neptune

The company decides to use Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) and decommission the legacy SMTP server. The company has created and validated the SES domain, and it has lifted the SES limits.  
  
What should the company do to modify the application so it sends email messages through Amazon SES?

options.text: Configure the application to connect to Amazon SES by using TLS Wrapper. Create an IAM role that has ses:SendEmail and ses:SendRawEmail permissions. Attach the IAM role to an Amazon EC2 instance.
Configure the application to connect to Amazon SES by using STARTTLS. Obtain Amazon SES SMTP credentials. Use the credentials to authenticate with Amazon SES.
Configure the application to use the SES API to send email messages. Create an IAM role that has ses:SendEmail and ses:SendRawEmail permissions. Use the IAM role as a service role for Amazon SES.
Configure the application to use AWS SDKs to send email messages. Create an IAM user for Amazon SES. Generate API access keys. Use the access keys to authenticate with Amazon SES.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SES SMTP endpoints require TLS. STARTTLS upgrades an SMTP connection to TLS and is supported by SES on ports 25, 587, and 2587. Applications sending through the SES SMTP interface authenticate with SES SMTP credentials, which are distinct from AWS API credentials.

questions.explanation:

A company needs to migrate its website from an on-premises data center to AWS. The website consists of a load balancer, a content management system (CMS) that runs on a Linux operating system, and a MySQL database.  
  
The CMS requires persistent NFS-compatible storage for a file system. The new solution on AWS must be able to scale from 2 Amazon EC2 instances to 30 EC2 instances in response to unpredictable traffic increases. The new solution also must require no changes to the website and must prevent data loss.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Deploy the CMS to AWS Elastic Beanstalk with an Application Load Balancer and an Auto Scaling group. Use .ebextensions to mount the EFS file system to the EC2 instances. Create an Amazon Aurora MySQL database that is separate from the Elastic Beanstalk environment.

Create an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach volume. Deploy the CMS to AWS Elastic Beanstalk with a Network Load Balancer and an Auto Scaling group. Use .ebextensions to mount the EBS volume to the EC2 instances. Create an Amazon RDS for MySQL database in the Elastic Beanstalk environment.

Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Create a launch template and an Auto Scaling group to launch EC2 instances to support the CMS. Create a Network Load Balancer to distribute traffic. Create an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. Use an EC2 Auto Scaling scale-in lifecycle hook to mount the EFS file system to the EC2 instances.

Create an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach volume. Create a launch template and an Auto Scaling group to launch EC2 instances to support the CMS. Create an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic. Create an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster to support the MySQL database. Use EC2 user data to attach the EBS volume to the EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EFS provides NFS-compatible storage that seamlessly scales from 2 to 30 EC2 instances without data loss. AWS Elastic Beanstalk abstracts the complexity of infrastructure management and Auto Scaling orchestration, while .ebextensions automatically mount EFS to instances during scale-out. An Application Load Balancer provides Layer 7 routing for web traffic. Amazon Aurora MySQL as a separate managed service eliminates database management overhead. EBS Multi-Attach volumes do not provide NFS compatibility. Lifecycle hooks execute during scale-in, not scale-out, making them inappropriate for mounting shared storage.

**Learn more:** [Using Elastic Beanstalk with Amazon EFS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/services-efs.html) · [Amazon Aurora MySQL overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html)

A company uses an AWS CodeCommit repository and must retain a backup copy of the data in that repository in a second AWS Region.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery to replicate the CodeCommit repository data to the second Region.
Use AWS Backup to back up the CodeCommit repository on an hourly schedule. Create a cross-Region copy in the second Region.

Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke AWS CodeBuild when the company pushes code to the repository. Use CodeBuild to clone the repository. Create a .zip file of the content. Copy the file to an S3 bucket in the second Region.
Create an AWS Step Functions workflow on an hourly schedule to take a snapshot of the CodeCommit repository. Configure the workflow to copy the snapshot to an S3 bucket in the second Region

questions.explanation:
AWS CodeCommit emits repository state-change events to Amazon EventBridge, and a CodeBuild job can clone the repository and create an archive. Copying that archive to an Amazon S3 bucket in a different Region provides a cross-Region backup copy. AWS Backup does not list CodeCommit as a supported resource type, and CodeCommit repositories do not use Elastic Disaster Recovery replication or repository snapshots.

**Learn more:** [AWS CodeCommit events - Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eventbridge/latest/ref/events-ref-codecommit.html) · [Connect to an AWS CodeCommit repository](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/how-to-connect.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company that offers image-storage services plans to deploy a customer-facing solution on AWS. Millions of individual customers will use the solution. It will receive batches of large image files, resize the files, and retain the files in an Amazon S3 bucket for up to 6 months.  
  
The solution must accommodate substantial fluctuations in demand. It must also be reliable at enterprise scale and be able to rerun processing jobs if failures occur.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.text: Use AWS Step Functions to process the S3 event that occurs when a user stores an image. Run an AWS Lambda function that resizes the image in place and replaces the original file in the S3 bucket. Create an S3 Lifecycle expiration policy to expire all stored images after 6 months.

Use Amazon EventBridge to process the S3 event that occurs when a user uploads an image. Run an AWS Lambda function that resizes the image in place and replaces the original file in the S3 bucket. Create an S3 Lifecycle expiration policy to expire all stored images after 6 months.

Use S3 Event Notifications to invoke an AWS Lambda function when a user stores an image. Use the Lambda function to resize the image in place and to store the original file in the S3 bucket. Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move all stored images to S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA) after 6 months.

Use Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to process the S3 event that occurs when a user stores an image. Run an AWS Lambda function that resizes the image and stores the resized file in an S3 bucket that uses S3 Standard-Infrequent Access (S3 Standard-IA). Create an S3 Lifecycle policy to move all stored images to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 6 months.

questions.explanation:
AWS Step Functions supports workflow-level error handling, retries, and redriving failed Standard Workflow executions, enabling failed image-processing work to be rerun. AWS Lambda automatically scales for variable event-driven workloads, and an S3 Lifecycle expiration rule removes objects after the required six-month retention period rather than continuing to store them in another storage class.

**Learn more:** [Handling errors in Step Functions workflows](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/concepts-error-handling.html) · [Restarting state machine executions with redrive in Step Functions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/step-functions/latest/dg/redrive-executions.html)

A company uses Amazon OpenSearch Service to analyze data. It loads data from an Amazon S3 bucket that uses S3 Standard storage into an OpenSearch Service cluster with 10 data nodes. The data remains in the cluster for 1 month for read-only analysis. After 1 month, the company deletes the index containing the data from the cluster. For compliance, the company must retain a copy of all input data.  
  
The company is concerned about ongoing costs and asks a solutions architect to recommend a new solution.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements in the **MOST** cost-effective way?

options.text: Replace all the data nodes with UltraWarm nodes to handle the expected capacity. Transition the input data from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive when the company loads the data into the cluster.

Reduce the number of data nodes in the cluster to 2 Add UltraWarm nodes to handle the expected capacity. Configure the indexes to transition to UltraWarm when OpenSearch Service ingests the data. Transition the input data to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 1 month by using an S3 Lifecycle policy.

Reduce the number of data nodes in the cluster to 2. Add UltraWarm nodes to handle the expected capacity. Configure the indexes to transition to UltraWarm when OpenSearch Service ingests the data. Add cold storage nodes to the cluster Transition the indexes from UltraWarm to cold storage. Delete the input data from the S3 bucket after 1 month by using an S3 Lifecycle policy.

Reduce the number of data nodes in the cluster to 2. Add instance-backed data nodes to handle the expected capacity. Transition the input data from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive when the company loads the data into the cluster.

questions.explanation:
UltraWarm provides lower-cost storage for read-only OpenSearch indexes while a reduced hot data-node tier handles ingestion and index transitions. An S3 Lifecycle policy can transition the retained source objects from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after the one-month analysis period, preserving the required copy at a low archival-storage cost. Amazon S3 supports lifecycle transitions from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive.

**Learn more:** [UltraWarm storage for Amazon OpenSearch Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/opensearch-service/latest/developerguide/ultrawarm.html) · [Transitioning objects using Amazon S3 Lifecycle](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/lifecycle-transition-general-considerations.html)

",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution will meet these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L52",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Deploy the CMS to AWS Elastic Beanstalk with an Application Load Balancer and an Auto Scaling group. Use .ebextensions to mount the EFS file system to the EC2 instances. Create an Amazon Aurora MySQL database that is separate from the Elastic Beanstalk environment.","B":"Create an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach volume. Deploy the CMS to AWS Elastic Beanstalk with a Network Load Balancer and an Auto Scaling group. Use .ebextensions to mount the EBS volume to the EC2 instances. Create an Amazon RDS for MySQL database in the Elastic Beanstalk environment.","C":"Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Create a launch template and an Auto Scaling group to launch EC2 instances to support the CMS. Create a Network Load Balancer to distribute traffic. Create an Amazon Aurora MySQL database. Use an EC2 Auto Scaling scale-in lifecycle hook to mount the EFS file system to the EC2 instances.","D":"Create an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) Multi-Attach volume. Create a launch template and an Auto Scaling group to launch EC2 instances to support the CMS. Create an Application Load Balancer to distribute traffic. Create an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster to support the MySQL database. Use EC2 user data to attach the EBS volume to the EC2 instances."},"correctAnswer":"A","explanation":"Amazon EFS provides NFS-compatible storage that seamlessly scales from 2 to 30 EC2 instances without data loss. AWS Elastic Beanstalk abstracts the complexity of infrastructure management and Auto Scaling orchestration, while .ebextensions automatically mount EFS to instances during scale-out. An Application Load Balancer provides Layer 7 routing for web traffic. Amazon Aurora MySQL as a separate managed service eliminates database management overhead. EBS Multi-Attach volumes do not provide NFS compatibility. Lifecycle hooks execute during scale-in, not scale-out, making them inappropriate for mounting shared storage.

**Learn more:** [Using Elastic Beanstalk with Amazon EFS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/elasticbeanstalk/latest/dg/services-efs.html) · [Amazon Aurora MySQL overview](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/CHAP_AuroraOverview.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"7c77a168-43b2-46a4-b8f4-4e381619ff78","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02","mode":"default"}}]]

A company has created a mobile game. The game's backend operates on several virtual machines in an on-premises data center. Its business logic is exposed through a REST API with multiple functions. Player session data is kept in centralized file storage. Backend services use distinct API keys for throttling and for differentiating live traffic from test traffic.  
  
The game backend load fluctuates during the day. At peak times, server capacity is inadequate. Latency also occurs when retrieving player session data. Management has requested that a solutions architect present a cloud architecture that can accommodate the game's variable load and provide low-latency data access. The API model must remain unchanged.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements?

options.text: Implement the REST API using a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Run the business logic on an Amazon EC2 instance behind the NLB. Store player session data in Amazon Aurora Serverless.
Implement the REST API using an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Run the business logic in AWS Lambda. Store player session data in Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity.
Implement the REST API using Amazon API Gateway. Run the business logic in AWS Lambda. Store player session data in Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity.
Implement the REST API using AWS AppSync. Run the business logic in AWS Lambda. Store player session data in Amazon Aurora Serverless.

questions.explanation:
Amazon API Gateway preserves a REST API and supports API keys and usage plans for client identification and per-client throttling. API Gateway can route HTTP requests to AWS Lambda, whose execution environments scale automatically as request volume increases. Amazon DynamoDB on-demand capacity adapts automatically to variable traffic and provides single-digit-millisecond latency, making it suitable for highly responsive session-data access.

**Learn more:** [Usage plans and API keys for REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-api-usage-plans.html) · [Invoking a Lambda function using an Amazon API Gateway endpoint](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-apigateway.html)

A company wants to optimize AWS data-transfer and compute costs across developer accounts in the company’s AWS Organizations organization. Developers can configure VPCs and launch Amazon EC2 instances in one AWS Region. The EC2 instances retrieve approximately 1 TB of data daily from Amazon S3.  
  
Developer activity is causing excessive monthly data-transfer and NAT gateway processing charges between EC2 instances and S3 buckets, as well as high compute costs. The company wants to proactively enforce approved architectural patterns for all EC2 instance and VPC infrastructure that developers deploy in the AWS accounts. The company does not want this enforcement to adversely affect the speed at which developers can perform their tasks.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST cost-effective way?

options.text: Create SCPs to prevent developers from launching unapproved EC2 instance types. Provide the developers with an AWS CloudFormation template to deploy an approved VPC configuration with S3 interface endpoints. Scope the developers' IAM permissions so that the developers can launch VPC resources only with CloudFormation.

Create a daily forecasted budget with AWS Budgets to monitor EC2 compute costs and S3 data-transfer costs across the developer accounts. When the forecasted cost is 75% of the actual budget cost, send an alert to the developer teams. If the actual budget cost is 100%, create a budget action to terminate the developers' EC2 instances and VPC infrastructure.

Create an AWS Service Catalog portfolio that users can use to create an approved VPC configuration with S3 gateway endpoints and approved EC2 instances. Share the portfolio with the developer accounts. Configure an AWS Service Catalog launch constraint to use an approved IAM role. Scope the developers' IAM permissions to allow access only to AWS Service Catalog.

Create and deploy AWS Config rules to monitor the compliance of EC2 and VPC resources in the developer AWS accounts. If developers launch unapproved EC2 instances or if developers create VPCs without S3 gateway endpoints, perform a remediation action to terminate the unapproved resources.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 gateway endpoints provide VPC-to-S3 connectivity without an internet gateway or NAT device and have no additional charge, eliminating NAT gateway processing for this traffic. AWS Service Catalog portfolios provide approved VPC and EC2 products to developer accounts, and launch constraints make Service Catalog assume an approved IAM role to provision them. Restricting developers to Service Catalog access prevents unapproved deployments while allowing self-service provisioning.

**Learn more:** [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html) · [AWS Service Catalog Launch Constraints](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/servicecatalog/latest/adminguide/constraints-launch.html)

A company runs several workloads within a single AWS account. A new company policy requires that engineers provision only approved resources and use AWS CloudFormation to provision those resources. A solutions architect must create a solution that enforces this new restriction on the IAM role that engineers use to access AWS.  
  
What should the solutions architect do to create the solution?

options.text: Upload AWS CloudFormation templates that contain approved resources to an Amazon S3 bucket. Update the IAM policy for the engineers’ IAM role to only allow access to Amazon S3 and AWS CloudFormation. Use AWS CloudFormation templates to provision resources.

Update the IAM policy for the engineers’ IAM role with permissions to only allow provisioning of approved resources and AWS CloudFormation. Use AWS CloudFormation templates to create stacks with approved resources.

Update the IAM policy for the engineers’ IAM role with permissions to only allow AWS CloudFormation actions. Create a new IAM policy with permission to provision approved resources, and assign the policy to a new IAM service role. Assign the IAM service role to AWS CloudFormation during stack creation.
Provision resources in AWS CloudFormation stacks. Update the IAM policy for the engineers’ IAM role to only allow access to their own AWS CloudFormation stack.

questions.explanation:
A CloudFormation service role can be limited to permissions for only the approved resources, while engineers receive permissions to perform CloudFormation operations rather than direct resource-provisioning permissions. CloudFormation uses the service role’s credentials to create, update, and delete stack resources, enforcing infrastructure provisioning through CloudFormation and applying least privilege to the approved resource set.

**Learn more:** [CloudFormation service role](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/using-iam-servicerole.html) · [Configuring least-privilege permissions to use CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/least-privilege-cloudformation/permissions-use-cloudformation.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an on-premises data center and uses Kubernetes to build a new solution on AWS. The company uses Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) clusters for its development and test environments.  
  
For production workloads, the EKS control plane and data plane must be located on premises. The company requires an AWS-managed solution for Kubernetes management.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Install an AWS Outposts server in the on-premises data center. Deploy Amazon EKS by using a local cluster configuration on the Outposts server for the production workloads.
Install Amazon EKS Anywhere on the company's hardware in the on-premises data center. Deploy the production workloads on an EKS Anywhere cluster.
Install an AWS Outposts server in the on-premises data center. Deploy Amazon EKS by using an extended cluster configuration on the Outposts server for the production workloads.
Install an AWS Outposts server in the on-premises data center. Install Amazon EKS Anywhere on the Outposts server. Deploy the production workloads on an EKS Anywhere cluster.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EKS local clusters on AWS Outposts run both the Kubernetes control plane and worker nodes on the Outpost, while AWS fully manages the control plane. This meets the on-premises placement requirement with less operational responsibility than Amazon EKS Anywhere, where the customer manages the control plane. Extended EKS clusters do not qualify because their control plane runs in an AWS Region.

**Learn more:** [Deploy Amazon EKS on-premises with AWS Outposts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/eks-outposts.html) · [Kubernetes concepts - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/kubernetes-concepts.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs containerized application services on multiple Amazon EC2 instances that have public IP addresses. An Apache Kafka cluster runs on the EC2 instances. A PostgreSQL database has been migrated to Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL. The company anticipates a substantial increase in platform orders when it releases a new version of its flagship product.  
  
Which changes to the current architecture will reduce operational overhead and support the product release?

options.text: Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. Create additional read replicas for the DB instance. Create Amazon Kinesis data streams and configure the application services to use the data streams. Store and serve static content directly from Amazon S3.

Create an EC2 Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. Deploy the DB instance in Multi-AZ mode and enable storage auto scaling. Create Amazon Kinesis data streams and configure the application services to use the data streams. Store and serve static content directly from Amazon S3.

Deploy the application on a Kubernetes cluster created on the EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. Deploy the DB instance in Multi-AZ mode and enable storage auto scaling. Create an Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka cluster and configure the application services to use the cluster. Store static content in Amazon S3 behind an Amazon CloudFront distribution.

Deploy the application on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with AWS Fargate and enable auto scaling behind an Application Load Balancer. Create additional read replicas for the DB instance. Create an Amazon Managed Streaming for Apache Kafka cluster and configure the application services to use the cluster. Store static content in Amazon S3 behind an Amazon CloudFront distribution.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EKS with AWS Fargate removes the operational work of provisioning, configuring, and scaling container-hosting virtual machines while allowing the application to scale behind an Application Load Balancer. Amazon MSK provides managed Apache Kafka without requiring a migration to a different streaming technology. Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL read replicas are read-only instances that can serve read traffic, whereas Multi-AZ is primarily for high availability. Amazon CloudFront distributes and caches static S3 content from edge locations, reducing load on the application path.

**Learn more:** [Simplify compute management with AWS Fargate](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/fargate.html) · [What is Amazon MSK?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/msk/latest/developerguide/what-is-msk.html)

A company must create and manage multiple AWS accounts for several departments from one central location. The security team requires read-only access to every account from its own AWS account. The company uses AWS Organizations and has created an account for the security team.  
  
How should a solutions architect satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Use the OrganizationAccountAccessRole IAM role to create a new IAM policy with read-only access in each member account. Establish a trust relationship between the IAM policy in each member account and the security account. Ask the security team to use the IAM policy to gain access.

Use the OrganizationAccountAccessRole IAM role to create a new IAM role with read-only access in each member account. Establish a trust relationship between the IAM role in each member account and the security account. Ask the security team to use the IAM role to gain access.

Ask the security team to use AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to call the AssumeRole API for the OrganizationAccountAccessRole IAM role in the management account from the security account. Use the generated temporary credentials to gain access.

Ask the security team to use AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) to call the AssumeRole API for the OrganizationAccountAccessRole IAM role in the member account from the security account. Use the generated temporary credentials to gain access.

questions.explanation:
A cross-account IAM role in each member account can grant read-only permissions and trust the security account. Security-team principals can then use AWS STS to assume that role and receive temporary credentials. The default `OrganizationAccountAccessRole` is created for access from the AWS Organizations management account and grants administrative access, so it should be used only to establish the appropriately scoped role where needed.

**Learn more:** [Accessing member accounts in an organization with AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_accounts_access.html) · [Accessing a member account that has OrganizationAccountAccessRole with AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_accounts_access-cross-account-role.html)
