A company operates a static content distribution platform that serves customers globally. The customers consume content from their own AWS accounts.  
  
The company serves its content from an Amazon S3 bucket. The company uploads the content from its on-premises environment to the S3 bucket by using an S3 File Gateway.  
  
The company wants to improve the platform’s performance and reliability by serving content from the AWS Region that is geographically closest to customers. The company must route the on-premises data to Amazon S3 with minimal latency and without public internet exposure.  
  
Which combination of steps will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead? (Choose two.)

options.text: Implement S3 Multi-Region Access Points
Use S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) to copy content to different Regions
Create an AWS Lambda function that tracks the routing of clients to Regions
Use an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection to connect to a Multi-Region Access Point.
Use AWS PrivateLink and AWS Direct Connect to connect to a Multi-Region Access Point.

questions.explanation:
An S3 Multi-Region Access Point gives customers one global endpoint that automatically routes each request to the lowest-latency regional copy of the data, meeting the performance and reliability goal with minimal setup. Connecting the on-premises S3 File Gateway to that access point over AWS PrivateLink through an AWS Direct Connect private virtual interface keeps the upload path entirely on the AWS private network, satisfying the requirement to avoid public internet exposure; a Site-to-Site VPN, by contrast, still tunnels over the public internet as its underlying transport.

**Learn more:** [Configuring a Multi-Region Access Point for use with AWS PrivateLink](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/MultiRegionAccessPointsPrivateLink.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect is investigating an issue where a company cannot establish new sessions in Amazon WorkSpaces. An initial analysis shows that the issue involves user profiles. The Amazon WorkSpaces environment is configured to use Amazon FSx for Windows File Server as the profile-share storage. The FSx for Windows File Server file system is configured with 10 TB of storage.  
  
The solutions architect finds that the file system has reached its maximum capacity. The solutions architect must ensure that users can regain access. The solution must also prevent the issue from happening again.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Remove old user profiles to create space. Migrate the user profiles to an Amazon FSx for Lustre file system.

Increase capacity by using the update-file-system command. Implement an Amazon CloudWatch metric that monitors free space. Use Amazon EventBridge to invoke an AWS Lambda function to increase capacity as required.
Monitor the file system by using the FreeStorageCapacity metric in Amazon CloudWatch. Use AWS Step Functions to increase the capacity as required.
Remove old user profiles to create space. Create an additional FSx for Windows File Server file system. Update the user profile redirection for 50% of the users to use the new file system.

questions.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Windows File Server storage can be increased with the `update-file-system` command, restoring available profile-share space. Monitoring free capacity with Amazon CloudWatch and invoking Lambda-based automation when the threshold is reached provides ongoing capacity remediation before the file system fills again.

**Learn more:** [Increasing file system storage capacity – Amazon FSx for Windows File Server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/increase-storage-capacity.html) · [Increasing storage capacity dynamically – Amazon FSx for Windows File Server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/WindowsGuide/automate-storage-capacity-increase.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs an application on AWS. The application reads and writes objects stored in one Amazon S3 bucket. The company needs to modify the application so that it can be deployed in two AWS Regions.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Set up an Amazon CloudFront distribution with the S3 bucket as an origin. Deploy the application to a second Region Modify the application to use the CloudFront distribution. Use AWS Global Accelerator to access the data in the S3 bucket.

Create a new S3 bucket in a second Region. Set up bidirectional S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) between the original S3 bucket and the new S3 bucket. Configure an S3 Multi-Region Access Point that uses both S3 buckets. Deploy a modified application to both Regions.

Create a new S3 bucket in a second Region Deploy the application in the second Region. Configure the application to use the new S3 bucket. Set up S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) from the original S3 bucket to the new S3 bucket.

Set up an S3 gateway endpoint with the S3 bucket as an origin. Deploy the application to a second Region. Modify the application to use the new S3 gateway endpoint. Use S3 Intelligent-Tiering on the S3 bucket.

questions.explanation:
An S3 Multi-Region Access Point provides a single global endpoint that routes requests to the closest active S3 bucket. Bidirectional S3 Cross-Region Replication keeps the buckets synchronized when objects are written in either Region, supporting multi-Region reads and writes without requiring the application to select or manage separate bucket endpoints.

**Learn more:** [Configuring replication for use with Multi-Region Access Points](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/MultiRegionAccessPointBucketReplication.html) · [Managing multi-Region traffic with Multi-Region Access Points](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/MultiRegionAccessPoints.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a data-intensive application on AWS. The application runs on a cluster containing hundreds of Amazon EC2 instances. A shared file system, hosted on several EC2 instances, stores 200 TB of data. The application reads and changes data on the shared file system and produces a report. The job runs once each month, reads a subset of the shared file system files, and takes approximately 72 hours to finish. The compute instances scale in an Auto Scaling group, while the instances hosting the shared file system run continuously. All compute and storage instances are in the same AWS Region.  
  
A solutions architect must reduce costs by replacing the shared file system instances. The file system must deliver high-performance access to the required data throughout the 72-hour run.  
  
Which solution will deliver the **LARGEST** overall cost reduction while satisfying these requirements?

options.text: Migrate the data from the existing shared file system to an Amazon S3 bucket that uses the S3 Intelligent-Tiering storage class. Before the job runs each month, use Amazon FSx for Lustre to create a new file system with the data from Amazon S3 by using lazy loading. Use the new file system as the shared storage for the duration of the job. Delete the file system when the job is complete.

Migrate the data from the existing shared file system to a large Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume with Multi-Attach enabled. Attach the EBS volume to each of the instances by using a user data script in the Auto Scaling group launch template. Use the EBS volume as the shared storage for the duration of the job. Detach the EBS volume when the job is complete

Migrate the data from the existing shared file system to an Amazon S3 bucket that uses the S3 Standard storage class. Before the job runs each month, use Amazon FSx for Lustre to create a new file system with the data from Amazon S3 by using batch loading. Use the new file system as the shared storage for the duration of the job. Delete the file system when the job is complete.

Migrate the data from the existing shared file system to an Amazon S3 bucket. Before the job runs each month, use AWS Storage Gateway to create a file gateway with the data from Amazon S3. Use the file gateway as the shared storage for the job. Delete the file gateway when the job is complete.

questions.explanation:
Amazon FSx for Lustre provides high-performance shared file access for compute-intensive workloads and can link to an Amazon S3 data repository. With lazy loading, file data is loaded from S3 when the application accesses it, avoiding the cost and delay of staging the entire 200 TB dataset when the monthly job reads only a subset. Keeping the durable data in S3 Intelligent-Tiering and creating FSx for Lustre only for the 72-hour processing period eliminates the continuously running EC2 file-system infrastructure and minimizes temporary high-performance storage use.

**Learn more:** [Linking your file system to an Amazon S3 bucket - FSx for Lustre](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/create-dra-linked-data-repo.html) · [Overview of data repositories - FSx for Lustre](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/fsx/latest/LustreGuide/overview-dra-data-repo.html)

A company is planning a migration from an on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud. The company plans to use multiple AWS accounts that are managed in an organization in AWS Organizations. The company will create a small number of accounts initially and will add accounts as needed. A solutions architect must design a solution that turns on AWS CloudTrail in all AWS accounts.  
  
What is the MOST operationally efficient solution that meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function that creates a new CloudTrail trail in all AWS accounts in the organization. Invoke the Lambda function daily by using a scheduled action in Amazon EventBridge.
Create a new CloudTrail trail in the organization's management account. Configure the trail to log all events for all AWS accounts in the organization.

Create a new CloudTrail trail in all AWS accounts in the organization. Create new trails whenever a new account is created. Define an SCP that prevents deletion or modification of trails. Apply the SCP to the root OU.
Create an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook that creates a CloudTrail trail in all AWS accounts in the organization. Invoke the automation by using Systems Manager State Manager.

questions.explanation:
Creating an organization trail in the management account is the most operationally efficient approach for enabling CloudTrail across all AWS accounts in an organization. The trail automatically logs events from all member accounts without requiring per-account trail creation, and new accounts are automatically included. This eliminates manual trail creation for each account and reduces ongoing maintenance overhead compared to Lambda-based or Systems Manager automation.

**Learn more:** [Creating a trail for an organization](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awscloudtrail/latest/userguide/creating-trail-organization.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has 50 AWS accounts that belong to an organization in AWS Organizations. Every account has multiple VPCs. Which combination of steps meets these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: From the management account, share the transit gateway with member accounts by using AWS Resource Access Manager.
From the management account, share the transit gateway with member accounts by using an AWS Organizations SCP.

Launch an AWS CloudFormation stack set from the management account that automatically creates a new VPC and a VPC transit gateway attachment in a member account. Associate the attachment with the transit gateway in the management account by using the transit gateway ID.

Launch an AWS CloudFormation stack set from the management account that automatically creates a new VPC and a peering transit gateway attachment in a member account. Share the attachment with the transit gateway in the management account by using a transit gateway service-linked role.
From the management account, share the transit gateway with member accounts by using AWS Service Catalog.

questions.explanation:
AWS RAM is the mechanism for sharing a transit gateway with member accounts or an AWS Organization, allowing those accounts to create VPC attachments to the shared gateway. AWS CloudFormation StackSets can automatically deploy stacks to newly added AWS Organizations accounts, so a StackSet can create the VPC and its VPC transit gateway attachment using the shared transit gateway ID.

Several customers also have access to a legacy API that is running on a single standalone Amazon EC2 instance.  
  
The company wants to increase the security for these APIs to better prevent denial of service (DoS) attacks, check for vulnerabilities, and guard against common exploits.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

options.text: Use AWS WAF to protect both APIs. Configure Amazon Inspector to analyze the legacy API. Configure Amazon GuardDuty to monitor for malicious attempts to access the APIs.
Use AWS WAF to protect the API Gateway API. Configure Amazon Inspector to analyze both APIs. Configure Amazon GuardDuty to block malicious attempts to access the APIs.
Use AWS WAF to protect the API Gateway API. Configure Amazon Inspector to analyze the legacy API. Configure Amazon GuardDuty to monitor for malicious attempts to access the APIs.
Use AWS WAF to protect the API Gateway AP! Configure Amazon Inspector to protect the legacy API. Configure Amazon GuardDuty to block malicious attempts to access the APIs.

questions.explanation:
AWS WAF can protect API Gateway (where most traffic enters) but cannot attach directly to standalone EC2 instances. Amazon Inspector analyzes the legacy EC2 API for vulnerabilities, and GuardDuty monitors for malicious activity across both APIs without attempting to block (blocking is WAF's role). Option A incorrectly suggests WAF protects the EC2 instance. Option B incorrectly claims GuardDuty blocks attacks (it only detects). Option D misapplies Inspector to protection.

A company’s public API runs as tasks on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS). The tasks run on AWS Fargate behind an Application Load Balancer (ALB) and use Service Auto Scaling based on task CPU utilization. The service has operated successfully for several months.  
  
Recently, API performance degraded and made the application unusable. The company found that many SQL injection attacks had targeted the API and that the API service had scaled to its maximum capacity.  
  
A solutions architect must implement a solution that stops SQL injection attacks from reaching the ECS API service. The solution must permit legitimate traffic and maximize operational efficiency.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a new AWS WAF web ACL to monitor the HTTP requests and HTTPS requests that are forwarded to the ALB in front of the ECS tasks.
Create a new AWS WAF Bot Control implementation. Add a rule in the AWS WAF Bot Control managed rule group to monitor traffic and allow only legitimate traffic to the ALB in front of the ECS tasks.

Create a new AWS WAF web ACL. Add a new rule that blocks requests that match the SQL database rule group. Set the web ACL to allow all other traffic that does not match those rules. Attach the web ACL to the ALB in front of the ECS tasks.

Create a new AWS WAF web ACL. Create a new empty IP set in AWS WAF. Add a new rule to the web ACL to block requests that originate from IP addresses in the new IP set. Create an AWS Lambda function that scrapes the API logs for IP addresses that send SQL injection attacks, and add those IP addresses to the IP set. Attach the web ACL to the ALB in front of the ECS tasks.

questions.explanation:
An AWS WAF web ACL attached to the ALB filters requests before they reach the ECS service. The AWS Managed Rules SQL database rule group blocks patterns associated with SQL injection attacks, and allowing requests that do not match those rules preserves legitimate traffic. Using the managed rule group provides this protection without maintaining custom detection or IP-blocking automation.

A company has an application that stores user-uploaded videos in an Amazon S3 bucket that uses S3 Standard storage. Users access the videos frequently in the first 180 days after the videos are uploaded. Access after 180 days is rare. Named users and anonymous users access the videos.  
  
Most of the videos are more than 100 MB in size. Users often have poor internet connectivity when they upload videos, resulting in failed uploads. The company uses multipart uploads for the videos.  
  
A solutions architect needs to optimize the S3 costs of the application.  
  
Which combination of actions will meet these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Configure the S3 bucket to be a Requester Pays bucket.
Use S3 Transfer Acceleration to upload the videos to the S3 bucket.
Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration o expire incomplete multipart uploads 7 days after initiation.
Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition objects to S3 Glacier Instant Retrieval after 1 day.
Create an S3 Lifecycle configuration to transition objects to S3 Standard-infrequent Access (S3 Standard- IA) after 180 days.

questions.explanation:
Option C addresses the waste from failed multipart uploads by expiring incomplete uploads after 7 days, reducing unnecessary storage costs. Option E optimizes storage costs by transitioning infrequently accessed data to S3 Standard-IA after 180 days when access patterns change. Together, these lifecycle policies directly target the cost optimization needs described. S3 Transfer Acceleration (B) improves upload speed but does not reduce storage costs; Glacier (D) is too aggressive for data that may still be accessed occasionally after 180 days.

**Learn more:** [Delete incomplete multipart uploads using a lifecycle rule](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/mpu-abort-incomplete-mpu-lifecycle-config.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses AWS Organizations for a multi-account deployment in the AWS Cloud. The company’s finance team has a data-processing application that uses AWS Lambda and Amazon DynamoDB. The company’s marketing team needs to access data stored in the DynamoDB table.  
  
The DynamoDB table holds confidential data. The marketing team must be able to access only specific attributes of data in the DynamoDB table. The finance team and the marketing team use separate AWS accounts.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to give the marketing team the appropriate access to the DynamoDB table?

options.text: Create an SCP to grant the marketing team's AWS account access to the specific attributes of the DynamoDB table. Attach the SCP to the OU of the finance team.

Create an IAM role in the finance team's account by using IAM policy conditions for specific DynamoDB attributes (fine-grained access control). Establish trust with the marketing team's account. In the marketing team's account, create an IAM role that has permissions to assume the IAM role in the finance team's account.

Create a resource-based IAM policy that includes conditions for specific DynamoDB attributes (fine-grained access control). Attach the policy to the DynamoDB table. In the marketing team's account, create an IAM role that has permissions to access the DynamoDB table in the finance team's account.

Create an IAM role in the finance team's account to access the DynamoDB table. Use an IAM permissions boundary to limit the access to the specific attributes. In the marketing team's account, create an IAM role that has permissions to assume the IAM role in the finance team's account.

questions.explanation:
DynamoDB fine-grained access control uses IAM policy conditions to restrict which item attributes a principal can retrieve or modify. A role in the finance account can carry that constrained DynamoDB permissions policy and trust the marketing account; a marketing-account role can then assume it. An SCP cannot grant permissions, and a permissions boundary only limits the maximum permissions that an identity-based policy can grant. For cross-account DynamoDB resource policies, AWS also notes that a broad unconditional identity-based Allow can override the practical restriction intended by a conditional resource-policy Allow, so the stated resource-policy design does not reliably enforce the attribute limit.

**Learn more:** [Using IAM policy conditions for fine-grained access control - Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/specifying-conditions.html) · [Authorization with IAM identity-based policies and DynamoDB resource-based policies - Amazon DynamoDB](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/rbac-auth-iam-id-based-policies-DDB.html)

A media-storage application uploads users’ photos to Amazon S3 for processing by AWS Lambda functions. Application state is held in Amazon DynamoDB tables. Users report that some uploaded photos are not being processed correctly. The application developers trace the logs and discover that Lambda has photo-processing problems when thousands of users upload photos at the same time. These issues result from Lambda concurrency limits and DynamoDB performance when data is written.  
  
Which combination of actions should a solutions architect take to improve the application’s performance and reliability? (Choose two.)

options.text: Evaluate and adjust the RCUs for the DynamoDB tables.
Evaluate and adjust the WCUs for the DynamoDB tables.
Add an Amazon ElastiCache layer to increase the performance of Lambda functions.
Add an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue and reprocessing logic between Amazon S3 and the Lambda functions.
Use S3 Transfer Acceleration to provide lower latency to users.

questions.explanation:
DynamoDB write capacity is measured in WCUs, so evaluating and adjusting WCUs addresses the throughput needed when application state is saved during simultaneous uploads. An Amazon SQS queue between Amazon S3 and Lambda decouples and buffers upload events, allowing Lambda to process messages at a manageable rate and supporting retries/reprocessing when processing fails or is throttled.

**Learn more:** [Using Lambda with Amazon SQS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-sqs.html) · [Configuring scaling behavior for Amazon SQS event source mappings](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/services-sqs-scaling.html)

Modify the existing Amazon Route 53 records by adding health checks. Configure a fallback target if the health check fails. Modify DNS records to point to a publicly accessible webpage.

A company has AWS accounts that belong to an organization in AWS Organizations. The company wants to track Amazon EC2 usage as a metric. The company’s architecture team must receive a daily alert when EC2 usage is more than 10% higher than the average EC2 usage over the previous 30 days.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure AWS Budgets in the organization's management account. Specify a usage type of EC2 running hours. Specify a daily period. Set the budget amount to be 10% more than the reported average usage for the last 30 days from AWS Cost Explorer. Configure an alert to notify the architecture team if the usage threshold is met

Configure AWS Cost Anomaly Detection in the organization's management account. Configure a monitor type of AWS Service. Apply a filter of Amazon EC2. Configure an alert subscription to notify the architecture team if the usage is 10% more than the average usage for the last 30 days.

Enable AWS Trusted Advisor in the organization's management account. Configure a cost optimization advisory alert to notify the architecture team if the EC2 usage is 10% more than the reported average usage for the last 30 days.
Configure Amazon Detective in the organization's management account. Configure an EC2 usage anomaly alert to notify the architecture team if Detective identifies a usage anomaly of more than 10%.

questions.explanation:
AWS Budgets can create a usage budget for an EC2 running-hours usage type group, reset that budget daily, and send an alert when the actual usage reaches a configured threshold. Setting the daily budget amount to 110% of the EC2 usage average reported for the prior 30 days provides the required daily threshold. AWS Cost Anomaly Detection evaluates anomalous net unblended cost rather than directly monitoring a usage metric.

**Learn more:** [Creating a usage budget - AWS Cost Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/create-usage-budget.html) · [Detecting unusual spend with AWS Cost Anomaly Detection - AWS Cost Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/manage-ad.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is running several applications in the AWS Cloud. The applications are specific to separate business units in the company. The company is running the components of the applications in several AWS accounts that are in an organization in AWS Organizations.  
  
Every cloud resource in the company’s organization has a tag that is named BusinessUnit. Every tag already has the appropriate value of the business unit name.  
  
The company needs to allocate its cloud costs to different business units. The company also needs to visualize the cloud costs for each business unit.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: In the organization's management account, create a cost allocation tag that is named BusinessUnit. Also in the management account, create an Amazon S3 bucket and an AWS Cost and Usage Report (AWS CUR). Configure the S3 bucket as the destination for the AWS CUR. From the management account, query the AWS CUR data by using Amazon Athena. Use Amazon QuickSight for visualization.

In each member account, create a cost allocation tag that is named BusinessUnit. In the organization’s management account, create an Amazon S3 bucket and an AWS Cost and Usage Report (AWS CUR). Configure the S3 bucket as the destination for the AWS CUR. Create an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard for visualization.

In the organization's management account, create a cost allocation tag that is named BusinessUnit. In each member account, create an Amazon S3 bucket and an AWS Cost and Usage Report (AWS CUR). Configure each S3 bucket as the destination for its respective AWS CUR. In the management account, create an Amazon CloudWatch dashboard for visualization.

In each member account, create a cost allocation tag that is named BusinessUnit. Also in each member account, create an Amazon S3 bucket and an AWS Cost and Usage Report (AWS CUR). Configure each S3 bucket as the destination for its respective AWS CUR. From the management account, query the AWS CUR data by using Amazon Athena. Use Amazon QuickSight for visualization.

questions.explanation:
Cost allocation requires activating the BusinessUnit tag in the management account (not individual member accounts), creating a centralized AWS Cost and Usage Report, and querying the CUR data with Athena for flexibility. QuickSight provides superior data visualization capabilities compared to CloudWatch dashboards for business intelligence use cases. This approach aggregates costs from all member accounts in a single location without duplicating CUR across accounts.

**Learn more:** [Query and visualize AWS Cost and Usage data with Athena and QuickSight](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/big-data/query-and-visualize-aws-cost-and-usage-data-using-amazon-athena-and-amazon-quicksight/) · [Visualize QuickSight costs using CUR and cost allocation tags](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/business-intelligence/visualize-amazon-quicksight-costs-using-aws-cur-and-cost-allocation-tags/)

A company has migrated its forms-processing application to AWS. When users use the application, they upload scanned forms as files through a web application. A database stores user metadata and references to files stored in Amazon S3. The web application runs on Amazon EC2 instances and uses an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database.  
  
When forms are uploaded, the application sends notifications to a team through Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS). A team member then signs in and processes each form. The team member validates the form data and extracts relevant data before entering the information into another system that uses an API.  
  
A solutions architect must automate the manual form-processing work. The solution must provide accurate form extraction, minimize time to market, and minimize long-term operational overhead.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Develop custom libraries to perform optical character recognition (OCR) on the forms. Deploy the libraries to an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster as an application tier. Use this tier to process the forms when forms are uploaded. Store the output in Amazon S3. Parse this output by extracting the data into an Amazon DynamoDB table. Submit the data to the target system's APL. Host the new application tier on EC2 instances.

Extend the system with an application tier that uses AWS Step Functions and AWS Lambda. Configure this tier to use artificial intelligence and machine learning (AI/ML) models that are trained and hosted on an EC2 instance to perform optical character recognition (OCR) on the forms when forms are uploaded. Store the output in Amazon S3. Parse this output by extracting the data that is required within the application tier. Submit the data to the target system's API.

Host a new application tier on EC2 instances. Use this tier to call endpoints that host artificial intelligence and machine teaming (AI/ML) models that are trained and hosted in Amazon SageMaker to perform optical character recognition (OCR) on the forms. Store the output in Amazon ElastiCache. Parse this output by extracting the data that is required within the application tier. Submit the data to the target system's API.

Extend the system with an application tier that uses AWS Step Functions and AWS Lambda. Configure this tier to use Amazon Textract and Amazon Comprehend to perform optical character recognition (OCR) on the forms when forms are uploaded. Store the output in Amazon S3. Parse this output by extracting the data that is required within the application tier. Submit the data to the target system's API.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Textract is a managed document-analysis service that extracts text and structured form data, including key-value pairs. Amazon Comprehend can identify relevant entities in the extracted content. AWS Step Functions and AWS Lambda provide serverless orchestration and API integration, eliminating the need to build, train, host, and operate custom OCR or AI/ML infrastructure.

**Learn more:** [Form Data (Key-Value Pairs) - Amazon Textract](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/textract/latest/dg/how-it-works-kvp.html) · [Amazon Textract Documentation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/textract/)

A company runs an on-premises monitoring solution that uses a PostgreSQL database to persist events. The database cannot scale because of heavy ingestion and frequently exhausts its storage.  
  
The company wants to build a hybrid solution and has already established a VPN connection between its network and AWS. The solution must include these attributes:  
  
- Managed AWS services to reduce operational complexity.  
- A buffer that automatically scales with data throughput and needs no ongoing administration.  
- A visualization tool for creating dashboards that observe events in near-real time.  
- Support for semi-structured JSON data and dynamic schemas.  
  
Which combination of components will allow the company to create a monitoring solution that meets these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use Amazon Kinesis Data Firehose to buffer events. Create an AWS Lambda function to process and transform events.
Create an Amazon Kinesis data stream to buffer events. Create an AWS Lambda function to process and transform events.
Configure an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster to receive events. Use Amazon QuickSight to read from the database and create near-real-time visualizations and dashboards.
Configure Amazon Elasticsearch Service (Amazon ES) to receive events. Use the Kibana endpoint deployed with Amazon ES to create near-real-time visualizations and dashboards.
Configure an Amazon Neptune DB instance to receive events. Use Amazon QuickSight to read from the database and create near-real-time visualizations and dashboards.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Data Firehose is a fully managed streaming ingestion and delivery service that automatically scales to match data volume and throughput, requires no ongoing administration, and can use AWS Lambda to transform records. Amazon Elasticsearch Service (now Amazon OpenSearch Service) stores and indexes JSON documents with dynamic mappings and provides Kibana/OpenSearch Dashboards for operational, near-real-time visualizations. This combination supplies scalable event buffering and transformation plus a JSON-capable searchable event store with dashboards.

**Learn more:** [Data ingestion methods – AWS Whitepaper](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/building-data-lakes/data-ingestion-methods.html) · [Operational best practices for Amazon OpenSearch Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/opensearch-service/latest/developerguide/bp.html)

A company has deployed an ordering system that uses an event-driven architecture. During initial testing, the system stopped processing orders. Additional log analysis showed that a single order message in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) standard queue was causing an error in the backend and blocking every subsequent order message. The queue visibility timeout is configured as 30 seconds, and the backend processing timeout is configured as 10 seconds. A solutions architect must analyze faulty order messages and ensure the system keeps processing subsequent messages.  
  
Which action should the solutions architect take to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Increase the backend processing timeout to 30 seconds to match the visibility timeout.
Reduce the visibility timeout of the queue to automatically remove the faulty message.
Configure a new SQS FIFO queue as a dead-letter queue to isolate the faulty messages.
Configure a new SQS standard queue as a dead-letter queue to isolate the faulty messages.

questions.explanation:
An SQS dead-letter queue (DLQ) retains messages that repeatedly fail processing after the configured maximum receive count, isolating them for investigation while the source queue continues handling other messages. An SQS standard queue requires a standard queue as its DLQ; FIFO and standard queue types cannot be mixed in this source-DLQ relationship.

**Learn more:** [Amazon SQS CreateQueue API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/APIReference/API_CreateQueue.html) · [Configure a dead-letter queue using the Amazon SQS console](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSSimpleQueueService/latest/SQSDeveloperGuide/sqs-configure-dead-letter-queue.html)

A company's solutions architect must provide secure Remote Desktop access for users to Amazon EC2 Windows instances hosted in a VPC. The solution must integrate centralized user management with the company's on-premises Active Directory. Connectivity to the VPC occurs through the internet. The company has hardware that can establish an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements **MOST** cost-effectively?

options.text: Deploy a managed Active Directory by using AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory. Establish a trust with the on-premises Active Directory. Deploy an EC2 instance as a bastion host in the VPC. Ensure that the EC2 instance is joined to the domain. Use the bastion host to access the target instances through RDP.

Configure AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to integrate with the on-premises Active Directory by using the AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory AD Connector. Configure permission sets against user groups for access to AWS Systems Manager. Use Systems Manager Fleet Manager to access the target instances through RDP.

Implement a VPN between the on-premises environment and the target VPEnsure that the target instances are joined to the on-premises Active Directory domain over the VPN connection. Configure RDP access through the VPN. Connect from the company’s network to the target instances.

Deploy a managed Active Directory by using AWS Directory Service for Microsoft Active Directory. Establish a trust with the on-premises Active Directory. Deploy a Remote Desktop Gateway on AWS by using an AWS Quick Start. Ensure that the Remote Desktop Gateway is joined to the domain. Use the Remote Desktop Gateway to access the target instances through RDP.

questions.explanation:
AWS Site-to-Site VPN provides encrypted connectivity between the on-premises network and a VPC over the internet using a customer gateway device. With routing, DNS, and required Active Directory connectivity over that VPN, EC2 Windows instances can join the existing on-premises domain and users can authenticate with centrally managed domain accounts. Restricting RDP access to the VPN avoids exposing RDP publicly and avoids the additional cost of a managed AWS directory, AD Connector, bastion host, or Remote Desktop Gateway.

**Learn more:** [How AWS Site-to-Site VPN works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/s2svpn/how_it_works.html) · [Best practices for AD Connector](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directoryservice/latest/admin-guide/ad_connector_best_practices.html)

A company has an AWS Organizations organization that includes a large number of AWS accounts. One AWS account is designated as a transit account and contains a transit gateway that is shared with all other AWS accounts. AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections are configured between every company global office and the transit account. AWS Config is enabled across all accounts.  
  
The networking team needs to centrally manage a list of internal IP address ranges that belong to the global offices. Developers will use this list to securely access their applications.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Create a JSON file that is hosted in Amazon S3 and that lists all of the internal IP address ranges. Configure an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic in each of the accounts that can be invoked when the JSON file is updated. Subscribe an AWS Lambda function to the SNS topic to update all relevant security group rules with the updated IP address ranges.

Create a new AWS Config managed rule that contains all of the internal IP address ranges. Use the rule to check the security groups in each of the accounts to ensure compliance with the list of IP address ranges. Configure the rule to automatically remediate any noncompliant security group that is detected.

In the transit account, create a VPC prefix list with all of the internal IP address ranges. Use AWS Resource Access Manager to share the prefix list with all of the other accounts. Use the shared prefix list to configure security group rules in the other accounts.

In the transit account, create a security group with all of the internal IP address ranges. Configure the security groups in the other accounts to reference the transit account’s security group by using a nested security group reference of “/sg-1a2b3c4d”.

questions.explanation:
A customer-managed VPC prefix list provides a centrally maintained set of CIDR ranges. Its owner can share it with AWS accounts, organizational units, or an entire AWS Organization by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM), and consumer accounts can reference it in their own security group rules. Updating the prefix list updates the version used by those references, avoiding per-account automation or remediation workflows.

**Learn more:** [Share customer-managed prefix lists](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/sharing-managed-prefix-lists.html) · [Consolidate and manage network CIDR blocks with managed prefix lists](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/managed-prefix-lists.html)

A company must migrate 60 on-premises legacy applications to AWS. The applications use the .NET Framework and run on Windows.  
  
The company requires a solution that minimizes migration time, needs no application code changes, and avoids managing infrastructure.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Refactor the applications and containerize them by using AWS Toolkit for NET Refactoring. Use Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) with the Fargate launch type to host the containerized applications.
Use the Windows Web Application Migration Assistant to migrate the applications to AWS Elastic Beanstalk. Use Elastic Beanstalk to deploy and manage the applications.
Use the Windows Web Application Migration Assistant to migrate the applications to Amazon EC2 instances. Use the EC2 instances to deploy and manage the applications.

Refactor the applications and containerize them by using AWS Toolkit for NET Refactoring. Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) with the Fargate launch type to host the containerized applications.

questions.explanation:
Windows Web Application Migration Assistant supports migrating existing Windows/.NET web applications to a fully managed AWS Elastic Beanstalk environment. Elastic Beanstalk deploys and manages the application environment, enabling a rapid migration without refactoring or containerizing the applications. Direct use of Amazon EC2 would require the company to manage the infrastructure.

**Learn more:** [Migrate an ASP.NET Web Application to Elastic Beanstalk](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/hands-on/latest/migrate-aspnet-web-application-elastic-beanstalk/migrate-aspnet-web-application-elastic-beanstalk.html) · [AWS Elastic Beanstalk for .NET applications](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/whitepapers/latest/develop-deploy-dotnet-apps-on-aws/aws-elastic-beanstalk.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An environmental company is deploying sensors in major cities across a country to measure air quality. The sensors connect to AWS IoT Core to ingest time-series data readings. The company stores this data in Amazon DynamoDB.  
  
For business continuity, the company must be able to ingest and store data in two AWS Regions.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon Route 53 alias failover routing policy with values for AWS IoT Core data endpoints in both Regions Migrate data to Amazon Aurora global tables.

Create a domain configuration for AWS IoT Core in each Region. Create an Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing policy. Use AWS IoT Core data endpoints in both Regions as values. Migrate the data to Amazon MemoryDB for Redis and configure cross-Region replication.

Create a domain configuration for AWS IoT Core in each Region. Create an Amazon Route 53 health check that evaluates domain configuration health. Create a failover routing policy with values for the domain name from the AWS IoT Core domain configurations. Update the DynamoDB table to a global table.
Create an Amazon Route 53 latency-based routing policy. Use AWS IoT Core data endpoints in both Regions as values. Configure DynamoDB streams and cross-Region data replication.

questions.explanation:
AWS IoT Core resources and endpoints are Region-specific, so cross-Region continuity requires an IoT Core domain configuration in each Region and DNS failover to a healthy Regional endpoint. DynamoDB global tables automatically replicate a table across participating Regions, enabling the workload to store data in a local replica after Regional failover.

**Learn more:** [Resilience in AWS IoT Core](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/disaster-recovery-resiliency.html) · [Domain configurations - AWS IoT Core](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/iot/latest/developerguide/iot-custom-endpoints-configurable.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A software-as-a-service (SaaS)-based company provides customers with a case-management solution as part of its offering. The company uses a standalone Simple Mail Transfer Protocol (SMTP) server to send email messages from an application. The application also stores an email template for acknowledgement emails that populate customer data before it sends the email message to the customer.  
  
The company plans to migrate this messaging functionality to the AWS Cloud and must minimize operational overhead.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements in the MOST cost-effective manner?

options.text: Set up an SMTP server on Amazon EC2 instances by using an AMI from the AWS Marketplace. Store the email template in an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function to retrieve the template from the S3 bucket and to merge the customer data from the application with the template. Use an SDK in the Lambda function to send the email message.

Set up Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to send email messages. Store the email template in an Amazon S3 bucket. Create an AWS Lambda function to retrieve the template from the S3 bucket and to merge the customer data from the application with the template. Use an SDK in the Lambda function to send the email message.

Create an AWS Lambda function to call the SES template and to pass customer data to replace the parameters. Use the AWS Marketplace SMTP server to send the email message.

Set up Amazon Simple Email Service (Amazon SES) to send email messages. Store the email template on Amazon SES with parameters for the customer data. Create an AWS Lambda function to call the SendTemplatedEmail API operation and to pass customer data to replace the parameters and the email destination.

questions.explanation:
Amazon SES provides managed email delivery and can store reusable email templates with customer-data placeholders. The `SendTemplatedEmail` API accepts the template, replacement data, and destination, renders the personalized message, and queues it for delivery. This avoids operating EC2-based SMTP servers and avoids separate template retrieval and merge logic. [SendTemplatedEmail API](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ses/latest/APIReference/API_SendTemplatedEmail.html)

A company runs online contests through a mobile application on AWS. At the end of every contest, the company randomly chooses a winner. Contest durations vary. The company does not need to keep any contest data after that contest ends.  
  
Custom code hosted on Amazon EC2 instances processes contest data and selects a winner. The EC2 instances operate behind an Application Load Balancer and save contest entries in Amazon RDS DB instances. The company must create a new architecture that lowers the cost of operating the contests.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements in the **MOST** cost-effective way?

options.text: Migrate storage of the contest entries to Amazon DynamoDB. Create a DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster. Rewrite the code to run as Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) containers that use the Fargate launch type. At the end of the contest, delete the DynamoDB table.
Migrate the storage of the contest entries to Amazon Redshift. Rewrite the code as AWS Lambda functions. At the end of the contest, delete the Redshift cluster.

Add an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster in front of the RDS DB instances to cache the contest entries. Rewrite the code to run as Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) containers that use the Fargate launch type. Set the ElastiCache TTL attribute on each entry to expire each entry at the end of the contest.
Migrate the storage of the contest entries to Amazon DynamoDB. Rewrite the code as AWS Lambda functions. Set the DynamoDB TTL attribute on each entry to expire each entry at the end of the contest.

questions.explanation:
Amazon DynamoDB with on-demand capacity charges for actual reads and writes and has no idle throughput cost. DynamoDB TTL can automatically remove individual contest-entry items when their expiration timestamps are reached. AWS Lambda runs code without managed servers and charges for invocation duration, so it is well suited to variable, temporary workloads without retaining data after expiration.

A company runs a critical application that uses an Amazon RDS for MySQL database to store data. The RDS DB instance is deployed in Multi-AZ mode.  
  
A recent RDS database failover test resulted in a 40-second application outage. A solutions architect must design a solution that reduces the outage to less than 20 seconds.  
  
Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to satisfy these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Use Amazon ElastiCache for Memcached in front of the database
Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis in front of the database
Use RDS Proxy in front of the database.
Migrate the database to Amazon Aurora MySQL.
Create an Amazon Aurora Replica.
Create an RDS for MySQL read replica

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS Multi-AZ DB instance failovers typically take 60–120 seconds. Migrating to Amazon Aurora MySQL and providing an Aurora Replica enables a replica to be promoted as the writer during failure, which is much faster than creating a replacement writer. RDS Proxy provides a stable endpoint, preserves idle application connections, and eliminates client DNS-caching and connection-reestablishment delays while routing traffic to the new writer. Caching with ElastiCache does not reduce database failover time, and an asynchronous RDS for MySQL read replica does not provide Aurora’s in-cluster promotion behavior.

**Learn more:** [Failing over a Multi-AZ DB instance for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZ.Failover.html) · [High availability for Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Concepts.AuroraHighAvailability.html)

A company has deployed applications to thousands of Amazon EC2 instances in an AWS account. A security audit discovers that several unencrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes are attached to the EC2 instances. The company’s security policy requires the EBS volumes to be encrypted.  
  
The company needs to implement an automated solution to encrypt the EBS volumes. The solution also must prevent development teams from creating unencrypted EBS volumes.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Configure the AWS Config managed rule that identifies unencrypted EBS volumes. Configure an automatic remediation action. Associate an AWS Systems Manager Automation runbook that includes the steps to create a new encrypted EBS volume. Create an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) customer managed key. In the key policy, include a statement to deny the creation of unencrypted EBS volumes.

Use AWS Systems Manager Fleet Manager to create a list of unencrypted EBS volumes, Create a Systems Manager Automation runbook that includes the steps to create a new encrypted EBS volume. Create an SCP to deny the creation of unencrypted EBS volumes.

Use AWS Systems Manager Fleet Manager to create a list of unencrypted EBS volumes. Create a Systems Manager Automation runbook that includes the steps to create a new encrypted EBS volume. Modify the AWS account setting for EBS encryption to always encrypt new EBS volumes.

This two-pronged approach addresses both the backlog of unencrypted volumes and prevents future non-compliance.

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses an on-premises Active Directory service to authenticate users. The company wants to use that same authentication service for sign-in to the company’s AWS accounts, which use AWS Organizations. AWS Site-to-Site VPN connectivity already exists between the on-premises environment and each of the company’s AWS accounts.  
  
The company’s security policy requires conditional access to the accounts according to user groups and roles. User identities must be managed from one location.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) to connect to Active Directory by using SAML 2.0. Enable automatic provisioning by using the System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) v2.0 protocol. Grant access to the AWS accounts by using attribute-based access controls (ABACs).

Configure AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) by using IAM Identity Center as an identity source. Enable automatic provisioning by using the System for Cross-domain Identity Management (SCIM) v2.0 protocol. Grant access to the AWS accounts by using IAM Identity Center permission sets.

In one of the company’s AWS accounts, configure AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) to use a SAML 2.0 identity provider. Provision IAM users that are mapped to the federated users. Grant access that corresponds to appropriate groups in Active Directory. Grant access to the required AWS accounts by using cross-account IAM users.

Provision IAM roles that grant access to the AWS account for the federated users that correspond to appropriate groups in Active Directory. Grant access to the required AWS accounts by using cross-account IAM roles.

A company is moving a document-processing workload to AWS. The company has updated many applications to natively use the Amazon S3 API to store, retrieve, and modify documents that a processing server produces at a rate of approximately 5 documents per second. After document processing is complete, customers can download the documents directly from Amazon S3.  
  
During the migration, the company found that it could not immediately update the processing server that generates many documents to support the S3 API. The server runs on Linux and needs fast local access to the files it generates and modifies. When processing finishes, the files must be publicly available for download within 30 minutes.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements with the **LEAST** effort?

options.text: Migrate the application to an AWS Lambda function. Use the AWS SDK for Java to generate, modify, and access the files that the company stores directly in Amazon S3.

Set up an Amazon S3 File Gateway and configure a file share that is linked to the document store. Mount the file share on an Amazon EC2 instance by using NFS. When changes occur in Amazon S3, initiate a RefreshCache API call to update the S3 File Gateway.

Configure Amazon FSx for Lustre with an import and export policy. Link the new file system to an S3 bucket. Install the Lustre client and mount the document store to an Amazon EC2 instance by using NFS.
Configure AWS DataSync to connect to an Amazon EC2 instance. Configure a task to synchronize the generated files to and from Amazon S3.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 File Gateway exposes an S3 bucket through an NFS file share, writes client changes synchronously to local cache for low-latency access, and asynchronously uploads the resulting objects to Amazon S3. This lets an unchanged Linux file-based workload use standard file operations while making completed files available from S3. A RefreshCache operation updates the gateway’s cached inventory when objects are changed directly in the S3 bucket. AWS DataSync scheduled tasks have a minimum interval of one hour, so they cannot meet a 30-minute publication requirement.

A solutions architect must implement a solution so the application can accommodate the new, variable load.

questions.explanation:

Configure the IoT devices to publish to AWS IoT Core

A large payroll company has recently merged with a small staffing company. The combined company now has multiple business units, each with its own existing AWS account.  
  
A solutions architect must ensure the company can centrally manage billing and access policies across all AWS accounts. The solutions architect configures AWS Organizations by sending invitations from a centralized management account to all company member accounts.  
  
What should the solutions architect do next to satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Create the OrganizationAccountAccess IAM group in each member account. Include the necessary IAM roles for each administrator.
Create the OrganizationAccountAccessPolicy IAM policy in each member account. Connect the member accounts to the management account by using cross-account access.
Create the OrganizationAccountAccessRole IAM role in each member account. Grant permission to the management account to assume the IAM role.

Create the OrganizationAccountAccessRole IAM role in the management account. Attach the AdministratorAccess AWS managed policy to the IAM role. Assign the IAM role to the administrators in each member account.

questions.explanation:
For an existing account that joins an AWS organization by invitation, create the `OrganizationAccountAccessRole` IAM role in that member account and configure its trust policy to allow the management account to assume it. This provides the management account with cross-account administrative access to member accounts; AWS Organizations can then centrally manage the organization’s billing and policy controls.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an IoT platform on AWS. IoT sensors across multiple locations transmit data to the company’s Node.js API servers on Amazon EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. The data is stored in an Amazon RDS MySQL DB instance that uses a 4 TB General Purpose SSD volume.  
  
The number of sensors deployed in the field has grown over time and is expected to increase substantially. The API servers are continually overloaded, and RDS metrics indicate high write latency.  
  
Which of the following steps, together, will permanently resolve the issues and support growth as new sensors are provisioned while keeping the platform cost-efficient? (Choose two.)

options.text: Resize the MySQL General Purpose SSD storage to 6 TB to improve the volume’s IOPS.
Re-architect the database tier to use Amazon Aurora instead of an RDS MySQL DB instance and add read replicas.
Leverage Amazon Kinesis Data Streams and AWS Lambda to ingest and process the raw data.
Use AWS X-Ray to analyze and debug application issues and add more API servers to match the load.
Re-architect the database tier to use Amazon DynamoDB instead of an RDS MySQL DB instance.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Kinesis Data Streams provides a durable, scalable ingestion buffer, and AWS Lambda can consume and process stream records in batches and in parallel, removing synchronous sensor-ingestion pressure from the API servers. Amazon DynamoDB is a serverless, distributed NoSQL database designed for consistent performance at scale; its on-demand capacity mode automatically scales with demand and charges per read and write request. This architecture addresses the increasing write workload rather than merely increasing a relational database volume or adding read replicas, which do not solve primary write throughput.

**Learn more:** [Using Lambda to process records from Amazon Kinesis Data Streams](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-kinesis.html) · [DynamoDB on-demand capacity mode](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/on-demand-capacity-mode.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A software company hosts an application on AWS using resources across multiple AWS accounts and Regions. The application runs on a group of Amazon EC2 instances in an application VPC in the `us-east-1` Region, with an IPv4 CIDR block of `10.10.0.0/16`. In another AWS account, a shared services VPC is in the `us-east-2` Region, with an IPv4 CIDR block of `10.10.10.0/24`. When a cloud engineer uses AWS CloudFormation to try to peer the application VPC with the shared services VPC, an error message reports that peering failed.  
  
Which factors could cause this error? (Choose two.)

options.text: The IPv4 CIDR ranges of the two VPCs overlap
The VPCs are not in the same Region
One or both accounts do not have access to an Internet gateway
One of the VPCs was not shared through AWS Resource Access Manager
The IAM role in the peer accepter account does not have the correct permissions

questions.explanation:
VPC peering cannot be created when either VPC has an overlapping IPv4 CIDR block; `10.10.10.0/24` falls within `10.10.0.0/16`. Cross-account and inter-Region VPC peering is supported, but a CloudFormation-based cross-account peering setup requires a cross-account access role with the necessary permissions in the peer account. Internet gateways and AWS Resource Access Manager sharing are not prerequisites for VPC peering.

**Learn more:** [Create a VPC peering connection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/peering/create-vpc-peering-connection.html) · [Peer with a VPC in another AWS account](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/UserGuide/peer-with-vpc-in-another-account.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A weather service delivers high-resolution weather maps through a web application hosted on AWS in the eu-west-1 Region. The weather maps are updated often and are stored in Amazon S3 together with static HTML content. Amazon CloudFront fronts the web application.  
  
The company recently expanded to serve users in the us-east-1 Region, and these users intermittently report slow viewing of their weather maps.  
  
Which combination of steps will resolve the performance issues in us-east-1? (Choose two.)

options.text: Configure the AWS Global Accelerator endpoint for the S3 bucket in eu-west-1. Configure endpoint groups for TCP ports 80 and 443 in us-east-1.
Create a new S3 bucket in us-east-1. Configure S3 cross-Region replication to synchronize from the S3 bucket in eu-west-1.
Use Lambda@Edge to modify requests from North America to use the S3 Transfer Acceleration endpoint in us-east-1.
Use Lambda@Edge to modify requests from North America to use the S3 bucket in us-east-1.
Configure the AWS Global Accelerator endpoint for us-east-1 as an origin on the CloudFront distribution. Use Lambda@Edge to modify requests from North America to use the new origin.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Cross-Region Replication can maintain copies of the weather maps and static content in a bucket in us-east-1, reducing origin latency for users near that Region. Lambda@Edge can modify a CloudFront origin request according to the viewer’s country or region, directing North American requests to the closer us-east-1 S3 origin. AWS documents this pattern specifically for serving content from an S3 bucket nearer to the viewer.

**Learn more:** [Replicating objects within and across Regions - Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/replication.html) · [Lambda@Edge example functions - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/lambda-examples.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a fleet of servers on premises and a fleet of Amazon EC2 instances in AWS Organizations. The company’s AWS accounts contain hundreds of VPCs. The company needs to connect its AWS accounts to its on-premises network. AWS Site-to-Site VPN connections are already established to one AWS account. The company needs to control which VPCs can communicate with other VPCs.  
  
Which combination of steps will provide this level of control with the **LEAST** operational effort? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create a transit gateway in an AWS account. Share the transit gateway across accounts by using AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM).
Configure attachments to all VPCs and VPNs.
Setup transit gateway route tables. Associate the VPCs and VPNs with the route tables.
Configure VPC peering between the VPCs.
Configure attachments between the VPCs and VPNs.
Setup route tables on the VPCs and VPNs.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transit Gateway centrally connects VPC and Site-to-Site VPN attachments across accounts when it is shared through AWS RAM. Transit Gateway route tables associate attachments and control the routes between them, enabling segmentation of VPC-to-VPC communication without maintaining a VPC-peering mesh.

**Learn more:** [Work with AWS Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/working-with-transit-gateways.html) · [Transit gateway route tables in AWS Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/tgw-route-tables.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses an organization in AWS Organizations to manage multiple AWS accounts. The company hosts some applications in a VPC in the company's shared services account.  
  
The company has attached a transit gateway to the VPC in the shared services account.  
  
The company is developing a new capability and has created a development environment that requires access to the applications that are in the shared services account. The company intends to delete and recreate resources frequently in the development account. The company also wants to give a development team the ability to recreate the team's connection to the shared services account as required.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a transit gateway in the development account. Create a transit gateway peering request to the shared services account. Configure the shared services transit gateway to automatically accept peering connections.

Turn on automatic acceptance for the transit gateway in the shared services account. Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the transit gateway resource in the shared services account with the development account. Accept the resource in the development account. Create a transit gateway attachment in the development account.

Turn on automatic acceptance for the transit gateway in the shared services account. Create a VPC endpoint. Use the endpoint policy to grant permissions on the VPC endpoint for the development account. Configure the endpoint service to automatically accept connection requests. Provide the endpoint details to the development team.

Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function that accepts the transit gateway attachment when the development account makes an attachment request. Use AWS Network Manager to share the transit gateway in the shared services account with the development account. Accept the transit gateway in the development account.

questions.explanation:
Enabling automatic acceptance on the shared services transit gateway allows the development account to create transit gateway attachments without manual intervention from the shared services team. AWS Resource Access Manager (RAM) shares the transit gateway resource with the development account, enabling the dev team to create attachments independently as they recreate resources. This approach provides the flexibility needed for frequent resource recreation while maintaining centralized transit gateway management. TGW peering is designed for cross-Region scenarios, not cross-account sharing. VPC endpoints serve a different purpose for accessing AWS services, not for VPC interconnectivity.

**Learn more:** [Work with AWS Transit Gateway (RAM sharing)](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/working-with-transit-gateways.html) · [Accept a Transit Gateway resource share via AWS RAM](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/share-accept-tgw.html)

questions.explanation:
CORS must be configured on the Amazon API Gateway endpoint because it is the endpoint that receives the browser’s cross-origin registration request. API Gateway must return `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` for the permitted origin on its responses and provide the required preflight handling when applicable. CloudFront/S3 response headers do not authorize the separate API Gateway endpoint, and AWS WAF does not provide a CORS configuration setting.

**Learn more:** [CORS for REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-cors.html) · [Enable CORS on a resource using the API Gateway console](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-cors-console.html)

A delivery company must migrate its third-party route-planning application to AWS. The third party provides a supported Docker image in a public registry. The image can run in as many containers as needed to generate the route map.  
  
The company has split the delivery area into sections with supply hubs so delivery drivers travel the shortest possible distance from the hubs to customers. To decrease the time needed to generate route maps, each section uses its own group of Docker containers with a custom configuration that processes orders only within that section’s area.  
  
The company requires the ability to allocate resources cost-effectively according to the number of containers running.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Create an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster on Amazon EC2. Use the Amazon EKS CLI to launch the planning application in pods by using the --tags option to assign a custom tag to the pod.

Create an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster on AWS Fargate. Use the Amazon EKS CLI to launch the planning application. Use the AWS CLI tag-resource API call to assign a custom tag to the pod.

Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster on Amazon EC2. Use the AWS CLI with run-tasks set to true to launch the planning application by using the --tags option to assign a custom tag to the task.

Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster on AWS Fargate. Use the AWS CLI run-task command and set enableECSManagedTags to true to launch the planning application. Use the --tags option to assign a custom tag to the task.

questions.explanation:
Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate runs containers without requiring management of EC2 worker instances or Kubernetes control-plane and node operations. The ECS `run-task` operation can launch tasks with user-defined tags, while `enableECSManagedTags` adds ECS-managed task metadata. Task tags can distinguish the delivery section and support cost allocation for the running container workloads.

**Learn more:** [RunTask - Amazon ECS API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/APIReference/API_RunTask.html) · [Tagging Amazon ECS resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/ecs-using-tags.html)

A company needs to deploy an AWS WAF solution to manage AWS WAF rules across multiple AWS accounts. The accounts are managed in different OUs within AWS Organizations.  
  
Administrators must be able to add or remove accounts or OUs from managed AWS WAF rule sets as necessary. Administrators must also be able to automatically update and remediate noncompliant AWS WAF rules in every account.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Use AWS Firewall Manager to manage AWS WAF rules across accounts in the organization. Use an AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store parameter to store account numbers and OUs to manage. Update the parameter as needed to add or remove accounts or OUs. Use an Amazon EventBridge rule to identify any changes to the parameter and to invoke an AWS Lambda function to update the security policy in the Firewall Manager administrative account.

Deploy an organization-wide AWS Config rule that requires all resources in the selected OUs to associate the AWS WAF rules. Deploy automated remediation actions by using AWS Lambda to fix noncompliant resources. Deploy AWS WAF rules by using an AWS CloudFormation stack set to target the same OUs where the AWS Config rule is applied.

Create AWS WAF rules in the management account of the organization. Use AWS Lambda environment variables to store account numbers and OUs to manage. Update environment variables as needed to add or remove accounts or OUs. Create cross-account IAM roles in member accounts. Assume the roles by using AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) in the Lambda function to create and update AWS WAF rules in the member accounts.

Use AWS Control Tower to manage AWS WAF rules across accounts in the organization. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to store account numbers and OUs to manage. Update AWS KMS as needed to add or remove accounts or OUs. Create IAM users in member accounts. Allow AWS Control Tower in the management account to use the access key and secret access key to create and update AWS WAF rules in the member accounts.

questions.explanation:
AWS Firewall Manager provides centralized AWS WAF policy management across AWS Organizations. A policy can include specified accounts or OUs, and Firewall Manager can automatically remediate noncompliant in-scope resources. Updating the policy scope in the Firewall Manager administrative account accommodates changes to the accounts or OUs under management without building and operating organization-wide Config rules, StackSets, or custom cross-account WAF update logic.

**Learn more:** [Creating an AWS Firewall Manager policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/create-policy.html) · [Using AWS Firewall Manager policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/working-with-policies.html)

A retail company hosts an ecommerce website on AWS in multiple AWS Regions. The company requires the website to remain operational at all times for online purchases. The website stores its data in an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance.  
  
Which solution provides the **HIGHEST** database availability?

options.text: Configure automated backups on Amazon RDS. In the case of disruption, promote an automated backup to be a standalone DB instance. Direct database traffic to the promoted DB instance. Create a replacement read replica that has the promoted DB instance as its source.
Configure global tables and read replicas on Amazon RDS. Activate the cross-Region scope. In the case of disruption, use AWS Lambda to copy the read replicas from one Region to another Region.
Configure global tables and automated backups on Amazon RDS. In the case of disruption, use AWS Lambda to copy the read replicas from one Region to another Region.

Configure read replicas on Amazon RDS. In the case of disruption, promote a cross-Region and read replica to be a standalone DB instance. Direct database traffic to the promoted DB instance. Create a replacement read replica that has the promoted DB instance as its source.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon RDS for MySQL cross-Region read replica maintains a copy of the primary database in another Region. During a primary-Region disruption, the replica can be promoted to a standalone DB instance, database traffic can be redirected to it, and a replacement read replica can be created with the promoted instance as its source. This provides faster regional disaster recovery than restoring from automated backups. Amazon RDS for MySQL does not use DynamoDB global tables.

**Learn more:** [Creating a read replica in a different AWS Region](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.XRgn.html) · [Promoting a read replica to be a standalone DB instance](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/USER_ReadRepl.Promote.html)

The solutions architecture team estimates that the database will hold approximately 10 TB of data. As part of the design, they need a database solution that enables failover to a secondary Region.  
  
Which solution satisfies these business requirements at the **LOWEST** cost?

options.text: Deploy an Amazon Aurora DB cluster and take snapshots of the cluster every 5 minutes. Once a snapshot is complete, copy the snapshot to a secondary Region to serve as a backup in the event of a failure.
Deploy an Amazon RDS instance with a cross-Region read replica in a secondary Region. In the event of a failure, promote the read replica to become the primary.
Deploy an Amazon Aurora DB cluster in the primary Region and another in a secondary Region. Use AWS DMS to keep the secondary Region in sync.
Deploy an Amazon RDS instance with a read replica in the same Region. In the event of a failure, promote the read replica to become the primary.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS cross-Region read replicas maintain an asynchronously replicated copy in another AWS Region and can be promoted to a standalone DB instance for disaster recovery. This provides a secondary-Region recovery target without maintaining two independently managed Aurora clusters or repeatedly creating and copying 10 TB snapshots; a same-Region replica cannot provide Regional failover.

",["$","$L55",null,{"choices":{"A":"Change the CORS configuration on the S3 bucket. Add rules for CORS to the AllowedOrigin element for www.example.com.","B":"Enable the CORS setting in AWS WAF. Create a web ACL rule in which the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header is set to www.example.com.","C":"Enable the CORS setting on the API Gateway API endpoint. Ensure that the API endpoint is configured to return all responses that have the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header set to www.example.com.","D":"Enable the CORS setting on the Lambda function. Ensure that the return code of the function has the Access-Control-Allow-Origin header set to www.example.com."},"correctAnswer":"C","explanation":"CORS must be configured on the Amazon API Gateway endpoint because it is the endpoint that receives the browser’s cross-origin registration request. API Gateway must return `Access-Control-Allow-Origin` for the permitted origin on its responses and provide the required preflight handling when applicable. CloudFront/S3 response headers do not authorize the separate API Gateway endpoint, and AWS WAF does not provide a CORS configuration setting.

**Learn more:** [CORS for REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-cors.html) · [Enable CORS on a resource using the API Gateway console](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/how-to-cors-console.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"c620e882-b958-4128-bdaf-1448e3be64de","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02","mode":"default"}}]]
