",["$","p",null,{"children":"The company has split the delivery area into sections with supply hubs so delivery drivers travel the shortest possible distance from the hubs to customers. To decrease the time needed to generate route maps, each section uses its own group of Docker containers with a custom configuration that processes orders only within that section’s area."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"The company requires the ability to allocate resources cost-effectively according to the number of containers running."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":["Which solution meets these requirements with the ",["$","strong",null,{"children":"LEAST"}]," operational overhead?"]}],"
",["$","$L55",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster on Amazon EC2. Use the Amazon EKS CLI to launch the planning application in pods by using the --tags option to assign a custom tag to the pod.","B":"Create an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster on AWS Fargate. Use the Amazon EKS CLI to launch the planning application. Use the AWS CLI tag-resource API call to assign a custom tag to the pod.","C":"Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster on Amazon EC2. Use the AWS CLI with run-tasks set to true to launch the planning application by using the --tags option to assign a custom tag to the task.","D":"Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster on AWS Fargate. Use the AWS CLI run-task command and set enableECSManagedTags to true to launch the planning application. Use the --tags option to assign a custom tag to the task."},"correctAnswer":"D","explanation":"Amazon ECS on AWS Fargate runs containers without requiring management of EC2 worker instances or Kubernetes control-plane and node operations. The ECS `run-task` operation can launch tasks with user-defined tags, while `enableECSManagedTags` adds ECS-managed task metadata. Task tags can distinguish the delivery section and support cost allocation for the running container workloads.

**Learn more:** [RunTask - Amazon ECS API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/APIReference/API_RunTask.html) · [Tagging Amazon ECS resources](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/ecs-using-tags.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"2e08c087-8b14-46d5-bae3-80a0dad61c84","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02","mode":"default"}}]]
52:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company needs to deploy an AWS WAF solution to manage AWS WAF rules across multiple AWS accounts. The accounts are managed in different OUs within AWS Organizations."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Administrators must be able to add or remove accounts or OUs from managed AWS WAF rule sets as necessary. Administrators must also be able to automatically update and remediate noncompliant AWS WAF rules in every account."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":["Which solution satisfies these requirements with the ",["$","strong",null,{"children":"LEAST"}]," operational overhead?"]}],"
",["$","$L55",null,{"choices":{"A":"Use AWS Firewall Manager to manage AWS WAF rules across accounts in the organization. Use an AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store parameter to store account numbers and OUs to manage. Update the parameter as needed to add or remove accounts or OUs. Use an Amazon EventBridge rule to identify any changes to the parameter and to invoke an AWS Lambda function to update the security policy in the Firewall Manager administrative account.","B":"Deploy an organization-wide AWS Config rule that requires all resources in the selected OUs to associate the AWS WAF rules. Deploy automated remediation actions by using AWS Lambda to fix noncompliant resources. Deploy AWS WAF rules by using an AWS CloudFormation stack set to target the same OUs where the AWS Config rule is applied.","C":"Create AWS WAF rules in the management account of the organization. Use AWS Lambda environment variables to store account numbers and OUs to manage. Update environment variables as needed to add or remove accounts or OUs. Create cross-account IAM roles in member accounts. Assume the roles by using AWS Security Token Service (AWS STS) in the Lambda function to create and update AWS WAF rules in the member accounts.","D":"Use AWS Control Tower to manage AWS WAF rules across accounts in the organization. Use AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) to store account numbers and OUs to manage. Update AWS KMS as needed to add or remove accounts or OUs. Create IAM users in member accounts. Allow AWS Control Tower in the management account to use the access key and secret access key to create and update AWS WAF rules in the member accounts."},"correctAnswer":"A","explanation":"AWS Firewall Manager provides centralized AWS WAF policy management across AWS Organizations. A policy can include specified accounts or OUs, and Firewall Manager can automatically remediate noncompliant in-scope resources. Updating the policy scope in the Firewall Manager administrative account accommodates changes to the accounts or OUs under management without building and operating organization-wide Config rules, StackSets, or custom cross-account WAF update logic.

**Learn more:** [Creating an AWS Firewall Manager policy](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/create-policy.html) · [Using AWS Firewall Manager policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/waf/latest/developerguide/working-with-policies.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"cc5f25a1-45ea-4258-b72d-c1b5a8558d51","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02","mode":"default"}}]]

A solutions architect must migrate an on-premises legacy application to AWS. The application runs on two servers behind a load balancer. It requires a license file associated with the MAC address of the server’s network adapter. The software vendor takes 12 hours to send new license files. The application also uses configuration files containing a static IP address to access a database server; host names are not supported.  
  
Given these requirements, which combination of steps should be taken to implement a highly available architecture for the application servers in AWS? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create a pool of ENIs. Request license files from the vendor for the pool, and store the license files in Amazon S3. Create a bootstrap automation script to download a license file and attach the corresponding ENI to an Amazon EC2 instance.

Create a pool of ENIs. Request license files from the vendor for the pool, store the license files on an Amazon EC2 instance. Create an AMI from the instance and use this AMI for all future EC2 instances.
Create a bootstrap automation script to request a new license file from the vendor .When the response is received, apply the license file to an Amazon EC2 instance.
Edit the bootstrap automation script to read the database server IP address from the AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store, and inject the value into the local configuration files.
Edit an Amazon EC2 instance to include the database server IP address in the configuration files and re-create the AMI to use for all future EC2 stances.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon EC2 elastic network interface (ENI) retains its attributes when detached and reattached to another instance, allowing a pre-licensed MAC address to be attached to a replacement instance without waiting 12 hours for a vendor-issued license. Storing the associated license files in Amazon S3 and retrieving the matching file during bootstrap supports replacement instances. AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store centrally stores configuration values, so bootstrap automation can retrieve the database server’s current static IP address and inject it into the local configuration files.

**Learn more:** [Elastic network interfaces - Amazon EC2](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/us_en/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/using-eni.html) · [AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/systems-manager-parameter-store.html)

A company operates a latency-sensitive trading platform that uses Amazon DynamoDB as its storage backend. The company configured the DynamoDB table to use on-demand capacity mode. A solutions architect must design a solution to improve the trading platform’s performance. The new solution must provide high availability for the trading platform.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **lowest latency**?

options.text: Create a two-node DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster. Configure an application to read and write data by using DAX.
Create a three-node DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster. Configure an application to read data by using DAX and to write data directly to the DynamoDB table.
Create a three-node DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster. Configure an application to read data directly from the DynamoDB table and to write data by using DAX.
Create a single-node DynamoDB Accelerator (DAX) cluster. Configure an application to read data by using DAX and to write data directly to the DynamoDB table.

questions.explanation:
DAX serves cached DynamoDB reads from in-memory storage, reducing read latency. A three-node DAX cluster deployed across Availability Zones provides fault tolerance and high availability. Sending writes directly to DynamoDB uses a write-around approach that avoids the added work of DAX write-through caching, while reads still benefit from the DAX cache.

**Learn more:** [DAX and DynamoDB consistency models](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.consistency.html) · [DAX cluster components](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/amazondynamodb/latest/developerguide/DAX.concepts.cluster.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses AWS CloudFormation to deploy its infrastructure. The company is concerned that, if a production CloudFormation stack is deleted, important data in Amazon RDS databases or Amazon EBS volumes could be deleted as well.  
  
How can the company keep users from accidentally deleting data this way?

options.text: Modify the CloudFormation templates to add a DeletionPolicy attribute to RDS and EBS resources.
Configure a stack policy that disallows the deletion of RDS and EBS resources.
Modify IAM policies lo deny deleting RDS and EBS resources that are tagged with an
Use AWS Config rules to prevent deleting RDS and EBS resources.

questions.explanation:
The CloudFormation `DeletionPolicy` attribute controls what happens to an individual resource when its stack is deleted. Setting it to `Retain` preserves the RDS database or EBS volume and its contents after stack deletion; for supported resources, `Snapshot` can preserve recoverable data before deletion. CloudFormation stack policies apply to stack updates, rather than protecting resources during deletion of the entire stack.

**Learn more:** [DeletionPolicy attribute - AWS CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-attribute-deletionpolicy.html) · [AWS::EC2::Volume - AWS CloudFormation](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSCloudFormation/latest/TemplateReference/aws-resource-ec2-volume.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company developed an application that runs on Windows Server in VMware vSphere VMs hosted on premises. The application data is kept in a proprietary format that must be accessed through the application. The company manually provisioned both the servers and the application.  
  
As part of its disaster recovery plan, the company needs to host the application on AWS temporarily if its on-premises environment becomes unavailable. The company wants the application to return to on-premises hosting after the disaster recovery event is complete. The RPO is 5 minutes.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Configure AWS DataSync. Replicate the data to Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. When the on-premises environment is unavailable, use AWS CloudFormation templates to provision Amazon EC2 instances and attach the EBS volumes.

Configure AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery. Replicate the data to replication Amazon EC2 instances that are attached to Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes. When the on-premises environment is unavailable, use Elastic Disaster Recovery to launch EC2 instances that use the replicated volumes.

Provision an AWS Storage Gateway file gateway. Replicate the data to an Amazon S3 bucket. When the on-premises environment is unavailable, use AWS Backup to restore the data to Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes and launch Amazon EC2 instances from these EBS volumes.

Provision an Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system on AWS. Replicate the data to the file system. When the on-premises environment is unavailable, use AWS CloudFormation templates to provision Amazon EC2 instances and use AWS::CloudFormation::Init commands to mount the Amazon FSx file shares.

questions.explanation:
AWS Elastic Disaster Recovery provides continuous block-level replication of the on-premises server volumes to an AWS staging area, enabling very low RPOs and launch of recovery EC2 instances from the replicated state. It also supports replicating changes from recovery instances back to the on-premises source infrastructure for failback. This protects the complete manually provisioned Windows application and its proprietary data without requiring separate file-level replication, restores, or custom infrastructure automation.

**Learn more:** [Elastic Disaster Recovery Concepts](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/drs/latest/userguide/CloudEndure-Concepts.html) · [Using Elastic Disaster Recovery for recovery and failback](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/drs/latest/userguide/failback.html)

A company hosts a data-processing application on Amazon EC2 instances. The application polls an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system for newly uploaded files. When a new file is detected, the application extracts data from the file and runs logic to select a Docker container image to process the file. The application starts the appropriate container image and passes the file location as a parameter.  
  
The data processing that the container performs can take up to 2 hours. When the processing is complete, the code that runs inside the container writes the file back to Amazon EFS and exits.  
  
The company needs to refactor the application to eliminate the EC2 instances that are running the containers.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. Configure the processing to run as AWS Fargate tasks. Extract the container selection logic to run as an Amazon EventBridge rule that starts the appropriate Fargate task. Configure the EventBridge rule to run when files are added to the EFS file system.

Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. Configure the processing to run as AWS Fargate tasks. Update and containerize the container selection logic to run as a Fargate service that starts the appropriate Fargate task. Configure an EFS event notification to invoke the Fargate service when files are added to the EFS file system.

Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. Configure the processing to run as AWS Fargate tasks. Extract the container selection logic to run as an AWS Lambda function that starts the appropriate Fargate task. Migrate the storage of file uploads to an Amazon S3 bucket. Update the processing code to use Amazon S3. Configure an S3 event notification to invoke the Lambda function when objects are created.

Create AWS Lambda container images for the processing. Configure Lambda functions to use the container images. Extract the container selection logic to run as a decision Lambda function that invokes the appropriate Lambda processing function. Migrate the storage of file uploads to an Amazon S3 bucket. Update the processing code to use Amazon S3. Configure an S3 event notification to invoke the decision Lambda function when objects are created.

questions.explanation:
EFS does not support event notifications, eliminating options A and B. Lambda container images cannot sustain 2-hour executions (option D uses standard Lambda limits). Option C uses Fargate for long-running container tasks (up to 15+ hours), AWS Lambda for lightweight orchestration logic, and S3 for file storage with native event notification support. This migrates away from EC2 while preserving container execution capabilities.

**Learn more:** [Architect for AWS Fargate for Amazon ECS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/AWS_Fargate.html) · [Process Amazon S3 event notifications with Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/with-s3.html)

A company processes videos in the AWS Cloud by using Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group. Processing a video takes 30 minutes. Several EC2 instances scale in and out based on the number of videos in an Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) queue.  
  
The company has configured the SQS queue with a redrive policy that specifies a target dead-letter queue and a `maxReceiveCount` of 1. The company has set the SQS queue visibility timeout to 1 hour. The company has configured an Amazon CloudWatch alarm to notify the development team when messages are in the dead-letter queue.  
  
Several times each day, the development team is notified that messages are in the dead-letter queue and that videos have not been processed properly. An investigation finds no errors in the application logs.  
  
How can the company resolve this problem?

options.text: Turn on termination protection tor the EC2 Instances
Update the visibility timeout for the SQS queue to 3 hours
Configure scale-in protection for the instances during processing
Update the redrive policy and set maxReceiveCount to 0.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling has no inherent visibility into whether an instance is processing a long-running job and can terminate it during a scale-in event. Instance scale-in protection prevents Auto Scaling from selecting an actively processing instance for termination; the protection can be removed after processing completes. This prevents the SQS message from being left undeleted and subsequently reaching the dead-letter queue after another receive.

**Learn more:** [Design your applications to gracefully handle instance termination](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/gracefully-handle-instance-termination.html) · [Change instance termination protection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AWSEC2/latest/UserGuide/Using_ChangingDisableAPITermination.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A team gathers and routes behavioral data for an entire company. A solutions architect must review the infrastructure. The solutions architect needs to lower costs while preserving application functionality. What should the solutions architect do to meet these requirements?

Enable VPC Flow Logs and Amazon Detective. Review Detective findings for traffic that is not related to Kinesis Data Streams. Configure security groups to block that traffic.

questions.explanation:

A company operates its application on Amazon EC2 instances and AWS Lambda functions. The EC2 instances have a continuous, stable load. The Lambda functions have a variable and unpredictable load. The application has a caching layer that uses an Amazon MemoryDB for Redis cluster.  
  
A solutions architect must recommend a solution that minimizes the company's total monthly costs.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Purchase an EC2 instance Savings Plan to cover the EC2 instances. Purchase a Compute Savings Plan for Lambda to cover the minimum expected consumption of the Lambda functions. Purchase reserved nodes to cover the MemoryDB cache nodes.
Purchase a Compute Savings Plan to cover the EC2 instances. Purchase Lambda reserved concurrency to cover the expected Lambda usage. Purchase reserved nodes to cover the MemoryDB cache nodes.
Purchase a Compute Savings Plan to cover the entire expected cost of the EC2 instances, Lambda functions, and MemoryDB cache nodes.
Purchase a Compute Savings Plan to cover the EC2 instances and the MemoryDB cache nodes. Purchase Lambda reserved concurrency to cover the expected Lambda usage.

questions.explanation:
EC2 Instance Savings Plans provide the highest Savings Plan discount for stable EC2 usage within a selected instance family and Region. Compute Savings Plans cover EC2 and Lambda usage, so they can be applied only to the predictable minimum Lambda consumption while variable usage remains on demand. Amazon MemoryDB uses reserved nodes for commitment-based discounts; it is not eligible for Compute Savings Plans. Lambda reserved concurrency controls available concurrency and has no additional charge, so it does not provide a usage discount.

**Learn more:** [Compute Savings Plans and Reserved Instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/latest/userguide/sp-ris.html) · [Services eligible for Savings Plans benefits](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/savingsplans/latest/userguide/sp-services.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has numerous separate AWS accounts and has no centralized billing or management. Each AWS account runs services for distinct departments within the company. The company has a deployed Microsoft Azure Active Directory.

Which combination of steps will satisfy these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create a new AWS account to serve as a management account. Deploy an organization in AWS Organizations. Invite each existing AWS account to join the organization. Ensure that each account accepts the invitation.

Create AWS IAM Identity Center (AWS Single Sign-On) permission sets. Attach the permission sets to the appropriate IAM Identity Center groups and AWS accounts.
Configure AWS Identity and Access Management (IAM) in each AWS account to use AWS Managed Microsoft AD for authentication and authorization.

questions.explanation:

IAM Identity Center integrates with external identity providers such as Microsoft Entra ID (Azure AD) and can provision users and groups automatically through SCIM. A company is modifying how it manages patching for Amazon EC2 instances in its application account. At present, the company patches the instances through the internet by using a NAT gateway in a VPC in the application account.  
  
The company has EC2 instances configured as a patch source repository in a dedicated private VPC in a core account. The company wants to use AWS Systems Manager Patch Manager and the patch source repository in the core account to patch the EC2 instances in the application account. The company must stop all EC2 instances in the application account from accessing the internet.  
  
The EC2 instances in the application account must access Amazon S3, where the application data is stored. These EC2 instances require connectivity to Systems Manager and to the patch source repository in the private VPC in the core account.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements?

options.text: Create a network ACL that blocks outbound traffic on port 80. Associate the network ACL with all subnets in the application account. In the application account and the core account, deploy one EC2 instance that runs a custom VPN server. Create a VPN tunnel to access the private VPC. Update the route table in the application account.

Create private VIFs for Systems Manager and Amazon S3. Delete the NAT gateway from the VPC in the application account. Create a transit gateway to access the patch source repository EC2 instances in the core account. Update the route table in the core account.

Create VPC endpoints for Systems Manager and Amazon S3. Delete the NAT gateway from the VPC in the application account. Create a VPC peering connection to access the patch source repository EC2 instances in the core account. Update the route tables in both accounts.

Create a network ACL that blocks inbound traffic on port 80. Associate the network ACL with all subnets in the application account. Create a transit gateway to access the patch source repository EC2 instances in the core account. Update the route tables in both accounts.

questions.explanation:
Systems Manager interface VPC endpoints provide private connectivity for managed EC2 instances without an internet gateway or NAT device, and an Amazon S3 VPC endpoint provides private S3 access. Removing the NAT gateway prevents internet egress. VPC peering, with routes configured in both VPC route tables, provides private IP connectivity between the application VPC and the core VPC that hosts the patch source repository.

**Learn more:** [Improve the security of EC2 instances by using VPC endpoints for Systems Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/setup-create-vpc.html) · [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html)

A solutions architect must develop a business case to migrate a company's on-premises data center to the AWS Cloud. The solutions architect will use a configuration management database (CMDB) export containing all of the company's servers to create the case.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements in the MOST cost-effective manner?

options.text: Use AWS Well-Architected Tool to import the CMDB data to perform an analysis and generate recommendations.
Use Migration Evaluator to perform an analysis. Use the data import template to upload the data from the CMDB export.
Implement resource matching rules. Use the CMDB export and the AWS Price List Bulk API to query CMDB data against AWS services in bulk.
Use AWS Application Discovery Service to import the CMDB data to perform an analysis.

questions.explanation:
AWS Migration Evaluator creates migration business cases and supports manually importing IT asset data from discovery sources, including CMDB extracts. Using its data import template enables the server inventory to be analyzed for the migration assessment without building custom resource-matching and pricing logic.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has introduced a new security requirement. Under this requirement, the company must scan all traffic from corporate AWS instances in the company’s VPC for violations of its security policies. Based on these scans, the company can block access to and from particular IP addresses.  
  
To satisfy the new requirement, the company deploys a group of Amazon EC2 instances in private subnets to act as transparent proxies. The company installs approved proxy-server software on these EC2 instances. The company updates the route tables on every subnet to use the applicable EC2 instances running the proxy software as the default route. The company also creates security groups that comply with the security policies and assigns those security groups to the EC2 instances.  
  
Despite these configurations, traffic from the EC2 instances in the private subnets is not being forwarded correctly to the internet.  
  
What should a solutions architect do to fix this issue?

options.text: Disable source/destination checks on the EC2 instances that run the proxy software.

Add a rule to the security group that is assigned to the proxy EC2 instances to allow all traffic between instances that have this security group. Assign this security group to all EC2 instances in the VPC.
Change the VPCs DHCP options set. Set the DNS server options to point to the addresses of the proxy EC2 instances.

Assign one additional elastic network interface to each proxy EC2 instance. Ensure that one of these network interfaces has a route to the private subnets. Ensure that the other network interface has a route to the internet.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EC2 source/destination checks are enabled by default, allowing an instance to send or receive only traffic for which it is the source or destination. A transparent proxy forwards transit traffic for other hosts, so source/destination checks must be disabled on the proxy instances for forwarding to work. [AWS: Enable private resources to communicate outside the VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/work-with-nat-instances.html)

A solutions architect is assessing an application's resilience before launch. The application runs on an Amazon EC2 instance deployed in a private subnet of a VPC. An Auto Scaling group provisions the EC2 instance and has a minimum capacity of 1 and a maximum capacity of 1. The application stores data on an Amazon RDS for MySQL DB instance. The VPC has subnets configured across three Availability Zones and uses a single NAT gateway.  
  
The solutions architect must recommend a solution that ensures the application operates across multiple Availability Zones.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Deploy an additional NAT gateway in the other Availability Zones. Update the route tables with appropriate routes. Modify the RDS for MySQL DB instance to a Multi-AZ configuration. Configure the Auto Scaling group to launch the instances across Availability Zones. Set the minimum capacity and maximum capacity of the Auto Scaling group to 3.

Replace the NAT gateway with a virtual private gateway. Replace the RDS for MySQL DB instance with an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster. Configure the Auto Scaling group to launch instances across all subnets in the VPC. Set the minimum capacity and maximum capacity of the Auto Scaling group to 3.
Replace the NAT gateway with a NAT instance. Migrate the RDS for MySQL DB instance to an RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance. Launch a new EC2 instance in the other Availability Zones.

Deploy an additional NAT gateway in the other Availability Zones. Update the route tables with appropriate routes. Modify the RDS for MySQL DB instance to turn on automatic backups and retain the backups for 7 days. Configure the Auto Scaling group to launch instances across all subnets in the VPC. Keep the minimum capacity and the maximum capacity of the Auto Scaling group at 1.

questions.explanation:
A resilient multi-AZ architecture requires redundancy in the compute, database, and outbound-networking layers. An Auto Scaling group spanning Availability Zones distributes instances across those zones; setting its minimum and maximum capacity to 3 maintains three instances. An RDS for MySQL Multi-AZ deployment maintains a synchronous standby in a different Availability Zone for failover. A NAT gateway is zonal, so deploying one in each Availability Zone and routing each private subnet to its local NAT gateway prevents the loss of one NAT gateway’s Availability Zone from removing internet access for workloads in the other zones.

**Learn more:** [NAT gateway basics](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/nat-gateway-basics.html) · [Multi-AZ DB instance deployments for Amazon RDS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/UserGuide/Concepts.MultiAZSingleStandby.html)

A company plans to migrate its workloads from on premises to AWS. The workloads operate on Linux and Windows. The company has a large on-premises infrastructure consisting of physical machines and VMs that host many applications.  
  
The company must collect details about the system configuration, system performance, running processes, and network connections of its on-premises workloads. The company must also group the on-premises applications for AWS migrations. The company needs recommendations for Amazon EC2 instance types so it can run its workloads on AWS as cost-effectively as possible.  
  
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect take to satisfy these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Assess the existing applications by installing AWS Application Discovery Agent on the physical machines and VMs.
Assess the existing applications by installing AWS Systems Manager Agent on the physical machines and VMs.
Group servers into applications for migration by using AWS Systems Manager Application Manager.
Group servers into applications for migration by using AWS Migration Hub.
Generate recommended instance types and associated costs by using AWS Migration Hub.
Import data about server sizes into AWS Trusted Advisor. Follow the recommendations for cost optimization.

questions.explanation:
AWS Application Discovery Agent collects system configuration, performance, running-process, and network-connection data from supported Linux and Windows physical servers and VMs. AWS Migration Hub uses discovered server information to group servers into applications, and its EC2 instance recommendations provide least-cost suitable instance types along with associated pricing.

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs a compute workload using Amazon EC2 Spot Instances in an Auto Scaling group. The launch template specifies two placement groups and one instance type.  
  
Recently, a monitoring system has reported Auto Scaling instance-launch failures that correlate with longer wait times for system users. The company must improve the workload’s overall reliability.  
  
Which solution meets this requirement?

options.text: Replace the launch template with a launch configuration to use an Auto Scaling group that uses attribute-based instance type selection.
Create a new launch template version that uses attribute-based instance type selection. Configure the Auto Scaling group to use the new launch template version.
Update the launch template Auto Scaling group to increase the number of placement groups.
Update the launch template to use a larger instance type.

questions.explanation:
Attribute-based instance type selection lets Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling choose from a broad range of instance types that match defined compute requirements. For Spot capacity, this flexibility increases the likelihood of finding available capacity and avoids the launch failures associated with relying on one instance type. A new launch template version can define the instance attributes, and the Auto Scaling group can be configured to use that version.

**Learn more:** [Create mixed instances group using attribute-based instance type selection](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/create-mixed-instances-group-attribute-based-instance-type-selection.html) · [Create a launch template for an Auto Scaling group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/create-launch-template.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs an application on multiple Amazon EC2 instances in an Auto Scaling group behind an Application Load Balancer. Application load fluctuates during the day, and EC2 instances scale in and out regularly. Log files from the EC2 instances are copied to a central Amazon S3 bucket every 15 minutes. The security team finds that log files are missing from certain terminated EC2 instances.  
  
Which set of actions will ensure that log files from terminated EC2 instances are copied to the central S3 bucket?

options.text: Create a script to copy log files to Amazon S3, and store the script in a file on the EC2 instance. Create an Auto Scaling lifecycle hook and an Amazon EventBridge rule to detect lifecycle events from the Auto Scaling group. Invoke an AWS Lambda function on the autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATING transition to send ABANDON to the Auto Scaling group to prevent termination, run the script to copy the log files, and terminate the instance using the AWS SDK.

Create an AWS Systems Manager document with a script to copy log files to Amazon S3. Create an Auto Scaling lifecycle hook and an Amazon EventBridge rule to detect lifecycle events from the Auto Scaling group. Invoke an AWS Lambda function on the autoscaling:EC2_INSTANCE_TERMINATING transition to call the AWS Systems Manager API SendCommand operation to run the document to copy the log files and send CONTINUE to the Auto Scaling group to terminate the instance.

Change the log delivery rate to every 5 minutes. Create a script to copy log files to Amazon S3, and add the script to EC2 instance user data. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to detect EC2 instance termination. Invoke an AWS Lambda function from the EventBridge rule that uses the AWS CLI to run the user-data script to copy the log files and terminate the instance.

Create an AWS Systems Manager document with a script to copy log files to Amazon S3. Create an Auto Scaling lifecycle hook that publishes a message to an Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) topic. From the SNS notification, call the AWS Systems Manager API SendCommand operation to run the document to copy the log files and send ABANDON to the Auto Scaling group to terminate the instance.

questions.explanation:
An Auto Scaling termination lifecycle hook holds an instance in a wait state so a custom task can copy its logs before termination. EventBridge can trigger Lambda for the termination lifecycle event, and Lambda can use Systems Manager Run Command to execute an SSM document on the instance. Completing the terminating lifecycle action with `CONTINUE` permits the Auto Scaling group to finish termination after the log-copy task; `ABANDON` causes immediate termination for a terminating instance.

**Learn more:** [Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling lifecycle hooks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/lifecycle-hooks.html) · [Complete a lifecycle action in an Auto Scaling group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/completing-lifecycle-hooks.html)

A company is migrating a legacy application from an on-premises data center to AWS. The application uses MongoDB as a key-value database. Under the company’s technical guidelines, all Amazon EC2 instances must reside in a private subnet with no internet connection. Additionally, all connectivity between applications and databases must be encrypted. The database must be capable of scaling according to demand.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create new Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) tables for the application with Provisioned IOPS volumes. Use the instance endpoint to connect to Amazon DocumentDB.
Create new Amazon DynamoDB tables for the application with on-demand capacity. Use a gateway VPC endpoint for DynamoDB to connect to the DynamoDB tables.
Create new Amazon DynamoDB tables for the application with on-demand capacity. Use an interface VPC endpoint for DynamoDB to connect to the DynamoDB tables.
Create new Amazon DocumentDB (with MongoDB compatibility) tables for the application with Provisioned IOPS volumes. Use the cluster endpoint to connect to Amazon DocumentDB.

questions.explanation:
Amazon DocumentDB provides MongoDB compatibility for existing MongoDB applications, operates in Amazon VPC, and supports TLS for encrypted database connections. The cluster endpoint connects to the current primary instance for read and write operations and is the recommended connection method for production applications; it avoids dependence on an individual instance endpoint. Amazon DocumentDB storage scales automatically, while compute and read capacity can be scaled as workload demand changes.

**Learn more:** [Amazon DocumentDB: how it works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/documentdb/latest/devguide/how-it-works.html) · [Scaling Amazon DocumentDB clusters](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/documentdb/latest/devguide/db-cluster-manage-performance.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to migrate an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster from an existing AWS account to a new AWS account in the same AWS Region. Both accounts belong to the same organization in AWS Organizations.  
  
The company must minimize database service interruption before performing DNS cutover to the new database.  
  
Which migration strategies will meet this requirement? (Choose two.)

options.text: Take a snapshot of the existing Aurora database. Share the snapshot with the new AWS account. Create an Aurora DB cluster in the new account from the snapshot.
Create an Aurora DB cluster in the new AWS account. Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate data between the two Aurora DB clusters.
Use AWS Backup to share an Aurora database backup from the existing AWS account to the new AWS account. Create an Aurora DB cluster in the new AWS account from the snapshot.
Create an Aurora DB cluster in the new AWS account. Use AWS Application Migration Service to migrate data between the two Aurora DB clusters.

questions.explanation:
A shared manual Aurora DB cluster snapshot can seed a new Aurora cluster in the target account without taking the source database out of service. AWS DMS can then perform a full load and continue change data capture (CDC) so that changes made on the source are replicated to the target until cutover, limiting disruption to the final switchover. AWS Application Migration Service migrates servers, not database data.

**Learn more:** [Sharing a DB cluster snapshot - Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-share-snapshot.html) · [Auto migrating databases to Amazon Aurora using AWS Database Migration Service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/USER_DMS_migration.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company operates an ecommerce application in one AWS Region. The application uses a five-node Amazon Aurora MySQL DB cluster to store customer information and their recent orders. The DB cluster receives a high volume of write transactions during the day.  
  
The company must replicate the Aurora database data to another Region to satisfy disaster recovery requirements. The company has an RPO of 1 hour.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements at the **LOWEST** cost?

options.text: Modify the Aurora database to be an Aurora global database. Create a second Aurora database in another Region.
Enable the Backtrack feature for the Aurora database. Create an AWS Lambda function that runs daily to copy the snapshots of the database to a backup Region.
Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS). Create a DMS change data capture (CDC) task that replicates the ongoing changes from the Aurora database to an Amazon S3 bucket in another Region.
Turn off automated Aurora backups. Configure Aurora backups with a backup frequency of 1 hour. Specify another Region as the destination Region. Select the Aurora database as the resource assignment.

questions.explanation:
An AWS DMS change data capture task can continuously stream ongoing writes from the Aurora cluster to an S3 bucket in the target Region, comfortably meeting a one-hour RPO without paying for a running secondary database cluster. Aurora Global Database gives sub-second lag but requires provisioned compute and storage in the second Region around the clock, and hourly snapshot-copy or Backtrack-based approaches add scheduling overhead and slower recovery without lowering cost as much as landing incremental changes in S3.

**Learn more:** [Ongoing replication using AWS DMS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_Task.CDC.html)

options.text: Create a Direct Connect gateway in the central account. In each of the accounts, create an association proposal by using the Direct Connect gateway and the account ID for every virtual private gateway.
Create a Direct Connect gateway and a transit gateway in the central network account. Attach the transit gateway to the Direct Connect gateway by using a transit VIF.
Provision an internet gateway. Attach the internet gateway to subnets. Allow internet traffic through the gateway.
Share the transit gateway with other accounts. Attach VPCs to the transit gateway.
Provision VPC peering as necessary.

Provision only private subnets. Open the necessary route on the transit gateway and customer gateway to allow outbound internet traffic from AWS to flow through NAT services that run in the data center.

questions.explanation:
A Direct Connect gateway associated with a transit gateway over a transit VIF connects the on-premises Direct Connect network to VPCs attached to the transit gateway. AWS Resource Access Manager can share a transit gateway across accounts so each account can attach its VPCs. Routing private-subnet default traffic through the transit gateway to NAT services in the on-premises data center ensures that outbound internet access follows the required centralized on-premises egress path. [Direct Connect gateways and Transit Gateway associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-transit-gateways.html) [Work with AWS Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/working-with-transit-gateways.html)

**Learn more:** [Direct Connect gateways and Transit Gateway associations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/directconnect/latest/UserGuide/direct-connect-transit-gateways.html) · [Work with AWS Transit Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/tgw/working-with-transit-gateways.html)

A company is migrating infrastructure for its massive multiplayer game to AWS. The game’s application features a leaderboard where players can see rankings in real time. The leaderboard requires microsecond reads and single-digit-millisecond write latencies. The datasets are single-digit terabytes in size and must be available to accept writes in less than a minute if a primary node failure occurs.  
  
The company needs a solution in which data can persist for further analytical processing through a data pipeline.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements with the LEAST operational overhead?

options.text: Create an Amazon ElastiCache tor Redis cluster with cluster mode enabled, Configure the application to interact with the primary node.
Create an Amazon ROS database with a read replica. Configure the application to point writes to the writer endpoint. Configure the application to point reads to the reader endpoint.
Create an Amazon MemoryDB for Redis cluster in Muit-AZ mode Configure the application to interact with the primary node.
Create multiple Redis nodes on Amazon EC2 instances that are spread across multiple Availability Zones. Configure backups to Amazon S3.

questions.explanation:
Amazon MemoryDB for Redis is a fully managed, Multi-AZ in-memory database that delivers microsecond read and single-digit-millisecond write latencies while durably persisting data with a transaction log, so it can feed a downstream analytics pipeline. Its Multi-AZ architecture automatically fails over to a replica in under a minute on a primary node failure, meeting the durability and failover requirements with far less operational overhead than self-managing Redis on EC2 or pairing ElastiCache with a separate durable store.

**Learn more:** [Amazon MemoryDB for Redis](https://aws.amazon.com/memorydb/)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A retail company has organized its AWS accounts within an AWS Organizations organization. The company has configured consolidated billing and mapped its departments to these OUs: Finance, Sales, Human Resources (HR), Marketing, and Operations. Each OU contains multiple AWS accounts, with one account for each environment in a department. These environments are development, test, pre-production, and production.  
  
The HR department is releasing a new system that will launch in 3 months. To prepare, the HR department has purchased several Reserved Instances (RIs) in its production AWS account. The HR department will deploy the new application in this account. The HR department needs to ensure that other departments cannot share the RI discounts.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: In the AWS Billing and Cost Management console for the HR department's production account turn off RI sharing.
Remove the HR department's production AWS account from the organization. Add the account 10 the consolidating billing configuration only.
In the AWS Billing and Cost Management console. use the organization’s management account 10 turn off RI Sharing for the HR departments production AWS account.
Create an SCP in the organization to restrict access to the RIs. Apply the SCP to the OUs of the other departments.

questions.explanation:
With AWS Organizations consolidated billing, RI discounts can be shared among member accounts. The organization’s management account can deactivate Reserved Instance and Savings Plans discount sharing for a specific member account in Billing preferences. Disabling sharing for the HR production account keeps its RI discount from being used by other departmental accounts; SCPs do not govern RI discount sharing.

**Learn more:** [Reserved Instances and Savings Plans discount sharing - AWS Billing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/ri-turn-off.html) · [Customizing your Billing preferences - AWS Billing](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/billing-pref.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has five development teams, each of which has created five AWS accounts to develop and host applications. To monitor spending, the development teams sign in to every account monthly, note the current cost in the AWS Billing and Cost Management console, and submit that information to the company’s finance team.  
  
The company has strict compliance requirements and must ensure that resources are created only in AWS Regions in the United States. However, some resources have been created in other Regions.  
  
A solutions architect must implement a solution that enables the finance team to track and consolidate expenditures across all accounts. The solution must also ensure that the company can create resources only in Regions in the United States.  
  
Which combination of steps meets these requirements in the **MOST** operationally efficient manner? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create a new account to serve as a management account. Create an Amazon S3 bucket for the finance team. Use AWS Cost and Usage Reports to create monthly reports and to store the data in the finance team's S3 bucket.

Create a new account to serve as a management account. Deploy an organization in AWS Organizations with all features enabled. Invite all the existing accounts to the organization. Ensure that each account accepts the invitation.
Create an OU that includes all the development teams. Create an SCP that allows the creation of resources only in Regions that are in the United States. Apply the SCP to the OU.
Create an OU that includes all the development teams. Create an SCP that denies the creation of resources in Regions that are outside the United States. Apply the SCP to the OU.

Create an IAM role in the management account. Attach a policy that includes permissions to view the Billing and Cost Management console. Allow the finance team users to assume the role. Use AWS Cost Explorer and the Billing and Cost Management console to analyze cost.
Create an IAM role in each AWS account. Attach a policy that includes permissions to view the Billing and Cost Management console. Allow the finance team users to assume the role.

questions.explanation:
AWS Organizations consolidates billing for member accounts, and the management account can view combined costs and Billing and Cost Management information for those accounts. Inviting the existing accounts into an organization with all features enabled provides the policy-governance structure. An SCP attached to the OU that explicitly denies actions outside the permitted U.S. Regions prevents creation of regional resources elsewhere. A finance-team role in the management account with billing-view permissions provides centralized access to analyze the consolidated data through Cost Explorer and Billing and Cost Management.

**Learn more:** [Consolidating billing for AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/consolidated-billing.html) · [Controlling access to Cost Explorer](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/cost-management/latest/userguide/ce-access.html)

A company operates multiple AWS accounts. A recent security audit found many unencrypted Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volumes attached to Amazon EC2 instances.  
  
A solutions architect must encrypt the unencrypted volumes and make sure that unencrypted volumes are automatically detected in the future. The company also wants a solution that centrally manages multiple AWS accounts, with an emphasis on compliance and security.  
  
Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to fulfill these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Set up AWS Control Tower, and turn on the strongly recommended controls (guardrails). Join all accounts to the organization. Categorize the AWS accounts into OUs.
Use the AWS CLI to list all the unencrypted volumes in all the AWS accounts. Run a script to encrypt all the unencrypted volumes in place.
Create a snapshot of each unencrypted volume. Create a new encrypted volume from the unencrypted snapshot. Detach the existing volume, and replace it with the encrypted volume.
Create an organization in AWS Organizations. Set up AWS Control Tower, and turn on the mandatory controls (guardrails). Join all accounts to the organization. Categorize the AWS accounts into OUs.
Turn on AWS CloudTrail. Configure an Amazon EventBridge rule to detect and automatically encrypt unencrypted volumes.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EBS cannot encrypt an existing unencrypted volume directly. The supported migration is to create a snapshot, create a new encrypted volume from that snapshot, and replace the original volume. AWS Control Tower, built on AWS Organizations and organized with OUs, centrally governs multi-account environments. Its strongly recommended detective controls include a control that detects whether EBS volumes attached to EC2 instances are encrypted.

**Learn more:** [Amazon EBS encryption](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-encryption.html) · [Strongly recommended controls with detective behavior - AWS Control Tower](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/controltower/latest/controlreference/strongly-recommended-detective-controls.html)

A company plans to containerize a multi-tier web application and migrate it from an on-premises data center to AWS. The application has web, application, and database tiers. The company must make the application fault tolerant and scalable. Some frequently accessed data must remain available across application servers. Frontend web servers require session persistence and must scale for increases in traffic.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements with the **LEAST** ongoing operational overhead?

options.text: Run the application on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on AWS Fargate. Use Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) for data that is frequently accessed between the web and application tiers. Store the frontend web server session data in Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS).

Run the application on Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) on Amazon EC2. Use Amazon ElastiCache for Redis to cache frontend web server session data. Use Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) with Multi-Attach on EC2 instances that are distributed across multiple Availability Zones.

Run the application on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Configure Amazon EKS to use managed node groups. Use ReplicaSets to run the web servers and applications. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system. Mount the EFS file system across all EKS pods to store frontend web server session data.

Deploy the application on Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS). Configure Amazon EKS to use managed node groups. Run the web servers and application as Kubernetes deployments in the EKS cluster. Store the frontend web server session data in an Amazon DynamoDB table. Create an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) volume that all applications will mount at the time of deployment.

questions.explanation:
Amazon DynamoDB provides a managed, durable, horizontally scalable store for frontend session state, allowing web-server instances or pods to scale without losing session persistence. Amazon EFS provides shared file storage that application instances can mount concurrently. EBS Multi-Attach cannot meet a multi-Availability Zone availability requirement because attached instances must be in the same Availability Zone, while Amazon SQS is a messaging service rather than session storage. Managed EKS node groups reduce worker-node operational work while Kubernetes deployments provide scalable, self-healing web and application workloads.

**Learn more:** [Attach an EBS volume to multiple EC2 instances using Multi-Attach](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ebs/latest/userguide/ebs-volumes-multi.html) · [AWS Decision Guide: Choosing an AWS container service](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/pdfs/decision-guides/latest/containers-on-aws-how-to-choose/containers-on-aws-how-to-choose.pdf)

An events company operates a ticketing platform on AWS. Its customers configure and schedule their events on the platform. The events cause large traffic increases to the platform. The company knows the date and time for every customer event.  
  
The company operates the platform on an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. The ECS cluster comprises Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances in an Auto Scaling group. The Auto Scaling group uses a predictive scaling policy.  
  
The ECS cluster frequently requests an Amazon S3 bucket to download ticket assets. The ECS cluster and the S3 bucket are in the same AWS Region and AWS account. Traffic from the ECS cluster to the S3 bucket passes through a NAT gateway.  
  
The company must optimize platform cost without reducing platform availability.  
  
Which combination of steps meets these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create a gateway VPC endpoint for the S3 bucket.
Add another ECS capacity provider that uses an Auto Scaling group of Spot Instances. Configure the new capacity provider strategy to have the same weight as the existing capacity provider strategy.
Create On-Demand Capacity Reservations for the applicable instance type for the time period of the scheduled scaling policies.
Enable S3 Transfer Acceleration on the S3 bucket.
Replace the predictive scaling policy with scheduled scaling policies for the scheduled events.

questions.explanation:
An Amazon S3 gateway VPC endpoint routes S3 traffic directly from the VPC without a NAT device and has no additional charge, avoiding NAT gateway data-processing costs. Scheduled scaling is intended for predictable, known time-based load changes; it can increase capacity for an event and reduce it afterward, avoiding unnecessary On-Demand capacity while preserving capacity for the scheduled traffic.

**Learn more:** [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html) · [Scheduled scaling for Amazon EC2 Auto Scaling](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/ec2-auto-scaling-scheduled-scaling.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has moved a legacy application to the AWS Cloud. The application runs on three Amazon EC2 instances distributed across three Availability Zones, with one EC2 instance in each Availability Zone. The EC2 instances run in three private subnets in the VPC and are configured as targets for an Application Load Balancer (ALB) associated with three public subnets.  
  
The application must communicate with on-premises systems. Only traffic originating from IP addresses in the company's IP address range can access the on-premises systems. The company’s security team is bringing only one IP address from its internal IP address range into the cloud. The company has added this IP address to the company firewall allow list and has created an Elastic IP address for it.  
  
A solutions architect must create a solution that enables the application to communicate with the on-premises systems. The solution must also automatically mitigate failures.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Deploy three NAT gateways, one in each public subnet. Assign the Elastic IP address to the NAT gateways. Turn on health checks for the NAT gateways. If a NAT gateway fails a health check, recreate the NAT gateway and assign the Elastic IP address to the new NAT gateway.
Replace the ALB with a Network Load Balancer (NLB). Assign the Elastic IP address to the NLTurn on health checks for the NLIn the case of a failed health check, redeploy the NLB in different subnets.

Deploy a single NAT gateway in a public subnet. Assign the Elastic IP address to the NAT gateway. Use Amazon CloudWatch with a custom metric to monitor the NAT gateway. If the NAT gateway is unhealthy, invoke an AWS Lambda function to create a new NAT gateway in a different subnet. Assign the Elastic IP address to the new NAT gateway.

Assign the Elastic IP address to the ALB. Create an Amazon Route 53 simple record with the Elastic IP address as the value. Create a Route 53 health check. In the case of a failed health check, recreate the ALB in different subnets.

questions.explanation:
A public NAT gateway translates the private source addresses of the EC2 instances to its associated Elastic IP address for outbound traffic, providing the single allow-listed source IP required by the on-premises firewall. Monitoring the NAT gateway and automatically creating a replacement in another subnet, then associating the same Elastic IP address, restores that fixed egress identity after a failure. A single Elastic IP cannot be simultaneously associated with three separate NAT gateways, and load balancers do not provide outbound NAT for the private instances.

**Learn more:** [NAT gateway use cases - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/nat-gateway-scenarios.html) · [NAT gateway basics - Amazon VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/userguide/nat-gateway-basics.html)

A software company has deployed an application that uses a REST API through Amazon API Gateway, AWS Lambda functions, and an Amazon DynamoDB table. The application is experiencing an increasing number of errors during PUT requests. Most PUT calls are made by a small number of clients authenticated with particular API keys.  
  
A solutions architect has determined that one client generates a large number of the PUT requests. The API is noncritical, and clients can tolerate retrying unsuccessful calls. However, customers see the errors, which is harming the API’s reputation.  
  
What should the solutions architect recommend to improve the customer experience?

options.text: Implement retry logic with exponential backoff and irregular variation in the client application. Ensure that the errors are caught and handled with descriptive error messages.
Implement API throttling through a usage plan at the API Gateway level. Ensure that the client application handles code 429 replies without error.
Turn on API caching to enhance responsiveness for the production stage. Run 10-minute load tests. Verify that the cache capacity is appropriate for the workload.
Implement reserved concurrency at the Lambda function level to provide the resources that are needed during sudden increases in traffic.

questions.explanation:
API Gateway usage plans can set per-client throttling limits for clients identified by associated API keys. Limiting the high-volume client protects the API and its downstream services from being overwhelmed, while the client can handle the resulting HTTP 429 responses and retry requests at an appropriate rate.

**Learn more:** [Throttle requests to your REST APIs for better throughput in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-request-throttling.html) · [Usage plans and API keys for REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-api-usage-plans.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company centrally manages hundreds of AWS accounts in an organization using AWS Organizations. The company has recently begun allowing product teams to create and manage their own S3 access points in their accounts. The S3 access points must be accessible only within VPCs, and not from the internet.  
  
What is the **MOST** operationally efficient way to enforce this requirement?

options.text: Set the S3 access point resource policy to deny the s3:CreateAccessPoint action unless the s3:AccessPointNetworkOrigin condition key evaluates to VPC.
Create an SCP at the root level in the organization to deny the s3:CreateAccessPoint action unless the s3:AccessPointNetworkOrigin condition key evaluates to VPC.
Use AWS CloudFormation StackSets to create a new IAM policy in each AWS account that allows the s3:CreateAccessPoint action only if the s3:AccessPointNetworkOrigin condition key evaluates to VPC.
Set the S3 bucket policy to deny the s3:CreateAccessPoint action unless the s3:AccessPointNetworkOrigin condition key evaluates to VPC.

questions.explanation:
An SCP applied at the AWS Organizations root provides a single centralized preventive guardrail for every account in the organization. Denying `s3:CreateAccessPoint` when `s3:AccessPointNetworkOrigin` is not `VPC` ensures that new S3 access points cannot have an internet network origin. AWS documents this exact SCP pattern for requiring VPC-origin access points.

**Learn more:** [Configuring IAM policies for using access points - Amazon S3 User Guide](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/access-points-policies.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company runs applications on AWS in a multi-account environment. Its sales and marketing teams use separate AWS accounts within AWS Organizations.  
  
The sales team stores petabytes of data in an Amazon S3 bucket. The marketing team uses Amazon QuickSight for data visualizations and requires access to the data that the sales team stores in the S3 bucket. The company encrypted the S3 bucket with an AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key. The marketing team has already created the IAM service role that provides QuickSight access in the marketing AWS account. The company needs a solution that provides secure, cross-account access to the data in the S3 bucket.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Create a new S3 bucket in the marketing account. Create an S3 replication rule in the sales account to copy the objects to the new S3 bucket in the marketing account. Update the QuickSight permissions in the marketing account to grant access to the new S3 bucket.

Create an SCP to grant access to the S3 bucket to the marketing account. Use AWS Resource Access Manager (AWS RAM) to share the KMS key from the sates account with the marketing account. Update the QuickSight permissions in the marketing account to grant access to the S3 bucket.

Update the S3 bucket policy in the marketing account to grant access to the QuickSight role. Create a KMS grant for the encryption key that is used in the S3 bucket. Grant decrypt access to the QuickSight role. Update the QuickSight permissions in the marketing account to grant access to the S3 bucket.

Create an IAM role in the sales account and grant access to the S3 bucket. From the marketing account, assume the IAM role in the sales account to access the S3 bucket. Update the QuickSight rote, to create a trust relationship with the new IAM role in the sales account.

questions.explanation:
The lowest-overhead way to give an existing QuickSight service role cross-account read access to a KMS-encrypted S3 bucket is to update the bucket policy, in the account that owns the bucket, to allow that role's S3 actions, and to create a KMS grant on the customer managed key authorizing the same role to decrypt objects. This directly extends permissions to the role QuickSight already uses, without introducing a brand-new IAM role, a cross-account AssumeRole chain, and a new trust relationship, which is the extra operational overhead that the sts:AssumeRole-based approach requires. Sharing the KMS key through AWS RAM combined with an SCP does not grant resource access on its own, and replicating petabytes of data into a second bucket is both costly and unnecessary just to enable read access.

**Learn more:** [Set up cross-account access from QuickSight to Amazon S3](https://repost.aws/knowledge-center/quicksight-cross-account-s3) · [Grants in AWS KMS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/kms/latest/developerguide/grants.html)

A company uses AWS Organizations with a multi-account architecture. Its current security configuration for the account architecture includes SCPs, resource-based policies, identity-based policies, trust policies, and session policies.  
  
A solutions architect must enable an IAM user in Account A to assume a role in Account B.  
  
Which combination of steps must the solutions architect take to satisfy this requirement? (Choose three.)

options.text: Configure the SCP for Account A to allow the action.
Configure the resource-based policies to allow the action.
Configure the identity-based policy on the user in Account A to allow the action.
Configure the identity-based policy on the user in Account B to allow the action.
Configure the trust policy on the target role in Account B to allow the action.
Configure the session policy to allow the action and to be passed programmatically by the GetSessionToken API operation.

questions.explanation:
For cross-account role assumption, the IAM user in the trusted account must have an identity-based policy allowing `sts:AssumeRole`, and the target role in the trusting account must have a trust policy allowing that principal or account. An applicable SCP must also permit the action because SCPs define the maximum permissions available to principals in the account. Session policies restrict, rather than grant, permissions.

**Learn more:** [Cross-account policy evaluation logic](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/reference_policies_evaluation-logic-cross-account.html) · [Policies and permissions in AWS Identity and Access Management](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/IAM/latest/UserGuide/access_policies.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A solutions architect is developing an application that stores objects in an Amazon S3 bucket. The solutions architect must deploy the application in two AWS Regions that will be used at the same time. Objects in the two S3 buckets must stay synchronized with one another.  
  
Which combination of steps meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create an S3 Multi-Region Access Point Change the application to refer to the Multi-Region Access Point
Configure two-way S3 Cross-Region Replication (CRR) between the two S3 buckets
Modify the application to store objects in each S3 bucket
Create an S3 Lifecycle rule for each S3 bucket to copy objects from one S3 bucket to the other S3 bucket
Enable S3 Versioning for each S3 bucket
Configure an event notification for each S3 bucket to invoke an AWS Lambda function to copy objects from one S3 bucket to the other S3 bucket

questions.explanation:
An Amazon S3 Multi-Region Access Point supplies a single global endpoint that routes requests to buckets in multiple Regions. Two-way S3 Cross-Region Replication automatically replicates objects written in either bucket to the other, keeping the buckets synchronized. S3 replication requires Versioning to be enabled on both the source and destination buckets.

**Learn more:** [Configuring replication for use with Multi-Region Access Points](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/MultiRegionAccessPointBucketReplication.html) · [Create two-way replication rules for your Multi-Region Access Point](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/mrap-create-two-way-replication-rules.html)
