A company is moving its mobile banking applications to Amazon EC2 instances in a VPC. Backend service applications operate in an on-premises data center. The data center has an AWS Direct Connect connection to AWS. Applications running in the VPC must resolve DNS queries for an on-premises Active Directory domain that runs in the data center.  
  
Which solution satisfies these requirements with the **LEAST** administrative overhead?

options.text: Provision a set of EC2 instances across two Availability Zones in the VPC as caching DNS servers to resolve DNS queries from the application servers within the VPC.
Provision an Amazon Route 53 private hosted zone. Configure NS records that point to on-premises DNS servers.
Create DNS endpoints by using Amazon Route 53 Resolver. Add conditional forwarding rules to resolve DNS namespaces between the on-premises data center and the VPC.
Provision a new Active Directory domain controller in the VPC with a bidirectional trust between this new domain and the on-premises Active Directory domain.

questions.explanation:
Amazon Route 53 Resolver outbound endpoints and forwarding rules provide managed conditional DNS forwarding from a VPC to DNS resolvers on a connected on-premises network, including through AWS Direct Connect. A rule for the Active Directory DNS namespace forwards matching queries to the on-premises DNS servers without managing EC2 DNS servers or an additional domain controller.

**Learn more:** [Resolving DNS queries between VPCs and your network](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resolver-overview-DSN-queries-to-vpc.html) · [How Resolver endpoints forward DNS queries from your VPCs to your network](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/Route53/latest/DeveloperGuide/resolver-overview-forward-vpc-to-network.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company's web application has reliability issues. The application serves customers globally. The application runs on a single Amazon EC2 instance and performs read-intensive operations on an Amazon RDS for MySQL database.  
  
During high load, the application becomes unresponsive and requires a manual restart of the EC2 instance. A solutions architect must improve the application's reliability.  
  
Which solution will meet this requirement with the LEAST development effort?

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution. Specify the EC2 instance as the distribution’s origin. Configure a Multi-AZ deployment for the RDS for MySQL database. Use the standby DB instance for the read-intensive operations.

Run the application on EC2 instances that are in an Auto Scaling group. Place the EC2 instances behind an Elastic Load Balancing (ELB) load balancer. Replace the database service with Amazon Aurora. Use Aurora Replicas for the read-intensive operations.
Deploy AWS Global Accelerator. Configure a Multi-AZ deployment for the RDS for MySQL database. Use the standby DB instance for the read-intensive operations.
Migrate the application to AWS Lambda functions. Create read replicas for the RDS for MySQL database. Use the read replicas for the read-intensive operations.

questions.explanation:
Option B combines Auto Scaling groups to handle EC2 restart issues automatically, Elastic Load Balancing to distribute traffic across instances, and Aurora read replicas to offload read-intensive queries from the primary database. This solution provides global service resilience with minimal code changes. CloudFront (Option A) doesn't address the EC2 restart problem; Global Accelerator (Option C) doesn't help with database bottlenecks; Lambda (Option D) requires application refactoring.

**Learn more:** [Replication with Amazon Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/Aurora.Replication.html) · [Adding Aurora Replicas](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/aurora-replicas-adding.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to migrate its business-critical applications from an on-premises data center to AWS. The company has an on-premises Microsoft SQL Server Always On cluster installation. It wants to migrate to an AWS managed database service. A solutions architect must design a heterogeneous database migration on AWS.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Migrate the SQL Server databases to Amazon RDS for MySQL by using backup and restore utilities.
Use an AWS Snowball Edge Storage Optimized device to transfer data to Amazon S3. Set up Amazon RDS for MySQL. Use S3 integration with SQL Server features, such as BULK INSERT.

Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool to translate the database schema to Amazon RDS for MySQL. Then use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the data from on-premises databases to Amazon RDS.
Use AWS DataSync to migrate data over the network between on-premises storage and Amazon S3. Set up Amazon RDS for MySQL. Use S3 integration with SQL Server features, such as BULK INSERT.

questions.explanation:
A Microsoft SQL Server-to-Amazon RDS for MySQL migration is heterogeneous because the database engines differ. AWS Schema Conversion Tool converts the source schema and database code objects to a MySQL-compatible form, while AWS Database Migration Service migrates the data to Amazon RDS. This is the AWS-recommended two-step approach for heterogeneous SQL Server migrations.

**Learn more:** [Heterogeneous database migration for SQL Server](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/prescriptive-guidance/latest/migration-sql-server/heterogeneous-migration.html) · [What is the AWS Schema Conversion Tool?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/SchemaConversionTool/latest/userguide/CHAP_Welcome.html)

questions.question:
lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company plans to migrate its website to AWS. The website uses microservices and runs in containers deployed to an on-premises, self-managed Kubernetes cluster. All manifests that define the container deployments in the Kubernetes deployment are maintained in source control.  
  
All website data is stored in a PostgreSQL database. An open-source container image repository runs alongside the on-premises environment.  
  
A solutions architect must determine the AWS architecture the company will use for the website.  
  
Which solution will satisfy these requirements with the **LEAST** migration effort?

options.text: Create an AWS App Runner service. Connect the App Runner service to the open source container image repository. Deploy the manifests from on premises to the App Runner service. Create an Amazon RDS for PostgreSQL database.

Create an Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) cluster that has managed node groups. Copy the application containers to a new Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Deploy the manifests from on premises to the EKS cluster. Create an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.

Create an Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster that has an Amazon EC2 capacity pool. Copy the application containers to a new Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR) repository. Register each container image as a new task definition. Configure ECS services for each task definition to match the original Kubernetes deployments. Create an Amazon Aurora PostgreSQL DB cluster.

Rebuild the on-premises Kubernetes cluster by hosting the cluster on Amazon EC2 instances. Migrate the open source container image repository to the EC2 instances. Deploy the manifests from on premises to the new cluster on AWS. Deploy an open source PostgreSQL database on the new cluster.

questions.explanation:
Amazon EKS preserves the Kubernetes deployment model, allowing the existing Kubernetes manifests to be deployed instead of being translated into a different orchestrator’s task and service definitions. EKS managed node groups automate worker-node provisioning and lifecycle management, while Amazon ECR supplies a managed container registry and Aurora PostgreSQL provides PostgreSQL compatibility.

**Learn more:** [Simplify node lifecycle with managed node groups - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/managed-node-groups.html) · [Create a managed node group for your cluster - Amazon EKS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/eks/latest/userguide/create-managed-node-group.html)

A company in the United States (US) has acquired a company in Europe. Both companies use the AWS Cloud. The US company has built a new application with a microservices architecture. The US company is hosting the application across five VPCs in the us-east-2 Region. The application must be able to access resources in one VPC in the eu-west-1 Region.  

However, the application must not be able to access any other VPCs.  
  
The VPCs in both Regions have no overlapping CIDR ranges. All accounts are already consolidated in one organization in AWS Organizations.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively?

options.text: Create one transit gateway in eu-west-1. Attach the VPCs in us-east-2 and the VPC in eu-west-1 to the transit gateway. Create the necessary route entries in each VPC so that the traffic is routed through the transit gateway.

Create one transit gateway in each Region. Attach the involved subnets to the regional transit gateway. Create the necessary route entries in the associated route tables for each subnet so that the traffic is routed through the regional transit gateway. Peer the two transit gateways.
Create a full mesh VPC peering connection configuration between all the VPCs. Create the necessary route entries in each VPC so that the traffic is routed through the VPC peering connection.
Create one VPC peering connection for each VPC in us-east-2 to the VPC in eu-west-1. Create the necessary route entries in each VPC so that the traffic is routed through the VPC peering connection.

questions.explanation:
VPC peering connections are the most cost-effective solution for this scenario. Each peering connection is free to create and maintain; only data transfer charges apply (which all options incur). Five one-to-one peering connections from us-east-2 to eu-west-1 is simpler and cheaper than Transit Gateway, which charges per attachment and per GB transferred. Since there are no overlapping CIDR ranges and communication is only to a single destination VPC, peering is ideal.

A company plans to migrate its website from an on-premises data center to AWS. At the same time, it wants to move the website to a containerized, microservice-based architecture to improve availability and cost efficiency. The company’s security policy requires privileges and network permissions to be configured according to best practices, using least privilege.  
  
A solutions architect must create a containerized architecture that satisfies the security requirements and has deployed the application to an Amazon ECS cluster.  
  
Which steps are required after deployment to meet the requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create tasks using the bridge network mode.
Create tasks using the awsvpc network mode.
Apply security groups to Amazon EC2 instances, and use IAM roles for EC2 instances to access other resources.
Apply security groups to the tasks, and pass IAM credentials into the container at launch time to access other resources.
Apply security groups to the tasks, and use IAM roles for tasks to access other resources.

questions.explanation:
Amazon ECS `awsvpc` network mode provides task-level network isolation and is the mode that allows security groups to be associated with individual tasks. IAM roles for tasks deliver scoped temporary AWS credentials to the application containers, enabling least-privilege access to other AWS resources without supplying credentials at container launch.

**Learn more:** [Network security best practices for Amazon ECS](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/security-network.html) · [Amazon ECS task IAM role](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonECS/latest/developerguide/task-iam-roles.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company is building a new serverless API using Amazon API Gateway and AWS Lambda. The company has integrated the Lambda functions with API Gateway and uses several shared libraries and custom classes.  
  
A solutions architect must simplify deployment of the solution and optimize code reuse.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Deploy the shared libraries and custom classes into a Docker image. Store the image in an S3 bucket. Create a Lambda layer that uses the Docker image as the source. Deploy the API's Lambda functions as Zip packages. Configure the packages to use the Lambda layer.

Deploy the shared libraries and custom classes to a Docker image. Upload the image to Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). Create a Lambda layer that uses the Docker image as the source. Deploy the API's Lambda functions as Zip packages. Configure the packages to use the Lambda layer.

Deploy the shared libraries and custom classes to a Docker container in Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) by using the AWS Fargate launch type. Deploy the API's Lambda functions as Zip packages. Configure the packages to use the deployed container as a Lambda layer.

Deploy the shared libraries, custom classes, and code for the API's Lambda functions to a Docker image. Upload the image to Amazon Elastic Container Registry (Amazon ECR). Configure the API's Lambda functions to use the Docker image as the deployment package.

questions.explanation:
AWS Lambda layers are ZIP archives, not Docker images, so they cannot be sourced from Amazon S3, Amazon ECR, or an Amazon ECS container. Lambda supports deploying functions as container images from Amazon ECR; bundling the shared libraries, custom classes, and Lambda function code into that image creates a valid deployment package and keeps the common code together for reuse. [Managing Lambda dependencies with layers](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/chapter-layers.html)

**Learn more:** [Managing Lambda dependencies with layers - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/chapter-layers.html) · [Create a Lambda function using a container image - AWS Lambda](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/lambda/latest/dg/images-create.html)

A company has implemented a new policy allowing employees to work remotely from home when they connect through a VPN. The company hosts internal applications in VPCs across multiple AWS accounts. At present, the applications are reachable from the company’s on-premises office network by using an AWS Site-to-Site VPN connection. The VPC in the company’s main AWS account has VPC peering connections to VPCs in the other AWS accounts.  
  
A solutions architect must design a scalable AWS Client VPN solution for employees working from home.  
  
What is the **MOST** cost-effective solution that fulfills these requirements?

options.text: Create a Client VPN endpoint in each AWS account. Configure required routing that allows access to internal applications.
Create a Client VPN endpoint in the main AWS account. Configure required routing that allows access to internal applications.
Create a Client VPN endpoint in the main AWS account. Provision a transit gateway that is connected to each AWS account. Configure required routing that allows access to internal applications.
Create a Client VPN endpoint in the main AWS account. Establish connectivity between the Client VPN endpoint and the AWS Site-to-Site VPN.

questions.explanation:
A Client VPN endpoint in the main account can route clients to the main VPC and to the connected peered VPCs, provided that Client VPN endpoint routes, authorization rules, and the associated subnet route tables are configured for each destination CIDR. This uses one endpoint and the existing VPC peering connections, avoiding the added cost and operational overhead of separate endpoints or a transit gateway.

**Learn more:** [AWS Client VPN routes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/clientvpn-admin/cvpn-working-routes.html) · [Troubleshooting AWS Client VPN access to a peered VPC](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpn/latest/clientvpn-admin/no-internet-access.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has multiple lines of business (LOBs) that roll up to a parent company. The company asks its solutions architect to develop a solution with these requirements:  
  
- Generate one AWS invoice for all AWS accounts used by its LOBs.  
- Break out the costs for each LOB account on the invoice.  
- Enable restrictions on services and features in the LOB accounts, as defined by the company's governance policy.  
- Delegate full administrator permissions to each LOB account, regardless of the governance policy.  
  
Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to satisfy these requirements? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use AWS Organizations to create an organization in the parent account for each LOB. Then invite each LOB account to the appropriate organization.
Use AWS Organizations to create a single organization in the parent account. Then, invite each LOB's AWS account to join the organization.
Implement service quotas to define the services and features that are permitted and apply the quotas to each LOB. as appropriate.
Create an SCP that allows only approved services and features, then apply the policy to the LOB accounts.
Enable consolidated billing in the parent account's billing console and link the LOB accounts.

questions.explanation:
A single AWS Organization consolidates billing for all member accounts under its management account and supports account-level cost tracking. Service control policies (SCPs) set the maximum permissions available in member accounts, so an LOB administrator can be granted AdministratorAccess while still being unable to use services or features disallowed by the SCP.

**Learn more:** [Consolidating billing for AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awsaccountbilling/latest/aboutv2/consolidated-billing.html) · [Service control policies (SCPs) - AWS Organizations](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/organizations/latest/userguide/orgs_manage_policies_scps.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses an AWS Organizations organization to manage its AWS accounts. The company deploys all infrastructure by using AWS CloudFormation. A finance team wants to create a chargeback model and has asked every business unit to tag resources with values from a predefined project list.  
  
When the finance team used the AWS Cost and Usage Report in AWS Cost Explorer and filtered by project, it found noncompliant project values. The company wants to require project tags for newly created resources.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** effort?

options.text: Create a tag policy that contains the allowed project tag values in the organization's management account. Create an SCP that denies the cloudformation:CreateStack API operation unless a project tag is added. Attach the SCP to each OU.

Create a tag policy that contains the allowed project tag values in each OU. Create an SCP that denies the cloudformation:CreateStack API operation unless a project tag is added. Attach the SCP to each OU.

Create a tag policy that contains the allowed project tag values in the AWS management account. Create an IAM policy that denies the cloudformation:CreateStack API operation unless a project tag is added. Assign the policy to each user.
Use AWS Service Catalog to manage the CloudFormation stacks as products. Use a TagOptions library to control project tag values. Share the portfolio with all OUs that are in the organization.

questions.explanation:
AWS Service Catalog TagOptions are centrally managed key-value templates that provide defined, user-selectable tag values. TagOptions associated with a portfolio or product are aggregated and applied when a provisioned product is launched; for CloudFormation products, this controls the project tag values used by the provisioned stacks. A single portfolio can be shared with the organization’s OUs, providing the control consistently across business units.

**Learn more:** [AWS Service Catalog TagOption Library](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/servicecatalog/latest/adminguide/tagoptions.html) · [Using TagOptions with AWS Organizations tag policies](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/servicecatalog/latest/adminguide/tagoption-policies.html)

An adventure company has introduced a new feature in its mobile app. Users can use the feature to upload hiking and rafting photos and videos at any time. The photos and videos are stored in Amazon S3 Standard storage in an S3 bucket and are delivered through Amazon CloudFront.  
  
The company needs to optimize storage costs. A solutions architect finds that most uploaded photos and videos are accessed infrequently after 30 days. However, some uploaded photos and videos continue to be accessed frequently after 30 days. The solutions architect must implement a solution that preserves millisecond retrieval availability for the photos and videos at the lowest possible cost.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure S3 Intelligent-Tiering on the S3 bucket.
Configure an S3 Lifecycle policy to transition image objects and video objects from S3 Standard to S3 Glacier Deep Archive after 30 days.
Replace Amazon S3 with an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system that is mounted on Amazon EC2 instances.
Add a Cache-Control: max-age header to the S3 image objects and S3 video objects. Set the header to 30 days.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 Intelligent-Tiering automatically monitors each object's access pattern and moves objects that have not been accessed for 30 consecutive days to its lower-cost Infrequent Access tier, while frequently accessed objects remain in the Frequent Access tier. These tiers provide low-latency, millisecond retrieval, so the storage cost is optimized without sacrificing immediate availability.

**Learn more:** [How S3 Intelligent-Tiering works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/intelligent-tiering-overview.html) · [Understanding and managing Amazon S3 storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],An entertainment company has recently released a new game. To provide players with a good experience during the launch period, the company deployed a fixed fleet of 12 r6g.16xlarge (memory optimized) Amazon EC2 instances behind a Network Load Balancer. The operations team used the Amazon CloudWatch agent and a custom metric to incorporate memory utilization into its monitoring strategy.  
  
Analysis of CloudWatch metrics during the launch period showed usage at approximately one quarter of the CPU and memory the company had anticipated. Initial game demand has decreased and is now more variable. The company decides to use an Auto Scaling group that monitors CPU and memory usage to dynamically scale the instance fleet. A solutions architect must configure the Auto Scaling group to meet demand as cost-effectively as possible.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Configure the Auto Scaling group to deploy c6g.4xlarge (compute optimized) instances. Configure a minimum capacity of 3, a desired capacity of 3, and a maximum capacity of 12.
Configure the Auto Scaling group to deploy m6g.4xlarge (general purpose) instances. Configure a minimum capacity of 3, a desired capacity of 3, and a maximum capacity of 12.
Configure the Auto Scaling group to deploy r6g.4xlarge (memory optimized) instances. Configure a minimum capacity of 3, a desired capacity of 3, and a maximum capacity of 12.
Configure the Auto Scaling group to deploy r6g.8xlarge (memory optimized) instances. Configure a minimum capacity of 2, a desired capacity of 2, and a maximum capacity of 6.

questions.explanation:
The r6g family is appropriate because the workload requires memory-optimized instances. An r6g.4xlarge provides one quarter of the vCPUs and memory of an r6g.16xlarge. A fleet that can scale from 3 to 12 r6g.4xlarge instances therefore aligns with the measured lower consumption while retaining capacity for variable demand, without paying for the substantially oversized r6g.16xlarge fleet.

**Learn more:** [Amazon EC2 R6g instances](https://aws.amazon.com/ec2/instance-types/r6g/)

options.text: Create an AMI of the existing EC2 instance. Create an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. Configure the Auto Scaling group to have a minimum of three instances.

Use AWS Transfer Family to create an FTP server that places the files in Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). Mount the EFS volume to the existing EC2 instance. Point the EC2 instance to the new path for file processing.

Use AWS Transfer Family to create an FTP server that places the files in Amazon S3. Use an S3 event notification through Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to add the metadata and update the delivery system.

Update the handheld devices to place the files directly in Amazon S3. Use an S3 event notification through Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to add the metadata and update the delivery system.

questions.explanation:
AWS Transfer Family supplies a fully managed FTP endpoint and can store uploads directly in Amazon S3, so existing FTP clients can continue to operate without relying on a single EC2 instance. S3 event notifications can publish uploaded-object events to Amazon SNS, and SNS can invoke AWS Lambda to retrieve delivery information, add metadata, and update the delivery system. This decouples scalable file transfer, durable object storage, and event-driven processing.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Transfer Family?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transfer/latest/userguide/what-is-aws-transfer-family.html) · [Transferring files over a server endpoint using a client](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transfer/latest/userguide/transfer-file.html)

A company plans to migrate an application from on premises to the AWS Cloud. The company will start the migration by moving the application’s underlying data storage to AWS. The application data resides on an on-premises shared file system, and the application servers connect to that shared file system through SMB.  
  
A solutions architect must implement a solution that uses an Amazon S3 bucket for shared storage. Until the application is completely migrated and its code is rewritten to use native Amazon S3 APIs, the application must retain access to the data through SMB. The solutions architect must migrate the application data to its new AWS location while continuing to allow the on-premises application to access the data.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a new Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Configure AWS DataSync with one location for the on-premises file share and one location for the new Amazon FSx file system. Create a new DataSync task to copy the data from the on-premises file share location to the Amazon FSx file system.
Create an S3 bucket for the application. Copy the data from the on-premises storage to the S3 bucket.
Deploy an AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS) VM to the on-premises environment. Use AWS SMS to migrate the file storage server from on premises to an Amazon EC2 instance.

Create an S3 bucket for the application. Deploy a new AWS Storage Gateway file gateway on an on-premises VM. Create a new file share that stores data in the S3 bucket and is associated with the file gateway. Copy the data from the on-premises storage to the new file gateway endpoint.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 File Gateway in AWS Storage Gateway provides a file interface to an S3 bucket and supports SMB access. Creating an SMB file share associated with the S3 bucket lets the on-premises application continue using SMB while files copied to the gateway are stored as objects in Amazon S3.

**Learn more:** [What is Amazon S3 File Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/what-is-file-s3.html) · [How Amazon S3 File Gateway works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/file-gateway-concepts.html)

A company plans to store a large volume of archived documents and make them available to employees through the corporate intranet. Employees will access the system by connecting through a client VPN service attached to a VPC. The data must not be publicly accessible.  
  
The stored documents are copies of data held on physical media elsewhere. Request volume will be low, and the company has no concerns about availability or retrieval speed.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements at the **LOWEST** cost?

options.text: Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure the S3 bucket to use the S3 One Zone-Infrequent Access (S3 One Zone-IA) storage class as default. Configure the S3 bucket for website hosting. Create an S3 interface endpoint. Configure the S3 bucket to allow access only through that endpoint.

Launch an Amazon EC2 instance that runs a web server. Attach an Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS) file system to store the archived data in the EFS One Zone-Infrequent Access (EFS One Zone-IA) storage class Configure the instance security groups to allow access only from private networks.

Launch an Amazon EC2 instance that runs a web server Attach an Amazon Elastic Block Store (Amazon EBS) volume to store the archived data. Use the Cold HDD (sc1) volume type. Configure the instance security groups to allow access only from private networks.

Create an Amazon S3 bucket. Configure the S3 bucket to use the S3 Glacier Deep Archive storage class as default. Configure the S3 bucket for website hosting. Create an S3 interface endpoint. Configure the S3 bucket to allow access only through that endpoint.

questions.explanation:
S3 Glacier Deep Archive is designed for long-term, rarely accessed archival data and provides Amazon S3’s lowest storage cost. Its delayed restore process is suitable when retrieval speed is not important, and the data is already duplicated on physical media. An S3 endpoint and restrictive bucket policy can limit S3 API access to the private VPC path. Glacier Deep Archive objects must be restored before they can be read.

**Learn more:** [Understanding and managing Amazon S3 storage classes](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/storage-class-intro.html) · [Understanding archival storage in S3 Glacier Flexible Retrieval and S3 Glacier Deep Archive](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/archival-storage.html)

A company uses a service to gather metadata from applications that it hosts on premises. Consumer devices, including TVs and internet radios, access the applications. Many legacy devices do not support certain HTTP headers and experience errors when those headers appear in responses. The company configured an on-premises load balancer to strip the unsupported headers from responses sent to legacy devices, identified by their User-Agent headers.  
  
The company wants to migrate the service to AWS, use serverless technologies, and preserve support for the legacy devices. The applications have already been migrated to a set of AWS Lambda functions.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the metadata service. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Configure the CloudFront distribution to forward requests to the ALB. Configure the ALB to invoke the correct Lambda function for each type of request. Create a CloudFront function to remove the problematic headers based on the value of the User-Agent header.

Create an Amazon API Gateway REST API for the metadata service. Configure API Gateway to invoke the correct Lambda function for each type of request. Modify the default gateway responses to remove the problematic headers based on the value of the User-Agent header.

Create an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API for the metadata service. Configure API Gateway to invoke the correct Lambda function for each type of request. Create a response mapping template to remove the problematic headers based on the value of the User-Agent. Associate the response data mapping with the HTTP API.

Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the metadata service. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Configure the CloudFront distribution to forward requests to the ALB. Configure the ALB to invoke the correct Lambda function for each type of request. Create a Lambda@Edge function that will remove the problematic headers in response to viewer requests based on the value of the User-Agent header.

questions.explanation:
A CloudFront Function associated with a viewer-response event can inspect the viewer request’s User-Agent header and modify the response headers before CloudFront sends the response to the device. This supports conditional removal of incompatible headers at the edge while the Application Load Balancer routes requests to the appropriate Lambda function. API Gateway gateway responses customize only API Gateway-generated error responses, not normal Lambda integration responses.

**Learn more:** [CloudFront Functions event structure](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/functions-event-structure.html) · [Gateway responses for REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-gatewayResponse-definition.html)

A company plans to migrate an Amazon RDS for Oracle database to an RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance in a different AWS account. A solutions architect must design a migration strategy that requires no downtime and minimizes the time needed to complete the migration. The strategy must replicate all existing data and any new data created during the migration. At the end of the migration process, the target database must be identical to the source database.  
  
All applications currently use an Amazon Route 53 CNAME record as the endpoint to communicate with the RDS for Oracle DB instance. The RDS for Oracle DB instance is in a private subnet.  
  
Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements? (Choose three.)

options.text: Create a new RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance in the target account. Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to migrate the database schema from the source database to the target database.
Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to create a new RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance in the target account with the schema and initial data from the source database.

Configure VPC peering between the VPCs in the two AWS accounts to provide connectivity to both DB instances from the target account. Configure the security groups that are attached to each DB instance to allow traffic on the database port from the VPC in the target account.

Temporarily allow the source DB instance to be publicly accessible to provide connectivity from the VPC in the target account. Configure the security groups that are attached to each DB instance to allow traffic on the database port from the VPC in the target account.

Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) in the target account to perform a full load plus change data capture (CDC) migration from the source database to the target database. When the migration is complete, change the CNAME record to point to the target DB instance endpoint.

Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) in the target account to perform a change data capture (CDC) migration from the source database to the target database. When the migration is complete, change the CNAME record to point to the target DB instance endpoint.

questions.explanation:
AWS SCT converts the Oracle schema and database code into a PostgreSQL-compatible form, while AWS DMS migrates data. A DMS full-load-plus-CDC task copies the existing data and continuously applies supported source changes, keeping the target synchronized until cutover. For databases in different VPCs and AWS accounts, VPC peering with routes and database-port security-group access provides private connectivity. Repointing the Route 53 CNAME to the target endpoint performs the application cutover without changing application connection configuration.

**Learn more:** [Migrating an Oracle Database to PostgreSQL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/sbs/chap-rdsoracle2postgresql.html) · [Setting up a network for DMS Schema Conversion](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/instance-profiles-network.html)

3e:[["$","p",null,{"children":"An international delivery company runs a delivery management system on AWS. Drivers use the system to upload delivery confirmation. Confirmation includes the recipient’s signature or a photo of the package with the recipient. The drivers’ handheld devices upload signatures and photos by FTP to a single Amazon EC2 instance. Each handheld device stores a file in a directory determined by the signed-in user, and the file name matches the delivery number. The EC2 instance then adds metadata to the file after querying a central database for delivery information. The file is subsequently placed in Amazon S3 for archiving."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"As the company grows, drivers report that the system rejects connections. The FTP server experiences dropped connections and memory problems; in response, a system engineer schedules a cron task to reboot the EC2 instance every 30 minutes. The billing team reports that files are not always present in the archive and that the central system is not always updated."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"A solutions architect must design a solution that maximizes scalability to ensure the archive always receives the files and systems are always updated. The handheld devices cannot be changed, so the company cannot deploy a new application."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution meets these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L51",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create an AMI of the existing EC2 instance. Create an Auto Scaling group of EC2 instances behind an Application Load Balancer. Configure the Auto Scaling group to have a minimum of three instances.","B":"Use AWS Transfer Family to create an FTP server that places the files in Amazon Elastic File System (Amazon EFS). Mount the EFS volume to the existing EC2 instance. Point the EC2 instance to the new path for file processing.","C":"Use AWS Transfer Family to create an FTP server that places the files in Amazon S3. Use an S3 event notification through Amazon Simple Notification Service (Amazon SNS) to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to add the metadata and update the delivery system.","D":"Update the handheld devices to place the files directly in Amazon S3. Use an S3 event notification through Amazon Simple Queue Service (Amazon SQS) to invoke an AWS Lambda function. Configure the Lambda function to add the metadata and update the delivery system."},"correctAnswer":"C","explanation":"AWS Transfer Family supplies a fully managed FTP endpoint and can store uploads directly in Amazon S3, so existing FTP clients can continue to operate without relying on a single EC2 instance. S3 event notifications can publish uploaded-object events to Amazon SNS, and SNS can invoke AWS Lambda to retrieve delivery information, add metadata, and update the delivery system. This decouples scalable file transfer, durable object storage, and event-driven processing.

**Learn more:** [What is AWS Transfer Family?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transfer/latest/userguide/what-is-aws-transfer-family.html) · [Transferring files over a server endpoint using a client](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/transfer/latest/userguide/transfer-file.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"94d2c68d-1f4a-4962-a911-5c3fa6fadfb5","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02","mode":"default"}}]]

",["$","p",null,{"children":"A solutions architect must implement a solution that uses an Amazon S3 bucket for shared storage. ",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution meets these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L51",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create a new Amazon FSx for Windows File Server file system. Configure AWS DataSync with one location for the on-premises file share and one location for the new Amazon FSx file system. Create a new DataSync task to copy the data from the on-premises file share location to the Amazon FSx file system.","B":"Create an S3 bucket for the application. Copy the data from the on-premises storage to the S3 bucket.","C":"Deploy an AWS Server Migration Service (AWS SMS) VM to the on-premises environment. **Learn more:** [What is Amazon S3 File Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/what-is-file-s3.html) · [How Amazon S3 File Gateway works](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/filegateway/latest/files3/file-gateway-concepts.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"a884bd19-6955-4d02-aea5-6c8189c7574e","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02","mode":"default"}}]]

",["$","p",null,{"children":["Which solution meets these requirements at the ",["$","strong",null,{"children":"LOWEST"}]," cost?"]}],"

4f:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company uses a service to gather metadata from applications that it hosts on premises. Consumer devices, including TVs and internet radios, access the applications. ",["$","p",null,{"children":"The company wants to migrate the service to AWS, use serverless technologies, and preserve support for the legacy devices. The applications have already been migrated to a set of AWS Lambda functions."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"Which solution meets these requirements?"}],"
",["$","$L51",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the metadata service. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Create a CloudFront function to remove the problematic headers based on the value of the User-Agent header.","B":"Create an Amazon API Gateway REST API for the metadata service. Configure API Gateway to invoke the correct Lambda function for each type of request. Modify the default gateway responses to remove the problematic headers based on the value of the User-Agent header.","C":"Create an Amazon API Gateway HTTP API for the metadata service. Configure API Gateway to invoke the correct Lambda function for each type of request. Create a response mapping template to remove the problematic headers based on the value of the User-Agent. Associate the response data mapping with the HTTP API.","D":"Create an Amazon CloudFront distribution for the metadata service. Create an Application Load Balancer (ALB). Configure the CloudFront distribution to forward requests to the ALB. Configure the ALB to invoke the correct Lambda function for each type of request. Create a Lambda@Edge function that will remove the problematic headers in response to viewer requests based on the value of the User-Agent header."},"correctAnswer":"A","explanation":"A CloudFront Function associated with a viewer-response event can inspect the viewer request’s User-Agent header and modify the response headers before CloudFront sends the response to the device. This supports conditional removal of incompatible headers at the edge while the Application Load Balancer routes requests to the appropriate Lambda function. API Gateway gateway responses customize only API Gateway-generated error responses, not normal Lambda integration responses.

**Learn more:** [CloudFront Functions event structure](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/functions-event-structure.html) · [Gateway responses for REST APIs in API Gateway](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/apigateway/latest/developerguide/api-gateway-gatewayResponse-definition.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"81186718-e06d-4320-b295-6b7b61f57edb","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02","mode":"default"}}]]
50:[["$","p",null,{"children":"A company plans to migrate an Amazon RDS for Oracle database to an RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance in a different AWS account. A solutions architect must design a migration strategy that requires no downtime and minimizes the time needed to complete the migration. The strategy must replicate all existing data and any new data created during the migration. At the end of the migration process, the target database must be identical to the source database."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":"All applications currently use an Amazon Route 53 CNAME record as the endpoint to communicate with the RDS for Oracle DB instance. The RDS for Oracle DB instance is in a private subnet."}],"
",["$","p",null,{"children":["Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to meet these requirements?"]}],"
",["$","$L51",null,{"choices":{"A":"Create a new RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance in the target account. Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to migrate the database schema from the source database to the target database.","B":"Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to create a new RDS for PostgreSQL DB instance in the target account with the schema and initial data from the source database.","C":"Configure VPC peering between the VPCs in the two AWS accounts to provide connectivity to both DB instances from the target account. Configure the security groups that are attached to each DB instance to allow traffic on the database port from the VPC in the target account.","D":"Temporarily allow the source DB instance to be publicly accessible to provide connectivity from the VPC in the target account. Configure the security groups that are attached to each DB instance to allow traffic on the database port from the VPC in the target account.","E":"Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) in the target account to perform a full load plus change data capture (CDC) migration from the source database to the target database. When the migration is complete, change the CNAME record to point to the target DB instance endpoint.","F":"Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) in the target account to perform a change data capture (CDC) migration from the source database to the target database. When the migration is complete, change the CNAME record to point to the target DB instance endpoint."},"correctAnswer":"ACE","explanation":"AWS SCT converts the Oracle schema and database code into a PostgreSQL-compatible form, while AWS DMS migrates data. A DMS full-load-plus-CDC task copies the existing data and continuously applies supported source changes, keeping the target synchronized until cutover. For databases in different VPCs and AWS accounts, VPC peering with routes and database-port security-group access provides private connectivity. Repointing the Route 53 CNAME to the target endpoint performs the application cutover without changing application connection configuration.

**Learn more:** [Migrating an Oracle Database to PostgreSQL](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/sbs/chap-rdsoracle2postgresql.html) · [Setting up a network for DMS Schema Conversion](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/instance-profiles-network.html)","trackingInfo":{"questionId":"1c3a21e5-4ef3-48fa-a707-afc0aea6a597","examProvider":"amazon","examName":"aws-certified-solutions-architect-professional-sap-c02","mode":"default"}}]]
A solutions architect must enhance an application hosted in the AWS Cloud. The application uses an Amazon Aurora MySQL DB instance that is experiencing overloaded connections. Most application operations insert records into the database. The application currently keeps credentials in a text-based configuration file.  
  
The solutions architect must implement a solution that enables the application to handle the current connection load. The solution must secure the credentials and provide the capability to rotate them automatically on a regular schedule.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Deploy an Amazon RDS Proxy layer. In front of the DB instance. Store the connection credentials as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager.
Deploy an Amazon RDS Proxy layer in front of the DB instance. Store the connection credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store
Create an Aurora Replica. Store the connection credentials as a secret in AWS Secrets Manager
Create an Aurora Replica. Store the connection credentials in AWS Systems Manager Parameter Store.

questions.explanation:
Amazon RDS Proxy pools and reuses database connections, which reduces connection-establishment overhead and prevents the Aurora MySQL DB instance from being overwhelmed by application connections. AWS Secrets Manager securely stores the database credentials used by the proxy and supports scheduled automatic rotation of database secrets. Aurora Replicas are intended to scale read workloads and do not address a write-heavy connection-load problem.

**Learn more:** [Amazon RDS Proxy for Aurora](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonRDS/latest/AuroraUserGuide/rds-proxy.html) · [Set up automatic rotation for Amazon RDS and Aurora secrets](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/secretsmanager/latest/userguide/rotate-secrets_turn-on-for-db.html)

An online survey company operates its application in the AWS Cloud. The application is distributed and consists of microservices running in an automatically scaled Amazon Elastic Container Service (Amazon ECS) cluster. The ECS cluster is a target for an Application Load Balancer (ALB). The ALB serves as a custom origin for an Amazon CloudFront distribution.  
  
The company has a survey containing sensitive data. The sensitive data must be encrypted as it moves through the application. Only the application's data-handling microservice should be able to decrypt the data.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create a symmetric AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key that is dedicated to the data-handling microservice. Create a field-level encryption profile and a configuration. Associate the KMS key and the configuration with the CloudFront cache behavior.

Create an RSA key pair that is dedicated to the data-handing microservice. Upload the public key to the CloudFront distribution. Create a field-level encryption profile and a configuration. Add the configuration to the CloudFront cache behavior.

Create a symmetric AWS Key Management Service (AWS KMS) key that is dedicated to the data-handling microservice. Create a Lambda@Edge function. Program the function to use the KMS key to encrypt the sensitive data.

Create an RSA key pair that is dedicated to the data-handling microservice. Create a Lambda@Edge function. Program the function to use the private key of the RSA key pair to encrypt the sensitive data.

questions.explanation:
Amazon CloudFront field-level encryption uses asymmetric RSA encryption for specified request fields. CloudFront encrypts using an uploaded public key, while the private key—held only by the data-handling microservice—enables decryption at the origin. Associating the field-level encryption profile and configuration with the cache behavior applies that protection to the relevant requests.

**Learn more:** [Use field-level encryption to help protect sensitive data - Amazon CloudFront](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonCloudFront/latest/DeveloperGuide/field-level-encryption.html)

A company is constructing a call center using Amazon Connect. The company’s operations team is defining a disaster recovery (DR) strategy across AWS Regions. The contact center includes dozens of contact flows, hundreds of users, and dozens of claimed phone numbers.  
  
Which solution will deliver DR with the **LOWEST RTO**?

options.text: Create an AWS Lambda function to check the availability of the Amazon Connect instance and to send a notification to the operations team in case of unavailability. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function every 5 minutes. After notification, instruct the operations team to use the AWS Management Console to provision a new Amazon Connect instance in a second Region. Deploy the contact flows, users, and claimed phone numbers by using an AWS CloudFormation template.

Provision a new Amazon Connect instance with all existing users in a second Region. Create an AWS Lambda function to check the availability of the Amazon Connect instance. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to invoke the Lambda function every 5 minutes. In the event of an issue, configure the Lambda function to deploy an AWS CloudFormation template that provisions contact flows and claimed numbers in the second Region.

Provision a new Amazon Connect instance with all existing contact flows and claimed phone numbers in a second Region. Create an Amazon Route 53 health check for the URL of the Amazon Connect instance. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for failed health checks. Create an AWS Lambda function to deploy an AWS CloudFormation template that provisions all users. Configure the alarm to invoke the Lambda function.

Provision a new Amazon Connect instance with all existing users and contact flows in a second Region. Create an Amazon Route 53 health check for the URL of the Amazon Connect instance. Create an Amazon CloudWatch alarm for failed health checks. Create an AWS Lambda function to deploy an AWS CloudFormation template that provisions claimed phone numbers. Configure the alarm to invoke the Lambda function.

questions.explanation:
The lowest recovery time objective is achieved by maintaining a fully provisioned standby Amazon Connect instance with its users and contact flows already present, detecting failure through Route 53 health checks and CloudWatch alarms, and automating only the remaining phone-number provisioning. This eliminates manual recovery and periodic polling delays while avoiding outage-time creation of the much larger set of hundreds of users. Amazon Connect phone-number claiming is performed in the Region where the target instance is created.

**Learn more:** [ClaimPhoneNumber API Reference](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/APIReference/API_ClaimPhoneNumber.html) · [Claim phone numbers to Amazon Connect instances across multiple AWS Regions](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/connect/latest/adminguide/claim-phone-number-multiple-regions.html)

A company must run large batch-processing jobs against data stored in an Amazon S3 bucket. The jobs run simulations. Their results are not time-sensitive, and the process can tolerate interruptions.  
  
Each job must process 15–20 GB of data while that data is stored in the S3 bucket. The company will save job output to a separate Amazon S3 bucket for additional analysis.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements in the **MOST** cost-effective way?

options.text: Create a serverless data pipeline. Use AWS Step Functions for orchestration. Use AWS Lambda functions with provisioned capacity to process the data.
Create an AWS Batch compute environment that includes Amazon EC2 Spot Instances. Specify the SPOT_CAPACITY_OPTIMIZED allocation strategy.
Create an AWS Batch compute environment that includes Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances and Spot Instances. Specify the SPOT_CAPACITY_OPTIMIZED allocation strategy for the Spot Instances.
Use Amazon Elastic Kubernetes Service (Amazon EKS) to run the processing jobs. Use managed node groups that contain a combination of Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances and Spot Instances.

questions.explanation:
AWS Batch with EC2 Spot Instances is well suited to interruptible, non-time-sensitive batch simulations and avoids the cost of On-Demand capacity. The `SPOT_CAPACITY_OPTIMIZED` allocation strategy selects Spot instance types with a preference for pools less likely to be interrupted, which supports reliable processing while retaining the cost advantage of Spot capacity.

**Learn more:** [Instance type allocation strategies for AWS Batch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/batch/latest/userguide/allocation-strategies.html) · [Use Amazon EC2 Spot best practices for AWS Batch](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/batch/latest/userguide/bestpractice6.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has migrated to AWS and uses AWS Business Support. The company needs to monitor the cost-effectiveness of Amazon EC2 instances across AWS accounts. The EC2 instances are tagged for department, business unit, and environment. Development EC2 instances have high cost and low utilization.  
  
The company must identify and stop underutilized development EC2 instances. An instance is underutilized when it has had average daily CPU utilization of 10% or less and network I/O of 5 MB or less for at least 4 of the past 14 days.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements with the **LEAST** operational overhead?

options.text: Configure Amazon CloudWatch dashboards to monitor EC2 instance utilization based on tags for department, business unit, and environment. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function to stop underutilized development EC2 instances.

Configure AWS Systems Manager to track EC2 instance utilization and report underutilized instances to Amazon CloudWatch. Filter the CloudWatch data by tags for department, business unit, and environment. Create an Amazon EventBridge rule that invokes an AWS Lambda function to stop underutilized development EC2 instances.

Create an Amazon EventBridge rule to detect low utilization of EC2 instances reported by AWS Trusted Advisor. Configure the rule to invoke an AWS Lambda function that filters the data by tags for department, business unit, and environment and stops underutilized development EC2 instances.

Create an AWS Lambda function to run daily to retrieve utilization data for all EC2 instances. Save the data to an Amazon DynamoDB table. Create an Amazon QuickSight dashboard that uses the DynamoDB table as a data source to identify and stop underutilized development EC2 instances.

questions.explanation:
The AWS Trusted Advisor Low Utilization Amazon EC2 Instances check evaluates running instances over the prior 14 days and flags instances with daily average CPU utilization of 10% or less and network I/O of 5 MB or less for at least 4 days. Trusted Advisor check-refresh notifications can be monitored with Amazon EventBridge, allowing a Lambda function to filter the flagged instances by their department, business unit, and environment tags and stop only development instances.

**Learn more:** [AWS Trusted Advisor cost optimization checks](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/cost-optimization-checks.html) · [Monitoring AWS Trusted Advisor check results with Amazon EventBridge](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/awssupport/latest/user/cloudwatch-events-ta.html)

A solutions architect is importing a VM from an on-premises environment by using the Amazon EC2 VM Import feature of AWS Import/Export. The solutions architect has created an AMI and has provisioned an Amazon EC2 instance that is based on that AMI. The EC2 instance runs inside a public subnet in a VPC and has a public IP address assigned.  
  
The EC2 instance does not appear as a managed instance in the AWS Systems Manager console.  
  
Which combination of steps should the solutions architect take to troubleshoot this issue? (Choose two.)

options.text: Verify that Systems Manager Agent is installed on the instance and is running.
Verify that the instance is assigned an appropriate IAM role for Systems Manager.
Verify the existence of a VPC endpoint on the VPC.
Verity that the AWS Application Discovery Agent is configured.
Verify the correct configuration of service-linked roles for Systems Manager.

questions.explanation:
Systems Manager requires both the Systems Manager Agent to be installed and running on the instance, and an appropriate IAM role with permissions to communicate with Systems Manager service. Without either component, the instance will not appear as a managed instance. VPC endpoints (Option C) are optional optimization. Application Discovery Agent (Option D) is for migration discovery, not Systems Manager management. Service-linked roles (Option E) are not required for basic Systems Manager functionality.

**Learn more:** [Configure instance permissions required for Systems Manager](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/systems-manager/latest/userguide/setup-instance-permissions.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company has many services running in its on-premises data center. The data center is connected to AWS using AWS Direct Connect (DX) and an IPSec VPN. The service data is sensitive and connectivity cannot traverse the internet. The company wants to expand into a new market segment and begin offering its services to other companies that are using AWS.  
  
Which solution will meet these requirements?

options.text: Create a VPC Endpoint Service that accepts TCP traffic, host it behind a Network Load Balancer, and make the service available over DX.
Create a VPC Endpoint Service that accepts HTTP or HTTPS traffic, host it behind an Application Load Balancer, and make the service available over DX.
Attach an internet gateway to the VPC, and ensure that network access control and security group rules allow the relevant inbound and outbound traffic.
Attach a NAT gateway to the VPC, and ensure that network access control and security group rules allow the relevant inbound and outbound traffic.

questions.explanation:
AWS PrivateLink requires a Network Load Balancer to expose services to consumer VPCs through VPC endpoints. NLBs support TCP traffic for any protocol, providing flexibility for diverse service types while maintaining security. The service is exposed only to authorized consumer VPCs over the Direct Connect private connection, preventing internet traversal. ALBs do not support PrivateLink directly. Internet Gateway and NAT Gateway options violate the security requirement that connectivity cannot traverse the public internet.

**Learn more:** [Create a service powered by AWS PrivateLink](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/create-endpoint-service.html) · [Share your services through AWS PrivateLink](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/privatelink-share-your-services.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company used infrastructure as code (IaC) to provision a set of two Amazon EC2 instances. The instances have remained unchanged for several years.  
  
The company's business has expanded rapidly during the past few months. In response, the company’s operations team implemented an Auto Scaling group to manage the sudden traffic increases. Company policy requires security updates to be installed monthly on all running operating systems.  
  
The latest security update required a reboot. Consequently, the Auto Scaling group terminated the instances and replaced them with new, unpatched instances.  
  
Which combination of steps should a solutions architect recommend to prevent this issue from happening again? (Choose two.)

options.text: Modify the Auto Scaling group by setting the Update policy to target the oldest launch configuration for replacement.
Create a new Auto Scaling group before the next patch maintenance. During the maintenance window, patch both groups and reboot the instances.

Create an Elastic Load Balancer in front of the Auto Scaling group. Configure monitoring to ensure that target group health checks return healthy after the Auto Scaling group replaces the terminated instances.
Create automation scripts to patch an AMI, update the launch configuration, and invoke an Auto Scaling instance refresh.
Create an Elastic Load Balancer in front of the Auto Scaling group. Configure termination protection on the instances.

questions.explanation:
A patched AMI must be made the Auto Scaling group’s launch configuration so that every replacement instance includes the security updates. An Auto Scaling instance refresh replaces the existing fleet with instances using that updated configuration. Elastic Load Balancing health checks keep traffic directed only to healthy registered targets while replacement instances initialize and become healthy.

**Learn more:** [Use an instance refresh to update instances in an Auto Scaling group](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/autoscaling/ec2/userguide/asg-instance-refresh.html) · [Health checks for Application Load Balancer target groups](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/en_en/elasticloadbalancing/latest/application/target-group-health-checks.html)

An online gaming company must rehost its gaming platform on AWS. Its gaming application needs high performance computing (HPC) processing and includes a leaderboard that changes often. A compute-optimized Ubuntu instance hosts a Node.js application that displays games. Game state is stored in an on-premises Redis instance.  
  
The company needs a migration strategy that optimizes application performance.  
  
Which solution meets these requirements?

options.text: Create an Auto Scaling group of m5.large Amazon EC2 Spot Instances behind an Application Load Balancer. Use an Amazon ElastlCache for Redis cluster to maintain the leaderboard.
Create an Auto Scaling group of c5.large Amazon EC2 Spot Instances behind an Application Load Balancer. Use an Amazon OpenSearch Service cluster to maintain the leaderboard.
Create an Auto Scaling group of c5.large Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances behind an Application Load Balancer. Use an Amazon ElastiCache for Redis cluster to maintain the leaderboard.
Create an Auto Scaling group of m5.large Amazon EC2 On-Demand Instances behind an Application Load Balancer. Use an Amazon DynamoDB table to maintain the leaderboard.

questions.explanation:
C5 instances are compute-optimized and are designed for compute-intensive workloads, including HPC and dedicated gaming servers. Amazon ElastiCache for Redis provides an in-memory Redis-compatible data store; Redis sorted sets support leaderboards by maintaining unique, ordered scores and reranking them in real time when scores change. On-Demand capacity avoids the interruption risk inherent in Spot Instances for this performance-sensitive application tier.

**Learn more:** [Specifications for Amazon EC2 compute optimized instances](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/ec2/latest/instancetypes/co.html) · [Common ElastiCache Use Cases and How ElastiCache Can Help](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonElastiCache/latest/dg/elasticache-use-cases.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company uses AWS Organizations. The company runs two firewall appliances in a centralized networking account. Each firewall appliance runs on a manually configured highly available Amazon EC2 instance. A transit gateway connects the VPC from the centralized networking account to VPCs of member accounts. Each firewall appliance uses a static private IP address that is then used to route traffic from the member accounts to the internet.  
  
During a recent incident, a badly configured script initiated the termination of both firewall appliances. During the rebuild of the firewall appliances, the company wrote a new script to configure the firewall appliances at startup.  
  
The company wants to modernize the deployment of the firewall appliances. The firewall appliances need the ability to scale horizontally to handle increased traffic when the network expands. The company must continue to use the firewall appliances to comply with company policy. The provider of the firewall appliances has confirmed that the latest version of the firewall code will work with all AWS services.  
  
Which combination of steps should the solutions architect recommend to meet these requirements MOST cost-effectively? (Choose three.)

options.text: Deploy a Gateway Load Balancer in the centralized networking account. Set up an endpoint service that uses AWS PrivateLink.
Deploy a Network Load Balancer in the centralized networking account. Set up an endpoint service that uses AWS PrivateLink.
Create an Auto Scaling group and a launch template that uses the new script as user data to configure the firewall appliances. Create a target group that uses the instance target type.
Create an Auto Scaling group. Configure an AWS Launch Wizard deployment that uses the new script as user data to configure the firewall appliances. Create a target group that uses the IP target type.
Create VPC endpoints in each member account. Update the route tables to point to the VPC endpoints.
Create VPC endpoints in the centralized networking account. Update the route tables in each member account to point to the VPC endpoints.

questions.explanation:
A Gateway Load Balancer fronting the firewall appliances, exposed as an endpoint service over AWS PrivateLink, is the purpose-built way to scale third-party inline appliances horizontally while preserving a single ingress/egress path. An Auto Scaling group backed by a launch template that runs the new startup script (with an instance-type target group) automates provisioning and horizontal scaling of the appliances. In this centralized-inspection design the Gateway Load Balancer endpoints are created once in the centralized networking account, and each member account's route tables are updated to send traffic to those shared endpoints, avoiding the cost of duplicating endpoints in every member account.

**Learn more:** [Centralized inspection architecture with AWS Gateway Load Balancer and AWS Transit Gateway](https://aws.amazon.com/blogs/networking-and-content-delivery/centralized-inspection-architecture-with-aws-gateway-load-balancer-and-aws-transit-gateway/)

A company needs to migrate its on-premises database fleet to Amazon RDS. The company is currently using a mixture of Microsoft SQL Server, MySQL, and Oracle databases. Some of the databases have custom schemas and stored procedures.  
  
Which combination of steps should the company take for the migration? (Choose two.)

options.text: Use Migration Evaluator Quick Insights to analyze the source databases and to identify the stored procedures that need to be migrated.
Use AWS Application Migration Service to analyze the source databases and to identify the stored procedures that need to be migrated.
Use the AWS Schema Conversion Tool (AWS SCT) to analyze the source databases for changes that are required
Use AWS Database Migration Service (AWS DMS) to migrate the source databases to Amazon RDS.
Use AWS DataSync to migrate the data from the source databases to Amazon RDS.

questions.explanation:
AWS Schema Conversion Tool (SCT) analyzes source Oracle, SQL Server, and MySQL databases to identify necessary schema changes and conversion requirements for the target RDS environment. AWS Database Migration Service (DMS) performs the actual data migration while supporting heterogeneous database conversions. Migration Evaluator and AWS Application Migration Service are tools for different use cases and do not specialize in database schema conversion and migration.

**Learn more:** [What is the AWS Schema Conversion Tool?](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/SchemaConversionTool/latest/userguide/CHAP_Welcome.html) · [Migrating your source schema using AWS SCT](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/dms/latest/userguide/CHAP_GettingStarted.SCT.html)

lassName":"button hollow icon-accent icon-only question-actions"}],A company maintains a data lake in Amazon S3 that hundreds of applications across multiple AWS accounts must access. The company’s information security policy requires that the S3 bucket not be accessed through the public internet and that every application receive only the minimum permissions it needs to operate.  
  
To satisfy these requirements, a solutions architect intends to use an S3 access point, restricted to specific VPCs, for each application.  
  
Which combination of actions should the solutions architect perform to implement this solution? (Choose two.)

options.text: Create an S3 access point for each application in the AWS account that owns the S3 bucket. Configure each access point to be accessible only from the application’s VPC. Update the bucket policy to require access from an access point.
Create an interface endpoint for Amazon S3 in each application's VPC. Configure the endpoint policy to allow access to an S3 access point. Create a VPC gateway attachment for the S3 endpoint.
Create a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 in each application's VPConfigure the endpoint policy to allow access to an S3 access point. Specify the route table that is used to access the access point.

Create an S3 access point for each application in each AWS account and attach the access points to the S3 bucket. Configure each access point to be accessible only from the application's VPC. Update the bucket policy to require access from an access point.
Create a gateway endpoint for Amazon S3 in the data lake's VPC. Attach an endpoint policy to allow access to the S3 bucket. Specify the route table that is used to access the bucket.

questions.explanation:
Amazon S3 access points provide distinct endpoints with individual access-point policies and VPC network origins, enabling least-privilege access for each application. The underlying bucket policy must allow or delegate authorization through the access points. An Amazon S3 gateway VPC endpoint in each application VPC, associated with that VPC’s route table and restricted by an endpoint policy, lets applications reach S3 privately without using an internet gateway or NAT device.

**Learn more:** [Configuring IAM policies for using access points](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/AmazonS3/latest/userguide/access-points-policies.html) · [Gateway endpoints for Amazon S3](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/vpc/latest/privatelink/vpc-endpoints-s3.html)

During an audit, a security team found that a development team was placing IAM user secret access keys in its code and committing the code to an AWS CodeCommit repository. The security team wants to automatically detect and remediate occurrences of this security vulnerability.  
  
Which solution will automatically ensure that the credentials are properly secured?

options.text: Run a script nightly using AWS Systems Manager Run Command to search for credentials on the development instances. If found, use AWS Secrets Manager to rotate the credentials
Use a scheduled AWS Lambda function to download and scan the application code from CodeCommit. If credentials are found, generate new credentials and store them in AWS KMS.
Configure Amazon Macie to scan for credentials in CodeCommit repositories. If credentials are found, trigger an AWS Lambda function to disable the credentials and notify the user.
Configure a CodeCommit trigger to invoke an AWS Lambda function to scan new code submissions for credentials. If credentials are found, disable them in AWS IAM and notify the user.

questions.explanation:
AWS CodeCommit triggers can invoke an AWS Lambda function for repository events such as code pushes. The function can scan each new submission for exposed IAM credentials and, upon detection, disable the relevant IAM access key and notify the user, providing automated detection and remediation at the repository boundary. Amazon Macie sensitive-data discovery analyzes Amazon S3 objects, not CodeCommit repositories.

**Learn more:** [Manage triggers for an AWS CodeCommit repository](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/codecommit/latest/userguide/how-to-notify.html) · [Supported storage classes and formats - Amazon Macie](https://docs.aws.amazon.com/macie/latest/user/discovery-supported-storage.html)
